John . . . bound . . . and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife 4. of his brother . . . . For John said to him: “It is not lawful for you to have 5. her.” And wishing to kill him, . . . the peopl- . . . , because they regarded him as a prophe- . . . . 6. But when the birth- . . . of Herod . . . , . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . [Col. 0233] 7. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 8. But she, instructed beforehand by her mother, [Note: [Col. 0233] Thus also the Canterbury manuscript: *εἶπε, Δός*, “she said, ‘Give.’”] said: “Give + me here on this dish the head of John the Baptist.” 9. And King Herod was grieved; because of the oath, [Note: [Col. 0233] After “oath,” “but” is lacking, also in the Canterbury manuscript; there, together with the same addition, “because of” (*διά*) is added in the Vercelli, Verona, and Brescia manuscripts.] and because of + those reclining with him, he ordered it given. 10. And he sent and . . . beheaded Jo- . . . in pri- 11. . . . . And . . . was . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . brought . . . . 12. His disciples came and took the body and buried him; and they came and reported it to Jesus. 13. When Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat [Col. 0235] to a deserted place apart. And when the crowds heard it, they followed him on foot from the cities. 14. And when Jesus saw a large crowd, he had compassion on them and healed their sick. 15. But when evening came, his disciples came to him, saying: “The place is deserted and the hour has already passed; dismiss the crowd, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.” 16. But Jesus said: “They need not go; give them something to eat yourselves.” They answered 17. him: “We have only five loaves and two fish.” 18. And Jesus said: “Bring [Col. 0235] them [Note: [Col. 0235] After “them,” “here” is lacking, also in the Canterbury manuscript.] to 19. me.” And having ordered the crowd to recline on the grass, he took the five loaves and two fis- . . . , looked up to heaven, blessed, and bro- . . . , and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the crowds. 20. And . . . all ate and were filled; and they gathered twelve full baskets of fragments left over. 21. The number of those eating was five thousand men, besides children and women. 22. And immediately Jesus ordered his disciples [Note: [Col. 0235] It adds “his”; thus also the Vercelli manuscript and the Greek text, *αὐτοῦ*.] his + to embark in the boat and go ahead [Note: [Col. 0235] After “go ahead,” “him” is lacking, as in the Canterbury manuscript.] across the sea, [Col. 0237] until he should dismiss the crowds. 23. And having dismissed the crowd, he went up the mountain alone to pray. When evening came, he was there alone. 24. But the boat was in the middle of the sea, tossed . . . [Note: [Col. 0237] Thus also the Greek text: *ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων*, “by the waves.”] by the waves; for the wind was contrary to them. 25. But in the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them [Note: [Col. 0237] “Jesus” is added, following the Greek text: *ὁ Ἰησοῦς*.] Jesus + walking 26. upon the sea. And seeing [Note: [Col. 0237] Thus also the Canterbury manuscript: *δέ*, “but.”] but + him walking upon the sea, they were troubled, saying: “It is an apparition.” And they cried out in fear. 27. But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying: “Take courage; do not [Col. 0237] fear; it is I.” 28. Peter answered and said: “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you upon the water.” 29. And he said: “Come.” Peter descended from the boat and walked upon the water, to come to Jesus. 30. But seeing the strong wind, he was afraid; and when he began to sink, he cried out, saying: “Lord, save me.” 31. And immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, caught hold of him, and said to him: “You of little faith, why 32. did you doubt?” And when they had entered the boat, the wind ceased. 33. Then those in the boat came, [Col. 0239] worshiped him, and said: “Truly, you are the Son of God.” 34. And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of 35. Gennesaret. And when the men of that place recognized him, they worshiped him. And immediately they sent throughout that whole region and brought to him all who were ill. 36. And they begged him that they might only touch the fringe of his garment. And all who touched it were made well.

## CHAPTER XV

1. Then scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem came to him, saying: 2. “Why do your disciples transgress the [Col. 0239] tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.” 3. But he answered and said to them: “Why do you also transgress God’s commandment because of your tradition? For God said: 4. ‘Honor your father [Note: [Col. 0239] It adds “your,” as does the Greek text: *σοῦ*.] your + and your mother’; and, ‘Whoever curses father shall surely die.’ 5. But you say: ‘Whoever says to father or mother, “Whatever gift from me might benefit you,” 6. [Note: [Col. 0239] Before “has not,” “and” is lacking also in the Canterbury manuscript.] has not honored his father’; and you have made God’s word void [Col. 0241] because of your tradition. 7. Hypocrites, Isaiah [Note: [Col. 0241] Thus also the Greek text, *Ἠσαίας*, following the Latin custom of rendering Greek Η as E.] + rightly prophesied concerning you, saying: 8. ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. 9. Yet in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of human beings.’ 10. And having called the crowds to himself, he said to them: “Hear and understand. 11. It is not what enters the mouth that defiles a person; rather, what will proceed from the mouth defiles a person.” 12. Then his disciples came and said to him: “Do you know that the Pharisees, hearing this saying, were [Col. 0241] offended?” 13. And Jesus answered and said: “Every plant which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be uprooted. 14. Leave them alone: they are blind guides of the blind. If a blind person provides guidance to a blind person, both fall into a pit.” 15. Peter answered and said to him: “Explain this parable to us.” 16. He said: “Are you also still without understanding? 17. Do you not understand that everything entering the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled into the privy? 18. But those things which proceed from the mouth come forth from the heart, and they defile [Col. 0243] a person. 19. For evil thoughts come forth from the heart: murders, sexual immorality, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies. 20. These are what defile a person. But to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a person.”

21. And Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon. 22. And behold, a Canaanite woman coming out from those borders cried out, saying: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is grievously tormented by a demon.” 23. But Jesus answered her not a word. And his disciples came and urged him, saying: “Send [Col. 0243] her away, because she cries after 24. us.” But he answered and said: “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of 25. Israel.” But she came and worshiped him, saying: “Help me, Lord.” 26. He answered and said to her: [Note: [Col. 0243] Thus also the Canterbury manuscript: *οὐκ ἔξεστι*, “it is not lawful.”] “It is not lawful + to take the children’s bread and give it to 27. dogs.” But she said: “Certainly, Lord; for even the dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.” 28. Then Jesus answered and said: “O woman, great is your faith; let it be done to you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.

29. And as Jesus passed on from there, he came again beside the Sea of Galilee; and going up the mountain, [Col. 0245] 30. he sat there. And great crowds came to him, bringing with them the lame, blind, disabled, mute, and many others; and they laid them at his feet, and he healed them, 31. so that the crowds marveled as they saw them, and they glorified the God of Israel. 32. But Jesus, having summoned his disciples, said: “I have compassion on the crowds, because [Note: [Col. 0245] Thus also the Greek text: *ἤδη ἡμέρᾳ τρεῖς εἰσι καί*, “it is already three days and . . .”] it is already three days that + they remain with me and have no food; and I do not wish to dismiss them fast- . . . , lest they faint [Col. 0245] on the way.” 33. But the disciples say to him: “Where then in a deserted place could we get so many loaves . . . as to satisfy so great a crow- . . . ?” 34. And Jesus said to them: “How many loaves do you have?” They said: “Seven, and a few little fish.” 35. And he ordered the crowd to recline upon the ground. 36. And Jesus took the loaves and fish, gave thanks, and gave them to his disciples, and the dis- . . . gave them to the people. 37. And all ate and were filled; and they gathered . . . seven full baskets 38. of what was left over from the loaves. Those who ate were [Col. 0247] four thousand men, apart from children and 39. women. And, having dismissed the crowd, he entered the boat and came to the region of Magadan.

## CHAPTER XVI

1. And Pharisees and Sadducees came to him, testing him; and they asked him to show them a sign from heaven. 2. But he answered and said: “When evening has come, you say: ‘It will be fair, for the sky is red with clouds.’ 3. And in the morning: ‘There will be a storm today, because the sky is red.’ 4. You know how to assess the appearance of the sky, but cannot you recognize the signs of the times? [Col. 0247] An evil generation seeks a sign, and no sign shall be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.” And leaving 5. them, he went away. And when they had come across the sea, his disciples forgot to take bread. [Note: [Col. 0247] Thus also the Greek text: *ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς*, “but Jesus.”] 6. But Jesus + said to them: “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.” [Note: [Col. 0247] Thus also the Canterbury Latin and Greek manuscript: *τότε*, “then.”] 7. Then + they reasoned among themselves, saying: “Because we did not take bread.” 8. While they were reasoning, Jesus said to them: “Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, because you do not have bread? 9. Do you not yet under- . . . , nor remember the five loaves and the five [Col. 0249] thousand men, and how many baskets you took up? 10. Nor the seven loaves and the four thousand men, and how many baskets 11. you took up? Why do you not understand that I did not speak [Note: [Col. 0249] After “I said,” “to you” is lacking, also in the Canterbury manuscript.] about bread +? Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” 12. Then they understood that he did not [Note: [Col. 0249] Thus also the Greek text: *εἶπε*, “he said.”] say + to them that they should beware of le- . . . , but of the teaching of the Pharisees, they should beware. 13. Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi and asked his disciples, saying: “Who [Note: [Col. 0249] It adds “me,” as does the Greek text: *μὲ*.] do people say that I +, the Son of Man, am?” [Col. 0249] 14. And they said: [Note: [Col. 0249] Before “John,” “others” is lacking also in the Canterbury manuscript.] “John + the Baptist; others Elijah; still others Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.” 15. He said to them: “But who do you 16. say that I am?” Simon Peter answered: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” 17. Jesus answered and said to him: “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. 18. For I say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I shall build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against 19. it. And I shall give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.” [Col. 0251] 20. Then he commanded his disciples that they should tell no one that he was the Christ.

21. From then on Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go [Note: [Col. 0251] Thus also the Greek text in the neuter: *εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα*, “to Jerusalem.”] to Jerusalem + and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests, and be killed, and [Note: [Col. 0251] The Canterbury manuscript has *μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας*, “after three days,” from Mark.] after the third day + rise again. 22. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, [Note: [Col. 0251] Thus also the Canterbury manuscript: *καὶ λέγειν*, “and to say.”] and to say +: [Note: [Col. 0251] The Greek text reads *ἴλεώς σοι*, “may it be merciful/favorable to you.”] “May it be favorable to you +, Lord; this shall not happen to you.” [Note: [Col. 0251] Thus also the Greek text: *ὁ δέ*, “but he.”] 23. But he +, turning to Peter, said: “Get behind me, Satan; [Col. 0251] you are a stumbling-block to me, because you do not set your mind on the things of God but on those of human beings.” 24. Then . . . he said to his disciples: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself . . . and take up his cross and fol- 25. low me. For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it; but whoever loses his life because of me shall find it. 26. For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world but suffers loss of his life? Or what shall a person give in exchange for his life? 27. For the Son of Man is to come in the majesty of [Col. 0253] his Father with his angels, and he shall repay each person according to his works. 28. Amen I say to you: there are some of those standing here who shall not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in majesty.

## CHAPTER XVII
1. its. [Note: [Col. 0253] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἐγένετο, “and it came to pass.”] And it came to pass, after six days, that Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and led them apart up a high mountain; 2. and Jesus was transfigured before them. [Note: [Col. 0253] “Jesus” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ Ἰησοῦς.] And his face shone like the sun, while his garments became white 3. like snow. And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to him, speaking with him. [Note: [Col. 0253] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὤφθη, “appeared,” from Mark.] 4. Then Peter answered and said to Jesus: “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, let us make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” 5. While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. And behold, a voice was heard from the cloud, saying: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.” 6. When the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were greatly 7. afraid. And Jesus came and touched them, and said to them: “Rise, and do not 8. be afraid.” But when they lifted [Col. 0255] their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone. 9. And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: “See that you tell the vision to no one, until the Son of Man rises from the dead.” 10. And the disciples questioned him, saying: “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?” 11. But he answered and said: “Elijah indeed will come and restore 12. all things. But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished.” [Note: [Col. 0255] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτῷ, “to him,” from Mark.] 13. Then the disciples understood [Col. 0255] that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist: “So also the Son of Man must suffer at their hands.” [Note: [Col. 0255] Codex Cantabrigiensis likewise transfers here what the Vulgate Latin and Greek text have at the end of verse 12.]

14. And when he had come to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling before him and saying: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is moon-struck and suffers grievously; for he often falls into the fire, and sometimes into the water.” [Note: [Col. 0255] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐνίοτε, “sometimes.”] 15. “And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him.” 16. Jesus answered and said: “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I endure you? How long shall I be with you? Still … bring … him to me.” [Col. 0257] 17. And Jesus rebuked him, and the demon went out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour. 18. Then the disci…ples came to Jesus privately and said to him: “Why could we not … cast him out?” 19. He said to them: “Because of your unbelief. Amen I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible 20. for you. But this kind of demon is not cast out except by prayer and fasting.” 21. And while they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them: [Col. 0257] “The Son of Man is to be handed over into the hands of … 22. … him; and they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.” [Note: [Col. 0257] Codex Cantabrigiensis has μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας, “after three days,” as in the preceding chapter, verse 21.] When they heard this, they were greatly distressed. 23. And when they came to Capernaum, those who collected the tribute approached Peter and said to him: “Does your teacher not pay the tribute?” 24. And he said: “Certainly.” And when they entered the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: “What do you think? … kings … receive tribute or tax—from their sons or from strangers?” 25. He said: “From strangers.” Jesus said to him: “Then the sons are free.” [Col. 0259] 26. “But lest we cause them offense, go to the sea and cast a hook; take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth, you will find there a stater. [Note: [Col. 0259] “There” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐκεῖ.] Take it and give it to them for me and for yourself.”

## CHAPTER XVIII

1. On that day the disciples approached Jesus, saying: “… do you think is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” 2. And Jesus called a child to himself and placed him in their midst, 3. and said: “Amen I say to you, unless you turn and become like children, you shall not enter the kingdom 4. of heaven. Whoever therefore humbles himself like this child [Col. 0259] will be greatest in the kingdom of heaven. 5. And whoever receives one such child receives me. 6. But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a millstone turned by an ass be hung around his neck and that he be drowned in the depth of the sea. 7. Woe to this world because of stumbling-blocks. For … it is necessary that … stumbling-blocks come; but … woe to the person through whom the stumbling-block comes. 8. If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it away from you. It is better for you to enter life maimed or lame than, having two feet or two hands, to be cast into the eternal fire. [Col. 0261] 9. And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it away from you. It is better for you, having one eye, to enter life than, having two eyes, to be cast into the Gehenna of fire. 10. See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven. 11. But the Son of Man came to save what had perished. 12. What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep, [Note: [Col. 0261] “Man” is added, as also in the Greek text: ἀνθρώπῳ.] and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine in the mountains [Col. 0261] and go to seek the one that went astray? 13. And if it happens that he finds it, amen I say to you, he will rejoice over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray. 14. So it is not the will before your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

15. “And if your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between yourself and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother. 16. But if he does not listen to you, take with you one or two others, so that every word may stand on the testimony of two or three witnesses. [Col. 0263] 17. And if he does not listen to them, tell it to the church. But if he does not listen to the church, let him be to you as a gentile and a tax collector. 18. Amen I say to you: whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven. 19. … again, amen I say to you: if two agree on earth concerning any matter whatever they ask, it shall be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. [Note: [Col. 0263] “Amen” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἀμήν.] 20. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in their midst.” 21. Then Peter approached him [Col. 0263] and said to him: “Lord, if my brother sins against me, how many times shall I forgive him? Up to seven times?” 22. Jesus said to him: “I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven. 23. Therefore the kingdom of heaven is comparable to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. 24. And when he began to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed … ten thousand talents. 25. Since he had nothing with which to repay, his master ordered him, his wife, his children, and all that he had, to be sold, and the debt to be repaid. 26. That servant therefore fell down [Col. 0265] at his master’s feet and begged him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’ 27. Moved with compassion, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the debt. 28. But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii; and, seizing him, he choked him, saying: ‘Pay what you owe.’ 29. And his fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you.’ [Note: [Col. 0265] Before “I will repay,” *everything* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] 30. But he refused; rather, he went and put him in prison until he should pay the debt. 31. When his fellow servants saw what had happened, [Col. 0265] they were distressed; and they came and reported to their master all that had happened. 32. Then his master summoned him and said: ‘Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. 33. Ought you not also to have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?’ 34. And in anger his master handed him over to the torturers until he should repay the entire debt. 35. So also my Father who is in heaven will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.”

## CHAPTER XIX

1. And it came to pass, when Jesus had spoken [Col. 0267] these words, that he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judaea beyond the Jordan. [Note: [Col. 0265] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὅτε ἐλάλησεν, “when he had spoken.”] 2. And large crowds followed him, and he healed them … 3. And Pharisees approached him, testing him and saying: “Is it lawful for a man to dismiss his wife for any cause whatever?” 4. Jesus answered and said: “Have you not read that he who made [Note: [Col. 0267] After *made*, *man* is absent, as also in the Greek text.] from the beginning made male and female? And he said: 5. ‘For this reason a man shall leave father and mother and shall cling to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.’ [Col. 0267] 6. Thus they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined into one, it is not lawful to separate.” 7. They said to him: “Why then did Moses command a bill of divorce to be given and a dismissal?” 8. Jesus said to them: “Because of the hardness of your hearts Moses permitted you to dismiss your wives; but from the beginning it was not so. 9. But I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0268] After *to you*, *that* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] whoever dismisses his wife, [Note: [Col. 0267] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας, “except for a matter of sexual immorality.”] except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery.” [Note: [Col. 0267] After *commits adultery*, “and whoever marries a dismissed woman commits adultery” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis here and in chapter V, verse 32.] 10. His disciples said to him: “If the case of a man with his wife is so, it is not advantageous [Col. 0269] to marry.” 11. But Jesus said to them: “Not all accept this saying, but only those to whom it is given. 12. For there are eunuchs who were born thus from their mother’s womb; there are eunuchs who were made so by human beings; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who is able to accept this accept it.” 13. Then children were brought to him, that he might lay his hands on them and heal them. But his disciples prevented them. 14. Yet Jesus said: “Allow the children, and do not prevent them from coming to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” [Note: [Col. 0269] After *said*, *to them* is absent, also in the Greek text.] 15. And after laying his hand [Col. 0269] upon them, he departed from there.

16. And behold, one came up to him and said: “Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” 17. Jesus said to him: “Why do you ask me about what is good? One is good. But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.” 18. He said to him: “Which?” Jesus said: “You shall not kill; you shall not fornicate; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false testimony; 19. honor your father and your mother; and, you shall love your neighbor as yourself.” 20. The young man said to him: [Col. 0271] “I have kept all these things from my youth. What do I still lack?” 21. Jesus said to him: “If you wish to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.” 22. But when the young man heard this word, he went away sorrowful, for he had many possessions. 23. Jesus said to his disciples: “Amen I say to you that a rich person enters the kingdom of heaven with difficulty. 24. Again I say to you: it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter [Col. 0271] the kingdom of heaven.” 25. On hearing this, the disciples marvelled, [Note: [Col. 0271] They add “and were afraid,” with Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.] and were greatly afraid, saying: “Who then can be saved?” 26. Jesus looked at them and said: “With human beings this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” 27. Then Peter answered and said to him: “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then shall there be for us?” 28. Jesus said to them: “Amen I say to you: you who have followed me, in the renewal, when the Son of Man sits upon the throne of his majesty, will yourselves sit upon twelve thrones, judging [Col. 0273] the twelve tribes of Israel. 29. And everyone who has left house, brothers, sisters, father, mother, children, or fields for my name’s sake shall receive a hundredfold and shall possess eternal life. 30. But many who are first shall be last, and the last first.”

## CHAPTER XX

1. For the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard. 2. Having agreed with the workers on a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard. 3. Going out again about the third hour, he found others standing idle in the marketplace, [Note: [Col. 0273] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εὗρεν, “he found.”] 4. and said to them: “Go also into … vineyard m… and whatever … shall be right I will give you.” 5. And they went. Again [Note: [Col. 0273] After *again*, *but* is absent, also in the Greek text.] he went out about the sixth and ninth hours and did likewise. 6. About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing and said to them: “Why do you stand here idle all 7. day?” They said to him: “Because no one has hired us.” He said to them: “Go also into my vineyard.” 8. When even… had come …, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward: “Call the workers and pay them their wages, [Col. 0275] beginning with the last and continuing to the first.” 9. When those who had come about the eleventh hour arrived, they each received a denarius. 10. But when the first came, they thought that they would receive more …; yet they too each received a denarius. 11. And when they received it, they murmured [Note: [Col. 0275] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐγόγγυσαν, “they murmured.”] against the householder, 12. saying: “… These last … one hour … worked, and you have made them equal to us, who … bore … [the burden] of the day, …”

[Col. 0275] 13–14. “…? Take therefore what is yours and go. But I wish to give to this last one as also to you. 15. … Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish … with what is mine? Or is … your eye … because I am good? 16. … shall be last …”

17. Jesus, going up to Jerusalem, took his twelve disciples aside on the way, 18. and said to them: “Behold, we are going up to Jeru…salem, and the Son of 19. Man will be handed over … to the chief … priests and scribes, and they will condemn … him to death …” [Col. 0277] … 20. The mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him with her sons, worshipping and asking that something be given … 21. … he said: “… What do you want?” She said: “Command that … these two … one … at your right hand … and the other at your left … in your kingdom.” 22. He answered … “… [we] are able.” 23. Jesus said to them: [Note: [Col. 0277] “Jesus” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ Ἰησοῦς.] “You will indeed drink my cup …; but to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to give to you, [Col. 0277] but to those for whom it has been given … by my Father.” 24. … hearing … they were saddened because of the two brothers … 25. … of them; and … rulers … exercise authority 26. over them. It shall not be so among you; … whoever … shall be great among you … [Note: [Col. 0277] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔσται, “shall be.”] shall be … servant; 27. and whoever wishes …

[Note: [Col. 0277] This addition occurs also in the Greek and Latin Codices Cantabrigienses; yet in some particulars they differ from one another.]

“But you seek to increase from what is small, and, from what is greater, to become lesser.” [Col. 0279] [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: *to grow from what is least and diminish from what is great*; Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: ἐκ μικροῦ αὐξῆσαι, καὶ ἐκ μείζονος ἐλάττον εἶναι—that is, “to grow from what is small and become less from what is greater.”]

“On entering, and when invited [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: *when entering*; Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek has δειπνῆσαι, “to dine.”] to dine, [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: *to dine*; it agrees with Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek, which has δειπνῆσαι.] do not recline in the most prominent places, lest someone more distinguished than you should arrive; … the one who invited you to dinner [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: “the inviter to supper,” here and below; Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: ὁ δειπνοκλήτωρ, “the supper-inviter.”] should say to you: ‘Move still farther down,’ and you should be put to shame. But if you recline in a lower … place, and one lower than you should arrive, [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: “into the lowest place, and one lower than you comes”; Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: εἰς τὸν ἥττονα τόπον, “into the inferior place,” καὶ ἐπέλθῃ σου ἥττων, “and one inferior to you comes,” ἄνω καὶ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο χρήσιμον, “upward, and this will be useful to you.” Here is the complete Greek text of Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ὑμεῖς δὲ ζητεῖτε ἐκ μικροῦ αὐξῆσαι, καὶ ἐκ μείζονος ἔλαττον εἶναι. Εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ καὶ παρακληθέντες δειπνῆσαι, μὴ ἀνακλίνασθε (ms. ἀνακλείνασθαι) εἰς τοὺς ἐξέχοντας τόπους, μὴποτε ἐνδοξότερός σου ἐπέλθῃ, καὶ προσελθών ὁ δειπνοκλήτωρ εἴπῃ σοι, ἔτι Κάτω χώρει, καὶ καταισχυνθήσῃ. Ἔαν δὲ ἀναπέσῃς εἰς τὸν ἥττονα τόπον, καὶ ἐπέλθῃ σου ἥττων, ἐρεῖ σοι ὁ δειπνοκλήτωρ· σύναγε ἔτι ἄνω, καὶ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο χρήσιμον. That is: “But you seek to grow from what is small and to be less from what is greater. But when entering and invited to dine, do not recline in the prominent places, lest someone more distinguished than you arrive, and the dinner-inviter come and say to you, ‘Move still lower,’ and you be put to shame. But if you recline in the lower place and someone lower than you arrives, the dinner-inviter will say to you, ‘Move still farther up,’ and this will be useful to you.” The manuscript reads ἀνακλείνασθαι, “to recline,” for ἀνακλίνασθε, “recline.”] the one who invited you to dinner will say to you: [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: “gather yourself still farther upward, and this will be useful to you,” corresponding to the Greek σύναγε ἔτι ἄνω, “move up further.”] ‘Move still farther upward. And this will be more useful to you.’”

15. For then there will be [Col. 0309] great affliction, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will be. 22. 23. Then if anyone says to you, “Behold, here is Christ,” or “Behold, there,” do not believe it.

1. When morning had come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, to deliver him over to death. 2. And having bound him, they led him away and delivered him to Pontius Pilate, the governor. 3. Then Judas, who had betrayed him, seeing that he had been condemned . . ., moved by repentance, brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, 4. saying: “I have sinned in betraying innocent blood.” But they said: “What is that to us? See to it yourself.” [Col. 0337] 5. And, having thrown down the silver in the temple, he departed; and he went away and hanged himself with a noose. 6. But the chief priests, having received the money, said: “It is not lawful to put it into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.” 7. And having taken counsel among themselves, they bought the potter’s field for the burial of strangers. [Note: [Col. 0337] After *they bought*, “from them” is lacking, also in the Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis.] 8. Therefore that field was called Acheldemac, that is, “the field of blood,” unto this present day. 9. Then was fulfilled what was spoken through the Prophet, saying: “And they received thirty pieces of silver, [Col. 0339] the price of the one valued, whom they valued from the sons of Israel; 10. and they gave them for the potter’s field, for the burial of strangers.”

11. But Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying: “Are you the King of the Jews?” And Jesus said: “You say so.” 12. And when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. 13. Then Pilate said to him: “Do you not hear how many testimonies they bring against you?” 14. And he did not answer him a single word, [Note: [Col. 0339] Before *a single*, *to* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] so that the governor was greatly amazed. 15. Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner whom they wished. [Col. 0339] 16. At that time they had [Note: [Col. 0339] So also the Greek text, *εἶχον* (“they had”).] an infamous prisoner called Barabbas. 17. Therefore, when they had assembled, Pilate said: “Whom do you want me to release to you of the two: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called 18. Christ?” For he knew that they had delivered him up out of envy. 19. [Note: [Col. 0339] From here to verse 42 of this chapter, everything is mutilated in the Gothic.] While he was sitting upon the tribunal, his wife sent word to him, saying: “Have nothing to do with that righteous man. For today I suffered much in a dream because of him.” 20. But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus. 21. And the governor answered them: “Whom do you want me to release [Note: [Col. 0339] So also the Greek text, *ἀπολύω* (“I release”).] to you of the two?” [Col. 0341] But they said: [Note: [Col. 0341] So also the Greek text, *Βαραββᾶν*.] “Barabbas.” 22. Pilate said to them: “What then shall we do with Jesus, who is called 23. Christ?” They all said: “Let him be crucified.” The governor said to them: “For what evil has he done?” But they cried out more loudly: “Let him be crucified.” 24. Pilate, seeing that he was accomplishing nothing [Note: [Col. 0341] So also the Greek text, *ὠφελεῖ* (“profits/accomplishes”).], but that rather a disturbance was arising, took water and washed his hands before the people, saying: “I am innocent of this man’s blood; see to it yourselves.” 25. And the whole crowd answered and said: “His blood be upon us, and upon our children.” 26. Then he released Barabbas to them; but Jesus, after he had been scourged, he handed over to them to be crucified.

27. Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and assembled around him [Col. 0341] the whole 28. cohort. And they clothed him in a purple tunic and wrapped a scarlet cloak around him. 29. And they placed a crown of thorns upon his head and a reed in his right hand. Kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying: “Hail, King of the Jews!” 30. And they spat in his face, took the reed, and struck his head. 31. And after they had mocked him, they stripped him of the cloak, clothed him in his own garments, and led him away to crucify him. 32. As they were going out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon, coming toward them; [Note: [Col. 0341] It adds “coming toward them,” also the Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Greek *εἰς ἀπάντησιν αὐτοῦ*, together with the Saxon version.] they compelled this man to carry [Col. 0343] his cross. 33. And they came to the place called Golgotha, that is, “the place of a skull.” 34. And they gave him wine mixed with gall to drink. And when he had tasted it, he would not dri . . . 35. But after they had crucified him, they divided his garments among themselves, casting lots, so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “They divided my garments among themselves, and cast lots for my clothing.” 36. And sitting down, they kept watch over 37. him. And they placed above his head the written charge against him: “This is the King of the Jews.” 38. Then two robbers were crucified with him: [Col. 0343] one at the right and the other at the left. 39. And those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads and saying: 40. “Ha! You who destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days, save yourself. If you are the Son of God, come down 41. from the cross.” Likewise also the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes [Note: [Col. 0343] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *καὶ Φαρισαίων* (“and Pharisees”).] and Pharisees, 42. said: “He saved others; he cannot save himself. Mary Mag . . . lene, and . . . Mary of Jam . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . of Zebedee. . . . 57. [Col. 0347] . . . at the entrance of the tomb, 61. and departed. But Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the se . . . pulchre.

62. But on the following day, which . . . after the prepar . . . ation, the chief priests and Phar . . . assembled before Pila . . . 63. saying: “. . . . . . we rem . . . red . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . third . . . I shall rise.” 64. Therefore command that the tomb be guarded until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come and steal him and say to the people: ‘He has risen from the dead.’ And the last error will be worse than the first.” 65. Pilate said to them: [Col. 0349] “You ha . . . [Note: [Col. 0349] So also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis, *φύλακας* (“guards”).] guards; go, guard it as 66. you know how.” And they . . . went . . . and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone, with the guards.

## CHAPTER XXVIII

LXXIV. 1. But in the evening of the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb. 2. And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, approached, rolled back the stone, and sat upon it. 3. His appearance was like lightning, and his garments [Note: [Col. 0349] It adds *white*, also the Greek text, *λευκόν* (“white [garment]”).] white 4. like snow. And the guards were terrified by fear of him and became [Col. 0349] like dead men. 5. But the angel answered and said to the women: “Do not be afraid; for I know that you seek Jesus, who was crucified. 6. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come, and see the place where the Lord was laid. 7. And tell his disciples that he has risen; and he goes before you into Galilee: there you will see him. [Note: [Col. 0349] “Behold,” as in Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἰδού*. Likewise, “I have said,” with the Greek text, *εἶπον*.] Behold, I have told you.” 8. And they went out quickly from the tomb, with fear and great joy, running to announce it to his disciples. 9. And behold, Jesus . . . met them, saying: “Hail.” They . . . approached him and took hold of . . . his feet . . . and worshipped him. 10. Then Jesus said to them: [Col. 0351] “Do not be afraid. Go, announce it to my brothers, that they may go into Galilee; there they will see me.”

11. . . . will see . . . . When they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests and scribes all that had happened. 12. And the chief priests, having assembled with the elders, took counsel and gave a large sum of money to the soldiers, 13. saying: “Say: ‘His disciples came by night and stole him while you were asleep.’ 14. And if this is heard by the governor, we shall persuade him and keep you safe.” 15. But they, having taken the money, did as they had been instructed. And [Col. 0351] this report was spread among the Jews unto this present day. 16. But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them. 17. And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted. 18. And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying: “All authority in heaven and on 19. earth has been given to me. Go. [Note: [Col. 0351] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *νῦν* (“now”).] Now teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the 20. Holy Spirit; teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you all days, unto the consummation of the age.” [Note: [Col. 0351] They add “Amen,” as does the Greek text, *Ἀμήν*; which certainly is not Matthew’s, but the Church’s, declaring its assent to this Gospel, as to the others, by this word.] Amen.

**THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MATTHEW ENDS. — THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO JOHN BEGINS.**

**CODEX VERONENSIS.**

[Col. 0142]

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0142]

. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
