[Col. 0144] . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . Babylon. And after the deportation to 12. Babylon, Jeconiah begot Salathiel. Salathiel, moreover, begot Zerubbabel. 13. Zerubbabel begot Abiud. Abiud begot Eliakim. Eliakim 14. begot A. . . . . . . . . . . . [Col. 0144] . . . Ach . . . . 15. begot Eliud. Eliud begot Eleazar. Eleazar begot [Note: [Col. 0143] So also the Greek text, *Ματθάν*.] Matthan. 16. Matthas begot Jacob. Jacob begot Joseph, to whom the Virgin Mary was betrothed. And the Virgin Mary bore Jesus . . . 17. Therefore, from Abraham to David there are fourteen generations; from David to the deportation to Babylon there are fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to Christ there are fourteen generations. [Col. 0146] Thus all the generations from Abraham until the coming of Jesus Christ are forty-two generations. But the birth of Christ was thus: 18. When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph . . . being with child by the Holy Spirit. And Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, 19. and unwilling to expose her publicly, wished to dismiss her secretly. 20. While he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared . . . “Mary, your wife; for what shall be born from her is of the Holy Spirit. 21. And she shall bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus. For he [Col. 0146] shall save his people from their sins . . . . . . was spoken by the Lord through [Note: [Col. 0145] They add “Isaiah”; and so does Codex Cantabrigiensis, *Ἠσαΐου*.] Isaiah 22. the prophet, saying: “Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb 23. and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel,” which is interpreted, “God with us.” . . . 24. from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; and he took his wife and did not [Note: [Col. 0145] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἔγνω* (“knew”).] know 25. her until she had borne a son, and he called his name Jesus.

## CHAPTER II

1. Therefore, when Jesus had been born in Bethlehem, a city of [Note: [Col. 0145] So also the Greek text, *τῆς Ἰουδαίας* (“of Judaea”).] Judaea, in the days of [Col. 0148] King Herod, . . . from the East came [Note: [Col. 0147] So also the Greek text, *εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα* (“into Jerusalem”).] into Jerusalem, saying: 2. “Where is he who has been born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the East and have come to worship him.” 3. But King Herod, hearing this, was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. 4. And having assembled . . . the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Christ was to be born. But they said to him: 5. “In Bethlehem, a city of Judaea; for thus it was spoken through the 6. prophet: ‘And you, Bethlehem of Judaea, are by no means least among the princi . . . . . . from you shall come a ruler, who shall govern my people Israel.’” Then Herod secretly summoned 7. the Magi and diligently inquired of them the time when the star had appeared to them. 8. And he sent them to Bethlehem, saying: “Go and inquire carefully concerning the child; and when you have found him, report to me, so that I also may come and worship him.” [Note: [Col. 0147] Thus the Old Interpreter commonly renders it in Latin when the Greek text links clauses with aorists, as here: *Ὅπως κᾀγὼ ἐλθὼν προσκυνήσω αὐτόν*, “so that I too, having come, may worship him.”] 9. When they had heard the king, they departed. And behold, the star which they had seen in the East went before them, until it came, [Note: [Col. 0148] Here likewise the letter *e* is clear, though somewhat erased.] and stood over the child. 10. And seeing the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great [Col. 0150] joy. 11. And entering [Note: [Col. 0149] So also the Greek text, *εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν* (“into the house”).] into the house, they found the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they worshipped him; and opening their treasures, they offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, 12. and myrrh. And having been warned . . . not to return to Herod, they went back into their own country by another way. 13. After they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying: “Arise, take the child and his mother, flee into Egypt, and remain there until . . . for Herod is about to seek this child in order to destroy him.” 14. Joseph arose, took the child and his mother 15. by night, and [Col. 0150] went into Egypt. And he remained there until the death of Herod, so that what had been spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Out of Egypt I called my son.” 16. Then Herod, when he saw that he had been deceived by the Magi, was very angry; and he sent and killed all the boys who were in Bethlehem and in all its district, from two years old and under, according to the time which 17. he had learned from the Magi. Then was fulfilled what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying: “A voice was heard in Ramah, 18. weeping and much lamentation: Rachel [Col. 0152] weeping for her children . . . to be comforted, because they are no more.”

19. But after Herod had died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in 20. Egypt, saying: “Arise, take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who sought the child’s life have died.” 21. . . . And he arose, took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. 22. But hearing that Archelaus was reigning in Judaea in place of Herod his father, he was afraid to go there; and being warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region 23. of Galilee. And he came and dwelt [Note: [Col. 0151] So also the Greek text, *εἰς πόλιν* (“in/into a city”).] in a city called Nazareth, so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “He shall be called [Col. 0152] a [Note: [Col. 0151] Greek text: *Ναζωραῖος*.] Nazarene.”

## CHAPTER III

1. In those [Note: [Col. 0151] But *then* is lacking, and so also in the Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis.] days John the Baptist came, preaching 2. in the wilderness of Judaea and saying: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.” 3. For this is he of whom it was spoken through Isaiah the prophet: [Note: [Col. 0151] In the second recension, *saying* is added.] “A voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.” . . . [Col. 0154] 4. Now John himself had clothing . . . of camel . . ., and a leather belt around his loins; and his food was locusts and wild honey. 5. Then all Judaea and all who lived around the Jordan went out to him from Jerusalem; and they were baptized . . . in the Jor . . . 6. dan, confessing their sins. 7. But seeing many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them: “Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath [Note: [Col. 0153] From here to the words *descending as though*, etc., verse 16, the Codex Cantabrigiensis is written in a later hand.] to come? 8. Therefore bear fruit 9. worthy of repentance; [Col. 0154] and do not presume to say within yourselves: ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you, God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham. 10. Even now the axe is laid at the roots of the trees. Therefore every tree not bearing good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire. 11. I indeed baptize you in water unto repentance; but he who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He himself baptized you in the Spirit . . . 12. whose winnowing-fan is in his hand; and he shall thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, gather the wheat [Col. 0156] into his barn, but burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” 13. Then Jesus came from Galilee to John, to be baptized 14. by him in the Jordan. . . . John hindered him, saying: “I need to be 15. baptized by you, and do you come to me?” But Jesus answered and said to him: “Allow it now; for thus it is fitting for us to fulfil all righteousness.” 16. Then he allowed him. And when Jesus had been baptized, immediately he came up from the water. And behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending [Note: [Col. 0155] They add “from heaven”; so also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ*.] from heaven like a dove coming upon him. And behold, [Col. 0156] a voice from heaven saying [Note: [Col. 0155] They add “to him,” with Codex Cantabrigiensis, *πρὸς αὐτόν*.] to him: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

## CHAPTER IV

1. Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. 2. And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterwards he was hungry. 3. And the tempter came to him and said: “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become loaves.” 4. Jesus answered and said: “It is written: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, . . . by the word [Note: [Col. 0155] “Which proceeds from the mouth” is lacking, as also in the Greek and Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis.] of God.’” 5. Then the devil took [Col. 0158] him into the holy city, set him upon the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him: “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. 6. For it is written: ‘He commanded his angels concerning you, that they may bear you up in their hands, lest perhaps . . . your foot against a stone.’” 7. Jesus said to him again: “It is written: ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’” 8. Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their splendor, 9. and said to him: “All these I shall give you, if you fall down and worship me.” 10. Then Jesus said [Col. 0158] to him: “Go [Note: [Col. 0157] It adds “behind me,” as also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ὀπίσω μου*. In Codex Vercellensis, *me* is lacking.] behind me, Satan; for it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone.’” 11. Then the devil left him; and behold, angels came and ministered to him.

12. But when Jesus heard that John had been delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee. 13. And leaving the city of Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum by the sea, in the districts of Zebulun 14. and Naphtali, so that what had been spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “The land of Zebulun and the land 15. of Naphtali . . . the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, [Note: [Col. 0157] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *Γαλιλαίας*.] Galilee of the nations—16. the people who sat in darkness [Col. 0160] saw [Note: [Col. 0159] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *εἶδον*.] a great light; [Note: [Col. 0159] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *(καὶ) οἱ καθήμενοι* (“and those sitting”).] those sitting in the region and shadow of death, light has risen upon them.” 17. From that time Jesus began to preach and say: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”

18. As he was walking [Note: [Col. 0159] *Jesus* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen. And he said to them: 19. “Come after me, and I shall make you become fishers of human beings.” 20. But they immediately left their nets and followed him. 21. And proceeding from there, he saw two other brothers, James [Col. 0160] the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. 22. And they left their nets and their father and followed him. 23. And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity among . . . 24. . . . his reputation went throughout all Syria; and they brought to him all who were ill, afflicted with various diseases and torments, those who had demons, lunatics, and paralytics; and 25. [Note: [Col. 0159] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *πάντας* (“all”).] he healed them all. And great crowds followed [Col. 0162] him . . . from the Decapolis, from Jerusalem, from Judaea, and from beyond the Jordan.

## CHAPTER V

1. But seeing the great crowd, he went up the mountain; and when he had sat down, his disciples came to him. 2. And he opened his mouth and taught them, saying:

3. “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. 4. [Note: [Col. 0161] The fourth and fifth verses are transposed in the Greek and Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis and in the Greek text, as in the Veronese and Brescian codices.] Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted. 5. Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth. 6. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied. [Col. 0162] 7. Blessed are the merciful, for God shall have mercy on them. 8. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. 9. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God. 10. Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. 11. Blessed are you when they revile . . . [Note: [Col. 0161] These words, “revile . . . say,” are to be supplied as *revile, persecute, say*, in accordance with Codex Cantabrigiensis, which reads *διώξουσιν . . . ὀνειδίσωσιν* (“they will persecute . . . they may revile”). Codex Brixianus has *persecute*.] . . . and say every evil against you [Note: [Col. 0161] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης* (“for righteousness’ sake”), which likewise omits *lying*.] for 12. righteousness’ sake. Rejoice and exult, for your reward is abundant [Note: [Col. 0161] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ* (“in heaven”).] in heaven. For thus they persecuted the prophets who were [Col. 0164] before you—their fathers.

13. You are the salt . . . If it has lost its savor, with what shall it be salted? It is good for nothing, [Note: [Col. 0163] After *good for nothing*, *any longer* is lacking; so also in the Greek and Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis.] except to be cast out and trampled under foot by people. 14. You are the light of this world. A city situated upon a mountain cannot be hidden. Nor do they light 15. a lamp and put it under a bushel, but upon a lampstand, so that it may give light 16. to all who are in the house. Thus let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

17. “Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets. I have not come to abolish, but to fulfil. 18. Amen, I tell you: until heaven [Col. 0164] and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke shall pass away from the law until all things happen. 19. Therefore whoever abolishes one of these least commandments and teaches people accordingly shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does and teaches them shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. 20. For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

21. “You have heard that it was said to the people of old: ‘You shall not kill; and whoever kills shall be liable to judgment.’ 22. But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother without cause shall be liable to judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Racha,’ shall be liable to the council. Whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire. [Col. 0166] 23. Therefore, if you offer your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something 24. against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go: first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift. 25. Be quickly reconciled with your adversary while you are with him on the way, lest perhaps your adversary hand you over to the judge, the judge hand you over to the officer, and you be cast into prison. 26. Amen, I tell you: you shall not come out from there until you have paid even the last quadrans.

27. You have heard that it was said [Note: [Col. 0165] After *it was said*, “to the people of old” is lacking. So also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic.] “You shall not commit adultery.” 28. But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart. 29. But if your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and cast it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna. 30. And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members [Col. 0168] perish than that your whole body [Note: [Col. 0167] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἀπέλθῃ* (“go”).] go into Gehenna. 31. It was also said: “Whoever dismisses his wife, let him give her a bill of divorce.” 32. But I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0167] After *I tell you*, *that* is lacking, as in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] whoever dismisses his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery. [Note: [Col. 0167] “And whoever marries a dismissed woman commits adultery” is lacking. So also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

33. “Again you have heard that it was said to the people of old: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall render to the Lord your oaths.’ 34. But I tell you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is 35. God’s throne; nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by 36. Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great king. Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one [Col. 0168] hair white or black. 37. But let your speech be ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is more than this is from evil.

38. “You have heard that it was said: ‘An eye for an eye, [Note: [Col. 0167] Before *a tooth*, *and* is lacking, as in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] a tooth for 39. a tooth.’ But I tell you not to resist evil. Rather, if anyone strikes you on your right cheek, offer him the left also. 40. And to him who wishes to contend with you in court and desires to take your tunic, let him have your cloak also. 44. And whoever compels you for a thousand paces, go with him [Note: [Col. 0167] So also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἔτι* (“yet/further”).] still two more. 42. Give to everyone who asks you, and do not turn away from one who wishes to borrow from you.

43. “You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ [Col. 0170] 44. But I tell you: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, and pray [Note: [Col. 0169] According to the order of the Greek text, *ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων (ὑμᾶς) καὶ διωκόντων ὑμᾶς*: “for those who mistreat [you] and persecute you.”] for those who slander and persecute you, 45. so that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he commands his sun to rise upon evil and good people, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous. 46. For if you love those who love you, what reward will you have? Do not even tax collectors do this? 47. And if you greet only your brothers, what more do you do? Do not even the Gentiles do this? [Col. 0170] 48. Therefore you also must be perfect, as your Father, [Note: [Col. 0169] So also the Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis, according to the Greek text, *ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς* (“who is in the heavens”).] who is in heaven, is perfect.

## CHAPTER VI
1. Take care not to perform your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven. 2. Therefore, when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be honored by people. Truly I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0169] Thus also Cant. Lat.] they have received + their reward. 3. But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that 4. your alms may be in secret; and your Father, [Col. 0172] who sees you in secret, will repay you openly. 5. And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, who love to stand praying in synagogues and at the corners of streets so that they may be seen by people. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward. 6. But when you pray, enter your chamber and, having shut the door, pray to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees you in secret, will repay you openly. 7. But when praying, do not use many words, like the Gentiles. For they think that they are heard because of their much speaking. 8. Therefore do not be like them. For [Col. 0172] your Father knows what you need before you ask 9. him. Therefore pray thus: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. 10. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in heaven and on 11. earth. Give us this day our daily bread. 12. And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. 13. And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil. [Note: [Col. 0171] “Amen” is absent, also in cod. Cant.] 14. For if you forgive people their sins, your Father who is in 15. heaven will forgive you also. But if you do not forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive [Col. 0174] your sins. 16. And when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites. For they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people to be fasting. Truly I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0173] Before “they have,” *because* is absent. Thus also in cod. Cant.] they have their reward. 17. But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, 18. so that you may not appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father, who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you openly. 19. Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where rust and moth destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal. [Note: [Col. 0173] From here as far as verse 27 of chapter VIII, everything is absent in cod. Cant. Gr., according to Mill in the appendix.] 20. But store up for yourselves [Col. 0174] treasures in heaven, where neither rust nor moth destroys, and where thieves do not dig through and 21. steal. For where your treasure is, there [Note: [Col. 0173] Thus the Greek text, ἒσται, “will be.”] will be + your heart also. 22. The lamp of your body is your eye. 23. If your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body is dark. Therefore, if the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness itself! 24. No one can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will endure the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God [Col. 0176] and Mammon. 25. Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious in your heart about what you shall eat, nor about what you shall put on your body. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing? 26. Look at the birds of heaven: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more numerous than they? 27. And which of you can add one cubit to his stature? 28. And are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither labor nor spin. 29. Yet I tell you that [Col. 0176] not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed as one of these. 30. For if God thus clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the fire, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith? 31. Therefore do not be anxious, saying, “What shall we eat?” or “What shall we drink?” or [Note: [Col. 0175] Thus also the Greek text, τί (περιβαλώμεθα), “what shall we put on?”] what + shall we wear? 32. For the nations seek all these things. But your Father knows that you need all these things. 33. Therefore seek the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be supplied 34. to you. Do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. [Col. 0178] Sufficient for the day is its own evil.

## CHAPTER VII

1. Do not judge, lest you be judged. 2. For with the judgment with which you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure with which you measure, it will be measured to you. 3. Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye, but do not see the beam in your own eye? 4. Or how can you say to your brother, “Allow me to remove the speck from your eye,” when behold, there is a beam in your own eye? 5. Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see to remove the speck from your brother’s eye. 6. Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor throw your pearls [Col. 0178] before swine, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet and turn and tear you to pieces. 7. Ask, and it will be given you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened 8. to you. For everyone who asks receives; and whoever seeks finds; and to the one who knocks it will be opened. 9. Or what man among you, if his son asks him for bread, would hand him a stone? 10. Or if he asks for a fish, would he hand him a serpent? 11. Therefore if you, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father, who is in heaven, give good things to those who ask him. 12. Therefore, whatever you wish people [Note: [Col. 0177] They add *good things*; thus also Cyprian, *On the Lord’s Prayer*. In the same place *thus* is added, in accordance with the Greek text, οὕπω.] to do to you, good things, thus + do also [Col. 0180] to them. For this is the Law and the Prophets. 13. Enter through the narrow gate: [Note: [Col. 0179] The Latin Vulgate translates “because,” taking ὅτι in the Hellenistic sense for ὡς, “how.”] how + broad and spacious is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter 14. through it. How narrow is the gate, and constricted the way, that leads to life; and few are those who find it! 15. Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves. 16. By their fruits you will know them. Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? 17. Thus every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit. 18. A good tree cannot [Col. 0180] bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit. 19. Therefore every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. 20. Thus by their fruits you will know them. 21. Not everyone who says to me, “Lord, Lord,” will enter the kingdom of heaven; but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he will enter the kingdom of heaven. 22. Many will say to me on that day, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?” 23. And then I will swear to them: “Because I do not know you: depart from me, all you who work iniquity.” [Col. 0182] 24. Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them is like a wise man who built his house upon a rock. 25. The rain descended, the winds blew, the floods came, and beat upon that house, and it did not fall, for it was founded upon 26. a rock. And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them is like a foolish man who built his house upon sand. 27. The rain descended, the winds blew, the floods came, and beat upon that house; and it fell, and its ruin was great. 28. And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowds were astonished [Col. 0182] at his teaching. 29. For he was teaching them as one having authority, not as their scribes and Pharisees.

## CHAPTER VIII

1. And when he came down from the mountain, great crowds followed 2. him. And behold, a certain leper came and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me.” 3. And Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I will; be cleansed.” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed. 4. And Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that [Col. 0184] Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.” 5. After this, when he had entered Capernaum, a certain centurion came to him, begging him and saying, 6. “Lord, my servant lies paralyzed at home and is grievously tormented.” 7. Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.” 8. And the centurion answered and said to him, “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; but only speak the word, and my 9. servant will be healed. For I too am a man set under authority, having soldiers under me; and I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.” [Col. 0184] 10. When Jesus heard this, he marveled and said to those who followed him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith in Israel. 11. And I tell you that many will come from east and west, and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven; 12. but the children of this kingdom will go into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” 13. And Jesus said to the centurion, “Go; as you have believed, so may it be done to you.” And the servant was healed from that hour. 14. And when Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying ill with fever. 15. And he touched her hand, [Col. 0186] and the fever left her; and she arose and ministered to them. 16. But when evening came, they brought to him many who had demons; and by a word he cast out the unclean spirits and healed all who were ill, 17. so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “He himself took our infirmities and bore our diseases.” 18. But when Jesus saw many crowds around him, he ordered [Note: [Col. 0185] It adds “his disciples.” Thus also the Gothic codex, τοὺς μαθητάς, “the disciples.”] his disciples + to cross the sea. 19. And a certain scribe approached and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.” 20. Jesus said to him: [Col. 0186] “Foxes have dens, and birds of heaven nests in which to rest; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.” 21. And another disciple said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.” 22. But he said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.” 23. And when he embarked in a little boat, his disciples followed him. 24. And behold, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was covered by the waves; but he 25. was asleep. And the disciples came [Note: [Col. 0185] After “came,” “to him” is absent. Thus also in the Greek text.] and woke him, saying, “Lord, save us; we are perishing.” 26. Jesus said to them: [Col. 0188] “Why are you fearful, you of little faith?” Then he arose, rebuked the wind and sea, and there was a great calm. 27. But those men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the winds and sea obey him?” 28. And when he had crossed the sea into the region of the Gerasenes, two men with demons met him, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly dangerous, so that no one could pass by that way. 29. And they cried out, saying, “What have we to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come before the time to torment us?” 30. Now not far from them was a herd of many swine [Col. 0188] feeding. 31. And the demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, send us into the herd of swine.” 32. And Jesus said to them, “Go.” But they, going out, went away into the swine; and behold, the whole herd rushed headlong into the sea, and they died 33. in the waters. But those who fed them fled; and, coming into the city, they reported everything, including what had happened to those who had demons. 34. And behold, the whole city went out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to depart from their borders.

## CHAPTER IX

1. And embarking in a little boat, he crossed over and came into the city. 2. And behold, they brought [Col. 0190] him a paralytic lying on a bed. And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven you.” 3. But some of the scribes said within themselves, “This man blasphemes.” 4. And when Jesus saw their thoughts, he said, “Why do you think evil things in your hearts? 5. For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven’ [Note: [Col. 0189] After “sins,” *your* is omitted; thus also cod. Cant. Lat.], or to say, ‘Rise and walk’? 6. But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralytic—“Rise, take up your bed [Col. 0190] and go to your house.” 7. And he rose and went to his house. 8. Seeing this, the crowds were afraid and glorified God, who had given such authority to people. 9. And as Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man sitting at the tax office, Matthew by name. And he said to him, “Follow me.” And rising, he followed 10. him. And it came to pass, as he reclined in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Jesus and his disciples. 11. And when the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, [Col. 0192] “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” 12. But Jesus, hearing it, said, “Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do. 13. Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” 14. Then the disciples of John came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast frequently, but your disciples do not fast?” 15. And Jesus said to them, “Can the sons of the bridegroom [Note: [Col. 0191] Thus also cod. Cant., νηστεύειν, “fast.”] [Col. 0192] fast + while the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them; and then they will fast [Note: [Col. 0191] They add “in those days”; thus also cod. Cant., ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις, and the Saxon Version from Mark or Luke.] in those days. + 16. No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment; for it takes its strength from the garment, and the tear becomes worse. 17. Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, the wine is spilled, and the wineskins perish. But they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.” 18. While he was speaking these things to them, behold, [Col. 0194] one ruler came, named Jairus, and worshiped him, saying [Note: [Col. 0193] After “saying,” *Lord* is absent, as in the Greek text.], “My daughter has just died; but come, lay your hand upon her, and she will live.” 19. And Jesus rose and followed him with his disciples. 20. And behold, a woman who had suffered a flow of blood for twelve years came up behind him and touched his garment. 21. For she said within herself, “If only I touch his garment, I shall be healed.” 22. But he turned, saw her, and said, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well.” And the woman was healed from that hour. 23. And when Jesus came into the ruler’s house, seeing the flute-players and the tumultuous crowd, he said, 24. “Withdraw, for the girl is not dead but asleep.” And they mocked 25. him. But when the crowd had been put out, [Note: [Col. 0193] In accordance with cod. Cant., ἐλθών, “having come.”] he came + and took her hand. And the girl arose. 26. And this report went out through all that land. 27. And as Jesus passed on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David.” 28. And [Note: [Col. 0193] Thus also cod. Cant.: καὶ ἔρκεται εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ προσῆλθον, “and he comes into the house, and they approached.”] he came into the house, + and [Note: [Col. 0193] They add “two”; thus also cod. Cant., δύο.] two + blind men came to him. And Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I can do this?” They said to him, “Certainly, Lord.” 29. Then he touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith may it happen 30. to you.” And their eyes were opened. [Col. 0196] And Jesus sternly warned them, saying, “See that no one knows.” 31. But going out, they spread his fame through all that land. 32. As they were leaving, behold, they brought to him a man who was mute and deaf and had a demon. 33. And when the demon was cast out, the mute man spoke; and the crowds marveled, saying, “Never has anything like this appeared in Israel.” 34. But the Pharisees said, “By Beelzebul, the ruler of demons, this man casts out demons.” 35. And Jesus went around all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the gospel [Col. 0196] of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every infirmity; and many followed him. 36. But seeing the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and lying down like sheep without a shepherd. 37. Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the workers are few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers into his harvest.”

## CHAPTER X

1. And having called his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every sickness and every infirmity among the people. 2. Now these are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, [Col. 0198] 3. his brother; James of Zebedee and John his brother; Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew the tax collector; James of Alphaeus; Judas the Zealot; and Thomas; [Note: [Col. 0197] They add *and*, as cod. Cant., καί.] and + 4. Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Carioth, who betrayed him. 5. Jesus sent these twelve, commanding them, [Note: [Col. 0197] Here too *and* is added, also in cod. Cant., καί.] and + saying, “Do not go on the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter cities of the Samaritans; 6. but rather go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. 7. As you go, preach, saying, ‘The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’ 8. Heal the sick, raise the dead, [Col. 0198] cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give. 9. Do not possess gold, silver, or money in your belts; 10. no bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor footwear, nor a staff in your hands; for the worker is worthy of [Note: [Col. 0197] Thus also cod. Cant., μισθοῦ, “wages.”] his wages +. 11. Into whatever city you enter, inquire who in it is worthy; and remain there until 12. you depart. And when entering the house, greet it, saying, ‘Peace to this house.’ 13. And if that house is [Col. 0200] worthy, your peace will come upon it; but if it is not worthy, your peace will return to you. 14. And whoever does not receive you or hear your words, as you go out from that house or city, shake the dust from your feet. 15. Truly I tell you: it will be more tolerable for the land of the Sodomites and Gomorrhites on the day of judgment than for that city. 16. Behold, I send you like sheep among wolves. Therefore be prudent as serpents and innocent as doves. 17. And beware of people. For they will hand [Col. 0200] you over in councils and scourge you in their synagogues; 18. and before kings and governors [Note: [Col. 0199] Thus also cod. Cant., Greek and Latin: σταθήσεσθε, “you will stand.”] you will stand + because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles. 19. But when they hand you over, do not be anxious what you shall speak; for in that hour you will be given what you shall speak. 20. For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you. 21. Brother will hand brother over to death, and father his child; and children will rise up against parents and put them to 22. death. And you will be hated by all people because of my name; but whoever perseveres to the end will be saved. 23. But when they [Col. 0202] persecute you in this city, flee to another. [Note: [Col. 0201] They add, “but if, etc., as far as, ‘to another.’” Thus also cod. Cant. Greek: ἐὰν δὲ ἐν τῇ ἄλλῃ διώκουσιν ὑμᾶς φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ἄλλην, “but if in the other they persecute you, flee to another,” with the same Cant. Latin.] But if they persecute you in another, flee to another. + Truly I tell you, you will not finish the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes. 24. A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master. [Note: [Col. 0201] After “master,” *his own* is absent. Thus also in cod. Cant.] 25. It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and for the servant to be like his master. If they have called the master of the household Beelzebul, how much more his household members? 26. Therefore do not fear them. For nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, nor hidden that will not be known. 27. What I tell you [Col. 0202] in darkness, say in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim 28. from the housetops. And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; but rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna. 29. Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? Yet not one of them falls to the ground without the will of your Father, who is in 30. heaven. [Note: [Col. 0201] Thus also cod. Cant.: ἀλλὰ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν, “but even the hairs of your head,” from Luke.] But even the hairs of your head + are all numbered. 31. Therefore do not fear: you are worth far more than sparrows. 32. Therefore everyone who confesses me before people, I also will confess [Col. 0204] him before my Father who is in heaven. 33. But whoever denies me before people, I also will deny him before my Father who is in heaven. 34. Do not suppose that I came to send peace upon the earth; I did not come to send peace, but a 35. sword. For I came to set [Note: [Col. 0203] Thus also cod. Cant., υἱόν, “a son,” from Luke.] a son + against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; 36. and a man’s enemies are his household members. 37. Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; [Note: [Col. 0203] These words, “and whoever,” etc., as far as “worthy of me,” are absent in cod. Cant. Greek and Latin.] and whoever loves his son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me 38. +. And whoever does not take up [Col. 0204] his cross and follow me is not worthy of me. 39. Whoever finds his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it. 40. Whoever receives you receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. 41. Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward; [Note: [Col. 0203] (c) These words, “and whoever receives,” etc., as far as “will receive,” are absent in Cant. Greek and Latin.] and whoever receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward. + 42. And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in my name—truly I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0203] Thus also cod. Cant., οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται ὁ μισθὸς αὐτοῦ, “his reward shall certainly not be lost.”] his reward will not perish. +

## CHAPTER XI

1. And it came to pass, [Col. 0206] when Jesus had finished [Note: [Col. 0205] It adds “these words,” also in Cantabr. and in the Gospel codex in Gonville and Caius College cited by Mill, here and at chapter VII, verse 26.] these words, + commanding his twelve disciples, that he departed from there to teach and preach in their cities. 2. But John, when he had heard in prison of the works of Christ, sent [Note: [Col. 0205] Cod. Cant. Greek and Latin, and Gothic: διὰ μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, “through his disciples.”] his disciples, + 3. and said to them, “Go and say: Are you the one who is to come, or are we to expect another?” 4. And Jesus answered and said to them, “Go and report to John what [Note: [Col. 0205] Thus the Greek text: ἀκούετε καὶ βλέπετε, “you hear and see.”] you hear and see +. 5. The blind see, [Note: [Col. 0205] They add *and* three times: the first and second in agreement with the Greek text, the third with cod. Cant., καί.] and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised, and good news is proclaimed to the poor. 6. And blessed is whoever is not [Col. 0206] offended by me.” 7. As they went away, Jesus began to teach the crowds concerning John the Baptist: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind? 8. But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft [Note: [Col. 0205] They add “garments.” Thus the Greek text, ἱματίοις.] garments +? Behold, those who wear soft garments are in the houses of kings. 9. But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet. 10. This is he [Note: [Col. 0205] After “this is,” *for* is absent, as in cod. Cant.] of whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, and he will prepare your way before you.’ 11. Truly I tell you, among those born of women no prophet greater than John the Baptist has arisen; [Col. 0208] yet the lesser one in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. 12. But from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven is being forced, and those forcing it seize it. 13. For every prophet and the Law prophesied until John; 14. and if you are willing to know it, he is Elijah who is to come. 15. Let the one who has ears to hear, hear. 16. But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplace and calling to one another, say- 17. ing: ‘We will sing to you, and you did not dance; we mourned [Note: [Col. 0207] They add “to you.” Thus the Greek text, ὑμῖν.] to you, + and you did not lament.’ 18. For John came [Col. 0208] neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’ 19. The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man and a drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’ 20. Then he began to reproach the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done because they had not repented. 21. Woe to you, Chorazin; [Note: [Col. 0207] Thus also cod. Cant., καί, “and.”] and + Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes. 22. Nevertheless I tell you: Tyre and Sidon will be more tolerably dealt with on the day of judgment than [Col. 0210] you. 23. And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted up to heaven? [Note: [Col. 0209] They add *or*. Thus also cod. Cant. Latin and Greek, ἤ.] Or + will you descend to hell? For if there had been done in Sodom—here the copyist omitted the words “the mighty works which were done”—in you, perhaps it would have remained until the present day. 24. Truly I tell you, the land of the Sodomites will be dealt with more leniently on the day of judgment than you. 25. At that time Jesus answered and said: “I confess to you, Father, Lord God of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them 26. to little children. Yes, [Col. 0210] Father, for so it was pleasing before you. 27. All things have been handed over to me by my Father. And no one knows the Son except the Father; nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and the one to whom the 28. Son chooses to reveal him. Come to me, all who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh 29. you. Take my yoke upon yourselves and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. 30. For my yoke is sweet, and my burden is light.”

## CHAPTER XII

1. At that time Jesus went through the grainfields [Note: [Col. 0209] Thus the Greek text, τοῖς σάββασι, “on the Sabbaths.”] on the Sabbaths +; and his disciples, [Col. 0212] being hungry, began to pluck ears of grain and eat. 2. But the Pharisees, seeing [Note: [Col. 0211] It adds “them.” Thus cod. Cant., αὐτούς, “them.” Perhaps the Vercelli manuscript also had the same reading.] them, + said to him, “Behold, your disciples are doing what it is not lawful for them to do on the Sabbaths.”

3. But he said to them: “Have you not read what David did when he himself and those with him were hungry: 4. how he entered the house of God and would eat the loaves of presentation, [Note: [Col. 0211] Thus also the Latin and Greek text of Codex Cantabrigiensis.] which + it was not lawful for them to eat, nor for those with him, except for priests alone? 5. Or have you not read in the Law that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple [Col. 0212] violate the sabbath and are without guilt? 6. But I tell you that one greater than the sabbath is here. 7. For if you knew what this means, ‘I desire mercy rather than sacrifice,’ you would never have condemned the innocent. 8. For the Son of Man is Lord [Note: [Col. 0211] Before *of the sabbath*, *etiam* (“also”) is absent. And so it is in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] of the sabbath.”

9. And passing on from there, he came into their synagogue. 10. And behold, there was a man [Note: [Col. 0211] They add *there was*, as does the Greek text, ἦν.] + with a withered hand; and they questioned him, saying: “Is it lawful to heal on the sabbaths?” so that they might accuse him. 11. But he said to them: “Which of you [Note: [Col. 0211] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, ἔχει.] has + one sheep, and [Note: [Col. 0211] *If . . . it* is absent, as in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] if it falls + into a pit on the sabbath, will not take [Col. 0214] it and lift it up? 12. How much more valuable is a human being than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the sabbaths.” 13. Then he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched out his hand, and it was restored to him like the other. 14. And the Pharisees, going out, took counsel against him, that they might destroy him.

15. But Jesus, knowing, withdrew from there. And many followed him, and he healed them. [Note: [Col. 0213] The words *but all whom he healed* are added, as in the Latin and Greek of Codex Cantabrigiensis: πάντας δὲ οὓς ἐθεράπευσεν, “but all whom he healed.”] And all whom he healed + he commanded them 16. not to make him widely known, 17. that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:

18. “Behold my servant, whom [Col. 0214] I have chosen,  
my beloved, in whom [Note: [Col. 0213] Thus also the Greek text, ἡ ψυχή μου, “my soul.”] my soul + was well pleased.  
I shall put my Spirit upon him,  
and he shall announce judgment to the nations.  
19. He shall not contend nor cry out,  
nor shall anyone hear his voice in the streets.  
20. A bruised reed he shall not break,  
and smoking flax he shall not quench,  
until he casts victory forth unto judgment;  
21. and in his name the nations shall hope.”

22. Then a man possessed by a demon, blind, mute, and deaf, was brought to him; and he healed him, so that he spoke, saw, and [Col. 0216] heard. 23. And all the crowds were astonished and said: “Can this be the Son of David?” 24. But the Pharisees, hearing it, said: “This man does not cast out demons except by [Note: [Col. 0215] The Greek text has Βεελζεβούλ, as does Codex Vercellensis; Codex Veronensis does not double the *e*.] Belzebul +, ruler of demons.” 25. But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself shall be laid waste; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand. 26. For if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then shall his kingdom stand? 27. And if I cast out [Note: [Col. 0215] Thus also the Greek text, τὰ δαιμόνια, “the demons.”] demons + by Belzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they shall be your judges. [Col. 0216] 28. But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then surely the kingdom of God has come upon you. 29. Or how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? Then he will plunder his house. 30. He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters. 31. Therefore I tell you: every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven people; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit shall not have that sin forgiven. 32. And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man shall be forgiven; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit shall not be forgiven, neither in this age [Col. 0218] nor in the age to come. 33. Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; for a tree is known by its fruit. 34. Brood of vipers, how can you speak good things since you are evil? For the mouth speaks from the abundance of the heart. 35. A good person brings forth good things from a good treasure, and an evil person brings forth evil things from an evil treasure. 36. Truly I tell you: for every idle word that people speak, they shall render account for it on the day of judgment. 37. For each person shall be justified by his words, and condemned by his words.”

38. Then some of the scribes and Pharisees approached him, saying: “Teacher, we wish to see some sign from you.” 39. But Jesus answered them: “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign; and no sign shall be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet. 40. For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster for three days and three nights, so [Note: [Col. 0217] They add *also*, as Codex Cantabrigiensis does: καί.] also + shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights. 41. The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching. [Col. 0220] And behold, one greater than Jonah is here. 42. The queen of the south shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the farthest regions of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here. 43. But when an unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it wanders through dry and desolate places seeking rest, and does not 44. find it. Then it says, ‘I shall return to the house from which I came out.’ And when it comes, if it finds it empty, swept clean, 45. and adorned, then it goes and takes with itself seven other spirits more wicked than itself; and entering in, they dwell there. And the latter condition of that person becomes [Col. 0220] even worse than the former. So shall it be with this most wicked generation.”

46. While he was speaking these things to the crowds, behold, his mother and brothers stood outside, seeking to speak with him.

47. But someone said to him: “Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak with you.” 48. But he, answering the one who spoke to him, said: “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?” 49. And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said: “Behold my mother and my brothers. 50. For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, that person is my brother, sister, and mother.”

## CHAPTER XIII

[Col. 0222]

1. On that same day [Note: [Col. 0221] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Ἐξῆλθεν, “went out.”] Jesus went out + [Note: [Col. 0221] *From the house* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] beside the sea and sat down. 2. Therefore I do not speak to them in parables: [Note: [Col. 0223] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἵνα βλέποντες μὴ βλέπωσι, καὶ ἀκούοντες μὴ ἀκούωσι, καὶ μὴ ἀσυνῶσι, μή ποτε ἐπιστρέψωσι· καὶ τότε πληρωθήσεται, “that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not hear or understand, lest perhaps they turn; and then it shall be fulfilled”; Codex Vercellensis agrees.] so that, seeing, they may not see, and hearing, they may hear and not understand, lest at any time 14. they turn. You shall hear with your hearing and not understand;  
and seeing you shall see and not see.  
15. For the heart of this people has grown fat,  
and with their ears they have heard heavily,  
and they have burdened their eyes,

stop up their ears and burden their eyes,

Then, when tribulation [Note: [Col. 0223] Thus also the Greek text, ἤ, “or.”] or + persecution arises because of the word, they are immediately caused to stumble. 22. He himself answered and said, “Elijah indeed is to come [Note: [Col. 0255] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἀποκαταστῆσαι, “to restore.”] to restore + 12. all things. But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did [Note: [Col. 0255] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτῷ, “to him,” from Mark.] to him + whatever they wished. 13. Then the disciples understood [Col. 0256] that he had spoken to them concerning John the Baptist: [Note: [Col. 0255] Codex Cantabrigiensis also transfers here what the Latin Vulgate and Greek text have at the end of v. 12.] Thus the Son of Man also must suffer at their hands +. 14. And when he had come to the crowd, a man approached him, falling on his knees before him, begging him and saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is moon-struck [lunaticus] and grievously afflicted; for he often falls into the fire and [Note: [Col. 0255] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐνίοτε, “sometimes.”] sometimes + into 15. the water. And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not heal him.” 16. Jesus answered and said, “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I endure you? How long shall I be with you? Bring him here to me.” [Col. 0258] 17. And Jesus rebuked him, and the demon went out from him; and the boy was cured from that hour. 18. Then the disciples came privately to Jesus and said to him, “Lord, why could we not cast it out?” 19. Jesus said to them, “Because of your unbelief. Amen, I tell you: if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.” 20. “But this kind of demon is not cast out except by prayer and fasting.” 21. While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said, “It is about to happen [Col. 0258] that the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men; 22. and they will kill him, and [Note: [Col. 0257] Codex Cantabrigiensis has μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας, “after three days,” as in the preceding chapter, v. 21.] after the third day + he will rise.” When the disciples heard this, they were greatly grieved. 23. When they came to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma approached Peter and said to him, “Does your master not pay the didrachma, or 24. tribute?” He said, “Certainly.” And when he entered + the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take tribute or tax—from their sons or 25. from strangers?” He said, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free.” [Col. 0260] He replied, 26. “Certainly.” “But lest we give them offense, go to the sea, cast in a hook, and take the first fish that comes up. When you open its mouth, you will find [Note: [Col. 0259] It adds ibi, “there,” as does Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐκεῖ.] there + a stater. Take it and give it to them for me and for yourself.”

## CHAPTER XVIII

1. At that time the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” 2. And Jesus called a child and set him in their midst, 3. and said, “Amen, I tell you, unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven. 4. Therefore whoever humbles himself like this child will be greatest in the kingdom of heaven. [Col. 0260] 5. And whoever receives one such child in my name receives me. 6. But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a millstone turned by an ass be hung about his neck and that he be drowned in the depths of the sea. 7. Woe to this world because of stumbling-blocks. For stumbling-blocks must come; nevertheless, woe to that person through whom the stumbling-block comes. 8. If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or lame than, having two feet or two hands, to be cast into eternal fire. [Col. 0262] 9. And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it away from you. For it is better for you to enter life with one eye than, having two eyes, to be cast into the Gehenna of fire. 10. Take care not to despise one of these little ones [Note: [Col. 0261] It adds “who believe in me.” So too Codex Cantabrigiensis: τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, “of those believing in me,” from v. 6 of this chapter.] who believe in me +. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in 11. heaven. The Son of Man came to save that which was lost. 12. What do you think? If a man [Note: [Col. 0261] It adds homini, “to a man,” as does the Greek text: ἀνθρώπῳ.] has + one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine in the mountains [Col. 0262] and go in search of the one that went astray? 13. And if it happens that he finds it, amen, I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray. 14. Thus it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish. 15. If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between yourself and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother. 16. But if he does not listen to you, take with you one or two others, so that by the mouth of two or three witnesses [Col. 0264] every word may stand. 17. If he does not listen to them, tell it to the church. But if he does not listen to the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector. 18. Amen, I tell you: whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven. 19. Again, [Note: [Col. 0263] It adds Amen, as does Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἀμήν.] amen + I tell you: if two of you agree on earth concerning any matter whatsoever that you ask, it shall be done for you by my Father who is in 20. heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in their midst.”

[Col. 0264] 21. Then Peter came to him and said, “Lord, if my brother sins against me, how many times shall I forgive him? Up to seven times?” 22. Jesus said to him, “I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven. 23. Therefore the kingdom of heaven is likened to a king who wished to settle accounts with 24. his servants. And when he began to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents. 25. Since he had nothing with which to repay, his master ordered him to be sold, along with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and for the debt to be paid. 26. Then [Col. 0266] that servant fell down and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience, lord, and I will repay everything.’ 27. [Note: [Col. 0265] After reddam, “I will repay,” tibi, “to you,” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Moved with compassion, that servant’s master released him and forgave him the debt. 28. But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants, who owed him a hundred denarii. Seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay what you owe.’ 29. His fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and [Note: [Col. 0265] Before reddam, “I will repay,” omnia, “everything,” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] I will repay you.’ 30. But he would not; instead, he went away and put him in prison until he should pay the debt. 31. When his fellow servants saw what [Col. 0266] was happening, they were greatly distressed; and they came and told their master everything that had happened. 32. Then his master summoned him and said to him, ‘Wicked servant, I forgave you the whole debt because you begged 33. me. Ought you not also to have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?’ 34. And his master, being angry, handed him over to the torturers until he should repay the entire debt. 35. So also my Father who is in heaven will do to you, unless each one of you forgives his brother from your hearts.”

## CHAPTER XIX

1. And it came to pass, [Note: [Col. 0265] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὅτε ἐλάλησεν, “when he had spoken.”] when Jesus had spoken + these words, [Col. 0268] that he departed from Galilee and came into the region of Judaea beyond 2. the Jordan. Great crowds followed him, and he healed them there. 3. Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to dismiss his wife for any reason whatever?” 4. Jesus answered and said to them, “Have you not read that he who made [Note: [Col. 0267] After fecit, “made,” hominem, “man,” is absent, also in the Greek text.] male and female from the beginning made them? And he said: 5. ‘For this reason a man shall leave father and mother and shall cleave to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.’ 6. Therefore they are no longer two, [Col. 0268] but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no human being separate.” 7. They said to him, “Why then did Moses command that a bill of divorce be given and the wife dismissed?” 8. Jesus said to them, “Because of the hardness of your hearts Moses permitted you to dismiss your wives; but from the beginning it was not so. 9. But I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0267] After vobis, “you,” quia, “that,” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] whoever dismisses his wife [Note: [Col. 0267] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας, “except on account of sexual immorality.”] except on account of sexual immorality + and marries another commits adultery.” [Note: [Col. 0267] After moechatur, “commits adultery,” the words “and whoever marries a dismissed woman commits adultery” are absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis here and in ch. V, v. 32.] 10. His disciples said to him, “If this is the case of a man with a wife, it is not expedient [Col. 0270] to marry.” 11. But Jesus said to them, “Not everyone receives this saying, but those to whom it has been given. 12. For there are eunuchs who were born thus from their mother’s womb; there are eunuchs made by human beings; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who can receive it, receive it.” 13. Then children were brought to him that he might lay his hands upon them and pray. But the disciples rebuked 14. them. Jesus, however, [Note: [Col. 0269] After ait, “said,” eis, “to them,” is absent, also in the Greek text.] said +, “Permit them, and do not forbid them to come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” [Col. 0270] 15. And after laying his hands upon them, he departed from there. 16. And behold, one came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do in order to have eternal life?” 17. But Jesus said to him, “Why do you ask me concerning the good? One is good, God. But if you wish to enter eternal life, keep 18. the commandments.” He said to him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “You shall not kill; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; 19. honor your father and your mother; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself.” 20. The young man said to him, [Col. 0272] “I have kept all these things from my youth. What do I still lack?” 21. Jesus said to him, “If you wish to be perfect, go, sell all that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.” 22. But when the young man heard this saying, he went away sorrowful, for he possessed many possessions. 23. Jesus said to his disciples, “Amen, I tell you, a rich person enters the kingdom of heaven with difficulty. 24. Again I tell you: it is easier for a camel to pass through a needle’s eye than for a rich person to enter the kingdom [Col. 0272] of heaven.” 25. When the disciples heard these things, they were greatly astonished [Note: [Col. 0271] They add “and were afraid,” with Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.] and were afraid +, saying, “Who then can be saved?” 26. Jesus looked at them and said, “With human beings this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” 27. Then Peter answered and said to him, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will there be for us?” 28. Jesus said to them, “Amen, I tell you that you who have followed me, in the renewal, when the Son of Man sits upon the throne of his majesty, will yourselves also sit upon twelve thrones, judging [Col. 0274] the twelve tribes of Israel. 29. And everyone who has left house, or brother, or sisters, or mother, or children, or fields for my name’s sake shall receive a hundredfold and shall inherit eternal life. 30. But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

## CHAPTER XX

1. The kingdom of heaven is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard. 2. Having agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard. 3. And going out [Col. 0274] about the third hour, [Note: [Col. 0273] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εὗρεν, “he found.”] he found + others standing idle in the marketplace 4. and said to them, “Go also yourselves into the [Note: [Col. 0273] After vineam, “vineyard,” meam, “my,” is absent, as in the Greek text.] vineyard +, and I will give you whatever is just.” 5. So they went. [Note: [Col. 0273] After iterum, “again,” autem, “but,” is absent, also in the Greek text.] Again + he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise. 6. About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing there, and said to them, “Why are you standing here idle all 7. day?” They said to him, “Because no one has hired us.” He said to them, “Go also yourselves into my vineyard.” 8. When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his steward, “Call the laborers and give them their wages, [Col. 0276] beginning with the last and ending with the first.” 9. When those who had come about the eleventh hour arrived, they each received a denarius. 10. When the first came, they thought they would receive more; but they too each received a denarius. 11. And when they received it, [Note: [Col. 0275] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐγόγγυσαν, “they murmured.”] they murmured + against the householder, 12. saying, “These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the heat.” 13. But he answered one of them and said, “Friend, I do you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius? [Col. 0276] 14. Take what is yours and go. But I wish to give this last one the same as to you. 15. Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish? Or is your eye evil because I am good? 16. So the last shall be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few chosen.” 17. As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples apart and said to them, 18. “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man 19. will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes; they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, [Col. 0278] scourge, and crucify; and on the third day he will rise.” 20. Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, worshipping and asking something of him. 21. He said to her, “What do you desire?” She said to him, “Command that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.” 22. Jesus answered and said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup which I am about to drink?” They said to him, “We can.” 23. [Note: [Col. 0277] It adds Jesus, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ Ἰησοῦς, “Jesus.”] Jesus said + to them, “You shall indeed drink my cup; but to sit at my right hand [Col. 0278] or at my left is not mine to give to you, but belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.” 24. When the ten heard it, they were grieved at the two brothers. 25. But Jesus called them to himself and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and their great men exercise authority over them. 26. It shall not be so among you. But whoever wishes to become great among you [Note: [Col. 0277] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔσται, “shall be.”] shall be + your 27. servant; and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave; 28. just as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

[Note: [Col. 0277] This addition is also in the Greek and Latin Codices Cantabrigienses; in some copies, however, they differ among themselves.]

But you [Col. 0280] seek [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: “to grow from the least, and from the great to become smaller”; Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: ἐκ μικροῦ αὐξῆσαι, καὶ ἐκ μείζονος ἐλάττον εἶναι—that is, “to grow from the small, and from the greater to become less.”] to grow from the small and to become greater out of the lesser +. [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: introeuntes, “entering.”] But when you enter + and are invited [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: coenare, “to dine”; and Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek agrees, having δειπνῆσαι, “to dine.”] to a dinner +, do not recline in the more prominent places, lest one more distinguished than you arrive; and [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin, reads here and below “the inviter to dinner”; Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: ὁ δειπνοκλήτωρ, “the inviter to dinner.”] the one who invited you to dinner + come and say to you, “Go still lower,” and you be put to shame. But if [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: “in the lowest place, and one lower than you comes”; Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: εἰς τὸν ἥττονα τόπον, “into the lower place,” καὶ ἐπέλθῃ σου ἥττων, “and one lower than you comes,” ἄνω καὶ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο χρήσιμον, “upward, and this will be useful to you.” Here is the complete Greek text of Codex Cantabrigiensis: “But you seek to grow from the small, and from the greater to become less. And when you enter and are invited to dine, do not recline [manuscript: ἀνακλείνασθαι] in the prominent places, lest one more glorious than you come; and when the inviter to dinner comes near, he may say to you, ‘Go still lower,’ and you will be ashamed. But if you recline in the lower place, and one lower than you comes, the inviter to dinner will say to you: ‘Move still higher,’ and this will be useful to you.”] you recline in a lower place and one humbler than you arrives +, the one who invited you to dinner will say to you, [Note: [Col. 0279] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: collige adhuc superius, “move still further up”; and Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: σύναγε ἔτι ἄνω, “move still upward.”] “Come further up.” And [Col. 0280] this will be more advantageous to you +. 29. As they went out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him. 30. And behold, two blind men sitting beside the road heard that Jesus was passing by and cried out, saying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David.” 31. But the crowd rebuked them so that they might be silent. Yet they cried out all the more, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.” 32. Jesus stopped, called them, and said, “What do you want me [Note: [Col. 0279] Before faciam, “I do,” ut, “that,” is absent, also in the Greek text.] to do 33. for you?” They said to him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.” [Col. 0282] 34. Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes; and immediately they saw and followed him.

## CHAPTER XXI

1. And it came to pass, when he drew near to Jerusalem and came + [Note: [Col. 0281] It adds in, as does the Greek text: εἰς, “into.”] to Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, that Jesus sent two disciples, 2. saying to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and you will find a donkey tied there and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them 3. to me. If anyone says anything to you, say that the Lord needs their service, and immediately he will send them.” 4. This [Note: [Col. 0281] Before factum est, “it happened,” totum, “wholly,” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] happened [Col. 0282] so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Say to the daughter of 5. Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, gentle, seated upon a colt, the foal of a donkey, a young [Note: [Col. 0281] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: ὑποζύγιον, “beast under the yoke,” a pack animal.] beast of burden +.” 6. The disciples went and did as Jesus commanded them. 7. They brought the donkey and the colt, laid their garments upon it, and [Note: [Col. 0281] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek: ἐκάθητο ἐπ’ αὐτόν, “he sat upon it.”] he sat upon it +. 8. A very great crowd spread their garments upon the road; others cut branches from the trees and spread them in the road. [Col. 0284] 9. The crowds going before him and those following cried out, saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!” 10. When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred, saying, 11. “Who is this?” [Note: [Col. 0283] Codex Cantabrigiensis reads: οἱ δὲ πολλοὶ εἶπον, “but the many said.”] The many + said, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee.” 12. Jesus entered the temple [Note: [Col. 0283] After templum, “temple,” Dei, “of God,” is absent also in the Coptic, Ethiopic, and Saxon versions; nor do Mark and Luke have it.] and cast out all those selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves. 13. He said to them, “It is written: ‘My house [Col. 0284] shall be called a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.” 14. The blind and lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them. 15. But when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonders which Jesus did, and the children crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they were in- 16. dignant and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Certainly. Have you never read: ‘Out of the mouth of infants and nursing children you have perfected praise’?” 17. Leaving them, he went out of the city to Bethany and lodged there. 18. In the morning, [Note: [Col. 0283] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek: παράγων, “passing by.”] as he was passing + into the city, he was hungry. [Col. 0286] 19. Seeing a fig tree by the road, he came to it and found nothing on it except leaves only. He said to it, “May fruit never grow from you forever.” And immediately the fig tree withered. 20. When the disciples saw it, they were astonished and said, “How did it wither immediately?” 21. Jesus answered and said, “Amen, I tell you: if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree; but even if you say to this mountain, [Note: [Col. 0285] After quare, “why,” ergo, “then,” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] ‘Be taken up and thrown + into the sea,’ it shall happen. 22. And all things whatsoever you ask in prayer, believing, you shall receive.” 23. When he came [Col. 0286] into the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people came to him, saying, “By what authority do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?” 24. Jesus answered and said to them, “I too will ask you one thing. If you tell me this, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things. 25. [Note: [Col. 0286] So also the Greek text, using the neuter τὸ βάπτισμα, “the baptism.”] The baptism of John—whence was it? From heaven or from men?” But they reasoned among themselves, saying, 26. “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the crowd, for they all regard + John [Col. 0288] as a prophet.” 27. They answered Jesus and said, “We do not know.” He too said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things. 28. But what do you think? A man had two sons. Coming to the first, he said, ‘Son, go work today in the 29. vineyard.’ He answered, ‘I will not.’ But afterward, moved by repentance, he went into the vineyard. 30. He came to the other and said likewise. But he answered, ‘I go, lord,’ and 31. did not go.
