Which [Col. 0288] of the two did the will of the father?” They said to him, “The last +.” Jesus said to them, “Amen, I tell you: tax collectors and prostitutes will go before you into the kingdom of God. 32. For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Yet you, when you saw this, did not afterward repent so as to believe him. 33. Hear another parable. There was a householder who planted a vineyard, set a hedge around it, dug a winepress in it, and built [Col. 0290] a tower. He leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad. 34. When the season for fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to receive his fruits. 35. But the tenants seized his servants: they beat one, stoned another, and killed another. 36. Again he sent other servants, more numerous than the first, and they did the same to them. 37. Finally he sent them his only son, saying, [Note: [Col. 0289] Some Greek manuscripts and the Syriac, Persian, and Arabic versions, as well as Irenaeus and Chrysostom, add “perhaps,” from Luke.] ‘Perhaps + they will respect my son.’ 38. But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.’ [Col. 0290] 39. They seized him, [Note: [Col. 0289] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἀπέκτειναν καὶ ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος, “they killed and cast [him] outside the vineyard,” and the old Saxon version.] killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard +. 40. Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?” 41. They said to him, “He will destroy those wicked men miserably, and lease his vineyard to other tenants, who [Note: [Col. 0289] So also the Greek text: ἀποδώσουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς καρπούς, “will render him the fruits.”] will render him its fruits + in their seasons.” 42. Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone rejected by the builders has become the head of the corner. This [Note: [Col. 0289] Iste, “this,” relates to γωνίας, “corner.”] was made by the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’? 43. Therefore I tell you: the kingdom of God shall be taken away from you and given to a people producing its fruit.” [Note: [Col. 0289] The whole of v. 44 is absent, also in the Greek and Latin Codices Cantabrigienses.] [Col. 0292] 45. When the chief priests and Pharisees heard his parables, they knew that he spoke concerning them. 46. Though they sought to seize him, they feared the crowd, because the crowd regarded him as a prophet.

## CHAPTER XXII

1. Jesus answered and again spoke to them in parables, saying, 2. “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast for his son. 3. He sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding feast, but they would not come. Again he sent other servants, saying, 4. ‘Tell those invited: Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and fattened animals have been killed, and everything is ready. Come [Col. 0292] to the wedding feast.’ 5. But they disregarded it and went away, [Note: [Col. 0291] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οἱ μὲν . . . οἱ δὲ, “some . . . others.”] some to their own farm and others to their own business; 6. while the rest seized his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them. 7. [Note: [Col. 0291] It adds ille, “that,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐκεῖνος, “that one,” which Verona omits; autem, “but,” is omitted.] When that king heard it, he was angry. He sent [Note: [Col. 0291] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τὸ στράτευμα, “the army.”] his army +, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. 8. Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. 9. Therefore go to the outlets of the roads, and call to the 10. wedding feast whomever you find.’ His servants went out into the roads and gathered together [Col. 0294] [Note: [Col. 0293] So also the Greek text: ὅσους, “as many as.”] all + whom they found, bad and good; and the wedding feast was filled with those reclining at table. 11. But the king entered to inspect those reclining at table and saw there a man not dressed [Note: [Col. 0293] So the Italic version, tenacious of its wording here and elsewhere and closely following the syntax of the Greek text, which has ἔνδυμα, “garment.”] in a wedding garment +. 12. He said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here without having a wedding garment?’ But he was speechless. 13. Then the king said to the attendants, [Note: [Col. 0293] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἄρατε αὐτὸν ποδῶν καὶ χειρῶν, καὶ, “take him by feet and hands, and.”] ‘Take him by the feet and hands, and + cast him into the outer darkness. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’ 14. For many are called, but few chosen.” 15. Then the Pharisees went away and took counsel [Col. 0294] how they might entrap him in speech. 16. They sent their disciples with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and that you care for no one’s opinion, for you do not regard human persons. [Note: [Col. 0293] Before quid, “what,” dic ergo nobis, “tell us therefore,” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis; Mark and Luke do not have it.] What + do you think? Is it lawful to pay tax to Caesar or not?” 18. But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said, “Why do you test me, hypocrites? 19. Show me the coin of the tax.” They brought him a denarius. 20. [Note: [Col. 0293] Before ait, “said,” et, “and,” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Jesus said + to them, “Whose image is this, and whose inscription?” 21. They said to him, “Caesar’s.” Then Jesus said [Col. 0296] to them, “Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” 22. When they heard this, they marveled; and leaving him, they went away. 23. On that day Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no resurrection, and questioned him, saying, “Teacher, Moses said: ‘If someone dies without having a son, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’ 25. Now there were among us seven brothers. The first married and died without offspring, leaving his wife to his brother. 26. Likewise the second and the third, through the seventh. 27. Finally, after them all, [Col. 0296] the woman also died. 28. In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her.” 29. Jesus answered and said to them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures or the power 30. of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like [Note: [Col. 0295] After Angeli, “angels,” Dei, “of God,” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] angels + in heaven. 31. But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying: 32. ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” 33. When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at his teaching. 34. But when the Pharisees heard [Col. 0298] that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together [Note: [Col. 0297] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek: ἐπ’ αὐτόν, “to him.”] and came to him +. 35. One of them, a doctor of the law, questioned him, testing him, 36. [Note: [Col. 0297] It adds et dicens, “and saying,” also the Greek text: καὶ λέγων.] and saying +, “Teacher, which commandment is great 37. in the law?” Jesus said to him, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. 38. This is the greatest and first commandment. 39. The second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. 40. On these two commandments hang the whole law and the prophets.” 41. While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them, saying, 42. “What do you think about the Christ? Whose [Col. 0298] son is he?” They said to him, “David’s.” 43. He said to them, “How then does David, in the Spirit, call him Lord, saying: 44. ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I place your enemies [Note: [Col. 0297] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek: ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου, “beneath your feet.”] beneath your feet +’? 45. If David calls him Lord [Note: [Col. 0297] It adds in spiritu, “in the Spirit,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν πνεύματι.] in the Spirit +, how is he his son?” 46. And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day onward to question him any further.

## CHAPTER XXIII
1. Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples, 2. saying: “The scribes and Pharisees have seated themselves upon Moses’ chair. 3. Therefore keep and do all things whatsoever they tell you; but do not act according to their deeds, [Col. 0300] for they speak, yet do not themselves act. 4. They bind heavy burdens and lay them upon people’s shoulders, but they are unwilling to move them with their own finger. 5. Indeed, they perform all their works in order to be seen by people: for they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge their fringes. 6. They love the chief place at banquets [Note: [Col. 0299] So also the Greek text, *tēn prōtoklisian*, “the first reclining-place.”], and the foremost seats in synagogues, and 7. greetings in the marketplace, and to be called Rabbi by people. 8. But you are not to be called Rabbi; for one is your Teacher, and you are all brothers. 9. And do not call anyone your father on earth; for one is your Father, [Col. 0300] who is in heaven. 10. Nor are you to be called masters, because your one Master is Christ. 11. Whoever is greater among you shall be your servant. 12. But whoever exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.

13. “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven against people. For you yourselves do not enter, nor do you allow those entering to enter. 14. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour widows’ houses, praying under a lengthy pretext [Note: [Col. 0299] So also the Greek text, *prophasei makra*, “under a long pretext.”]; for this reason you shall receive a greater judgment. 15. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you traverse sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he has become one, you make him [Col. 0302] a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves. 16. Woe to you, blind guides, who say: ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound.’ [Note: [Col. 0301] So also the Greek text, *en tō naō*, “by/in the temple.”] 17. Fools and blind men! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the 18. gold? And whoever [Note: [Col. 0301] A page is missing.]

. . . [lacuna] . . .

[Col. 0302]

. . . [lacuna] . . .

[Col. 0304]

. . . outwardly handsome to people, but within they are full of the bones of the dead and of every impurity. 28. So also you outwardly indeed appear righteous to people, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity. 29. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, and 30. say: ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners [Col. 0304] in the blood of the prophets.’ 31. Thus you bear testimony against yourselves that you are sons of those who killed the prophets. 32. And you, fill up the measure of your fathers. 33. Brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna? 34. Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes; and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city, 35. so that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you [Col. 0306] killed between the temple and the altar. 36. Amen, I tell you: all these things shall come upon this generation.

37. “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you: how often I wished to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks beneath her wings, and you were unwilling! 38. Behold, your house is left [Note: [Col. 0305] So also the Greek text, *aphietai*, “is left.”] to you desolate. 39. But I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0305] It adds *quia*, ‘because/that,’ as does the Codex of Canterbury, Greek *hoti*.] that you shall not see me henceforth until you say: ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

## CHAPTER XXIV

1. And Jesus, going out from the temple, was departing. And his disciples approached him [Col. 0306] in order to show him the structures of the 2. temple. But he answered and said to them: “Do you see all these things? Amen, I tell you: not one stone here shall be left upon another that will not be thrown down.” 3. And as he sat upon the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying: “Tell us, when will these things be? And what will be the sign of your coming and of the consummation of the age?” 4. And Jesus answered and said: “See that no one deceives you in any 5. way. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am Christ,’ and they will deceive many. 6. And you will hear of battles and reports of wars. See that you are not troubled, [Col. 0308] for these things must happen, but the end is not yet. 7. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there shall be famines and earthquakes in various places [Note: [Col. 0307] ‘And pestilences’ is absent, also in the Canterbury Latin and Greek codices.], 8. all these being the beginnings of sufferings.

9. “Then they will deliver you over to tribulation and kill you; and you will be hated by all nations because of my name. 10. And then many will fall away, and will betray one another and hate one another. 11. And many false prophets will arise and deceive many. 12. And because iniquity will abound, the love of many will grow cold. 13. But whoever perseveres to the end—to the end—that person [Col. 0308] shall be saved. 14. And this Gospel of the kingdom shall be preached throughout the whole world, as a testimony to all nations; and then the consummation shall come.

15. “Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—[Note: [Col. 0307] The Greek texts render these words not quite appropriately: *to rhēthen dia Daniēl tou prophētou, hestōs*, ‘that which was spoken through Daniel the prophet, standing.’ For both *to rhēthen* and *hestōs* refer to the preceding neuter noun *bdelygma*, which signifies ‘abomination.’] 16. then let those who are in Judaea flee 17. to the mountains; and let the one upon the roof not come down to take anything from his house; 18. and let the one in the field not turn back to take his garment. 19. But woe to those who are pregnant and nursing in those days. 20. Pray that your flight may not occur in winter or on a sabbath. 21. For then there will be [Col. 0310] great tribulation, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the age until now, nor ever shall occur. 22. And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days shall be shortened. 23. Then, if anyone says to you, ‘Behold, Christ is here,’ [Note: [Col. 0309] Before *Christus*, *est*, ‘is,’ is absent, also in the Greek text.] or ‘there,’ do not believe it. 24. For false Christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so that, if possible, even the elect might be led astray. 25. Behold, I have told you beforehand. 26. Therefore, if they say to you, ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ or ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it. 27. For as lightning comes out of the east and appears [Col. 0310] as far as the west, so shall the coming of the Son of Man be. 28. Wherever the body shall be, there the eagles [Note: [Col. 0309] Before *aquilae*, ‘eagles,’ *et*, ‘also,’ is absent also in the Greek text.] shall gather.

29. “But immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun shall be darkened, the moon shall not give its light, the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven 30. shall be shaken. Then the sign of the Son of Man shall appear in heaven; and then all the tribes of the earth shall beat their breasts, and they shall see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty. 31. And he shall send his angels with a trumpet and a loud voice, and they shall gather [Col. 0312] his elect from the four corners of heaven, from the extremities of the heavens to their furthest boundary. [Note: [Col. 0311] This addition is found also in the Canterbury Latin and Greek codex: *archomenōn de toutōn ginesthai, anablepsate, kai eparate tas kephalas hymōn; dioti engizei hē apolutrōsis hymōn*—‘But when these things begin to happen’ (Canterbury Latin: *incipientibus autem his fieri*), ‘look up and raise your heads, because your redemption draws near.’] But when these things begin to happen, look up and raise your heads, because your redemption draws near.

32. “Now learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and leaves are coming forth, you know that summer is near; 33. so also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors. 34. Amen, I tell you that this generation shall not pass away until all things 35. happen. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. 36. But concerning that day or hour no one knows—not even the angels of heaven, [Note: [Col. 0311] It adds ‘nor the Son,’ also the Canterbury codex, Greek *oude ho huios*, from Mark.] nor the Son—[Col. 0312] but the Father alone. 37. But as it was in the days of Noah, so shall the coming of the Son of Man be. 38. For as they were in those days [Note: [Col. 0311] It adds *illis*, ‘those,’ as does the Canterbury codex, Greek *ekeinais*.] before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day on which he entered the ark, 39. and they did not know until the flood came and carried them all away, so shall the coming of the Son of Man be [Note: [Col. 0311] After *erit*, ‘shall be,’ *et*, ‘also,’ is absent, also in the Canterbury codex.]. 40. Then two shall be in the field: one shall be taken and one left. Two women shall be grinding at the mill: one shall be taken and one left. 41. [Note: [Col. 0311] This addition is likewise found in the Canterbury Latin and Greek codex: *Dyo epi klinēs mias, heis paralambanetai, kai heis aphietai*—‘Two upon one bed: one is taken and one is left’—from Luke. It is also read by Chrysostom, Juvencus, Hilary, the Saxon version, and many Latin codices in Luke as cited by Brugensis, and by some Greek codices as cited by Stephanus and Mill.] Two in one bed: one shall be taken and one left.

42. “Therefore keep watch, [Col. 0314] because you do not know at what hour your Lord will come. 43. But know this: that if the master of the house knew at what hour the thief was coming [Note: [Col. 0313] So also the Greek text, *erchetai*, ‘comes.’], he would certainly keep watch and would not allow his house 44. to be broken into. Therefore you also do not know at what hour the Son of Man will come. 45. Who, then, is the faithful and prudent servant whom his master has appointed over his household, to give them food at the proper time? 46. Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, shall find [Note: [Col. 0313] So also the Greek text, *heurēsei*, ‘will find.’] doing so. 47. Amen, I tell you that he will appoint him over all his possessions. 48. But if that evil servant should say [Col. 0314] in his heart, ‘My master delays his coming,’ 49. and should begin to beat his fellow servants and eat and drink with drunkards, 50. the master of that servant shall come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour which he does not know, and shall cut him in two, 51. and assign his portion with the hypocrites. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

## CHAPTER XXV

1. Then the kingdom of heaven shall be considered like ten virgins, who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride. 2. Five of them were foolish and five prudent. 3. But the five foolish, having taken their lamps [Note: [Col. 0313] So also the Greek text, *erchetai*, “comes.”], [Col. 0316] did not take oil with them; 4. whereas the prudent took oil in their vessels with their lamps [Note: [Col. 0315] Here the Greek text too adds *suis*, ‘their own,’ *heautōn*, and below *hautōn*.]. 5. But while the bridegroom delayed, they all became drowsy and slept. 6. At midnight a cry arose: ‘Behold, the bridegroom comes; rise, go out to meet him.’ 7. Then all those virgins rose and took up their lamps. 8. But the foolish said to the wise: ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.’ 9. The prudent answered, saying: ‘No, lest perhaps there should not be enough for us and for you; go rather to those who sell it and buy some for yourselves.’ 10. While they went to buy it, the bridegroom came; and those who were ready [Col. 0316] entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut. 11. Later the remaining [Note: [Col. 0315] Before *reliquae*, ‘remaining,’ *et*, ‘also,’ is absent in the Canterbury codex.] virgins came, saying: ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’ 12. But he answered and said: ‘Amen, I tell you: I do not know you.’ 13. Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

14. “For it is as when a man about to travel abroad calls his servants and entrusts his possessions to them. 15. To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability [Note: [Col. 0315] It adds *suam*, ‘his own,’ also the Canterbury codex, Greek *autou*.], and departed. 16. Immediately, the one who had received five talents went and traded [Col. 0318] with them and gained another five. 17. Likewise, the one who received two gained another two with them. 18. But the one who received one talent dug [Note: [Col. 0317] Before *fodit*, ‘dug,’ *abiens*, ‘having gone away,’ is absent, also in the Canterbury codex.] in the earth and hid his master’s money. 19. After a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them. 20. And the one who had received five talents came forward and offered another five talents in addition, saying: ‘Lord, you gave me five talents; behold, I have gained another five.’ 21. His master said to him: ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you have been faithful over a little, I shall appoint you over much; enter into the joy of your master.’ [Col. 0318] 22. Then the one who had received two talents came forward and said: ‘Lord, you entrusted two talents to me; behold, I have gained another two.’ 23. His master said to him: ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you have been faithful over a little, I shall appoint you over much; enter into the joy of your master.’ 24. But the one who had received one talent came forward and said: ‘Lord, I knew that you are a harsh man: you reap where you have not sown and gather where you have not scattered. 25. And because I was afraid, I went away and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’ 26. But his master answered and said to him: ‘Wicked and slothful servant, you knew that I reap where I do not sow and gather where I have not 27. scattered. Therefore you ought to have deposited my money with the bankers, and when I came I would have received [Col. 0320] what is mine with interest. 28. Take the talent from him, therefore, and give it to the one who has ten talents. 29. For to everyone who has, more shall be given and he shall abound; but from the one who does not have, even what he has [Note: [Col. 0319] So also the Greek text, *echei*, ‘he has.’] shall be taken away from him. 30. And cast the worthless servant [Note: [Col. 0319] So also the Canterbury codex, Greek *balete exō*, ‘cast out.’] outside into the outer darkness. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

31. “But when the Son of Man comes in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then he shall sit upon the throne of his majesty. 32. And all nations shall be gathered before him, and he shall separate them from one another, 33. as a shepherd separates sheep from goats; and he shall set [Col. 0320] the sheep [Note: [Col. 0319] After *oves*, ‘sheep,’ *quidem*, ‘indeed,’ is absent, likewise in the Canterbury codex.] at his right hand and the goats at his left. 34. Then the King shall say to those at his right hand: ‘Come, blessed of my Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. 35. For I was hungry and you gave me food; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; 36. I was a stranger and you welcomed me; naked and you clothed me; sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me.’ 37. Then the righteous shall answer him, saying: ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed [Col. 0322] you, or thirsty and give you drink? 38. And when did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe 39. you? Or when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’ 40. And the King shall answer and say to them: ‘Amen, I tell you: insofar as you did it to one of these least brothers [Note: [Col. 0321] So also the Greek text, *toutōn tōn adelphōn*, ‘of these brothers.’] of mine, you did it to me.’ 41. Then he shall say to those at his left: ‘Depart from me, accursed ones, into the eternal fire, which my Father prepared [Note: [Col. 0321] So also the Canterbury codex, Greek *hon hētoimasen ho patēr mou*, ‘which my Father prepared.’] for the devil and his angels. 42. For I was hungry and you gave me no food; I was thirsty and you gave [Col. 0322] me no drink; 43. I was a stranger and you did not welcome me; naked and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison and you did not visit me.’ 44. Then they themselves shall answer [Note: [Col. 0321] Before *et ipsi*, ‘they themselves,’ *ei*, ‘him,’ is absent, also in the Canterbury codex.], saying: ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or in prison, or sick, and not minister to you?’ 45. Then he shall answer them, saying: ‘Amen, I tell you: insofar as you did not do it to one of these least ones, neither did you do it to me.’ And these shall go into eternal fire, but the righteous into eternal life.”

## CHAPTER XXVI

[Col. 0324]

1. And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, that he said to his disciples: 2. “You know that after two days the Passover will take place, and the Son of Man is delivered over [Note: [Col. 0323] So also the Greek text, *paradidotai*, “is delivered over.”] to be crucified.” 3. Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the court of the chief priest, who was called 4. Caiaphas; and they took counsel to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him. 5. But they said: “Not on the feast day, lest a disturbance arise among the people.”

6. Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon 7. the leper, a woman came to him with an alabaster vessel [Col. 0324] of costly ointment and poured it upon his head as he reclined [Note: [Col. 0323] So also the Canterbury codex, *tēn kephalēn autou anakeimenou autou*, “his head, while he was reclining.”]. 8. But when the disciples saw it, they were indignant, saying: “Why has this waste of this 9. ointment [Note: [Col. 0323] They add *hujus unguenti*, ‘of this ointment,’ as do the Coptic, Syriac, Arabic, Persian, and Ethiopic versions, and many Greek codices: *tou myrou*, from Mark.] occurred? For it could have been sold for a price and given to the poor.” 10. But Jesus, knowing this, said to them: “Why do you trouble this woman? For she has performed a good work for me. 11. For you will always have the poor with you, but you will not always have me. 12. For in pouring this ointment upon my body, she did it for my burial. 13. Amen, I tell you: wherever this Gospel is preached throughout the whole world, what she has done [Col. 0326] shall also be told in remembrance of her.”

14. Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests and said to them: 15. “What are you willing to give me, and I will hand him over to you?” 16. And they assigned to him thirty staters [Note: [Col. 0325] So also the Canterbury Latin and Greek codices, *statēras*.]. From then on he sought an opportunity to hand him over to them [Note: [Col. 0325] It adds *eis*, ‘to them,’ as does the Canterbury codex, Greek *autois*.].

17. On the first day of unleavened bread, the disciples approached Jesus, saying: “Where do you wish us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?” 18. But he [Note: [Col. 0325] So also the Greek text, *ho de*, “but he.”] said to them: “Go into the city, to a certain man, and say to him: ‘The Teacher says: My time is near; with you I keep the Passover with my disciples.’” 19. And the disciples did as [Col. 0326] Jesus commanded them, and prepared the Passover.

20. When evening came, he reclined with his twelve 21. disciples. And while they were eating, he said: “Amen, I tell you that one of you will betray me.” 22. Greatly grieved, they began each one to say: “Surely it is not I, Lord?” 23. But he answered and said: “He who dips his hand with me in the dish, he shall betray me. 24. Indeed, the Son of Man goes as it is written concerning him; but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed. It would have been good for that man 25. not to have been born.” But Judas, [Note: [Col. 0325] Greek text: *ho paradidous*, “the one betraying.”] who was about to betray him, [Col. 0328] answered and said: “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” Jesus said to him: “You have said it.”

26. While they were dining, Jesus took bread and blessed it; and having broken it, he gave it to his disciples and said: “Take and eat from this, all of you, for this is my body.” 27. And taking the cup, he gave thanks and gave it to them, saying: “Take and drink from this. 28. For this is my blood of the new and eternal covenant, which shall be shed for many for the remission of sins. 29. But I tell you: I shall not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.” [Col. 0328] 30. And when a hymn had been sung, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

31. Then he said to them: “You will all suffer offense because of me this night. For it is written: ‘I shall strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered.’ 32. But after I rise again, I shall go before you into Galilee.” 33. But Peter answered and said: “Even if [Note: [Col. 0327] So also the Canterbury codex, Greek *ei*, “if.”] all are offended because of you, I shall never be offended.” 34. Jesus said to him: “Amen, I tell you that this [Note: [Col. 0327] Before *hac*, ‘this,’ *in*, ‘in,’ is absent, also in the Canterbury codex.] night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.” 35. Peter said to him: “Even if I must die with you, I shall not [Col. 0330] deny you.” Likewise all the disciples said.

36. Then Jesus came with them to an estate called Gethsemane [Note: [Col. 0329] Canterbury codex: *Gethsamanei*.], and said to his disciples: “Sit here while I go over there to pray.” 37. And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, he began to be sorrowful and distressed. 38. Then he said to them: “My soul is sorrowful unto death; remain here and keep watch with me.” 39. And going a little farther, he fell upon his face, praying and saying: “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.” [Col. 0330] 40. Then he came to his disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter: “So, were you unable to keep watch with me for one hour? 41. Keep watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” 42. Again, a second time, he went away and prayed, saying: “My Father, if this [Note: [Col. 0329] So also the Alexandrian, Medicean, Ephraem, and Colbertine codices, with Chrysostom as cited by Mill.] cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will 43. be done.” And again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy with 44. sleep. And leaving them, he went away again and prayed, saying the same words. 45. Then he came to his disciples and said to them: “Sleep now and rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near, [Col. 0332] and the Son of Man is delivered over [Note: [Col. 0331] So also the Greek text, *paradidotai*, “is delivered over.”] into the hands of sinners. 46. Rise, let us go. Behold, the one who betrays me has drawn near.”

47. While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people. 48. Now the one who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying: “Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him.” 49. And immediately approaching Jesus, he said: “Hail, Rabbi,” and kissed 50. him. And Jesus said to him: “Friend, for what have you come?” Then they approached, laid hands upon Jesus, and seized [Col. 0332] him.

51. And behold, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, and struck [Note: [Col. 0331] So also the Canterbury codex, *epataxen*, “struck.”] the servant of the chief priest and cut off [Note: [Col. 0331] So also the Canterbury codex, *kai apheilen*, “and took off.”] his ear. 52. Then Jesus said to him: “Return your sword to its place, for all who take the sword shall perish by the sword. 53. Or do you think that I cannot now [Note: [Col. 0331] It adds *modo*, ‘now,’ as does the Greek text, *arti*.] ask my Father, and he will furnish me with [Note: [Col. 0331] After *mihi*, ‘to me,’ *modo*, ‘now,’ is absent, also in the Greek text.] more than twelve legions of angels? 54. How then will the Scriptures of the Prophets be fulfilled, that it must happen thus?” 55. At that hour Jesus said to the crowds: “Have you come out [Note: [Col. 0331] So also the Canterbury codex, *ēlthate*, ‘you have come,’ here and very often elsewhere, in place of *ēlthete*.] as against a robber, with swords and [Col. 0334] clubs, to seize me? Daily I sat with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize me. 56. But all this happened in order that the Scriptures of the Prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him and fled.

57. But those who had seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the chief priest, where the scribes and elders had assembled. 58. Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the court of the chief priest. And entering within, he sat with the attendants to see the outcome. 59. Now the chief priests and the entire council sought false testimony against Jesus, in order to deliver him over to death; [Col. 0334] 60. and they found none, though many false witnesses had come forward. At last two false witnesses came and said: [Note: [Col. 0333] So also the Canterbury codex, *ēkousamen autou legontos*, “We heard him saying.”] “We heard this man say: 61. ‘I am able to destroy this temple of God and rebuild it after three days.’” 62. And the chief priest rose and said to him: “Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you?” 63. But Jesus was silent. And the chief priest answered [Note: [Col. 0333] It adds *respondens*, ‘answering,’ as does the Greek text, *apokritheis*.] and said to him: “I adjure you by the living God to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.” 64. Jesus said to him: “You have said it. Amen, I tell you: henceforth you shall see the Son of Man seated [Col. 0336] at the right hand of Power [Note: [Col. 0335] After *virtutis*, ‘Power,’ *Dei*, ‘of God,’ is absent also in the Greek text.], and coming upon the clouds of heaven.” 65. Then the chief priest tore his garments, saying: “He has blasphemed. What further need have we of witnesses? Behold, now you have heard the blasphemy [Note: [Col. 0335] It adds *ejus*, ‘his,’ as does the Greek text, *autou*.]—what do you think?” 66. And they all answered and said [Note: [Col. 0335] So also the Canterbury codex, *apekrithēsan pantes kai eipon*, “they all answered and said.”]: “He is deserving of death.” 67. Then they spat in his face and struck him with blows, 68. saying: “Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?”

69. But Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and one maidservant came to him, saying: “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.” 70. But he denied it before them all, saying: “I do not know what you say, nor [Note: [Col. 0335] It adds ‘nor do I understand,’ also the Canterbury codex, Greek *oude epistamai*, from Mark.] do I understand.” [Col. 0336] 71. And as he was going out to the gateway [Note: [Col. 0335] So also the Greek text, *exelthonta*, “as he was going out.”], another maidservant saw him and said to those who were there: “This man also was with Jesus the Nazarene.” 72. And again he denied it with an oath, saying: “I do not know [Note: [Col. 0335] So also the Canterbury codex, *legōn: ouk oida*, “saying: I do not know.”] the man.” 73. And after a little while those standing there came up and said to Peter: “Truly you also are one of them [Note: [Col. 0335] Before *tu*, ‘you,’ *et*, ‘also,’ is absent in the Canterbury codex.], for your speech too is similar [Note: [Col. 0335] So also the Canterbury codex, *homoiazei*, ‘is similar,’ from Mark.].” 74. Then he began to curse himself and to swear that he did not know the man. And immediately a cock crowed. 75. And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which he had said to him [Note: [Col. 0335] It adds *ei*, ‘to him,’ as does the Greek text, *autō*.]: “Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.” And he went out [Col. 0338] and wept most bitterly.

## CHAPTER XXVII
1. But when morning had come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, to deliver him to death.  
   [Note: [Col. 0337] According to the Greek reading, *elabon* (“they took”).]  
2. And having bound him, they led him away and delivered him to Pontius Pilate, the governor.  
3. Then Judas, who had betrayed him, seeing that he had been condemned, was moved by repentance and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,  
4. saying, “I have sinned, in that I have betrayed innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? You see to it.”  
5. And, having thrown down the silver in the Temple, he withdrew; and he went and hanged himself with a noose.  
6. Then the chief priests, having received the silver, said, “It is not lawful to put it into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.”  
7. And, having taken counsel among themselves, they bought the potter’s field with it, as a burial-place for strangers.  
   [Note: [Col. 0337] After “they bought,” “with it” is absent, also in the Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis.]  
8. For this reason that field has been called Acheldemach, that is, “the Field of Blood,” to this day.  
9. Then was fulfilled what had been spoken through the Prophet, saying: “And they received thirty pieces of silver,  
10. the price of him who was priced, whom they priced from the children of Israel; and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.”  
11. But Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “You say so.”  
12. And when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.  
   [Note: [Col. 0339] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *apekrineto* (“he answered”).]  
13. Then Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear how many testimonies they give against you?”  
14. And he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor wondered greatly.  
   [Note: [Col. 0339] Before “a single,” *ad* (“to”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]  
15. Now on the feast-day the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner whom they wished.  
16. And they had a notable prisoner called Barabbas.  
   [Note: [Col. 0339] So also the Greek text: *eichon* (“they had”).]  
17. Therefore, when they had assembled, Pilate said, “Whom do you wish me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”  
18. For he knew that they had delivered him up out of envy.  
19. But while he was sitting on the judgment-seat, his wife sent word to him, saying, “Let there be nothing between you and that righteous man; for today I have suffered much in a dream because of him.”  
   [Note: [Col. 0339] From here through verse 42 of this chapter, everything is mutilated in the Gothic text.]  
20. But the chief priests and elders persuaded the people to ask for Barabbas, but to destroy Jesus.  
21. And the governor answered and said, “Which of the two do you wish me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”  
   [Note: [Col. 0339] So also the Greek text: *apolyō* (“I release”).]  
   [Note: [Col. 0341] So also the Greek text: *Barabban* (“Barabbas,” accusative).]  
22. Pilate said to them, “What then shall we do with Jesus who is called Christ?”  
23. They all said, “Let him be crucified.” The governor said to them, “For what evil has he done?” But they cried out the more, “Let him be crucified.”  
24. But Pilate, seeing that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather that a disturbance was arising among the people, took water and washed his hands before the people, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this man; see to it yourselves.”  
   [Note: [Col. 0341] So also the Greek text: *ōphelei* (“it profits,” “he accomplishes”).]  
25. And the whole crowd answered and said, “His blood be upon us and upon our children.”  
26. Then he released Barabbas to them; but Jesus, having been scourged, he delivered up to be nailed to a cross.  
27. Then the soldiers of the governor took him into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around him.  
28. And they put a purple garment upon him and wrapped a scarlet cloak around him;  
   [Note: [Col. 0341] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *kai endysantes himation porphyrou* (“and having clothed [him] in a purple garment”).]  
29. and they placed a crown of thorns upon his head and a reed in his right hand. And kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews.”  
30. And spitting upon his face, they took the reed and struck his head.  
31. And after they had mocked him, they stripped the cloak from him, put his own garments on him, and led him away to nail him to a cross.  
32. As they went out, they found a Cyrenian man coming to meet them; they compelled him to carry his cross.  
   [Note: [Col. 0341] It adds “coming to meet them,” also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis, *eis apantēsin autou* (“to meet him”), together with the Saxon version.]  
33. And they came to the place called Golgotha, which is “the Place of the Skull.”  
34. And they gave him wine mixed with gall to drink; and when he had tasted it, he would not drink.  
35. But after they had crucified him, they divided his garments among themselves, casting lots, that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “They divided my garments among themselves, and upon my clothing they cast a lot.”  
36. And sitting down, they guarded him.  
37. And they placed above his head his written accusation: “This is the King of the Jews.”  
38. Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left.  
39. And those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads  
40. and saying, “Ha! You who destroyed the Temple of God and rebuilt it in three days, save yourself. If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.”  
41. Likewise the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes and Pharisees,  
   [Note: [Col. 0343] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *kai Pharisaiōn* (“and Pharisees”).]  
42. said, “He saved others; he cannot save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we shall believe him.  
43. He trusts in God; let God now deliver him, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”  
   [Note: [Col. 0343] It adds “if,” also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis: *ei* (“if”).]  
   [Note: [Col. 0343] So also the Greek text: *auton* (“him”).]  
44. And the robbers who had been crucified with him likewise reproached him.  
45. And after he had been crucified, from the sixth hour darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.  
46. About the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Heli, Heli, lama zaptani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”  
   [Note: [Col. 0345] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin: *Zapthani*; Cantabrigiensis Greek: *zaphthanei*, and in a later hand *saphthanei*.]  
47. But some of those standing there, hearing it, said, “This man calls Elijah.”  
48. And immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink.  
49. But the rest said, “Leave him; let us see whether Elijah will come and save him.”  
   [Note: [Col. 0345] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *eipon* (“they said”).]  
   [Note: [Col. 0345] According to the Greek text: *ei* (“whether,” “if”).]  
   [Note: [Col. 0345] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *kai sōsei* (“and will save”).]  
   [Note: [Col. 0345] “v” in place of “b.”]  
50. But Jesus again cried out with a loud voice and gave up the spirit.  
51. And behold, the veil of the Temple was torn into two parts from top to bottom; the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split;  
52. and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of sleeping saints rose,  
53. and, coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.  
54. But the centurion and those who were with him guarding Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and the things that were happening, were greatly afraid and said, “Truly this man was the Son of God.”  
55. And there were many women there at a distance, watching, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him,  
   [Note: [Col. 0347] So also the Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Greek text: *theōrousai* (“watching”).]  
56. among whom were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.  
57. But when evening had come, a certain rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph, came; he too was a disciple of Jesus.  
   [Note: [Col. 0347] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *Arimatheias* (“of Arimathea”).]  
58. This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered that the body be given over.  
59. And having received the body of Jesus, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth  
60. and placed him in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock. And he rolled a great stone against the entrance of the tomb and went away.  
   [Note: [Col. 0347] So also the Greek text: *elatomēsen* (“he cut out”).]  
61. And Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.  
62. But on the following day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees assembled before Pilate,  
63. saying, “Lord, we remember that while still alive that deceiver said, ‘After the third day I shall rise.’  
64. Therefore order the tomb to be guarded until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come and steal him and say to the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’ And the last error will be worse than the first.”  
65. Pilate said to them, “You have guards; go, guard it as you know how.”  
   [Note: [Col. 0349] So also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis: *phylakas* (“guards”).]  
66. And they went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone together with the guards.

## CHAPTER XXVIII

1. But at the evening of the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.  
2. And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, approached, rolled away the stone, and sat upon it.  
3. His appearance was like lightning, and his garments white as snow.  
   [Note: [Col. 0349] It adds “white,” also the Greek text: *leukon endyma* (“a white garment”).]  
4. And from fear of him the guards were terrified and became like dead men.  
5. But the angel answered and said to the women, “Do not be afraid; for I know that you seek Jesus, who was crucified.  
6. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord had been laid.  
7. And go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen; and behold, he goes before you into Galilee. There you shall see him. Behold, I have told you.”  
   [Note: [Col. 0349] “Behold,” as in Codex Cantabrigiensis, *idou*. Likewise, “I have told,” with the Greek text, *eipon*.]  
8. And they went out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, running to report it to his disciples.  
9. And behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings.” And they approached, took hold of his feet, and worshipped him.  
10. Then he said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go, report to my brothers that they may go into Galilee; there they shall see me.”  
11. And when they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had happened.  
12. And having assembled with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a large sum of money  
13. to the soldiers, saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole him while we were asleep.’  
14. And if this should come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you secure.”  
15. But they received the money and did as they had been instructed. And this report has been spread among the Jews to this day.  
16. But the eleven disciples went to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them.  
17. And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted.  
18. And Jesus approached and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.  
19. Therefore go now, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,  
   [Note: [Col. 0351] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *nyn* (“now”).]  
20. teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I commanded you. And behold, I am with you all days, until the consummation of the age. Amen.”  
   [Note: [Col. 0351] They add “Amen,” as does the Greek text, *Amēn*; this certainly belongs not to Matthew but to the Church, declaring its assent to this Gospel, as also to the others, by this word.]

**THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MATTHEW ENDS. — THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO JOHN BEGINS.**

**CODEX CORBEIENSIS**

[Col. 0141]

[Note: [Col. 0141] A manuscript codex of Saint-Germain presents this entire series of the earlier patriarchs, consonant with the Hebrew truth, in the form in which we published it before the sacred text of the Gospel according to Matthew. The series appears to have been added by the ancients so that the order of generations might be woven from Adam to Christ: that is, from the first Adam, the earthly man, to the second and heavenly man, of whom the Apostle wrote to the Corinthians.]

I. God made Adam. Adam begot Seth; Seth begot Enos; Enos begot Cainan; Cainan begot Mahalaleel; Mahalaleel begot Jared; Jared begot Enoch; Enoch begot Methuselah; Methuselah begot Lamech; Lamech begot Noah; Noah begot Shem; Shem begot Arphaxad; Arphaxad begot Salah; Salah begot Eber; Eber begot Peleg; Peleg begot Reu; Reu begot Serug; Serug begot Nahor; Nahor begot Terah; Terah begot Abraham.

The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham. Abraham begot Isaac; Isaac begot Jacob. And Jacob begot Judah and his brothers. And Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez begot Hezron; Hezron begot Aram; Aram begot Amminadab; Amminadab begot Nahshon; Nahshon begot Salmon; Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab; Boaz begot Obed by Ruth; Obed begot Jesse; Jesse begot David the king. David the king begot Solomon by her who had been Uriah’s wife. Solomon begot Rehoboam. Rehoboam begot Abijah. Abijah begot Asa. Asa begot Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat begot Joram. Joram begot Uzziah. Uzziah begot Jotham. Jotham begot Ahaz. Ahaz begot Hezekiah. Hezekiah begot Manasseh. Manasseh begot Amos. Amos begot Josiah. Josiah begot Jeconiah and his brothers at the deportation to Babylon. And after the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah begot Shealtiel; Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel; Zerubbabel begot Abiud; Abiud begot Eliakim; Eliakim begot Azor; Azor begot Zadok; Zadok begot Achim; Achim begot Eliud; Eliud begot Eleazar; Eleazar begot Matthan; Matthan begot Jacob; Jacob begot Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0141] “Begot Perez, and Perez [begot …].”]  
[Note: [Col. 0142] “David. David begot Solomon.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0143] “Abiud. Abiud begot Asaph. Asaph begot Jehoshaphat.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0143] The manuscript of Cambridge retains the same reading at Luke III, where some falsifier copied the series of generations from Matthew and from the books of Kings: *Tou Iōsaphad, tou Asaph, tou Abioud* — “of Jehoshaphat, of Asaph, of Abiud.” For Amon the same manuscript reads Amos, as do our two Latin manuscripts.]  
[Note: [Col. 0143] Read “Amon.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0143] “Achim begot Eliam; Elium begot Eleazar.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0144] The first hand had written “Eleazar” in the Saint-Germain manuscript, which some corrector altered thus: “Achim begot Eliachin; Eliachin [begot …],” writing what was uncorrected as though it were uncorrected.]  
[Note: [Col. 0144] “Joseph, to whom the virgin Mary was betrothed, begot Jesus, who,” etc. This remarkable variant reading was not erased by the corrector, although he supplied another, the common reading, in the margin of the codex.]

Therefore, from Abraham to David there are fourteen generations; from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to Christ, fourteen generations.

[Note: [Col. 0145] “A righteous man.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0145] “To dismiss her quietly.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0145] “Will be born from her.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0145] Cyprian: “will have been born from her,” *Against the Jews*, book I, section 7.]  
[Note: [Col. 0145] “Will call.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0146] “The prophet Isaiah.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0146] “They will call.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0146] “A son, and he called.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0145] Jerome, in book I of his *Commentary on Matthew*, observes that some have grievously erred here: “From this passage,” he says, “some most perversely suppose that Mary had other children also, saying that one is not called ‘firstborn’ unless he has brothers.” Perhaps the copyist of the codex wished to remove the occasion of this error by omitting the words “her firstborn son.”]

But the generation of Christ was thus. When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit. But Joseph, her husband, being righteous and unwilling to expose her publicly, wished to dismiss her secretly. But while he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your wife; for that which has been born in her is of the Holy Spirit. And she will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus; for he himself will save his people from their sins.” But all this happened in order that what had been spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb and bear a son, and shall call his name Emmanuel,” which is interpreted, “God with us.” Then Joseph, rising from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and took his wife; and he did not know her until she had borne her firstborn son, and he called his name Jesus.

Now when Jesus had been born in Bethlehem of Judah in the days of King Herod, behold, Magi came from the East to Jerusalem, saying, “Where is he who has been born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the East and have come to worship him.” But King Herod, hearing this, was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. And gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where Christ would be born. They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judah; for thus it has been written through the prophet: ‘And you, Bethlehem, land of the Jews, are you the least among the rulers of Judah? For from you has come forth a leader who shall rule my people Israel.’”

[Note: [Col. 0146] “The city of Judaea.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0147] “He gathered all [the chief priests], etc.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0147] “Where is Christ born?”]  
[Note: [Col. 0147] “Bethlehem of Judaea, you are not least among the rulers of Judah … a ruler shall come forth who shall govern [my people].”]  
[Note: [Col. 0147] The second Greek codex of Robert Estienne reads in the same manner; and Grotius, in his annotations on this passage of Matthew, considers that it should be read interrogatively: “Are you perhaps the least?” etc. The Latin Fathers Hilary, Ambrose, and Leo the Great read, however, as does the Saint-Germain manuscript: “You are not the least,” etc.]  
[Note: [Col. 0148] “He secretly summoned the Magi and carefully inquired … when the star appeared to them. And he sent them.”]

Then Herod, secretly summoning the Magi, carefully learned from them the time when the star had appeared to them. And sending them to Bethlehem, he said, “Go and inquire carefully concerning the child, and when you have found him, report to me, so that I too, coming, may worship him.” When they had heard the king, they went; and behold, the star which they had seen in the East went before them, until, coming, it stood above the place where the child was. And seeing the star, they rejoiced exceedingly with great joy. And entering the house, they found the child with Mary his mother; and falling down, they worshipped him. And opening their treasures, they offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. And, having received an answer in a dream not to return to Herod, they returned to their own region by another way.

[Note: [Col. 0148] “And may come.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0148] “It came and stood [above the child].” The Latin version in the Cambridge manuscript reads thus.]

When they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph, saying, “Rise, take the child and his mother, flee into Egypt, and remain there until I tell you. For Herod is going to seek the child in order to destroy him.” He arose, took the child and his mother by night, and withdrew into Egypt. And he remained there until the death of Herod, in order that what had been spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

[Note: [Col. 0149] “Warned.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0149] “To destroy this child. Joseph, rising …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0149] “Went away.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0149] “Completion,” evidently an OCR error for *consummationem*; the text reads “death.”]

Then Herod, seeing that he had been deceived by the Magi, was greatly enraged; and he sent and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and throughout all its borders, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had learned from the Magi. Then was fulfilled what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet: “A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great wailing: Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more.”

[Note: [Col. 0150] “When he saw … he was.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0150] “Of Judaea and all the surrounding regions.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0150] “Great.”]

II. But after Herod had died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt, saying, “Rise, take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel; for those who sought the child’s life are dead.” And he arose, took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But hearing that Archelaus was reigning in Judaea in place of Herod his father, he was afraid to go there; and, warned in a dream, he withdrew into the regions of Galilee. And coming, he lived in the city called Nazareth, in order that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “He shall be called a Nazarene.”

[Note: [Col. 0151] “Behold, the Angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0151] “To destroy [the child’s life]. And rising …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0151] “There.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0152] “And he came, and …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0152] “Through the prophets.” Jerome asserts that the Saint-Germain manuscript preserves the true reading of this passage: in book I of his *Commentary* he says, “But now, by calling them prophets in the plural, he shows that he has not taken words from the Scriptures, but the sense.” Lucas Brugensis nevertheless found the reading of the Corbie manuscript, which we printed in the sacred text, in ancient codices. See his variant readings of the New Testament.]

In those days John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness of Judaea and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.” For this is he who was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “A voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.” John himself had clothing of camel hair and a leather belt around his loins; and his food was locusts and wild honey. Then Jerusalem, all Judaea, and all the region around the Jordan went out to him; and they were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.

[Note: [Col. 0152] “Of whom it was said.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0153] “He had his garment.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0153] “They went out to him from Jerusalem, and all who lived around the Jordan, confessing their sins; and they were baptized by him in …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0153] “John.”]

But when he saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, “Brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath? Therefore bear fruit worthy of repentance. And do not wish to say within yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father.’ For I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham. Even now the axe has been laid to the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire. I indeed baptize you in water for repentance; but he who is to come after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.

[Note: [Col. 0154] “And do not put yourselves forward, saying …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0154] “Roots.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0154] “Comes.”]

“His winnowing-fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing-floor; and he will gather his wheat into his granary, but will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”

[Note: [Col. 0154] “Having a winnowing-fan.”]

Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him. But John tried to prevent him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?” Jesus answered and said to him, “Allow it now; for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he allowed him.

[Note: [Col. 0155] “And John prevented him, saying …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0155] “And while Jesus was being baptized, a great light shone from the water, so that all who were gathered were afraid. And when Jesus had been baptized, immediately,” etc. The source from which the Latin translator drew words of this kind can scarcely be conjectured, because they are absent from the primary Greek texts. The Saint-Germain manuscript alone preserves this addition; yet, unless our judgment deceives us, the presbyter Juvencus seems also to have read it. For in the first book of his *Evangelical History* he writes:

> Recalling these things, he passed through the glassy waters of the stream;  
> For him as he rises, the manifest presence of God shines forth, etc.

[Col. 0156] This brightness may be believed to be the same as the great light shining in the water while Jesus was being baptized, according to our manuscript codex.]

But Jesus, having been baptized, immediately came up from the water. And behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon himself. And behold, a voice from the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

[Note: [Col. 0155] “From heaven … coming upon him.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0156] “Saying to him.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0156] “In whom I am well pleased; hear him.” Hilary, *On the Trinity*, book IX, no. 20: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him.” The Colbert manuscript confirms that he read it so. Cyprian, however, has: “in whom I have thought well; hear him.”]

III. Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward he was hungry. And the tempter approached and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become loaves.” But he answered and said, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.’”

[Note: [Col. 0156] “The tempter came to him and said …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0156] “To whom Jesus answered and said … by bread alone … by every word of God.”]

Then the devil took him into the holy city and set him upon the pinnacle of the Temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. For it is written: ‘He has commanded his angels concerning you, that they may bear you up in their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone.’” Jesus said to him, “Again it is written: ‘You shall not test the Lord your God.’” Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, and said to him, “All these things I will give you, if, falling down, you worship me.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go behind me, Satan. For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.’” Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and ministered to him.

[Note: [Col. 0157] “Against a stone.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0157] “Again Jesus: It is written …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0157] “Glory.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0158] “Falling down.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0157] The Cambridge exemplar, with twelve Greek manuscripts, has *opisō mou*, “behind me.” Hilary and other earlier Latin writers read in the same way.]  
[Note: [Col. 0158] “Departed from him.”]

But when Jesus heard that John had been delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee. And leaving the city of Nazareth, he came and lived in maritime Capernaum, in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali, so that what had been spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations: the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and for those sitting in the region and shadow of death, a light has risen.”

[Note: [Col. 0159] “Saw a great [light]. Those sitting in the region of the shadow of death.”]

From that time Jesus began to preach and say, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”

[Note: [Col. 0159] “But as he was passing …”]

And walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting nets into the sea; for they were fishermen. And he said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of human beings.” And they immediately left their nets and followed him. And going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left their nets and father and followed him.

[Note: [Col. 0159] “Their own.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0160] “Their nets and their father.”]

And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the Gospel of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people. And the report of him went out into all Syria, and they brought to him all who were ill, afflicted with various diseases and torments, those who had demons, lunatics, and paralytics; and he healed them. And great crowds followed him from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judaea, and from beyond the Jordan.

[Note: [Col. 0160] “Healing.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0160] “Report.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0160] “He healed them. And they followed …”]  
[Note: [Col. 0161] “Decapolis, and from Jerusalem … and from Judaea, and beyond the Jordan.”]

#### IV.

But Jesus, seeing the crowds, went up onto the mountain; and when he had sat down, his disciples came to him, and, opening his mouth, he taught them, saying:

“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.  
[Note: Col. 0161: “and opened [his mouth].”]

“Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth.  
[Note: Col. 0161: “gentle.”]

“Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.

“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.

“Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.”  
[Note: Col. 0161: “for God will have mercy on them.” Hilary and Leo the Great agree in reading, “for God will have mercy on them”; likewise the presbyter Juvencus in his *Gospel History*.]

“Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.  
[Note: Col. 0161: “pure.”]

“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

“Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

“Blessed are you when people curse you, persecute you, and falsely say every evil thing against you because of me. Rejoice and exult, for your reward is abundant in heaven. For thus they persecuted the prophets who were before you.”  
[Note: Col. 0162: “when people have hated you, curse and persecute you, and say every evil thing against you for righteousness’ sake.” “Do not rejoice when all people bless you; for thus their fathers did to the false prophets.” “You,” etc. Col. 0161: “... Those three letters, *cor.*, have been worn away.”]

“You are the salt of the earth. But if salt has lost its savour, by what shall it be salted? It is good for nothing further, except to be cast out and trodden under foot by men.  
[Note: Col. 0163: “is good for nothing, except.”]

“You are the light of the world. A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden. Nor do people light a lamp and put it under a bushel, but upon a lampstand, that it may give light to all who are in the house. So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.”  
[Note: Col. 0163: “of this world”; “magnify.”]

“Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish, but to fulfil. Amen I say to you: until heaven and earth pass away, one iota or one stroke shall not pass from the Law until all these things are accomplished.  
[Note: Col. 0164: “these.”]

“Whoever, therefore, shall break one of these least commandments and teach men so shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.  
[Note: Col. 0164: “thus, great.”]

“For I tell you: unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven.

“You have heard that it was said to the ancients: ‘You shall not kill; and whoever kills shall be liable to judgment.’  
[Note: Col. 0164: “was said: ‘You shall not.’]

“But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother without cause shall be liable to judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.”  
[Note: Cols. 0165–0166: All the older Latin Fathers read in the same way: Cyprian, *Testimonies*, book III, no. 8, p. 64; Hilary, *Commentary on Matthew*; Augustine, *On the Lord’s Sermon on the Mount*, book I, chapter 9; and, finally, Jerome, book II *Against the Pelagians* and book I of his *Commentary on Matthew*, where he teaches that the two words *without cause* are to be deleted and erased from the Gospel text. Col. 0165: “whoever says, ‘Fool.’”]

“If, therefore, you offer your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and first go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.  
[Note: Col. 0165: “you shall offer.”]

“Be quickly in agreement with your adversary while you are on the way with him, lest perhaps your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and you be cast into prison. Amen I say to you: you shall not depart from there until you have paid the last quadrans.

“You have heard that it was said to the ancients: ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart. If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and cast it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be cast into Gehenna.  
[Note: Col. 0165: “for you.” Col. 0166: “go.”]

“And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.  
[Note: Col. 0166: “for.” Col. 0167: “your”; “than that.”]

“It was also said: ‘Whoever dismisses his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.’ But I say to you that everyone who dismisses his wife, except on account of fornication, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries a dismissed woman commits adultery.  
[Note: Col. 0167: “a divorce”; “commits adultery.”]

“Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall render to the Lord your oaths.’ But I say to you: do not swear at all—neither by heaven, for it is God’s throne; nor by earth, for it is his footstool; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. Nor shall you swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black. But let your speech be: ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is more than this is from evil.”  
[Note: Col. 0167: “you shall not swear falsely; but you shall render to the Lord.” Col. 0168: “and.”]

“You have heard that it was said: ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, if anyone strikes you on your right cheek, offer him the other also.  
[Note: Col. 0168: “on your right cheek, offer him the left also.”]

“To him who wishes to contend with you at law and take your tunic, let go your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go a thousand paces, go with him another two. Give to the one who asks of you; and do not turn away from the one who wishes to borrow from you.”  
[Note: Col. 0168: “another two.” “To everyone who asks of you.” “Do not turn yourself away from him.”]

“You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute and slander you, that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven; for he makes his sun rise upon good and evil alike, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.  
[Note: Col. 0169: “for those who persecute you and slander you”; “causes [the sun] to rise.”]

“For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even tax collectors do this? And if you greet only your brothers, what more do you do? Do not even the Gentiles do this? Therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.”  
[Note: Col. 0169: “if you love.” “What more do you do? Do not even the Gentiles do these things?” “And ... as your Father who is in heaven is perfect.”]

“Take heed lest you do your righteousness before men in order to be seen by them; otherwise you shall have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.  
[Note: Col. 0169: “but.” Col. 0170: “so that.”]

“Therefore, when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before yourself, as hypocrites do in synagogues and lanes, that they may be honoured by men. Amen I say to you: they have received their reward.  
[Note: Col. 0170: “and in streets and lanes”; “have received.”]

“But when you give alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand does, so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.  
[Note: Col. 0170: “your left hand”; “in secret ...” Cols. 0171–0172: “openly. And when praying, do not use many words.” Cyprian reads, “will repay you openly.” Our manuscript of Saint-Germain comes closer to the Greek *ἐν τῷ φανερῷ* (*en tō phanerō*), “in public” or “openly.” On the word *openly*, consult Augustine, book II of *On the Lord’s Sermon on the Mount*, and the observations of Th. Mareschall on the Gothic Version.]

“And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, who love to stand and pray in synagogues and at the corners of streets, in order to be seen by men. Amen I say to you: they have received their reward. But when you pray, enter into your chamber, and, having shut the door, pray to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.”

#### V.

“But when praying, do not use many words like the Gentiles. For they think that in their much speaking they will be heard.  
[Note: Col. 0171: “that they may be heard in their much speaking.”]

“Therefore do not be like them. For your Father knows what you need before you ask him. Thus, therefore, you shall pray:  
[Note: Col. 0171: “be likened to them.” Col. 0172: “of him”; “him.”]

“Our Father, who art in heaven,  
hallowed be thy name.  
Thy kingdom come.  
Thy will be done,  
as in heaven, so also on earth.  
Give us this day our daily bread.  
And forgive us our debts,  
as we also forgive our debtors.  
And lead us not into temptation.  
But deliver us from evil.”

[Note: Col. 0171: This reading, *daily*, occurs in Cyprian, Ambrose, Augustine, and others. Jerome changed it to *supersubstantial*; but the Church has always retained the word *daily* in the Lord’s Prayer.]

“For if you forgive men their sins, your heavenly Father will also forgive you your offences. But if you do not forgive men, neither will your Father forgive you your sins.”  
[Note: Col. 0172: “Your Father who is in heaven also forgives you.”]

“And when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites. For they disfigure their faces, so that they may appear to men to be fasting. Amen I say to you: they have received their reward.  
[Note: Col. 0173: “But when you fast, anoint your heads and wash your faces, that you may not appear to men to be fasting, but to your Father, who,” etc.]

“But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, so that you may not appear to men to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.”  
[Note: Col. 0173: “your ... openly.”]

“Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where rust and moth destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.  
[Note: Col. 0173: “destroy.”]

“But lay up for yourselves treasure in heaven, where neither rust nor moth destroys, and where thieves neither break in nor steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart also is.  
[Note: Col. 0173: “treasures”; “and.” Col. 0174: “will be”; “will be.”]

“The lamp of your body is your eye. If your eye is sound, your whole body shall be full of light.  
[Note: Col. 0174: “If therefore your eye is sound.”]

“But if your eye is evil, your whole body shall be dark. If, then, the light that is in you is darkness, how great will that darkness be!  
[Note: Col. 0174: “are.”]
