“No one can serve two masters; for he will either hate the one and love the other, or endure the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and Mammon.  
[Note: Col. 0174: “will hate ... will love”; “or he will endure the one.”]

“Therefore I say to you: do not be anxious about your life—what you shall eat—nor about your body, what you shall wear. Is not life more than food, and the body than clothing?  
[Note: Col. 0175: “consider in your heart what you shall eat or what you shall drink”; “your life”; “more than clothing?”]

“Look at the birds of heaven: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they?  
[Note: Col. 0175: “by much.”]

“But which of you, by worrying, can add one cubit to his stature? And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not labour or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which exists today and tomorrow is cast into an oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of the least faith?  
[Note: Col. 0175: “is cast into the fire.” Col. 0176: “of little faith.”]

“Therefore do not be anxious, saying: ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘With what shall we be clothed?’ For the Gentiles seek all these things. For your Father knows that you need all these things. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow; for tomorrow shall be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own evil.”  
[Note: Col. 0176: “What shall we wear? For the Gentiles seek all these things. But ... you need all these things.” “They shall be supplied to you. Therefore do not think about tomorrow.” Cols. 0175–0176: Cyprian: “For tomorrow itself shall be anxious for itself.” Here below, it frequently agrees with our manuscript codex of Saint-Germain.]

#### VI.

“Do not judge, that you may not be judged. For in whatever judgment you judge, you shall be judged; and with whatever measure you have measured, it shall be measured back to you.  
[Note: Col. 0177: “in which”; “judgment shall be made concerning you”; “the same.”]

“Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye, but do not see the beam in your own eye? Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Allow me to remove the speck from your eye,’ when, behold, there is a beam in your own eye? Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

“Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet and, turning, tear you apart.”  
[Note: Col. 0177: “cast”; “destroy.”]

“Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives; whoever seeks finds; and to the one who knocks it shall be opened. Or which man among you, if his son asks him for bread, will offer him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will offer him a serpent?  
[Note: Col. 0178: “from whom his son asks bread”; “will offer.”]

“Therefore, if you, though evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him?  
[Note: Col. 0178: “good gifts.”]

“Therefore, whatever you wish men to do to you, do also to them. For this is the Law and the Prophets.  
[Note: Col. 0178: “good”; “thus.”]

“Enter through the narrow gate. For broad is the gate and spacious the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it.  
[Note: Col. 0179: “is the way.”]

“How narrow is the gate, and confined the way, that leads to life; and few are those who find it!  
[Note: Col. 0179: “is the gate.”]

“Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves. By their fruits you shall know them.  
[Note: Col. 0179: “beware”; “in garments of sheep, inwardly.”]

“Do men gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? Thus every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit. A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit. Every tree which does not produce good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire. Therefore by their fruits you shall know them.”  
[Note: Col. 0179: “A good tree produces good [fruit], etc.” “bad fruit.” Col. 0180: “is cast. Therefore.”]

“Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.  
[Note: Col. 0180: “will enter”; “those who do”; “they will enter.”]

“Many will say to me on that day: ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name, cast out demons in your name, and done many mighty works in your name?’ And then I shall confess to them: ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’”  
[Note: Col. 0180: “I shall say to them that I did not know you.”]

“Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them shall be likened to a wise man who built his house upon a rock. And rain came down, floods came, winds blew, and rushed against that house; and it did not fall, for it was founded upon a rock.  
[Note: Col. 0181: “these words of mine and does them is like.” “A rock. Rain came down; winds blew; floods arrived and struck against the house,” etc.]

“And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them shall be like a foolish man who built his house upon the sand of the sea. And rain came down, floods came, winds blew, and rushed against that house; and it fell, and its ruin was great.”  
[Note: Col. 0181: “is.” “Sand of the sea. Rain came down; winds blew; floods arrived and struck against the house,” etc. Col. 0182: “its ruin was.”]

#### VII.

And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowds were astonished at his teaching. For he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes or Pharisees.  
[Note: Col. 0182: “and Pharisees.”]

But when he had come down from the mountain, great crowds followed him. And behold, a leper came and worshipped him, saying: “Lord, if you will, you are able to cleanse me.” And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying: “I will; be cleansed.” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed. And Jesus said to him: “See that you tell no one; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”  
[Note: Col. 0182: “And as he descended from the mountain”; “a certain man came worshipping”; “Jesus.”]

And when he had entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, begging him and saying: “Lord, my servant lies at home paralysed and grievously tormented.” Jesus said to him: “I will come and heal him.” The centurion answered: “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter beneath my roof; but only speak the word, and my servant shall be healed. For I too am a man under authority, having soldiers under me; and I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”  
[Note: Col. 0183: “After these things, when”; “a certain”; “I shall come and heal”; “placed under authority and I have”; “I say, ‘Do this.’”]

When Jesus heard this, he marvelled; and he said to those following him: “Amen I say to you, I have not found such great faith in Israel. But I say to you that many shall come from east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven; but the children of the kingdom shall be cast into outer darkness. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” And Jesus said to the centurion: “Go; and as you have believed, so let it be done to you.” And the servant was healed in that hour.  
[Note: Col. 0184: “in none [have I found] such [faith], etc.” “shall go into”; “of eyes.” Cols. 0183–0184: Lucas Brugensis observes in his notes on variant readings in Greek editions of the Gospel according to Matthew that in certain Greek copies the following was added after verse 13: “And the centurion, returning to his house at that very hour, found the servant well.” Thus it is evident that these words were not written rashly by the Latin translator of the manuscript codex of Saint-Germain. Compare this with Luke, chapter VII, verse 10. “And the centurion returned to his house and at that same hour found the servant well. And when,” etc.]

And when Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying ill with fever. He touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she immediately arose and ministered to them.  
[Note: Col. 0185: “left”; “immediately.”]

When evening came, they brought to him all who were ill; and he cast out spirits by a word, and healed all who were ill, that what had been spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “He himself took our infirmities and bore our illnesses.”  
[Note: Col. 0185: “those possessed by demons, and by a word he cast out demons and healed all who were ill”; “for he himself ... bore our illnesses.”]

But Jesus, seeing great crowds around him, commanded them to go across the water. And one scribe came to him and said: “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.” Jesus said to him: “Foxes have dens, and birds of heaven nests in which to rest; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.” Another of his disciples said to him: “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.” But Jesus said to him: “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”  
[Note: Col. 0185: “a great crowd around him commanded his disciples that they should go ... And a certain scribe came to him and said”; “you go.” Col. 0186: “his.” “To him Jesus answered and said.”]

#### VIII.

And when he went up into the boat, his disciples followed him. And behold, a great disturbance arose on the sea, so that the boat was covered by the waves; but he was sleeping. They came and awakened him, saying: “Lord, save us; we are perishing.” Jesus said to them: “Why are you afraid, you of little faith?” Then, rising, he commanded the winds and the sea, and there came a great calm. The men marvelled, saying: “What kind of man is this, that winds and sea obey him?”  
[Note: Col. 0186: “a great storm arose”; “that boat was covered by waves”; “his disciples”; “deliver”; “And he said to them: ‘Why.’” Col. 0187: “rising, he commanded the wind”; “But those men”; “who is this, that.”]

And when he had crossed the water into the country of the Gerasenes, two men possessed by demons came to meet him, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that no one could pass by that way. And behold, they cried out, saying: “What have we to do with you, Son of God? Have you come here before the time to torment us?” Now not far from them was a large herd of swine feeding. The demons begged him, saying: “If you cast us out from here, send us into the herd of swine.” And he said to them: “Go.” They went out and entered the swine; and behold, the entire herd rushed headlong into the sea and died in the waters. The herdsmen fled; and, coming into the city, they reported everything, including what had happened to those who had had demons. And behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to depart from their territory.  
[Note: Col. 0187: “Jesus”; “possessed by demons ... exceedingly dangerous”; “Jesus”; “have you come before”; “feeding. The demons.” Col. 0188: “Jesus”; “going”; “rushing headlong”; “going”; “had demons”; “when they had seen him, they begged him.”]

#### IX.

And, entering the boat, he crossed over and came to his own city. And behold, they brought to him a paralytic lying upon a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic: “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven you.”  
[Note: Col. 0188: “of Judaea. And behold, they brought.” Cols. 0189–0190: The same reading is found in Saint Leo the Great, Sermon 60, *On the Passion of the Lord*, 11, and also in Hilary’s *Commentary on Matthew*.]

And behold, certain scribes said within themselves: “This man blasphemes.” Jesus, seeing their thoughts, said: “Why do you think evil in your hearts? For which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’? But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralytic—“Rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.” And he arose and went to his house. The crowds, seeing this, were afraid and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.  
[Note: Col. 0189: “But certain [scribes said] within themselves: ‘He blasphemes.’” “For.” “They are forgiven.” “and.” “Rising, he went.” Col. 0190: “glorified”; “such.”]

And as Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man sitting at the tax office, Matthew by name. And he said to him: “Follow me.” And he followed him. And it came to pass, as he reclined in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Jesus and his disciples. The Pharisees, seeing it, said to his disciples: “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” But Jesus, hearing it, said: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”  
[Note: Col. 0190: “at the tax office”; “rising”; “reclining”; “came and reclined with Jesus and with”; Col. 0191: “Why does your Teacher eat with”; “the healthy”; “what it is: ‘I desire mercy rather than sacrifice.’” Cols. 0191–0192: The Greek copies agree, where *εἰς μετάνοιαν* (*eis metanoian*) is added, that is, “unto repentance.” But the variant readings of our manuscript codices found in Saint Hilary and Saint Augustine deserve closer notice. In chapter X of Matthew, Hilary first reads, “I desire mercy rather than sacrifice,” like the manuscript codex of Saint-Germain; later, “I desire mercy, not sacrifice,” according to the Corbie copy. The same is found in Augustine, book II of *On the Harmony of the Evangelists*, no. 61. In the Gospel text, indeed, it is: “I desire mercy, and not sacrifice”; and then, in the quoted prophetic saying: “I desire mercy rather than sacrifice.”]

Then the disciples of John came to him, saying: “Why do we and the Pharisees fast frequently, but your disciples do not fast?” And Jesus said to them: “Can the children of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them; and then they shall fast in those days.”

X. But no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for it takes its fullness [Note: [Col. 0192] strength] from the garment, and the tear becomes worse. Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins [Note: [Col. 0192] the wine bursts the wineskins and] will burst, and the wine will be spilled and the wineskins perish. But they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.

While he was saying these things to them, behold, [Col. 0193] [Note: [Col. 0193] a certain ruler] one ruler came up and worshipped him, saying: “Lord, my daughter has just died; but come, lay your hand upon her, and she will live.” And Jesus rose and followed him, [Note: [Col. 0193] with his disciples.] and his disciples also. And behold, a woman who had suffered [Note: [Col. 0193] had] from a flow of blood for twelve years came up behind him and touched [Note: [Col. 0193] his garment.] the fringe of his garment. For she said within herself: “If only I touch his garment, I shall be saved.” But Jesus turned, and seeing her, said: [Note: [Col. 0193] Be of good courage] “Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well.” And the woman was made well from that hour.

And when Jesus had come into [Note: [Col. 0194] the ruler’s house.] the house of a certain ruler and saw the flute-players and the noisy crowd, he said: “Go away; for the girl is not dead, but asleep.” And they laughed at him. But when the crowd had been put out, [Note: [Col. 0194] coming up, he took hold of] he took her hand. And the girl rose. And this report went out through all that land.

And as Jesus was passing on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying: “Have mercy on us, Son of David.” [Note: [Col. 0194] And he came into the house, and the blind men came to him, beseeching him. And he said to them:] When he had come into the house, the blind men came to him. And Jesus said to them: “Do you believe that I can do this for you?” They said to him: “Certainly, Lord.” Then he touched their eyes, saying: “According to your faith, let it be done to you.” And [Col. 0195] their eyes were opened; and Jesus sternly charged them, saying: “See that no one knows.” But when they went out, they spread his fame throughout [Note: [Col. 0195] all that land. As they were going out] that whole land.

And when they had gone out, behold, they brought him a mute man [Note: [Col. 0195] and deaf, possessing a demon] possessed by a demon. And after the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds marvelled, saying: “Never has anything like this appeared in Israel.” But the Pharisees said: “By the [Note: [Col. 0195] Beelzebul, prince of … demons [ [Col. 0195] Jerome, in his book *On Hebrew Names*, warns that *Beelzebub*, not *Beelzebul*, should be read. “At the end of the name,” he says, “the letter *b* must be read, not *l*; for a fly is called *zebub*.” Thus, in Jerome’s time, *Beelzebul* was read in Latin copies.]] prince of demons he casts out demons.”

And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every [Note: [Col. 0195] infirmity among the people; and many followed him. But Jesus, seeing [Col. 0196] ] infirmity. But seeing the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they [Note: [Col. 0196] were] were distressed and cast down, like sheep without a shepherd. Then he said to his disciples: “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the labourers are few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send labourers into his harvest.”

And having summoned his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over [Note: [Col. 0196] to cast out unclean spirits, and to heal every disease and every infirmity among the people.] unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every sickness and every infirmity. Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who was called Peter, and Andrew [Col. 0197] his brother; James son of Zebedee, and John his brother; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax-collector; James son of Alphaeus, and [Note: [Col. 0197] Judas the Zealot, and Simon [ [Col. 0197] I have been unable to find anything similar among the variant Greek or Latin readings of the New Testament, nor in Augustine, who in Book II of *On the Harmony of the Evangelists* says that Luke does not differ from Matthew in the names of the apostles, except in the name of Judas of James, whom Matthew calls Thaddaeus; [Col. 0198] some manuscripts, however, have Lebbaeus. Whence this name Judas the Zealot was derived into the Saint-Germain manuscript is still less clear to me—especially since Simon, not any Judas among the disciples, is called the Zealot in Luke 6:15.]] Thaddaeus; Simon the Cananaean; and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.

Jesus sent out these twelve, instructing them [Note: [Col. 0197] and] and saying: “Do not go into the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter [Note: [Col. 0197] enter:] a city of the Samaritans; but go rather to the lost [Note: [Col. 0197] which have perished] sheep of the house of Israel. As you go, preach, saying: ‘The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’ Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, [Note: [Col. 0197] demons] cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give. Do not possess gold or silver or money in your belts; nor a bag for the journey, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff [Note: [Col. 0198] in your hands:]; for the labourer is worthy of his wages.

“Into whatever city [Note: [Col. 0198] or village you enter,] you enter, inquire who [Note: [Col. 0198] in it is worthy, and there] is worthy there, and remain there until you depart. As you enter a house, greet it, saying: ‘Peace [Note: [Col. 0198] to this house. And if the house is] to this house.’ If indeed that house is [Col. 0199] worthy, your peace shall come upon it; but if it is not worthy, your peace shall return to you. And whoever does not [Note: [Col. 0199] receive … hear] receive you or hear your words, go out [Note: [Col. 0199] from the house or city] from that house or city and shake off the dust from your feet [Note: [Col. 0199] as a testimony to them.]. Amen, I say to you: it will be more tolerable for [Note: [Col. 0199] the land of the Sodomites and Gomorrheans] Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.

“Behold, [Note: [Col. 0199] I] I send you as sheep [Note: [Col. 0199] in the midst of wolves. Therefore be …] among wolves. Therefore be prudent as serpents and simple [Note: [Col. 0199] as doves. Take heed to yourselves] as doves. But beware of men. For they will hand you over in councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you; and [Note: [Col. 0200] you will stand before kings and governors for my name, as a testimony to … them and the Gentiles. But when they hand you over, do not be anxious] before governors and kings [Note: [Col. 0199] the word *autem* has been omitted.] you will stand because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles. But when they hand you over, do not be anxious about how or what you are to speak; for in that hour you will be given what you are to say. For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.

“For [Note: [Col. 0200] but … to death] brother will hand brother over to death, and father his child; children will rise against parents and [Note: [Col. 0200] to death] put them to death. And you will be [Note: [Col. 0200] hated by all people] an object of hatred to all because of my name. But whoever perseveres to the end will be saved. And when [Col. 0201] they persecute you in this city, flee to another. [Note: [Col. 0201] A considerable number of Greek copies, and some very ancient Latin ones, agree. See Lucas Brugensis’s variant readings of the New Testament on Matthew chapter 10.] But if they persecute you in another, flee to a different one. Amen, I say to you: you will not finish the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

“A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master. [Note: [Col. 0201] It is enough] It is enough for the disciple to become like his teacher, and [Note: [Col. 0201] and the servant like] for the servant to become like his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household? Therefore do not fear them. For nothing is covered that will not [Note: [Col. 0201] be revealed, nor] be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not [Note: [Col. 0201] be known.] be made manifest. What I tell you in darkness, say in the light; and what you hear [Note: [Col. 0201] you have heard,] in the ear, proclaim upon the housetops.

“And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; [Note: [Col. 0202] but rather fear him] rather, fear him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna. Are not two sparrows sold for an *as*? Yet not one of them falls [Note: [Col. 0202] upon] to the ground without the will of your Father who is in heaven. But even all the hairs of your head are [Note: [Col. 0202] numbered] numbered. Therefore do not fear: [Note: [Col. 0202] for you are much better than sparrows.] you are worth more than many sparrows.

“Everyone, therefore, who confesses me [Note: [Col. 0202] confesses me, I also will confess him] before men, [Col. 0203] I also will confess him before my Father who is in heaven; but whoever denies me before men, [Note: [Col. 0203] I also will deny him] I also will deny him before my Father who is in heaven. Do not think that I came to bring peace upon the earth; I came not to bring peace, but a sword. For I came [Note: [Col. 0203] to separate] to divide a son against his father, and a daughter against her mother, [Note: [Col. 0203] and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law:] and a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law; and a man’s enemies will be those of his household.

“He who [Note: [Col. 0203] loves … more than] loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter [Note: [Col. 0203] more than] more than me is not worthy of me. And he who does not [Note: [Col. 0204] take … and follow me,] take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me. He who [Note: [Col. 0204] finds] loves his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find [Note: [Col. 0204] it. He who receives (thus consequently)] it. He who receives you receives me; and he who receives me receives him who sent me. He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward; and he who receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward. And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in my name—amen, I say to you—will not [Note: [Col. 0204] lose his reward.] lose his reward.

XI. And it came to pass, [Col. 0205] when Jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, that he went on from there to teach and preach in their cities. But John, [Note: [Col. 0205] having heard in prison of the works of Christ, sent two of his disciples and sent word to Jesus, saying:] when he was confined in prison, heard of the works of Christ; he sent two of his disciples to Jesus, saying: “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to await another?” And Jesus answered [Note: [Col. 0205] said] them: “Go, report to John what you have heard and seen: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, and the poor receive the gospel; and blessed is he [Note: [Col. 0205] who is not] who is not offended because of me.”

As they went away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John [Note: [Col. 0205] the Baptist:]: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed [Note: [Col. 0206] shaken by the wind?] shaken by the wind? But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold, those who wear soft garments are in kings’ houses. But what did you go out to see? A prophet? [Note: [Col. 0206] and I tell you, more than] Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet. For this is [Note: [Col. 0206] is of] he of whom it is written: ‘Behold, [Note: [Col. 0206] I] I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’

“Amen, I say to you: among those born of women none [Note: [Col. 0206] a prophet greater] greater than John [Col. 0207] the Baptist has arisen; yet he who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent [Note: [Col. 0207] seize] seize it. For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John; and if you are willing [Note: [Col. 0207] to know, he] to receive it, he is Elijah who is to come. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

“But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplace [Note: [Col. 0207] and calling to one another and saying: We sang] who call to their companions and say: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not mourn.’ For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say: ‘He has a demon.’ [Note: [Col. 0207] came] And the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say: ‘Behold, a glutton and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax-collectors and sinners.’ And wisdom has been vindicated by her children.”

Then [Note: [Col. 0208] Jesus began to rebuke] he began to reproach the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they had not repented. “Woe to you, [Note: [Col. 0208] Chorazin] Chorazin! And Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes. Nevertheless I say to you: it will be more tolerable for Tyre and [Note: [Col. 0208] Sidon, more mildly] Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

[Col. 0209] “And you, Capernaum, [Note: [Col. 0209] which will be exalted to heaven, down to [ [Col. 0209] Saint Jerome found this reading in the Saint-Germain manuscript, for he says: “In another copy we find: ‘And you, Capernaum, which have been exalted to heaven, shall descend to hell.’” There is [Col. 0210] a double interpretation, etc. Consult his *Commentary*, Book II, on Matthew chapter 11.]] will you be exalted to heaven? You will descend to hell. For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Sodom, [Note: [Col. 0209] perhaps they would have remained until the present day] it might perhaps have remained to this day. Nevertheless I say to you: it will be more tolerable for [Note: [Col. 0209] the land of Sodom] Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”

At that time [Note: [Col. 0209] Jesus answered and said: I confess to you, Father, Lord,] Jesus said: “I confess to you, God, Father of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little ones. Yes, Father, because [Note: [Col. 0209] because thus it was well pleasing before you.] so it pleased you. All things have been handed over to me by my Father. And no one [Note: [Col. 0210] knows] knows the Son except the Father; nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.

“Come to me, all you who labour and are burdened, and I will refresh you. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is sweet, and my burden is light [Note: [Col. 0210] is.].

XII. At that time Jesus went [Note: [Col. 0210] through grainfields on sabbaths] through the grainfield on the sabbath; and his disciples [Col. 0211] [Note: [Col. 0211] being hungry, began to pluck ears of grain,] were hungry and began to pluck ears of grain and eat. But when the Pharisees [Note: [Col. 0211] saw them,] saw them, they said to him: “Behold, your disciples are doing what is not lawful [Note: [Col. 0211] for them to do on sabbaths. But he said to them:] to do on the sabbath.” But Jesus answered them: “Have you not read what David did [Note: [Col. 0211] when] when he and those who were with him were hungry: how he entered the house of God and ate [Note: [Col. 0211] ate,] the bread of the Presence, which it was not lawful for him or those who were with him to eat, but only for priests? Or have you not read in the Law that, on sabbaths, priests in the temple violate the sabbath and are guiltless?

“For I tell you that something greater is [Note: [Col. 0211] Here is something greater than the temple [ [Col. 0211] Jerome notes that *hic* is to be read as an adverb: “‘Here,’” he says, “is not a pronoun but an adverb of place, because the place which contains the Lord [Col. 0212] of the temple is greater than the temple.”]] here than the temple. But if you knew what [Note: [Col. 0211] is] this means, ‘I desire mercy rather than sacrifice,’ you would never have condemned the innocent. For the Son of Man is Lord of the sabbath.”

And Jesus went on from there [Note: [Col. 0212] and came into their synagogue] and came into their synagogue. And behold, there was a certain man there with [Note: [Col. 0212] behold, there was a man having] a withered hand; and they questioned him, saying: “Is it lawful to heal on sabbaths?” so that they might accuse him. [Note: [Col. 0212] But he said to them: “Which one of you has a sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the sabbath, will he not take hold of it and lift it out? How much more valuable is a man than a sheep?” etc., as in the Vulgate.] But Jesus said to them: “Which of you, if he has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the sabbath, will not take hold of it and [Col. 0213] lift it out? How much, then, does a man differ from a sheep? Therefore is it lawful to do good on sabbaths, or not?” Then he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, [Note: [Col. 0213] and it was restored] and it became like the other.

And when the Pharisees [Note: [Col. 0213] having gone out … were making] had gone out from there, they took counsel against him, that they might [Note: [Col. 0213] destroy him.] destroy him. [Note: [Col. 0213] But Jesus, knowing … and they followed him.] Jesus, learning this, withdrew from there; many followed him, and [Note: [Col. 0213] he healed them all. And he commanded them not to make him public. That it might be fulfilled] he healed them. But he sternly charged all those whom he healed not to make him known, that what had been spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:

“Behold my servant, whom I chose,
my beloved, [Note: [Col. 0214] my beloved, in whom my soul was well pleased.] whom my soul received.
I will put my Spirit upon him,
and he will announce judgment to the Gentiles.
He will not contend or cry out,
nor will anyone hear [Note: [Col. 0214] anyone hear his voice in the streets. A bruised reed] his voice in the streets.
A bruised reed he will not break,
and smouldering flax he will not extinguish,
[Note: [Col. 0214] until he casts forth victory unto judgment [ [Col. 0214] Saint Hilary: “Until, when he casts forth victory unto judgment.”]] until he establishes judgment for victory.
And in his name the Gentiles will hope.”

Then a certain man was brought to him, [Note: [Col. 0214] a man possessing a demon, blind and mute, and he healed him] possessed by a demon, blind, deaf, and mute; and he healed him, so that [Note: [Col. 0214] the mute man spoke and saw. And they were astonished at him] the deaf man heard, saw, and spoke. And [Col. 0215] all the crowds marvelled and said: “Can this be the Son of David?” But the Pharisees, [Note: [Col. 0215] hearing it, said:] hearing this, said: “This man casts out demons only by [Note: [Col. 0215] Beelzebul] Beelzebub, prince of demons.”

But Jesus, seeing [Note: [Col. 0215] Knowing] their thoughts, said [Note: [Col. 0215] to them:]: “Every kingdom divided [Note: [Col. 0215] against itself will be laid waste:] against itself will be desolated, and every city or house divided [Note: [Col. 0215] against] against itself will not stand. [Note: [Col. 0215] For if] Therefore, if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand? And if I cast out demons by [Note: [Col. 0215] Beelzebul] Beelzebub, by whom do your sons [Note: [Col. 0215] cast them out?] cast them out? [Note: [Col. 0216] Therefore they] Therefore they shall be your judges. But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has drawn near [Note: [Col. 0216] has drawn near upon you] to you.

“Or how can anyone [Note: [Col. 0216] anyone enter] enter a strong man’s house and plunder his goods, unless he first [Note: [Col. 0216] bind the strong man?] binds the strong man himself? Then he will plunder his house. He who is not with me is [Note: [Col. 0216] against] against me, and he who does not gather with me [Note: [Col. 0216] scatters.] scatters.

“Therefore I say to you: every sin and blasphemy [Note: [Col. 0216] are forgiven to men. And whoever speaks a word against] are forgiven to men; but whoever blasphemes against the Spirit of God is not forgiven. And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man shall be forgiven; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not [Note: [Col. 0216] be forgiven] be forgiven, neither in this age nor [Col. 0217] in the age to come.

“Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; for every tree is known by its [Note: [Col. 0217] for a tree will be known by its fruit.] fruit. Offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? [Note: [Col. 0217] For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. A good man, etc.] For out of the abundance of the heart each person speaks evil from his mouth. A good man brings forth good things from a good treasure, and an evil man brings forth evil things from an evil treasure. But I say to you that, for every idle word that men speak, they will give [Note: [Col. 0217] for it] account of it on the day of judgment. [Note: [Col. 0217] For each person shall be justified by his words, or condemned by his words.] For by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned.”

Then certain scribes of the Pharisees [Note: [Col. 0218] certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered Jesus,] answered him, saying: “Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.” [Note: [Col. 0218] But Jesus] But he answered them: “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet. For as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster for three days and three nights, so [Note: [Col. 0218] also] the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.

“The men of [Note: [Col. 0218] Ninevites] Nineveh will rise in judgment with [Note: [Col. 0218] this generation, and will condemn it:] this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching. [Col. 0219] And behold, one greater than [Note: [Col. 0219] Jonah is here.] Jonah is here. The queen of the south [Note: [Col. 0219] will rise … this generation, and condemn it … from the ends] will rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.

“But when an unclean spirit has gone out from a person, it [Note: [Col. 0219] walks] wanders through dry and deserted places [Note: [Col. 0219] seeking rest and does not find it.] seeking rest, and does not find it. Then it says: ‘I will return to [Note: [Col. 0219] the house from which] my house, from which I came out.’ And when it comes, if it [Note: [Col. 0219] finds it empty, swept clean, and put in order.] finds it empty and swept clean, [Note: [Col. 0219] Then it goes and takes with it … more wicked than itself. And [Col. 0220] entering, they will dwell in him:] then it goes and takes seven other spirits more wicked than itself; entering, they dwell there, and that person’s latter condition becomes worse [Note: [Col. 0220] more than the former.] than the former. So it will also be with this most wicked generation.”

While he was speaking to the crowds, behold, [Note: [Col. 0220] While he was speaking to] his mother and brothers were standing outside, [Note: [Col. 0220] desiring to speak, etc., as in the Vulgate through “saying to him.”] desiring to speak with him. But he answered those who were speaking with him: “Who is my mother, [Note: [Col. 0220] and who are my brothers?] and who are my brothers?” And stretching out his hand [Note: [Col. 0220] toward his disciples,] toward his disciples, he said: “Behold, my mother and my brothers. For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, [Note: [Col. 0220] he is my brother,] he is to me brother and sister and mother.”

[Col. 0221] XIII. On that day [Note: [Col. 0221] he went out … beside] Jesus went out and sat beside the sea. And great crowds were gathered to him, [Note: [Col. 0221] so that he went up into a boat and sat …] so that he went aboard a boat and sat there, while the whole crowd stood on the shore. And he spoke many things to them in parables, saying: “A [Note: [Col. 0221] sower went out to sow. And] sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the way; and the birds of heaven came and ate it. [Note: [Col. 0221] But some fell on rocky places, where] But others fell upon rocky places, where there was not much soil; and [Note: [Col. 0221] immediately they sprang up, etc., as in the Vulgate.] they sprang up at once. But when the sun rose, they were scorched and withered because they had no root. Others fell among thorns; and the thorns [Note: [Col. 0221] grew] sprang up and choked them. But others fell into good soil and [Note: [Col. 0222] yielded fruit, some] yielded fruit: one a hundredfold, [Note: [Col. 0222] and] another sixtyfold, and another thirtyfold. He who has ears [Note: [Col. 0222] to hear, let him hear.] to hear, let him hear.”

And the disciples came to him and said: “Why do you speak to them in parables?” [Note: [Col. 0222] But he answered them: Because] He answered them: “Because it has been given to you [Note: [Col. 0222] to know the mystery of the kingdom; to them] to know the secrets of God; but to them it has not been given. For to him who has, more will be given, and he will abound; but from him who does not have, [Col. 0223] even what he has will be taken away.

“For this reason I speak to them in parables: so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may [Note: [Col. 0223] hear and not understand, lest at any time they turn. And then] not hear or understand. And then the prophecy of Isaiah will be fulfilled in them, which says: ‘Go and say to this people: [Note: [Col. 0223] You shall hear with hearing] You shall hear with the ear, and not understand; and seeing [Note: [Col. 0223] you shall see and not behold. The heart has grown fat] you shall not see. For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have heard heavily [Note: [Col. 0223] they have heard; lest at any time], and they have shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I heal them.’

“But blessed are your eyes [Note: [Col. 0224] because they see, and your ears which] which see, and your ears which hear. Amen, I say to you, many prophets and righteous people desired to see what [Note: [Col. 0224] you see, and to hear] you see and did not see it, and to hear what [Note: [Col. 0224] you heard,] you hear and did not hear it.

“Therefore hear the parable of the sower. Everyone who hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it—the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart: this is the one sown beside the way. The one sown on rocky ground is he who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy; [Note: [Col. 0224] receives it; but does not] he has no root in himself, but is temporary. Then, when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, he immediately falls away.

“But the one [Note: [Col. 0224] sown among thorns] sown among thorns is he who [Col. 0225] hears the word, and the anxiety of this age [Note: [Col. 0225] of this age and the pleasure of riches] and the deceitfulness of riches [Note: [Col. 0225] choke] choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful. But the one sown in good soil is he who hears the word and understands it, and bears fruit and produces: one a hundredfold, another [Note: [Col. 0225] another sixtyfold, another] sixtyfold, and yet another thirtyfold.”

He set before them another parable, saying: “The kingdom of heaven has become like a man who sowed good seed in his field. But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel [Note: [Col. 0225] among the wheat] among the wheat, and went away. [Note: [Col. 0225] But when it had grown] But when the blade had grown and borne fruit, then the darnel also appeared. And the servants of the [Note: [Col. 0226] householder, and] householder came to him and said: ‘Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then does it have darnel?’ And he said to them: ‘An enemy has done this.’ [Note: [Col. 0226] The servants say to him, “Do you wish,”] The servants said to him: ‘Do you wish us to go and gather it?’ But he said: ‘No, lest in gathering the darnel you uproot [Note: [Col. 0226] the wheat with it. But let] the wheat along with it. Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest-time I shall say to the reapers: Gather the darnel first and bind [Note: [Col. 0226] it into bundles] it into bundles to burn it, [Col. 0227] but gather the wheat into my barn.’”

He set before them another parable, saying: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field. It is indeed the least of all seeds; but when it has grown, it is greater [Note: [Col. 0227] than all vegetables, so that] than all herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of heaven come and dwell in its branches.”

He spoke another parable to them: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, [Note: [Col. 0227] which, when taken,] which a woman took and hid in three [Note: [Col. 0227] measures] measures of meal, until all of it was leavened.”

Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and without parables he did not speak to them, so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”

Then, having dismissed the crowds, he came into the house; and his disciples came to him, saying: [Note: [Col. 0227] Explain … the parable of the wheat and the darnel in the field. But Jesus answered] “Explain to us the parable of the darnel and the field.” He answered: “He who [Note: [Col. 0228] sows] sows the good seed is the Son of Man. The field is [Note: [Col. 0228] this] the world. The good seed are the children of the kingdom. The darnel are [Note: [Col. 0228] these are children of wickedness] wicked children. [Col. 0229] The enemy who sowed [Note: [Col. 0229] it is] it is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age [Note: [Col. 0229] of the age. The reapers, however,] and the reapers are angels.

“Therefore, just as the darnel is gathered and burned in fire, so it will be at the end of the age. The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who commit iniquity, and cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then the righteous will shine like the sun [Note: [Col. 0229] in the kingdom of their Father.] in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

“The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field. When a man finds it, he hides it; and, because of his joy, he goes away and sells all that he has and buys that field. [Note: [Col. 0229] What is said concerning the precious pearl is omitted through a copyist’s negligence in the Corbie manuscript. The omission was easy because the word *Again* is repeated in succession [Col. 0230].] Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking fine pearls. Having found [Note: [Col. 0229] But having found one precious pearl, he went away.] one precious pearl, he went and sold everything [Note: [Col. 0229] whatever] that he had, and bought it.

“Again, the kingdom of heaven is like [Note: [Col. 0229] a net cast into the sea, which gathered fish of every kind. When it was full, they drew it to shore; and sitting down, they selected the good into their vessels,] a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering fish of every kind. When it was full, they drew it out; and sitting beside the shore, they put the good [Col. 0231] into vessels, but threw the bad away. So [Note: [Col. 0231] shall it be at] it will be at the end of the age: the angels will go out [Note: [Col. 0231] and separate] and separate the wicked from among the righteous, and throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping [Note: [Col. 0231] of the eyes,] and gnashing of teeth.”

“Have you understood all these things?” They said to him: [Note: [Col. 0231] Certainly, Lord. And he said to them:] “We have understood.” And he said to them: “Therefore every scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old.”

And it came to pass, when Jesus [Note: [Col. 0231] had finished] had finished these parables, [Note: [Col. 0231] he went on from there. And having come] he went on from there. And when he came into his own country, he taught them in their synagogues, so that they marvelled and said: “Where did this man get this wisdom [Note: [Col. 0232] this wisdom.] and these mighty works? Is this not [Note: [Col. 0232] the son [ [Col. 0231] *Scribe*, through a copyist’s error, in place of *carpenter.*] of Joseph the carpenter? … Is his mother called Mary?] the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas? And are not all his sisters [Note: [Col. 0232] are they not all with us?] with us? Where then did he get [Note: [Col. 0232] all these things? … at him.] this wisdom?” And they took offence at him.

But Jesus said to them: “A prophet is not without honour except [Note: [Col. 0232] in his own country. And therefore he did not perform … many] in his own city and in his own house.” And he performed no further mighty works there because of their unbelief.

XIV. At that time Herod the tetrarch heard [Note: [Col. 0232] **the report of Jesus: and said:**] of the reputation of Jesus, and said to his servants: “This is John [Col. 0233] the Baptist [Note: [Col. 0233] **the Baptist: he himself has risen**] whom I myself beheaded; he has risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works operate in him.” [Note: [Col. 0233] **For Herod had seized John, bound him, and put him in**] But Herod, having apprehended John, bound him and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother. For John said to him: “It is not lawful for you [Note: [Col. 0233] **to have her**] to have your brother’s wife.” And wishing to kill him, he feared the people, because [Note: [Col. 0233] **they held him as a prophet. But when the day of Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the middle of the dining-room**] they regarded him as a prophet. But when Herod’s birthday arrived, the daughter of Herodias danced at the banquet and pleased Herod. [Note: [Col. 0233] **as in the Vulgate as far as the word “Give”**] Therefore he promised with an oath that he would give her whatever she asked of him. But the girl, prompted by her mother, said to him: “Give me John the Baptist’s head on a platter.” And King Herod was grieved because of [Note: [Col. 0234] **the oath, and because of those reclining with him he commanded it to be given. And he sent**] the oath, and because of those reclining with him, he commanded it to be given. And at once he sent and beheaded John in prison. And his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl; [Note: [Col. 0234] **but the girl**] she in turn brought it to her mother. And John’s disciples came [Note: [Col. 0234] **his**] and took his body and buried [Note: [Col. 0234] **it**] him; and they came and reported it to Jesus.

When Jesus heard this, he withdrew [Note: [Col. 0234] **withdrew . . . in a boat**] from there by boat, [Col. 0235] to a deserted place [Note: [Col. 0235] **apart. And when**] alone. When the crowds heard this, they followed him [Note: [Col. 0235] **on foot from**] on foot from their cities. [Note: [Col. 0235] **and when he came out**] And coming out, he saw a great crowd, had compassion on them, and [Note: [Col. 0235] **healed their sick. And when evening had come**] healed their infirm.

But when it had become late, his disciples came to him, saying: “The place [Note: [Col. 0235] **is, and**] where we are is deserted, and the hour has already passed. Dismiss [Note: [Col. 0235] **the crowds into the villages**] this crowd, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.” [Note: [Col. 0235] **But Jesus said to them**] And Jesus said to them: “They have no need to go; give them something to eat yourselves.” [Note: [Col. 0235] **They said to him**] But they said: “We have [Note: [Col. 0235] **here**] with us only five loaves and two fish.” [Note: [Col. 0235] **And Jesus said to them: Bring them to me**] Jesus answered and said: “Bring them here.” And [Note: [Col. 0236] **when he had commanded**] he commanded the crowd to recline upon [Note: [Col. 0236] **the grass, having taken**] the grass; and, having taken the five loaves and the two fish, [Note: [Col. 0236] **looking up to . . . he blessed, and**] looking up to heaven, he blessed them and broke them, and gave them to the disciples [Note: [Col. 0236] **the loaves**], and the disciples to the crowds. And all ate and were satisfied. [Note: [Col. 0236] **And they gathered the remains**] And they took up what remained: twelve full baskets. [Note: [Col. 0236] **Now the number of those eating was five thousand men**] And those who ate numbered five thousand men, besides boys and women.

[Note: [Col. 0236] **And immediately Jesus commanded his disciples**] Then he commanded his disciples to get into the boat and [Note: [Col. 0236] **go before**] cross the strait, [Col. 0237] until [Note: [Col. 0237] **he himself**] he dismissed [Note: [Col. 0237] **the crowds. And when the crowd had been dismissed**] the crowd. And when he had dismissed them, he went up the mountain [Note: [Col. 0237] **alone to pray.**] and prayed alone. When evening came, he was there alone.

[Note: [Col. 0237] **But the boat, now in the middle of the sea, was tossed by the waves. In the fourth**] The boat was in the middle of the sea and was tossed by waves, for the wind was against them. But in the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking upon the sea. When they saw [Note: [Col. 0237] **him walking upon**] him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying that it [Note: [Col. 0237] **was**] was a phantom. [Note: [Col. 0237] **This present addition appears to have been transferred here from Mark, chapter 6, verse 52.**] For they had not understood, neither concerning the loaves; for their heart was dull. And for fear [Note: [Col. 0237] **they cried out; but immediately Jesus . . . to them**] they cried out.

At once he spoke to them, saying: “Take courage [Note: [Col. 0237] **do not be afraid; it is I. Simon Peter answered [Col. 0238] and said to him**] and do not be afraid.” And Simon Peter answered him: “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you upon the water.” [Note: [Col. 0238] **But he said**] And he said: “Come.” And [Note: [Col. 0238] **Peter, descending from the boat, walked**] Peter descended from the boat and walked on the water in order to come to Jesus. But seeing the strong wind, [Note: [Col. 0238] **he was afraid**] he became frightened; and when he began [Note: [Col. 0238] **to sink**] to sink, he cried out: “Lord, save me.” And [Note: [Col. 0238] **immediately**] immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, caught hold of him, and said: “You of little faith, why did you doubt?” And when he had entered the [Note: [Col. 0238] **boat**] boat, the wind ceased. [Note: [Col. 0238] **And those who were in the boat came and**] And those who were in the boat [Col. 0239] worshipped him, saying: “Truly, you are the Son of God.”

And when they had crossed over, they came into the land of [Note: [Col. 0239] **Gennesar. And when the men of that place recognized him, they sent throughout that whole region, and**] Gennesar. And when the people of that place recognized him, they worshipped him. Then immediately they sent throughout the whole district and brought to him all who were ill. And they begged him that they might [Note: [Col. 0239] **even**] merely touch the fringe of his garment. And all who touched it [Note: [Col. 0239] **were made well**] were healed.

XV. Then [Note: [Col. 0239] **scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem**] scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem came to him, saying: “Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash [Note: [Col. 0239] **their hands when**] their hands when they eat bread.” [Note: [Col. 0240] **But he**] But he answered them: “Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition? For God said: ‘Honor your father and mother’; and, ‘He who curses father [Note: [Col. 0240] **or . . . shall die**] or mother shall surely die.’ But you say: [Note: [Col. 0240] **Whatever gift from me would benefit you, he shall not honor**] ‘Whoever curses father or mother shall be liable to the fire of Gehenna’; and thus he has not honored his father [Note: [Col. 0240] **or**] or his mother. And you have made void [Note: [Col. 0240] **the commandment**] the word [Col. 0241] of God for the sake of your tradition [Note: [Col. 0241] **your. Hypocrites**]—the tradition [Note: [Col. 0241] **These words have been taken from the seventh chapter of the same Mark, verse 13, in the Corbie manuscript.**] which you have handed down. Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied well concerning you, saying: [Note: [Col. 0241] **This people . . . but their heart**] ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. In vain do they worship me, teaching [Note: [Col. 0241] **doctrines**] doctrine and commandments of men.’”

And having called the crowds to him, he said [Note: [Col. 0241] **to them**] to them: “Hear and understand. What enters the mouth does not defile a person; but what proceeds from the mouth [Note: [Col. 0241] **this**] defiles a person.” Then [Note: [Col. 0241] **his disciples came and said to him**] his disciples came to him and said: “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard [Note: [Col. 0241] **this saying**] this saying?” But Jesus answered: “Every planting which my heavenly [Note: [Col. 0242] **Father**] Father has not planted shall be uprooted. Leave them alone: for they are blind leaders of the blind. But if a blind person [Note: [Col. 0242] **gives guidance to a blind person, both . . . will fall**] shows the way to a blind person, both fall into a pit.”

Peter answered and said [Note: [Col. 0242] **to him: Explain this parable to us. But he said . . . are you still without understanding?**]: “Explain this comparison to us.” To them he said: “Are you also still without understanding? Do you not understand that everything entering the mouth goes into the stomach and [Note: [Col. 0242] **is expelled into the privy**] is cast out through the privy? But the things [Note: [Col. 0242] **that proceed . . . come forth, and they themselves defile**] which come out of the mouth proceed from the heart. These are what defile [Col. 0243] a person. For from the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual immorality, thefts, false testimony, blasphemies, [Note: [Col. 0243] **As in the Vulgate. [ [Col. 0243] The following words in the Corbie manuscript have been transferred here from chapter 7 of Saint Mark, verse 22.]] greed, wickedness, deceit, shamelessness, the evil eye. These are what make a person unclean. But to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a person.”

And Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the [Note: [Col. 0243] **districts . . . of Sidon**] region of Tyre and Sidon. And behold, a Canaanite woman who had come out from those borders [Note: [Col. 0243] **cried out to him, saying**] cried to him: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is grievously afflicted by a demon.” [Note: [Col. 0243] **But Jesus did not**] But he did not answer her a word. And [Note: [Col. 0243] **As in the Vulgate.**] his disciples came and begged him: “Dismiss her, for she cries after us.” But he answered: “I have not been sent except to the lost [Note: [Col. 0243] **which have perished**] sheep of the house of Israel.” But she [Note: [Col. 0244] **came and**] came and worshipped him, saying: “Help me, Lord.” [Note: [Col. 0244] **But he**] But he answered her: “It is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to dogs.” But she said: [Note: [Col. 0244] **Certainly**] “Yes, Lord; for even [Note: [Col. 0244] **little dogs**] the puppies eat of the crumbs [Note: [Col. 0244] **As in the Vulgate.**] of their masters.” Then Jesus answered and said to her: “O woman, great is your faith [Note: [Col. 0244] **As in the Vulgate.**]; let it be done for you as you wish.” [Note: [Col. 0244] **And she was healed**] And her daughter was made well from that hour.

And when Jesus had [Note: [Col. 0244] **passed from there, he came**] withdrawn [Col. 0245] from there, he came beside the sea of Galilee; and going up the mountain, he sat there. [Note: [Col. 0245] **The order of these epithets is disturbed not only in our Latin manuscripts, but also in several Greek copies and in the Anglo-Saxon version.**] And [Note: [Col. 0245] **great crowds came up to him, bringing with them the blind, lame, crippled, mute, and many others, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] great crowds came up to him, bringing with them deaf people, blind people, lame people, maimed people, infirm people, and many other mute people; and they laid them at his feet, and he healed [Note: [Col. 0245] **them all**] them, so that the crowds marvelled, seeing the mute speaking, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

XVI. But Jesus, having called his disciples, said: [Note: [Col. 0245] **I have compassion on the crowd, because it is now three days that they have remained with me**] “I have compassion on this crowd, because it is now three days that they have stayed with me and have nothing to eat; and I do not wish to send them away fasting, lest they faint on the way.” [Note: [Col. 0245] **They say to him**] The disciples said to him: “Where then [Note: [Col. 0246] **in the desert, so many loaves**] are we to get loaves in the desert sufficient to satisfy the crowds?” Jesus said to them: “How many loaves do you have?” [Note: [Col. 0246] **As in the Vulgate.**] They answered: “Seven, and [Note: [Col. 0245] **From another miracle, which all the Evangelists mention, the number of fish here is specified in the Corbie manuscript. For the Gospel records not seven loaves, but only five, with two fish.**] two fish.” And he commanded the crowd [Note: [Col. 0246] **to recline upon the ground. And Jesus took the loaves and fish, gave thanks, and gave, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] to recline on the ground. And taking the seven loaves and the two fish, he gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds. And all ate and were satisfied. And they took up [Note: [Col. 0246] **what remained of, etc., as in the Vulgate as far as Magadan.**] seven baskets full of the bread remaining over. And those who ate [Col. 0247] were about four thousand, besides boys and women. And, having dismissed the crowds, he got into the boat and came into the region of Magadan.

And Pharisees and Sadducees came to him, testing him; and asked him, saying, [Note: [Col. 0247] **that he might show them a sign from heaven. But he**] that he should show them a sign from heaven. But Jesus answered them: “When evening has come, you say, ‘It will be fair, for the sky is red [Note: [Col. 0247] **with clouds. And in the morning**].’ And in the morning: ‘There will be a storm, for the sky is red with gloom.’ Hypocrites, you know how to discern the appearance [Note: [Col. 0247] **therefore of the sky**] of the sky, but cannot recognize the signs of the times? An evil generation [Note: [Col. 0247] **seeks**] desires a sign, and no sign shall be given it except the sign of Jonah.” And leaving them, he went [Note: [Col. 0247] **And when they had crossed the strait, his disciples forgot [Col. 0248] to take bread. But Jesus said to them: Take heed**] to the region beyond; and his disciples forgot to take bread with them. And he said to them: “See and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” [Note: [Col. 0248] **Then they reasoned among themselves, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] But they reasoned within themselves: “He says this because we have not brought bread.”

When Jesus perceived it, he said to them: [Note: [Col. 0248] **While they were reasoning, he said: Why do you reason among yourselves**] “Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have no bread? Do you not yet understand, nor [Note: [Col. 0248] **remember the five loaves, five, etc., as in the Vulgate as far as ‘Sadducees.’**] remember the five loaves and the five [Col. 0249] thousand people, and how many baskets you took up? Or the seven loaves among four thousand people, and how many hampers you carried away? How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread: ‘Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees’?” Then they understood that he had not told them to refrain from the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, but from their teaching.

[Note: [Col. 0249] **that they should beware of the Sadducees. And Jesus came . . . into the region . . . and was asking**] And when Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, he questioned his disciples, saying: [Note: [Col. 0249] **Whom do people say that I, the Son of Man, am? [ [Col. 0249] The same reading occurs in Hilary, Leo the Great, and others who used copies of the Old Vulgate. It is also found in Augustine, Book II, *On the Harmony of the Evangelists*, although there he follows Jerome’s corrected text of the Latin translation. And he rightly reads the pronoun *me*, because it stands in the Greek sources: Τίνα με λέγουσιν, that is, “Whom do they say that I am?”]] [Note: [Col. 0250] **“Whom” instead of “how many,” through a copyist’s fault.**] “Whom do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?” But they [Note: [Col. 0250] **said John**] answered: “John the Baptist; others Elijah; others Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.” [Note: [Col. 0250] **as in the Vulgate as far as ‘And I’**] He said to them: “But whom do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered him: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus answered and said to him: “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I [Note: [Col. 0250] **say to you, you are, etc., as in the Vulgate as far as, ‘and whatever’**] tell you that you are Peter, and [Note: [Col. 0249] **This is how it was written in the Latin copies used by Saint Cyprian. Consult the new edition of the works of that martyr.**] upon this rock I shall build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. I shall give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. And whatever [Col. 0251] you bind upon earth shall be bound [Note: [Col. 0251] **also in**] in heaven; and whatever you loose upon earth shall be loosed [Note: [Col. 0251] **also in**] in heaven.”

Then he instructed his disciples [Note: [Col. 0251] **that they should tell no one that he himself was the Christ. From that time**] to tell no one that he was the Christ. From that day Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, [Note: [Col. 0251] **and scribes**] chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day. And Peter, [Note: [Col. 0251] **taking**] looking at him, began [Note: [Col. 0252] **to rebuke him and say, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] to say: “Far be it from you, Lord; this shall not happen.” But Jesus turned and said to him: [Note: [Col. 0252] **But he . . . said to Peter**] “Get behind me, Satan; you are a stumbling block [Note: [Col. 0252] **to me. Then Jesus said**] to me, because you do not savor the things of God but those of human beings.”

Then Jesus said to his disciples: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny [Note: [Col. 0252] **himself to himself**] himself, take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it; [Note: [Col. 0252] **as in the Vulgate as far as ‘the majesty of his Father’**] but whoever loses it for my sake shall find it. What does it profit a person if he gains the whole world and suffers loss of his life? Or what shall a person give in exchange for his life? For the Son of Man is coming in the majesty [Col. 0253] of his Father with his angels, and then he shall repay each person according to [Note: [Col. 0253] **his works**] their deeds. Amen I say to you: [Note: [Col. 0253] **because there are some standing here**] there are some here among those standing by who shall not taste death until they see the Son of Man [Note: [Col. 0253] **the Son of Man in his kingdom**] coming into the kingdom of his Father.”

XVII. And it came to pass after [Note: [Col. 0253] **six days, as in the Vulgate as far as ‘And behold’**] the sixth day that Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and led them privately up a high mountain. And Jesus was transfigured before them. His face shone like light, and his garments became white as snow. And behold, [Note: [Col. 0253] **Moses appeared to them, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] Moses and Elijah were seen with him, speaking with him. Peter said to Jesus: “Lord, it is good for us to be here; and if you wish, I shall make three tents: one for you, [Note: [Col. 0253] **and one for Moses**] one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” While he was still speaking, behold, a [Note: [Col. 0254] **bright cloud overshadowed them**] white cloud overshadowed them. And behold, a voice from the cloud said: “This is my [Note: [Col. 0254] **beloved . . . listen to him. And hearing, etc., as in the Vulgate as far as ‘touched’**] dearest Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.” Hearing this, the disciples fell upon their faces and were greatly afraid. Jesus came, and touched [Note: [Col. 0254] **them, saying**] them, and said: “Rise, and do not be afraid.” [Note: [Col. 0254] **Lifting**] But lifting [Col. 0255] their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone.

[Note: [Col. 0255] **As they descended**] And as they descended from the mountain, Jesus commanded them: [Note: [Col. 0255] **Tell no one the vision**] “See that you tell no one until the Son of Man rises from the dead.” [Note: [Col. 0255] **And they asked**] Then his [Note: [Col. 0255] **disciples. Why**] disciples asked him: “Why then do the scribes say [Note: [Col. 0255] **that Elijah must first come? But he . . . will come to restore all things. But I say**] that Elijah must come first?” He answered: “Elijah indeed shall come in order to restore all things. But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did [Note: [Col. 0255] **So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτῷ, ‘to him,’ from Mark.**] to him [+] whatever they wished.” [Note: [Col. 0255] **Two of our manuscript codices preserve this order of the context; but in the Vulgate, “So also the Son of Man,” [Col. 0256] etc., is placed before “Then they understood,” etc., in conformity with the Greek source.**] Then [Note: [Col. 0255] **the disciples understood that . . . And when he had come to the crowd**] his disciples understood that he had spoken to them of John. “So also the Son of Man [Note: [Col. 0256] **must suffer**] is about to suffer from them.”

And behold, a man from the crowd came to him, [Note: [Col. 0256] **a certain man . . . before him, saying**] falling on his knees and begging: “Lord, have mercy on my son, because he is afflicted by the moon and grievously [Note: [Col. 0256] **As in the Vulgate as far as ‘into the fire’**] suffers; for he often falls through the demon into the fire and sometimes into the water. And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not [Note: [Col. 0256] **heal him. Jesus answered and said: O generation**] heal him.” Jesus answered him: “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long [Note: [Col. 0256] **shall I endure you? How long shall I be with you? etc., as in the Vulgate as far as ‘cast it out.’**] am I with you? How long shall I endure you? Bring him here.” [Col. 0257] And Jesus commanded it, and immediately the demon came out of him; and the boy was healed from that hour.

Then the disciples came privately to Jesus and said: “Why could we not cast it out?” He said to them: “Because of your unbelief. Amen I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and [Note: [Col. 0257] **it shall move**] it shall move; and nothing shall be impossible for you.” [Note: [Col. 0257] **But this [ [Col. 0257] Everything said about the kind of demons cast out by prayer and fasting is omitted in the Corbie manuscript; but the Saint-Germain copy retains that verse entire, as it is read in the Latin Vulgate, as the Variant Readings sufficiently indicate. [Col. 0258]] etc., as in the Vulgate as far as ‘Jesus.’**] [Note: [Col. 0257] **Everything said about the kind of demons cast out by prayer and fasting is omitted in the Corbie manuscript; but the Saint-Germain copy retains that verse entire, as it is read in the Latin Vulgate, as the Variant Readings sufficiently indicate. [Col. 0258]] But while they were returning into Galilee, Jesus said: [Note: [Col. 0257] **The Son of Man is about to . . . be handed over, etc., as in the Vulgate as far as ‘greatly.’**] “The Son of Man will begin to be handed over into the hands of sinners; and they shall kill him, and on the third day he shall rise.” When they heard this, his disciples were greatly grieved.

And when they came to Capernaum, [Note: [Col. 0258] **those who collected the didrachma came to Peter**] those who collect the tribute came and said: “Why does your teacher [Note: [Col. 0258] **As in the Vulgate as far as ‘opening its mouth’**] not pay the tribute?” When Peter entered the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive tribute or tax— from their own people, or from strangers?” He answered: “From strangers.” Jesus said to him: “Then the sons [Col. 0259] are free.” Peter said: “Yes, Lord.” “Nevertheless, lest we offend them, go to the sea and cast a hook; take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth, you shall find [Note: [Col. 0259] **there, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] a stater. Give it to them for me and for yourself.”

XVIII. On that day the disciples came to Jesus, saying: “Who [Note: [Col. 0259] **indeed is greater**] shall be greater in the kingdom of heaven?” And [Note: [Col. 0259] **Jesus called a little child and**] Jesus, calling a child, set him in their midst and said: “Amen I say to you, unless you are converted [Note: [Col. 0259] **As in the Vulgate.**] and become as this child is, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. [Note: [Col. 0259] **For whoever humbles himself as this child, he shall be greater in the kingdom of heaven. And whoever receives one such child [Col. 0260] etc., as in the Vulgate.**] And whoever receives one such child in my name receives me. But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it is better for him that a millstone be hung about his neck and that he [Note: [Col. 0260] **be plunged down**] be cast into the depths of the sea.

“Woe to this world because of stumbling-blocks. For stumbling-blocks must come; nevertheless [Note: [Col. 0260] **woe to the person through . . . whom it comes**] woe to that person through whom the stumbling-block comes. If [Note: [Col. 0260] **your hand . . . your, etc., as in the Vulgate as far as ‘to enter’**] your hand or foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it from you. It is good for you to enter life crippled or lame, rather than, having two feet or two hands, to be cast into [Note: [Col. 0260] **the eternal fire**] the fire of Gehenna. [Col. 0261] And if your eye causes you to stumble, [Note: [Col. 0261] **you, pluck it out . . . from you: it is good for you . . . to enter into life**] take it out and cast it from you. It is more useful for you to enter life with one eye than, having two eyes, to be cast into the fire of Gehenna.

“See that you do not despise [Note: [Col. 0261] **one of the little ones [ [Col. 0261] Thus Hilary, adding with our manuscripts, ‘who believe in me’; Thomas Mareschallus noted the same thing in the Anglo-Saxon Version.] who believe in me**] any of these little ones [Note: [Col. 0261] **Thus Hilary, adding with our manuscripts, ‘who believe in me’; Thomas Mareschallus noted the same thing in the Anglo-Saxon Version.**] who believe in me. For I tell you that their angels [Note: [Col. 0261] **in heaven always see**] always see the face of my Father who is in heaven. [Note: [Col. 0261] **For [ [Col. 0262] This entire verse is also lacking here in the Corbie manuscript; the Saint-Germain codex, however, retains it, agreeing with the Vulgate edition.] he came, as in the Vulgate.**] [Note: [Col. 0262] **This entire verse is also lacking here in the Corbie manuscript; the Saint-Germain codex, however, retains it, agreeing with the Vulgate edition.**]

“What do you think? If [Note: [Col. 0261] **a person has**] a man has a hundred sheep, and one of them strays, does he not [Note: [Col. 0262] **leave**] leave the ninety-nine upon the mountains and go to seek the one that strayed? And if it happens that he finds it, amen I say to you, [Note: [Col. 0262] **that he will rejoice over it more than**] he shall rejoice over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not stray. Thus it is not the will before your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

“But if your brother sins against you, go [Note: [Col. 0262] **and, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] and rebuke him alone with yourself alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother. [Note: [Col. 0262] **But if, etc., as in the Vulgate.**] But if he does not listen to you, take one or two with you, and in the presence of two or three witnesses every [Col. 0263] word shall stand. But if [Note: [Col. 0263] **he does not listen to them**] he does not listen even to them, tell the church. But if he does not listen even to the church, let him be to you as a Gentile [Note: [Col. 0263] **and a tax collector.**] and as a tax collector.

“Amen I say to you: whatever you bind upon earth shall be [Note: [Col. 0263] **bound also**] bound in heaven, and whatever you loose upon earth shall be loosed [Note: [Col. 0263] **also in heaven. Again, amen I say**] in heaven. Amen I say to you: if two [Note: [Col. 0263] **of you**] agree upon earth concerning any matter whatsoever for which they ask, [Note: [Col. 0263] **it shall be done**] it shall come to pass for them from my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered [Note: [Col. 0263] **gathered in**] only in my name, [Note: [Col. 0264] **there I am also . . . among them. There are not [ [Col. 0263] I have been unable to find any trace of this addition anywhere.] gathered in my name among whom I am not**] there I am in their midst.”

Then Peter came to him and said: “Lord, if my brother sins against me, how often shall I forgive him? [Note: [Col. 0264] **as far as**] Seven times?” Jesus said to him: “I do not say to you, as far as seven times, but [Note: [Col. 0264] **as far as**] seventy times seven.”

XIX. Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. And when he had begun to settle accounts, one was brought before him who owed ten thousand talents. But since he had nothing with which to repay, his master ordered him to be sold, and his wife and children and all that he had, and the debt to be repaid. But that servant fell down and begged him, saying: “Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay everything to you.” Moved with pity for that servant, the master released him and forgave him the entire debt. But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and, seizing him, he was choking him, saying: “Pay what you owe.” And that fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying: “Have patience with me, and I will repay everything to you.” But he would not; rather, he went away and put him in prison until he should repay the whole debt.
