“Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall perform your oaths to the Lord.’ But I say to you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, because it is God’s throne; nor by earth, because it is his footstool; nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King. Nor shall you swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.

“But let your speech be ‘yes, yes’; ‘no, no.’ What is beyond these is from evil. You have heard that it was said: ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I say to you, do not resist evil; rather, if anyone strikes you on the right cheek, offer him the other also. To one who wishes to contend with you in court and take your tunic, yield your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go one thousand paces, go with him two. Give to everyone who asks you, and do not turn away from one who wishes to borrow from you.

“You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you: Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray [Note: [Col. 0169] According to the order of the Greek text, ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων (ὑμᾶς) καὶ διωκόντων ὑμᾶς: “for those who insult [you] and persecute you.”] for those who slander and persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven, who causes his sun to rise on the good and the evil, and rains upon the righteous and the unrighteous.

“For if you love those who love you, what reward will you have? Do not even tax collectors do that? And if you greet only your friends, what more do you do? Do not even Gentiles do that? Therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

“Take care not to perform [Note: [Col. 0169] The letter *a* has been erased.] your almsgiving before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.”

Therefore, when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in synagogues and streets, so that they may be honoured by people. Amen, I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0169] So also the Latin Cantabrigiensis, according to the Greek text, ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, “who is in the heavens.”] they have received + their reward. But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand does, so that your [Note: [Col. 0170] The *a* has been erased.] alms may be in secret; and your Father, [Col. 0172] who sees in secret, will repay you openly. And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, who love to pray standing in synagogues and at the street-corners, in order to be seen by people. Amen, I tell you that they have received their reward.

[Note: [Col. 0172] This pericope is lacking in the manuscript.] But when you pray, enter your chamber and, having shut your door, pray to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you openly. But when praying, do not use many words as the Gentiles do; for they think that they are heard because of their wordiness. Therefore do not be like them. For your Father knows what you need before you ask him.

Thus, therefore, you shall pray: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. May thy kingdom come. May thy will be done, as in heaven, also on earth. Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we too forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation. But deliver us from evil. [Note: [Col. 0171] “Amen” is lacking, also in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript.] For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory for ages. Amen. For if you forgive people their sins, your Father who is in heaven will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive people their sins, neither will the Father forgive [Col. 0174] your sins. And when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites. For they disfigure their faces, so that they may appear to people to be fasting. Amen, I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0173] They have *before*; “because” is lacking. Thus also in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript.] they have received their reward. But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, so that you may not appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret.

And your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you. Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal. [Note: [Col. 0173] From here as far as verse 27 of chapter VIII, everything is lacking in the Greek Cantabrigiensis manuscript, according to Mill in the Appendix.]

But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break in or steal. For where your treasure is, there [Note: [Col. 0173] Thus the Greek text: ἔσται, “will be.”] will + your heart also be.

The lamp of the body is the eye. If, therefore, your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. If, then, the light which is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

No one can serve two masters. For he will either hate one and love the other, or obey one and despise the other. You cannot serve God [Col. 0176] and Mammon.

Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you shall eat or what you shall drink; nor about your body, what you shall wear. Is not life more than food, and the body than clothing? Look at the birds of heaven: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of much greater worth than they? But which of you, by being anxious, can add one cubit to his stature? And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither labour nor spin. Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed as one of these. But if God thus clothes the grass of the field, which exists today and tomorrow is thrown into an oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little [Note: [Col. 0175] The *a* is lacking.] faith! Therefore do not be anxious, saying, “What shall we eat?” or “What shall we drink?” or [Note: [Col. 0175] Thus also the Greek text, τί (περιβαλώμεθα), “what shall we put on?”] what + shall we wear? For the Gentiles seek all these things. For your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow; for tomorrow will itself be anxious [Col. 0178] about itself. Sufficient for the day is its own evil.

Do not judge, so that you may not be judged. For by the judgment with which you judge, you shall be judged; and by the measure with which you measure, it shall be measured back to you. Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye, but do not see the beam in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, “Let me remove the speck from your eye,” when behold, there is a beam in your own eye? Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see to remove the speck from your brother’s eye. Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor throw your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet and turn and tear you apart. Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it shall be opened. Or what man among you, if his son asks him for bread, will offer him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will offer him a serpent? If therefore you, though evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him.

Therefore, whatever you wish people to do to you, [Note: [Col. 0177] They add “good things”; so also Cyprian, *On the Lord’s Prayer*. In the same place is added “thus,” according to the Greek text, οὕτω.] thus + you [Col. 0180] also do to them. For this is the Law and the Prophets. Enter through the narrow gate, for the gate is wide and the way spacious which leads to destruction, and many enter through it. How narrow is the gate and constricted the way which leads to life, and few are those who find it.

But beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will know them by their fruits.

Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? Thus every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit. A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit.

For every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore, you will know them by their fruits.

Not everyone who says to me, “Lord, Lord,” will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven. Many will say to me on that day, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, cast out demons in your name, and perform many mighty deeds in your name?” And then I shall declare to them: “I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity.” [Col. 0182] Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them [Note: [Col. 0181] Thus in the manuscript. The final *m* has been erased.] I will compare him to a wise man, who built his house upon rock. And the rain came down, the floods came, the winds blew, and struck against that house; and it did not f[Note: [Col. 0181] The *a* has been erased.]all, for it was founded upon [Note: [Col. 0181] The scribe omitted those three letters.] the rock. And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be compared to a foolish man, who built his house upon sand. And the rain came down, the floods came, the winds blew, and struck against that house; and it f[Note: [Col. 0182] The *a* has been erased.]ell, and its fall was great. And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowds marvelled at his teaching. For he taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes. And when he came down from the mountain, great crowds followed him. And behold, a certain leper came and worshipped him, saying, “Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me.” And Jesus, having stret[Note: [Col. 0182] The scribe omitted the letters *den*.]ched out his hand, touched him, saying, “I will; be cleansed.” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed. And Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift which [Col. 0184] Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.” After these things, when he had entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, beseeching him and saying, “Lord, my servant lies paralysed at home and is grievously tormented.” And Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.” And the centurion answered him, “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; but only speak the word, and my servant will be healed. For I too am a man having soldiers under my authority, and I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.” When Jesus heard this, he marvelled and said to those following him, “Amen, I tell you, I have not found such faith even in Israel. But I tell you that many shall come from the e[Note: [Col. 0183] The aspirated *h* has been erased.]ast and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven; but the children of this kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” And Jesus said to the centurion, “Go; and as you have believed, so be it to you.” And the servant was healed in that hour. And when Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying sick with a fever; and he t[Note: [Col. 0183] Perhaps the scribe omitted the preceding letters *te*.]ouched her hand, [Col. 0186] and the fever left her; and she rose and ministered to them. But when evening had come—(Here an entire page of the manuscript has perished, which perhaps a recent binder either did not possess or, because it was worn away, neglected, to the great loss of posterity. What follows is read on the next page.)—[Col. 0188] and the sea, and there was a great calm. But the men marvelled, saying, “What sort of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?” And when he had crossed the sea into the region of the Gerasenes, two demon-possessed men, coming out of the tombs, met him. They were exceedingly fierce, so that no one was able to pass by that way. And they cried out, saying, “What have we to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here before the time to torment us?” Now not far from them a large herd of pigs was feeding. And the demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, command us to go into the herd of pigs.” And he said to them, “Go.” So, coming out, they went into the herd of pigs; and behold, the whole herd rushed headlong into the sea and died in the waters. But those who tended them fled; and, coming into the city, they reported everything, including what had happened to those possessed by demons. And behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to depart from their region. And having embarked in a boat, he crossed over and came to his own city. And behold, they brought [Col. 0190] to him a paralytic lying on a bed. And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.” And behold, some of the scribes said among themselves, “This man blasphemes.” And Jesus, seeing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts? For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’? But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralytic—“Rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.” And he rose and went to his house. But when the crowds saw it, they marvelled and were afraid, and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

And as Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax-office. And he said to him, “Follow me.” And he rose and followed him. And it came to pass, as he reclined in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Jesus and his disciples. And when the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, [Col. 0192] “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” But Jesus, hearing it, said to them, “Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are ill do. Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” Then John’s disciples came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast frequently, but your disciples do not fast?” And Jesus said to them, “Can the sons of the bridegroom [Note: [Col. 0191] Thus also in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript: νηστεύειν, “to fast.”] fast + while the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then they shall fast. No one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for its fullness pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear results. Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, the wine is spilled, and the wineskins are ruined. But they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.” While he was saying these things to them, behold, [Col. 0194] a certain ruler came and worshipped him, saying, “Lord, my daughter has just died; but come, lay your hand upon her, and she will live.”

And Jesus rose and followed him with his disciples. And behold, a woman who had suffered from an issue of blood for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment. For she said within herself, “If only I touch his garment, I shall be healed.” But Jesus turned, and seeing her, said, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well.” And the woman was healed from that hour. And when Jesus came into the ruler’s house and saw the flute-players and the noisy crowd, he said to them, “Depart; for the girl is not dead, but sleeps.” And they ridiculed him. But when the crowd had been put out, he went in and took her hand, and the girl rose. And this report went out through all that land. And as Jesus passed on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David.” And when he had come into the house, those blind men came to him. And Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this for you?” They said to him, “Certainly, Lord.” Then Jesus touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith, let it be done to you.” And their eyes [Col. 0196] were opened.

And Jesus sternly charged them, saying, “See that no one knows.” But they, going out, spread his fame throughout that whole land. As they were going out, behold, they brought to him a mute man [Note: [Col. 0196] The following word, *deaf*, has been erased, though it is still visible.] possessed by a demon. And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke; and the crowds marvelled, saying, “Never has anything like this appeared in Is[Note: [Col. 0196] The *d* has been erased.]rael.” But the Pharisees said, “By the prince of demons he casts out demons.” And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity. And seeing the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and prostrate like sheep without a shepherd.

Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the labourers are few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send labourers into his harvest.”

And calling his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every disease and every infirmity. Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew [Col. 0198] his brother; James, son of Zebedee, and John his brother; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James, son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, who is called Thaddaeus; Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. These twelve Jesus sent out, commanding them [Note: [Col. 0197] Here too “and” is added, also in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript: καί.] and + saying: “Do not go into the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter cities of the Samaritans; but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And as you go, preach, saying, ‘The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’ Heal the sick, cleanse lepers, cast out demons; freely you have received, freely give. Do not acquire gold, silver, or money in your belts; no bag for the journey, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the labourer is worthy of his [Note: [Col. 0197] Thus also in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript: μισθοῦ, “wage.”] reward +.

“And into whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and remain there until you depart. And when entering the house, greet it, saying, ‘Peace to this house.’ And if that house is [Col. 0200] worthy, your peace shall come upon it; but if it is not worthy, your peace shall return to you. And whoever does not receive you or hear your words, when you go out [Note: [Col. 0199] Cyprian reads ‘when you stand,’ as do two manuscript codices of ours.] from that house or city, shake the dust from your feet. Amen, I tell you: it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.

“Behold, I send you as sheep among wolves. Be prudent as serpents and innocent as doves. But beware [Note: [Col. 0200] That word *vos* (‘you’) appears to have been erased by the copyist with two lines as superfluous in the text.] of people. For they will hand you over to councils, and scourge you in their synagogues; and you will be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles. But when they hand you over, do not be anxious about how or what you shall speak; for in that hour what you shall speak will be given to you. For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who will speak in you. Brother will hand over brother to death, and father child; children will rise against parents and put them to death. And you will be hated by all because of my name; but the one who endures to the end shall be saved. But when they persecute [Col. 0202] you in this city [Note: [Col. 0202] The letter *m* is marked as erased by the copyist.] flee to another. Amen, I tell you: you will not finish the cities of Is[Note: [Col. 0202] The letter *d* has been expunged.]rael before the Son of Man comes.

“A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master. It is enough for a disciple to be like his teacher, and for a servant to be like his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more his household! Therefore do not fear them. For nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, nor hidden that will not be known. What I tell you in darkness, say in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim from the housetops. And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna. Are not two sparrows sold for an *as*? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground without the will of your Father. But even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Therefore do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows. Therefore everyone who confesses me before people, I also will confess [Col. 0204] him before my Father who is in heaven; but whoever denies me before people, I too will deny him before my Father who is in heaven.

“Do not suppose that I came to bring peace upon the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword. For I came to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother; and a person’s enemies will be members of his household.

“He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. [Note: [Col. 0203] These words, ‘and he who,’ etc., as far as ‘worthy of me,’ are lacking in the Greek and Latin Cantabrigiensis manuscript.] And he who loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. + And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me. Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.

“Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. [Note: [Col. 0203] These words, ‘and whoever receives,’ etc., as far as ‘will receive,’ are lacking in the Greek and Latin Cantabrigiensis manuscript.] And whoever receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward. +

“And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple—amen, I tell you—will not lose his reward.”

And it came to pass, [Col. 0206] when Jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, that he departed from there to teach and preach in their cities.

But when John heard in prison of the works of Christ, he sent [Note: [Col. 0205] The Greek and Latin Cantabrigiensis manuscript, and the Gothic, have διὰ μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, “through his disciples.”] his disciples and said to him, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?” And Jesus answered and said to them, “Go, report to John what you hear and see: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor receive good news; and blessed is whoever is not offended by me.” And as they went away, Jesus began to say to the crowds concerning John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind? But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft [Note: [Col. 0205] They add ‘garments’; thus also the Greek text, ἱματίοις.] garments +? Behold, those who wear soft garments are in royal houses. But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

“For this is he of whom it has been written: ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’ Amen, I tell you: among those born of women none greater than John the Baptist has arisen; [Col. 0208] yet the one who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

“But from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and violent people seize it.

“For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John. And if you are willing to receive it, he is Elijah who is to come. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.

“But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplace and crying to one another, saying: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we lamented, and you did not mourn.’ For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’ But the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a glutton and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’ And wisdom has been vindicated by her children.” Then he began to reproach the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they did not repent: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago certainly have repented in sackcloth and ashes. Nevertheless, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

[Col. 0210] “And you, Capernaum, which have been exalted up to heaven, shall descend to Hades. For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Sodom, it might have remained to the present day. Nevertheless, I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.” At that time Jesus answered and said: “I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, who [Note: [Col. 0210] Thus.] have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for thus it was well-pleasing in your sight. All things have been delivered to me by my Father. And no one knows the Son except the Father; nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and the one to whom the Son wishes to reveal him. Come to me, all who labour and are burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is pleasant and my burden light.” At that time Jesus went [Note: [Col. 0209] Thus also the Greek text, τοῖς σάββασι, “on the Sabbaths.”] on the Sabbaths + through the grainfields; but his disciples, [Col. 0212] being hungry, began to pluck ears of grain and eat. But the Pharisees, seeing it, said to him, “Behold, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.” But he said to them, “Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him: how he entered the house of God and ate the loaves of the presentation, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but for priests alone? Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbaths the priests in the temple violate the Sabbath and are without guilt? But I tell you that one greater than the temple is here. But if you knew what this means, ‘I desire mercy rather than sacrifice,’ you would never have condemned the innocent. For the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.” And passing on from there, he entered their synagogue. And behold, a man [Note: [Col. 0211] They add *erat* (‘was’), as does the Greek text, ἦν.] was + there with a withered hand. And they asked him, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” so that they might accuse him. But he said to them, “What man among you has one sheep and, if it f[Note: [Col. 0212] The *a* has been erased.]alls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it [Col. 0214] and lift it out of the pit? How much more valuable is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.” Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and it became sound like the other. But the Pharisees, going out from there, took counsel against him in order to destroy him. But Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there.

And great crowds followed him, and he charged them not to make him known, so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: “Behold my servant, whom I chose; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will announce judgment to the Gentiles. He will not contend or cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets. He will not break a bruised reed, and he will not quench smouldering flax, until he brings judgment forth unto victory; and in his name the Gentiles shall hope.”

Then there was brought to him a man possessed by a demon, blind and mute, and he c[Note: [Col. 0213] Two letters have been completely erased.]ured him, so that he spoke and saw.

[Col. 0216] And all the crowds were astonished and said, “Can this be the Son of David?”

But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, “This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebul, the prince of demons.” But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand. And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand? And if I cast out [Note: [Col. 0215] Thus also the Greek text, τὰ δαιμόνια, “the demons.”] demons + by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they shall be your judges. But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has indeed come upon you. Or how can anyone enter the house of a strong man and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? Then he will plunder his house. Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters. Therefore I tell you: every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven people. And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age [Col. 0218] nor in the age to come. Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; for a tree is known by its fruit. Offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. A good person brings forth good things from the good treasure [Note: [Col. 0217] The word *cordis* (‘of the heart’) has been erased, but is still discernible.] of the heart; and an evil person brings forth evil things from an evil treasure. But I tell you that for every idle word which people speak, they will render account for it on the day of judgment. For by your words you shall be justifi[Note: [Col. 0218] *v* is used in place of *b*.]ed, and by your words you shall be condem[Note: [Col. 0218] *v* is used in place of *b*.]ned.”

Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, “Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.” But Jesus answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet. For as Jonah was in the belly [Note: [Col. 0218] The *o* in *coeti* has been erased.] of the whale for three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights. The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching. [Col. 0220] And behold, one greater than Jonah is here. The queen of the south shall rise in judgment with this generation and shall conde[Note: [Col. 0219] *Condemnavit*; *v* is used in place of *b*.]mn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom. And behold, one greater than Solomon is here.

When an unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it wanders through dry places, seeking rest and finding none. Then it says, “I will return to my house, from which I came out.” And on coming it finds it empty, swept clean, and adorned. Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself; and entering in, they dwell there, and the last condition of that person becomes worse than the first. So too it will be with this most wicked generation.

While he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak with him. And someone said to him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak with you.” But he answered and said to the one speaking to him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?” And stretching out his hand over his disciples, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers. For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, that person is my brother and sister and mother.”

[Col. 0222] On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea. Great crowds gathered around him, so that he got into a boat and sat down, while the whole crowd stood on the shore. And he spoke many things to them in parables, saying: “Behold, the sower went out to sow. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road; and birds came and ate them. Others fell on rocky ground, where they did not have much soil; and they sprang up at once, because they had no depth of soil. But when the sun rose, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered. Others fell among thorns; and the thorns grew up and choked them. But others fell on good soil and yielded fruit: one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, another thirtyfold. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

[Note: Col. 0219: In *nequitiores* (“more wicked”), the letters *ti* have been cancelled by the scribe with a transverse stroke.]

[Note: Col. 0221: The *a* in *caeciderunt* (“fell”) has been rubbed away, as also below.]

[Note: Col. 0221: The *a* in *caeciderunt* has been rubbed away, as also below.]

[Note: Col. 0221: The *a* has been rubbed away.]

[Note: Cols. 0221–0222: This passage is blank in the manuscript; it seems indeed that letters once stood there, but they have been completely erased, and no trace remains.]

Then his disciples came to him and said, “Why do you speak to them in parables?” But he answered and said to them, “Because to you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given. For to whoever has, more will be given, and he will abound; but from whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away. [Col. 0224] Therefore I speak to them in parables, because though seeing they do not see, and though hearing they do not hear or understand. And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: ‘You shall hear with hearing and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see and shall not perceive. For the heart of this people has grown dull; they have heard heavily with their ears, and they have shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn, and I heal them.’ But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear. Amen, I say to you: many prophets and righteous persons desired to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.

“So then, hear the parable of the sower. Everyone who hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it—the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart: this is the one sown beside the road. But the one sown on rocky ground is the person who hears my word and immediately receives it with joy; yet he has no root in himself, but is temporary. When tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, he is immediately offended. The one sown among thorns is the person who hears the [Col. 0226] word, but the anxiety of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful. But the one sown on good soil is the person who hears the word and understands it; he bears fruit and produces, one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, another thirtyfold.”

[Note: Col. 0223: The two letters *re* in *adimpleretur* (“might be fulfilled”) have been cancelled by the scribe with a transverse stroke.]

[Note: Col. 0224: The word *meum* (“my”) has been rubbed away.]

[Note: Col. 0223: So also the Greek text, ἤ, “or.”]

[Note: Col. 0225: The *m* in *fructum* has been erased by the corrector.]

He set before them another parable, saying: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field. But while people slept, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away. When the blade had grown and produced fruit, then the weeds also appeared. The servants of the householder came and said to him, ‘Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where then does it have weeds?’ But he said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’ The servants said to him, ‘Do you want us to go and gather them?’ But he said, ‘No, lest while gathering the weeds you uproot the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I shall say to the reapers, “Gather the weeds first and bind them into bundles to burn them; [Col. 0228] but gather the wheat into my barn.”’”

[Note: Col. 0225: *Seminabit* (“will sow”) for *seminavit* (“sowed”).]

[Note: Col. 0226: One of the two *t*s has been rubbed away by the corrector.]

[Note: Col. 0225: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἅμα καί, “together also.”]

[Note: Col. 0226: Here likewise one of the two *t*s has been rubbed away.]

[Note: Col. 0227: Here likewise one of the two *t*s has been rubbed away.]

He spoke another parable to them, saying: “The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field. Though it is indeed the least of all seeds, when it has grown, it is greater than all vegetables and becomes a tree, so that the birds of heaven come and dwell in its branches.”

He spoke another parable to them: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened.”

All these things Jesus spoke in parables to the crowds, and without parables he spoke nothing to them, so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “I shall open my mouth in parables; I shall utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”

[Note: Col. 0227: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐλάλησεν, “he spoke.”]

[Note: Col. 0228: *Eructuabo* (“I shall utter”) for *eructabo*.]

Then, having dismissed the crowds, Jesus came into the house. His disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.” He answered and said to them: “The one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man. The field is this world. The good seed are the children of the kingdom; the weeds are the children of the evil one. [Col. 0230] The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the consummation of the age, and the reapers are angels. Therefore, as the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so it shall be at the consummation of this age. The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all stumbling-blocks and those who commit iniquity, and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then the righteous shall shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.

“Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field, which a man finds and hides; and for joy over it he goes, sells all that he has, and buys that field. Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking fine pearls. Having found one precious pearl, he went and sold all that he had and bought it. Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net cast into the sea, which gathered fish of every kind. When it was full, they drew it ashore; and sitting down, they put the good into their vessels, but threw the bad outside. [Col. 0232] So it shall be at the consummation of the age: angels shall go out and separate the wicked from the midst of the righteous, and cast them into the furnace of fire. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

Jesus said to them, “Have you understood all these things?” They said to him, “Certainly, Lord.” But he said to them, “Therefore every scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old.”

And when Jesus had finished these parables, he went away from there. Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogues, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works? Is this not the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas? And are not all his sisters among us? Where then did this man get all these things?” And they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his own country.” And he did not perform many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

[Note: Col. 0230: In *praetiosam* (“precious”), the *e* has been rubbed away.]

[Note: Col. 0230: *Retiae* (“of a net”) for *reti* (“a net”).]

[Note: Col. 0231: *Scribae*, through scribal error, for *scriba*.]

[Note: Col. 0231: *Aput*, with *t* for *d*.]

At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus, and said to his servants, “Surely this is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works operate in him.”

[Note: Col. 0232: *Y* is used for *u*.]

[Col. 0234] For Herod had seized John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip. For John had said to him, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.” And though he wished to kill him, he feared the people, because they regarded him as a prophet. But on Herod’s birthday, Herodias’s daughter danced in the midst of the dining hall and pleased Herod. Therefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask of him. But she, prompted beforehand by her mother, said, “Give me here on a dish the head of John the Baptist.” And the king was grieved; yet because of the oath and because of those dining with him, he commanded it to be given. He sent and beheaded John in prison. His head was brought on a dish and given to the girl, and the girl brought it to her mother. His disciples came, took his body, and buried it; and coming, they reported it to Jesus.

[Note: Col. 0233: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἶπε, Δός, “she said, ‘Give.’”]

[Note: Col. 0233: After *juramentum* (“oath”), *autem* (“however”) is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis at the same place; *propter* (“because of”), διά, is added in Vercellensis, Veronensis, and Brixianus.]

Hearing this, Jesus withdrew from there in a boat [Col. 0236] to a deserted place apart. When the crowds heard it, they followed him on foot from the towns. Jesus went out, saw a great crowd, had compassion on them, and healed their sick. When evening came, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and the hour has already passed. Dismiss the crowds, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.” But Jesus said to them, “They have no need to go away. Give them something to eat yourselves.” They said to him, “We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish.” And Jesus said to them, “Bring them here to me.” After ordering the crowd to recline on the grass, he took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds. They all ate and were satisfied. They took up twelve full baskets of the fragments left over. Those who ate were about five thousand men, besides women and children.

Then he immediately ordered the disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of him across the water, [Col. 0238] until he had dismissed the crowds. Having dismissed the crowd, he went up the mountain alone to pray. When evening came, he was there alone. But the boat was being battered by waves in the middle of the sea, for the wind was contrary. In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking upon the sea. When his disciples saw him walking upon the sea, they were terrified, saying, “It is a phantom,” and they cried out from fear. But Jesus immediately spoke to them, saying, “Take courage; it is I. Do not be afraid.” Peter answered him, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you over the waters.” He said, “Come.” Peter descended from the boat and walked over the water in order to come to Jesus. But seeing the strong wind, he was afraid; and when he began to sink, he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me.” Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, seized him, and said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?” When he had gone up into the boat, the wind ceased. Those in the boat [Col. 0240] came and worshipped him, saying, “Truly, you are God’s Son.”

When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret. When the men of that place recognized him, they sent throughout that whole region and brought to him all who were ill. They begged him that they might only touch the fringe of his garment; and all who touched it were made well.

[Note: Col. 0235: The *a* in *saecutae* (“followed”) has been rubbed away.]

[Note: Col. 0238: In this space letters have been erased in the manuscript.]

[Note: Col. 0237: “Jesus” is added, in accordance with the Greek text, ὁ Ἰησοῦς.]

[Note: Col. 0237: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”]

[Note: Col. 0239: In the word *fimbriam* (“fringe”), after *f* a letter has been rubbed away, of which no trace remains.]

Then scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem came to Jesus, saying, “Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.” But he answered and said to them, “Why do you also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition? For God commanded, saying, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever curses father or mother shall surely die.’

[Note: Cols. 0239–0240: In *Hierosolymis* (“Jerusalem”), the first vowel was *y*, altered by the corrector, who erased its horns, so that it became *i*.]

[Note: Col. 0240: *Labant* (“they wash”), for *lavant*.]

[Note: Col. 0239: *Tuum* (“your”) is added, as also in the Greek text, σοῦ.]

“But you say, ‘Whoever says to father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might have received from me is an offering,” need not honor his father or mother.’ Thus you have made void the commandment [Col. 0242] of God because of your tradition. Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied well concerning you, saying: ‘This people draw near to me with their mouth and honor me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. In vain they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of men.’

“And having called the crowd to him, he said to them, ‘Hear and understand: not what enters into the mouth defiles a person, but what proceeds from the mouth—this defiles a person.’ Then his disciples came and said to him, ‘Do you know that the Pharisees, having heard this saying, were offended?’ But he answered and said, ‘Every plant which my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted. Leave them alone: they are blind guides of the blind. If a blind man offers guidance to a blind man, both fall into a pit.’ Peter answered and said to him, ‘Explain this parable to us.’ But Jesus said, ‘Are you still without understanding? Do you not understand that everything entering into the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled into the latrine? But the things proceeding from the mouth come out of the heart, and those defile [Col. 0244] a person. For from the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies. These are what defile a person; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person.’”

[Note: Col. 0241: So also the Greek text: Ἠσαΐας, “Isaiah,” following the Latin convention of rendering Greek Η by E.]

[Note: Cols. 0241–0242: In the word *coinquinat* (“defiles”), the *i* has been erased by the corrector, though it remains visible; likewise in the following occurrence.]

[Note: Col. 0242: Again, the letter *i* has been erased.]

[Note: Col. 0242: Again, the letter *i* has been erased.]

Jesus departed from there and withdrew to the region of Tyre and Sidon. And behold, a Canaanite woman who had come out from those borders cried to him, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David. My daughter is grievously tormented by a demon.” But he did not answer her a word. His disciples came and begged him, saying, “Dismiss her, because she cries after us.” But Jesus answered and said, “I was sent only to the sheep that have perished from the house of Israel.” But she came and worshipped him, saying, “Lord, help me.” He answered and said, “It is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to dogs.” But she said, “Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.” Then Jesus answered and said to her, “O woman, great is your faith; let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.

[Note: Col. 0244: In *Israhel*, the *d* has been erased; it had been written *Isdrahel*.]

When Jesus had gone from there, [Col. 0246] he came again beside the Sea of Galilee; and ascending the mountain, he sat there. Great crowds came to him, bringing with them the lame, blind, mute, disabled, and many others; they laid them at Jesus’ feet, and he healed them. Thus the crowds marvelled when they saw the mute speaking, the disabled healthy, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples to him and said, “I have compassion on this crowd, because they have now remained with me for three days and have nothing to eat. I do not wish to send them away fasting, lest they fail on the road.” His disciples said to him, “Where are we to get so many loaves in a wilderness, to satisfy so great a crowd?” Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few little fish.” He ordered the crowds to recline on the ground. Taking the seven loaves and the fish, Jesus gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples; and the disciples gave them to the crowds. They all ate and were satisfied. They took up seven full baskets of fragments left over. Those who had eaten [Col. 0248] were four thousand men, besides women and little children. Having dismissed the crowd, he entered the boat and came into the region of Magadan.

Pharisees and Sadducees came to him, testing him, and asked him to show them a sign from heaven. But he answered and said to them, “When evening comes, you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.’ And in the morning, ‘There will be a storm today, for the sky is red and gloomy.’ Hypocrites, you know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you cannot discern the signs of the times.

[Note: Col. 0246: The *d* in *Sdrahel* has been erased by the corrector.]

[Note: Col. 0246: *Quod* (“what”) for *quot* (“how many”), through scribal error.]

[Note: Col. 0247: “Hypocrites” is added, also in the Greek text, ὑποκριταί.]

“A wicked and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” And leaving them, he went away.

When his disciples had come across the water, they forgot to take bread. Jesus said to them, “See to it and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” But they were reasoning among themselves, saying, “It is because we have not taken bread.” Knowing this, Jesus said, “Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have not taken bread? Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves for the five [Col. 0250] thousand people, and how many baskets you took up? Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand people, and how many baskets you took up? How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread? Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” Then they understood that he had not said to beware of bread-leaven, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

[Note: Col. 0247: The letters *is* in *eis* (“them”) have been erased.]

[Note: Col. 0247: So also the Greek text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς, “but Jesus.”]

[Note: Col. 0250: *Quod* (“what”) for *quot* (“how many”), through scribal error.]

[Note: Col. 0249: So also the Greek text: τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους, “the seven loaves.”]

[Note: Col. 0250: *Quod* for *quot*.]

[Note: Col. 0249: So also the Greek text: εἶπε, “he said.”]

When Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, “Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?” They said, “Some say John the Baptist; others Elijah; others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.” Jesus said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus answered and said to him, “Blessed are you, Simon Barjona, because flesh and blood have not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I shall build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. I shall give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever [Col. 0252] you bind upon earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose upon earth shall be loosed in heaven.” Then he commanded his disciples to tell no one that he was Jesus the Christ.

From then on Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, scribes, and chief priests, be killed, and rise on the third day. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying, “Be gracious to yourself, Lord; this shall not happen to you.” But he turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan. You are a stumbling-block to me, because you do not set your mind on the things of God, but on those of men.” Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life because of me will find it. For what will it profit a person if he gains the whole world but suffers loss of his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life? For the Son of Man is going to come in the glory [Col. 0254] of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each person according to his deeds.

[Note: Col. 0250: *Interrogabit* (“he will ask”) for *interrogavit* (“he asked”).]

[Note: Col. 0249: *Me* (“me”) is added, as also in the Greek text, μέ.]

[Note: Col. 0250: *Rebelavit* for *revelavit* (“revealed”).]

[Note: Col. 0251: The Greek text has ἴλεώς σοι: “Be gracious to yourself.”]

[Note: Col. 0251: *Ad* for *at* (“but”).]

“Amen, I say to you, there are some standing here who shall not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.” After six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and led them apart up a high mountain. He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became white as snow. And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him. Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, let us make three tabernacles here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. And behold, a voice from the cloud saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.” Hearing this, the disciples fell on their faces and were exceedingly afraid. But Jesus came, touched them, and said, “Rise, and do not be afraid.” [Col. 0256] Raising their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone.

As they were descending from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, “Tell no one of this vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.” His disciples asked him, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?” Jesus answered and said to them, “Elijah indeed will come first and will restore all things. But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is to suffer from them.” Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.

[Note: Col. 0253: *Syo*, with ypsilon for *u*, which the scribe also uses elsewhere.]

[Note: Col. 0254: The *a* in *caeciderunt* (“fell”) has been erased.]

When he came to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling and saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is moon-struck and suffers badly. For he often falls into the fire, and sometimes into the water. I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him.” Jesus answered, “O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I endure you? Bring him here to me.” [Col. 0258] Jesus rebuked it, and immediately the demon came out of him; and the boy was healed from that hour.

Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, “Why could we not cast it out?” Jesus said to them, “Because of your unbelief. Amen, I say to you: if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you. But this kind is cast out by nothing except prayer and fasting.” While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of people; they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.” And they were greatly grieved.

When they came to Capernaum, those who collected the tribute came to Peter and said, “Does your teacher not pay the tribute?” And he said, “Yes.” When he entered the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take tribute or tax—from their sons or from strangers?” Peter said to him, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free. [Col. 0260] But lest we offend them, . . . . . . go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up. When you open its mouth, you will find in it a denarius; take it and give it to them for me and for yourself.”

[Note: Col. 0255: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐνίοτε, “sometimes.”]

[Note: Col. 0258: *Exibit* (“will come out”) for *exivit* (“came out”).]

[Note: Col. 0258: The final *m* in *futurum* is missing; nor is there a superscribed stroke indicating it.]

[Note: Col. 0259: Here letters and nearly half a line are missing in the manuscript.]

At that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who do you think is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” Jesus called a little child, set him in their midst, and said, “Amen, I say to you, unless you turn and become like little children, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven. Whoever therefore humbles himself like this little child will be greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

[Note: Col. 0259: *Humilaverit* ("will humble") for *humiliaverit* ("will have humbled").]

Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me. But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a millstone turned by an ass be hung around his neck and that he be drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe to this world because of stumbling-blocks. For stumbling-blocks must come; nevertheless, woe to the person through whom the stumbling-block comes. If your hand or foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it from you: it is better for you to enter into life disabled or lame than, having two hands or two feet, to be cast into eternal fire. [Col. 0262] And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it from you: it is better for you to enter into life with one eye than, having two eyes, to be cast into eternal fire.

“See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven. For the Son of Man comes to save what had perished. What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep, and one of them has strayed, does he not leave the ninety-nine in the mountains and go seek the one that has strayed? And if it happens that he finds it, amen, I say to you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not stray. So it is not the will before your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

“If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between yourself and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother. But if he does not hear you, take with you one or two more, so that by the mouth of two or three witnesses every [Col. 0264] word may stand. If he does not hear them, tell it to the church. But if he does not hear the church, let him be to you as a gentile and a tax collector. Amen, I say to you: whatever you bind upon earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose upon earth shall be loosed in heaven.

[Note: Col. 0260: *Clodum* (“lame”) for *claudum*.]

[Note: Col. 0261: *Homini* (“to a man”) is added, as also in the Greek text, ἀνθρώπῳ.]

“Again, amen, I say to you: if two of you agree on earth concerning any matter whatever which they ask, it shall be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in their midst.”

Then Peter approached him and said, “Lord, if my brother sins against me, how often shall I forgive him? Up to seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven. Therefore the kingdom of heaven has been likened to a king who came to settle accounts with his servants. When he began to reckon, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents. But since he did not have the means to repay, his master commanded him to be sold, together with his wife, children, and all that he had, and for the debt to be repaid. [Col. 0266] The servant therefore fell down and pleaded with his master, saying, ‘Lord, be patient with me, and I shall repay you everything.’ Moved with pity, the lord released that servant and forgave him the debt.

“But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii. Seizing him, he choked him, saying, ‘Repay what you owe.’ His fellow servant fell at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I shall repay you everything.’ But he refused; instead, he went away and put him into prison until he should repay the debt. When his fellow servants saw what was happening, they were greatly distressed. They came and reported to their lord all that had happened. Then his lord summoned him and said to him, ‘Wicked servant, I forgave you the whole debt, because you begged me. Ought you not then also to have had mercy upon your fellow servant, as I had mercy upon you?’ And his lord, being angry, handed him over to the torturers until he should repay the whole debt. So also will my heavenly Father do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts their sins.”

[Note: Col. 0263: “Amen” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἀμήν.]

[Note: Col. 0264: Thus.]

When Jesus had finished these sayings, [Col. 0268] he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan. Great crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to dismiss his wife for any cause whatever?” Jesus answered and said to them, “Have you not read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this reason a man shall leave father and mother and shall cleave to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh’? Thus they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no human being separate.” They said to him, “Why then did Moses command that a document of divorce be given and that she be dismissed?” He said to them, “Because of the hardness of your hearts Moses permitted you to dismiss your wives; but from the beginning it was not so. But I say to you that whoever dismisses his wife, except on account of fornication, and marries another commits adultery; and whoever marries a dismissed woman commits adultery.” His disciples said to him, “If the case of a man with a wife is thus, it is not expedient to marry.” [Col. 0270] But he said to them, “Not all receive this saying, but those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who were born thus from their mother’s womb; there are eunuchs made by people; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who can receive it, receive it.”

[Note: Col. 0268: Thus.]

[Note: Col. 0267: After *fecit* (“made”), *hominem* (“man”) is absent, also in the Greek text.]

[Note: Col. 0267: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας, “except on account of fornication.”]

[Note: Col. 0268: The final *m* has been rubbed away by the corrector.]

Then little children were brought to him, that he might lay hands upon them and pray. But his disciples rebuked them. Jesus said to them, “Allow the little children, and do not prevent them from coming to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” After laying hands on them, he departed from there.

And behold, someone came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do in order to have eternal life?” He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God. But if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to him, “Which ones?” Jesus said: “You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; honor your father and mother; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself.” The young man said [Col. 0272] to him, “I have kept all these things from my youth. What do I still lack?” Jesus said to him, “If you wish to be perfect, go, sell all that you possess and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” Upon hearing this, the young man went away sorrowful, for he had many possessions.

Jesus said to his disciples, “Amen, I say to you: a rich person shall enter the kingdom of heaven only with difficulty. Again I say to you: it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.” When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?” Looking at them, Jesus said, “With people this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” Peter then answered and said to him, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then shall there be for us?”

[Note: Col. 0270: Thus.]

Jesus said to them, “Amen, I say to you: you who have followed me, at the renewal, when the Son of Man sits upon the throne of his majesty, shall yourselves sit upon twelve thrones, judging [Col. 0274] the twelve tribes of Israel. And everyone who leaves house, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or fields because of my name shall receive a hundredfold and shall possess eternal life. But many who are first shall be last, and the last first.”

[Note: Col. 0274: The *d* in *Sdrahel* has been erased by the corrector.]

For the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard. Having agreed with the laborers on a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard. Going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace, and said to them, “Go also into my vineyard, and I will give you whatever is right.” And they went. Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hours, and did likewise. Going out also about the eleventh hour, he found others standing idle in the marketplace and said to them, “Why do you stand here idle all day?” They said to him, “Because no one has hired us.” He said to them, “Go also and work in my vineyard, and you shall receive what is right.”

When evening came, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward, “Call the laborers and pay them [Col. 0276] their wage, beginning with the last and ending with the first.” When those who had come about the eleventh hour arrived, they each received a denarius. But when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; yet they too each received a denarius. On receiving it, they murmured against the householder, saying, “These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden and heat of the day.” But he answered one of them: “Friend, I do you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius? Take what is yours and go. But I wish to give this last man the same as to you. Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with what is mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?” Thus the first shall be last, and the last first. For many are called, but few chosen.

And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside on the road and said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes; and they will condemn him to death and deliver him to the Gentiles to be mocked, [Col. 0278] scourged, and crucified; and on the third day he will rise.”

Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him with her sons, worshipping and asking something of him. He said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.” Jesus answered them, “You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup which I am about to drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?” They said to him, “We are able.” He said to them, “You shall indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized; but to sit at my right or left is not mine to give to you, but belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”

When the ten heard it, they were indignant at the two brothers. But Jesus called them to himself and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you; but whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave. For the Son of Man also came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many. . . . . .”

[Col. 0280] And as he went out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him. And behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!” But the crowd rebuked them, that they should be silent. Yet they cried out all the more, saying, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!” Jesus stopped and called them, saying to them, “What do you want me to do for you?” They said to him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.” [Col. 0282] Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes; and immediately they saw, and followed him.

And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came [Note: [Col. 0281] The text, as also the Greek text, adds *in*, εἰς.] into Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, Jesus then sent two disciples, saying to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find an ass tied, and a colt with her; loose them and bring them to me. And if anyone says anything to you, say that the Lord has need of them, and he will immediately send them. . . .”

Now this [Note: [Col. 0281] Before *was done*, the whole passage is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] was done, that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: “Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, your king comes to you, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and upon a colt, the foal of a beast under the yoke. . . .”

The disciples went and did as Jesus commanded them. They brought the ass and the colt, laid their garments upon him, and he sat upon him. And a very great crowd spread their garments on the road; others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road. [Col. 0284] And the crowds that went before and those that followed cried out, saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!” When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred, saying, “Who is this?” The crowds said, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee.”

And Jesus entered the temple of God, and cast out all who sold and bought in the temple; he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those who sold doves. And he said to them, “It is written: ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.” The blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them. But when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things which Jesus did, and the children crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they were indignant and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Certainly. Have you never read: ‘Out of the mouth [Note: [Col. 0283] The manuscript writes *infantiym*, employing, as elsewhere, *y* for *u*.] of infants and nursing children you have perfected praise’?” Leaving them, he went outside the city to Bethany, and rested there.

In the morning, returning to the city, he was hungry. [Col. 0286] Seeing a single fig tree by the road, he came to it and found nothing on it except leaves alone. And he said to it, “May fruit never grow from you again, for ever.” And immediately the fig tree withered. Seeing this, the disciples marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree wither immediately?” Jesus answered them, “Amen, I say to you: if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it will happen. And whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you shall receive.”

When he entered the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people came to him as he was teaching and said, “By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?” Jesus answered them, “I too will ask you one question; if you tell me it, I too will tell you by what authority I do these things. [Note: [Col. 0285] Thus also the Greek text, in the neuter gender: τὸ βάπτισμα, ‘the baptism.’] The baptism of John: whence was it—from heaven or from human beings?” They reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ we fear the crowds, for all held John [Col. 0288] to be a prophet.” Answering Jesus, they said, “We do not know.” He said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

“What do you think? A certain man had two sons. Going to the first, he said, ‘Son, go today and work in the vineyard [Note: [Col. 0287] After *vineyard*, *my* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.].’ But he answered, ‘I will not’; afterward, moved by repentance, he went. Going to the other, he said similarly. But he answered, ‘I go, sir,’ and did not go. Which of the two did the father’s will?” They said to him, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Amen, I say to you: tax collectors and prostitutes go before you into the kingdom of God. For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Yet you, though you saw it, did not afterward repent so as to believe him.

“Hear another parable. There was a certain householder who planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a winepress in it, and built [Col. 0290] a tower. He leased it to tenants and went abroad. When the season for fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to receive his fruits. But the tenants seized his servants: they beat one, killed another, and stoned another. Again he sent other servants, more than the first; and they did the same to them. Finally he sent to them his only-begotten son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’ But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.’ Seizing him, they cast him outside the vineyard and killed him. Therefore, when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?” They said to him, “He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will render him the fruits in their seasons.” Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner. This was done by the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’? Therefore I say to you that the kingdom of God shall be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruits. [Col. 0292] And whoever falls upon this stone will be broken; but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him.”

When the chief priests and Pharisees heard his parables, they knew that he spoke about them. Seeking to seize him, they feared the crowds, because they held him to be a prophet.

Jesus again answered them in parables, saying, “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast for his son. He sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding, but they would not come. Again he sent other servants, saying, ‘Tell those invited: Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and fattened cattle have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding.’ But they disregarded it and went away, one to his field and another to his business. The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them. When the king [Note: [Col. 0291] *That one* is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐκεῖνος, which the Veronese manuscript omits.] heard this, he was angry; and, sending [Note: [Col. 0291] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τὸ στράτευμα, ‘the army.’] his army, he destroyed those murderers and burned their city. Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the outlets of the roads, and invite to the wedding whomever you find.’ Those servants went out into the roads and gathered [Col. 0294] all whom they found, both bad and good, and the wedding feast was filled with guests reclining at table.

“But when the king entered to see the guests reclining at table, he saw there a man not clothed in [Note: [Col. 0293] Thus throughout the Old Latin, tenacious of its words and here and elsewhere rigidly following the syntax of the Greek text, which has ἔνδυμα, ‘a garment.’] a wedding garment. He said to him, ‘Friend, how did you enter here without a wedding garment?’ But he was speechless. Then the king said to the attendants, ‘Bind his feet and hands, take him away, and cast him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’ For many are called, but few chosen.”

Then the Pharisees went away and took counsel how they might ensnare him in speech. They sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful, that you teach the way of God in truth, and that you are concerned for no one, for you do not regard human persons.
