Tell us, therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?” But Jesus, knowing their malice, said, “Why do you test me, hypocrites? Show me the tribute denarius.” They brought him a denarius. He said to them, “Whose image is this, and whose inscription?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.” Then Jesus said to them, [Col. 0296] “Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” Hearing this, they marveled; and leaving him, went away.

On that day Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying, “Teacher, Moses said: ‘If anyone dies without having children, his brother shall take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’ Now there were among us seven brothers. The first, having taken a wife, died; and, having no offspring, left his wife to his brother. Likewise the second and the third, down to the seventh. Last of all, the woman also died. Therefore, in the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be? For all had her.” Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, knowing neither the Scriptures nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven. But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was said to you by God: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead but of the living.” Hearing this, the crowds were astonished at his teaching.

But the Pharisees, hearing [Col. 0298] that he had silenced the Sadducees, assembled together [Note: [Col. 0297] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek: ἐπ’ αὐτόν, ‘against him’ / ‘to him’.] to him; and one of them, a doctor of the law, questioned him, testing him [Note: [Col. 0297] *And saying* is added, also in the Greek text: καὶ λέγων.] and saying, “Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?” Jesus said to him, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the first and greatest commandment. The second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ On these two commandments hang the whole law and the prophets.”

When the Pharisees had assembled, Jesus questioned them, saying, “What do you think concerning the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “David’s.” Jesus said to them, “How then does David, in the spirit, call him his Lord, saying: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies as the footstool of your feet’? If David [Note: [Col. 0297] *In the spirit* is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν πνεύματι.] in the spirit calls him Lord, how is he his son?” And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day onward to question him further.

Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples, saying, “The scribes and Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat. Therefore, whatever they tell you, . . . . observe and do; [Col. 0300] but do not do according to their works, for they say and do not do. For they bind heavy, unbearable burdens and lay them on people’s shoulders, but they are unwilling to move them with their own finger. They do all their works to be seen by human beings. For they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge the fringes of their garments. They love the first places at banquets, the chief seats in synagogues, greetings in the marketplace, and to be called Rabbi by people. But you are not to be called Rabbi, for one is your teacher, and all of you are brothers. And call no one your father on earth, for one is your Father, who is in heaven. Neither be called teachers, for one is your teacher, Christ. Whoever is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whoever exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who devour widows’ houses under the pretext of prolonged prayer; therefore you shall receive a more severe condemnation. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven before people. For you neither enter yourselves nor permit those entering to enter. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel sea and land to make one proselyte; [Col. 0302] and when he has become one, you make him twice as much a child of Gehenna as yourselves.

“Woe to you, blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound.’ Fools and blind men! For which is greater: the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold? And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift which is upon it is bound.’ Fools and blind men! For which is greater: the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift? Therefore, whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything upon it. Whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by him who dwells in it. Whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by him who sits upon it.

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left aside the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These things you ought to have done, without omitting those. Blind guides, straining out a gnat but swallowing a camel! Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who cleanse the outside of cup and dish, but within [Col. 0304] are full of robbery and injustice. Blind Pharisee, first cleanse the inside of cup and dish, that the outside also may become clean.

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful to people, but inwardly are full of the bones of the dead and every impurity. So also you outwardly appear righteous to people, but inwardly are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, saying, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets.’ Thus you testify against yourselves that you are sons of those who killed the prophets. You too fill up the measure of your fathers. Serpents, offspring of vipers! How will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?

“Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city, that upon you may come all righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you [Col. 0306] killed between the temple and the altar. Amen, I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.

“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wished to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not! Behold, your house shall be left to you desolate. For I tell you, [Note: [Col. 0305] *Because* is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὅτι.] that you will not see me henceforth until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

Jesus went out from the temple and was departing. His disciples came to point out to him the buildings of the temple. But Jesus said to them, “Do you see all these things? Amen, I say to you, not one stone shall be left here upon another which will not be thrown down.”

As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the consummation of the age?” Jesus answered them, “Take care that no one deceives you. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many. You will hear of wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed; [Col. 0308] for all these things must happen, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there will be pestilences, famines, and earthquakes in various places. But all these are the beginning of birth-pains. Then they will hand you over to tribulations, and to assemblies, and to authorities; you will stand before kings, and they will kill you; and you will be hated by all nations for my name’s sake. Then many will fall away, betray one another, and hate one another. Many false prophets will arise and deceive many. And because lawlessness will increase, the love of many will grow cold. But the one who endures to the end shall be saved. This gospel of the kingdom shall be proclaimed in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

“Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation [Note: [Col. 0307] The Greek text is translated here somewhat awkwardly: τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Δανιήλ τοῦ προφήτου, ἑστώς. For both τὸ ῥηθέν, ‘that which was spoken,’ and ἑστώς, ‘standing,’ refer to the preceding neuter βδέλυγμα, which means ‘abomination.’] spoken of through Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—then those in Judaea must flee to the mountains. Let one on the housetop not come down to take anything from his house; and let one in the field not return to take his garment. Woe to those who are pregnant and nursing in those days! Pray that your flight may not occur in winter or on a Sabbath. For then there will be great tribulation, [Col. 0310] such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever shall be. And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days shall be shortened. Then, if anyone says to you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ,’ or ‘There,’ do not believe it. For false Christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect. Behold, I have told you beforehand. If they say to you, ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it. For as lightning comes from the east and appears as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man. Wherever the body is, there the eagles will gather.

[Note: [Col. 0309] Before *eagles*, *and* is absent also in the Greek text.] And immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun shall be darkened, the moon shall not give its light, the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven shall be shaken. Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven; and then all tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with great power and glory. He will send his angels with a trumpet and a loud voice, and they will gather [Col. 0312] his elect from the four winds, from the extremities of the heavens to their ends.

“Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and leaves have come forth, you know that summer is near. So also, when you see all these things happening, know that he is near, at the doors. Amen, I say to you, this generation shall not pass away until all things happen. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

“But concerning that day and hour no one knows—not even the angels of heaven [Note: [Col. 0311] *Nor the Son* is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, from Mark.] nor the Son, but my Father alone. As it was in the days of Noah, so will be the coming of the Son of Man. For as they were in the days [Note: [Col. 0311] *Those* is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐκείναις.] before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and they did not know until the flood came and destroyed them all, so will be the coming of the Son of Man. . . . .

“Then two will be in the field: one will be taken, and one left. Two women will be grinding at one mill: one will be taken, and the other left. [Note: [Col. 0311] This taking is likewise found in Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek: Δύο ἐπὶ κλίνης μιᾶς, εἷς παραλαμβάνεται, καὶ εἷς ἀφίεται, ‘Two upon one bed: one is taken, and one is left,’ from Luke. It is also read by Chrysostom, Juvencus, Hilary, the Saxon version, and many Latin codices in Luke cited by Brugensis, as well as several Greek manuscripts cited by Stephanus and Mill.] Two in one bed: one will be taken, and the other left. Watch therefore, [Col. 0314] because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming. But know this: if the householder knew at what hour the thief [Note: [Col. 0313] Thus also the Greek text: ἔρχεται, ‘comes.’] was coming, he would certainly watch and would not allow his house to be broken into. Therefore you too be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not know.

“Who, then, is the faithful and prudent servant whom his master set over his household to give them food at the proper time? Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, finds doing so. Amen, I say to you, he will set him over all his possessions. But if that wicked servant says in his heart, ‘My master delays his coming,’ and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eats and drinks with drunkards, that servant’s master will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know; he will cut him in pieces and assign his portion with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

“Then the kingdom of heaven shall be like ten virgins, who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride. Five of them were prudent, and five foolish. But the five foolish, having taken their lamps, [Note: [Col. 0313] Thus also the Greek text: ἔρχεται, ‘comes.’] did not take oil with them; [Col. 0316] whereas the prudent took oil in their vessels with their lamps. While the bridegroom delayed, all nodded off and slept. But at midnight a cry arose: ‘Behold, the bridegroom comes; go out to meet him!’ Then all those virgins arose and trimmed their lamps. The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’ The wise answered, ‘Perhaps there will not be enough for us and you; go instead to the sellers and buy for yourselves.’ While they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and those who were ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut. Later the other [Note: [Col. 0315] Before *the other*, *and* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] virgins came, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’ But he answered, ‘Amen, I say to you, I do not know you.’ Watch therefore, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

“For it is like a man going abroad, who called his servants and entrusted his property to them. To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one—to each according to his own ability—and went away. Immediately the one who had received five talents went and traded [Col. 0318] with them, and gained another five talents. Likewise the one who had received two gained another two. But the one who had received one talent went away, dug in the earth, and hid his master’s money. After a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them. The one who had received five talents came forward and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Master, you entrusted five talents to me; behold, I have gained another five talents.’ His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you were faithful over a little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.’ The one who had received two talents also came forward and said, ‘Master, you entrusted two talents to me; behold, I have gained another two talents.’ His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you were faithful over a little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.’

“The one who had received one talent also came forward and said, ‘Master, I know you: you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter. Fearing you, I went away and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’ But his master answered him, ‘Wicked and slothful servant! You knew that I reap where I do not sow and gather where I did not scatter. Therefore you ought to have deposited my money with bankers, and when I came [Col. 0320] I should certainly have received what was mine with interest. Take the talent from him, then, and give it to the one who has ten talents. For to everyone who has, more will be given and he will abound; but from the one who has not, even what he seems to have shall be taken away. Cast the useless servant into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. . . .

“When the Son of Man comes in his majesty, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his majesty. Before him [Note: [Col. 0320] In the particular Greek manuscript, it is absent in the word *shall be gathered*.] all nations will be gathered, and he will separate them from one another as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. He will place [Note: [Col. 0319] After *sheep*, *indeed* is absent; likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] the sheep on his right and the goats on his left. Then the king will say to those on his right: ‘Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you received me; naked and you clothed me; I was sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me.’ Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, [Col. 0322] or thirsty and give you drink? When did we see you a stranger and receive you, or naked and clothe you? Or when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’ The king will answer them, ‘Amen, I say to you: insofar as you did it to one of these least brothers of mine, you did it to me.’

“Then he will say also to those on his left: ‘Depart from me, accursed ones, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry and you did not give me food; I was thirsty and you did not give me drink; I was a stranger and you did not receive me; naked and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.’ Then they too will answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and not serve you?’ Then he will answer them: ‘Amen, I say to you: insofar as you did not do it to one of these least ones, neither did you do it to me.’ And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

[Col. 0324] And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, that he said to his disciples, “You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of Man will be delivered up to be crucified.”

Then the chief priests, scribes, and elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the chief priest, who was called Caiaphas. They took counsel to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him. But they said, “Not during the feast, lest there be a disturbance among the people.”

Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, a woman came to him with an alabaster vessel of costly ointment and poured it upon [Note: [Col. 0323] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου αὐτοῦ, ‘his head as he reclined.’] his head as he reclined.

His disciples, seeing this, were indignant, saying, “Why this waste? For this could have been sold for a high price and given to the poor.” Jesus, knowing this, said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a good work to me. You always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.

“For by pouring this ointment upon my body, she did it for my burial.

“Amen, I say to you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her.” [Col. 0326] Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests and said to them, “What are you willing to give me, and I will deliver him to you?” They fixed for him thirty pieces of silver. From that time he sought an opportunity to deliver him up.

On the first day of unleavened bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him, “Where do you wish us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?” [Note: [Col. 0325] Thus also the Greek text: ὁ δέ, ‘but he.’] But he said, “Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, ‘The Teacher says: My time is near; I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.’” The disciples did as Jesus commanded them and prepared the Passover.

When evening came, Jesus reclined at table with the twelve disciples. As they were eating, he said, “Amen, I say to you: one of you will deliver me up.” Greatly distressed, they began each to say, “Surely it is not I, Lord?” He answered, “The one who dips his hand with me in the dish will deliver me up. The Son of Man indeed goes as it is written concerning him; but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is delivered up. It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.” Judas answered, [Note: [Col. 0325] Greek text: ὁ παραδιδούς, ‘the one delivering up.’] who was about to deliver him up, [Col. 0328] saying, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” Jesus said to him, “You have said so.”

As they were dining, Jesus took bread; and after blessing it, broke it and gave it to his disciples, saying, “Take and eat; for this is my body.” Taking the cup, he gave thanks and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you. For this is my blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. But I tell you, I shall not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.”

And when the hymn had been sung, they went out to the Mount of Olives. Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will take offence at me on this night. For it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’ But after I have risen, I will go before you into Galilee.” Peter answered and said to him, “Even if all are offended because of you, I shall never be offended.” Jesus said to him, “Amen, I tell you: on this night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.” Peter said to him, “Even if I must die with you, [Col. 0330] I shall not deny you.” And all the disciples said likewise.

Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane [Note: Codex Cantabrigiensis: Γεθσαμανεί, “Gethsemane”], and said to his disciples, “Sit here while I go there to pray.” And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, he began to be sorrowful and distressed. Then Jesus said to them, “My soul is sorrowful unto death; remain here and keep watch with me.” And going a little farther, he fell upon his face, praying and saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.” Then he came to his disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “So, could you not keep watch with me for one hour? Keep watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

Again, a second time, he went away and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass from me unless I drink it, your will be done.” And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy. Leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words. Then he came to his disciples and said to them, “Sleep now and take your rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near [Col. 0332], and the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of sinners. Rise; let us go. Behold, he who delivers me up has drawn near.”

And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the Twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people. Now he who delivered him up gave them a sign, saying, “Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him.” And immediately, approaching Jesus, he said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed him. But Jesus said to him, “Friend, for what have you come?” Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus, and seized him. And one of those who was with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, and struck [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐπάταξεν, “he struck”] the servant of the chief priest and cut off [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἀφεῖλεν, “and removed/cut off”] his ear. Then Jesus said to him, “Return your sword to its place. For all who take up the sword will perish by the sword. Or do you think that I cannot ask my Father, and he will provide me with more than twelve legions of angels? [Note: After *mihi*, “to me,” *modo*, “now,” is absent, also in the Greek text.] How then will the Scriptures of the Prophets be fulfilled, that it must happen in this way?”

At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs [Col. 0334], to seize me? Day after day I sat among you teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But all this has happened in order that the Scriptures of the Prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him and fled.

But those who had seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas, the chief priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered. Peter, however, followed him from a distance as far as the house of the chief priest. And, entering inside, he sat with the attendants in order to see the outcome. Now the chief priests and elders and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, and found none.

And though many false witnesses came forward, they found no charge. At last two false witnesses came and said [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἠκούσαμεν αὐτοῦ λέγοντος, “we heard him saying”], “We heard this man say, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and build it again after three days.’” And the chief priest rose and said to him, “Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you?” But Jesus was silent. And the chief priest answered [Note: The text adds *respondens*, “answering,” as also does the Greek text: ἀποκριθείς] and said to him, “I adjure you by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.” Jesus said to him, “You have said it. Yet I tell you: henceforth you will see the Son of Man seated [Col. 0336] at the right hand of power [Note: After *virtutis*, “of power,” *Dei*, “of God,” is absent also in the Greek text], and coming upon the clouds of heaven.”

Then the chief priest tore his garments, saying:

“He has blasphemed. What further need have we of witnesses? Behold, now you have heard his blasphemy [Note: The text adds *ejus*, “his,” as does the Greek text: αὐτοῦ]. What do you think?” They answered and said, “He is deserving of death.” Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists; others slapped him on the face, saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?”

But Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and one of the maidservants came to him, saying, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.” But he denied it before them all, saying, “I do not know what you are saying.” As he went out [Note: So also the Greek text: ἐξελθόντα, “having gone out”] to the gate, another woman saw him and said to those who were there, “This man also was with Jesus the Nazarene.” Again he denied it with an oath, saying, “I do not know the man.” A little later those standing there came up and said to Peter, “Surely you also are one of them, for your speech makes you plain.” Then he began to curse and to swear that he did not know the man. And immediately a cock crowed. Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which he had said to him [Note: The text adds *ei*, “to him,” as also the Greek text: αὐτῷ]: “Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.” And he went out [Col. 0338] and wept bitterly.

When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus in order to put him to death. And they bound him, led him away, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor. Then Judas, who had betrayed him, seeing that he had been led to judgment, was moved by repentance and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, saying, “I have sinned by delivering up innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”

And throwing the silver pieces into the temple, he departed; and going away, he hanged himself. Then the chief priests, taking the silver pieces, said, “It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because they are the price of blood.” And having taken counsel, they bought with them the potter’s field as a burial-place for strangers. Therefore that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day. Then was fulfilled what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying: “And they took the thirty pieces of silver, [Col. 0340] the price of the one whose price was set, whom they had appraised from among the children of Israel, and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me.”

Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “You say so.”

And while he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then he said to him, “Do you not hear how many things they testify against you?” And he did not answer him a single [Note: Before *ullum*, “any/single,” *ad*, “to,” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis] word, so that the governor marvelled greatly.

Now at the festival the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner whom they wished. They had [Note: So also the Greek text: εἶχον, “they had”] at that time a notable prisoner called Barabbas. Therefore, when they had assembled, Pilate said, “Whom do you wish me to release to you: Barabbas or Jesus who is called Christ?” For he knew that they had delivered him up through envy. [Note: From here through verse 42 of this chapter, everything is mutilated in the Gothic version.]

While he was sitting on the tribunal, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man; for I have suffered much today in a dream because of him.” But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas, but to destroy Jesus. Pilate the governor answered and said to them, “Which of the two do you wish me to release [Note: So also the Greek text: ἀπολύω, “I release”] to you?” And they said, “Barabbas” [Note: So also the Greek text: Βαραββᾶν, “Barabbas”]. Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?” They all said to him, “Let him be crucified.” The governor said to them, “For what evil has he done?” But they cried out all the more, saying, “Let him be crucified.”

Pilate, seeing that he accomplished nothing, but that rather a disturbance was arising, took water and washed his hands before the people, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; see to it yourselves.” And all the people answered and said, “His blood be upon us and upon our children.” Then he released Barabbas to them; but, having scourged Jesus, he delivered him over to them to be crucified.

Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around him. And stripping him, they clothed him in a purple garment [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἐνδύσαντες ἱμάτιον πορφυροῦν, “and clothing him in a purple garment”], and put a scarlet cloak around him. Plaiting a crown of thorns, they placed it upon his head and put a reed in his right hand. Then, falling at his feet, they mocked him, saying, “Greetings, King of the Jews.” And spitting upon him, they took the reed and struck his head. After they had mocked him, they took off the cloak, clothed him in his own garments, and led him away to crucify him.

As they went out, they found a man of Cyrene named Simon; they compelled him to carry [Col. 0344] his cross. And coming to a place called Golgotha, that is, the place of Calvary, they gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink. And when he had tasted it, he would not drink. After they had crucified him, they divided his garments by casting lots. And sitting down, they kept watch over him there. They placed above his head the written charge against him: “This is Jesus, King of the Jews.” Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left.

Those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads and saying, “You who destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days, save yourself. If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.” Likewise the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes, elders [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ Φαρισαίων, “and Pharisees”], and Pharisees, said, “He saved others; he cannot save himself. If he is King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him. He trusts in God; let him now deliver him, if he wants him [Note: So also the Greek text: αὐτόν, “him”]. For he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’” [Col. 0346] The robbers also who had been crucified with him reproached him in the same way.

Now from the sixth hour darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour. And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” But some of those standing there, hearing it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.” Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink. But the others said, “Leave him; let us see whether [Note: In accordance with the Greek text: εἰ, “whether/if”] Elijah comes to save him.” But Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, gave up his spirit.

And behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom; the earth shook, rocks were split, tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep arose. And coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.

Now the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things happening, were greatly afraid [Col. 0348], saying, “Truly this man is the Son of God.” There were also many women there, watching from a distance [Note: So Codex Cantabrigiensis Latin and the Greek text: θεωροῦσαι, “watching”]; they had followed Jesus from Galilee and ministered to him. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

When evening came, a certain rich man from Arimathea [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἀριμαθείας, “of Arimathea”] named Joseph came; he too was a disciple of Jesus. He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered the body to be given. Taking the body of Jesus, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth and placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out of the rock. Rolling a great stone against the door of the tomb, he went away. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.

On the next day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate, saying, “Lord, we remember that that deceiver said while still alive, ‘After the third day I shall rise.’ Therefore command that the tomb be guarded until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come and steal him and say to the people, ‘He has risen from the dead’; and the last error will be worse than the first.” Pilate said to them, “[Col. 0350] You have guards [Note: So Codex Cantabrigiensis Latin and Greek: φύλακας, “guards”]; go and guard it as you know how.” So they went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone with the guards.

Now late on the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb. And behold, there was a great earthquake. For an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and came and rolled the stone away from the entrance, and sat upon it. His appearance was like lightning, and his garments were white [Note: The text adds *candida*, “white,” as does the Greek text: λευκόν, “white garment”] as snow.

For fear of him the guards were shaken and became like dead men. But the angel answered and said to the women, “Do not be afraid. For I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord was laid. And go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead; and behold, he goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he told you.” And they quickly departed from the tomb with fear and great joy, running to report it to the disciples.

But as they went away to report it to his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings.” They came near, took hold of his feet, and worshipped him. Then Jesus said to them:

[Col. 0352] “Do not be afraid. Go, report to my brothers that they are to go into Galilee, and there they will see me.” When they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had happened. And having assembled with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers, saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole him while we were asleep.’ And if this is heard by the governor, we will persuade him and keep you safe.” So they took the money and did as they had been instructed. And this report has been spread among the Jews to this day.

But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain which Jesus had appointed for them. And seeing him, they worshipped him; but some doubted. And Jesus came near and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Therefore go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I commanded you. And behold, I am with you all days, until the consummation of the age.” Amen [Note: They add “Amen,” as does the Greek text, Ἀμήν. This certainly does not belong to Matthew, but to the Church, declaring its assent by this word to this Gospel, as to the others.].

[Col. 0351] THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MATTHEW ENDS. — [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Εὐαγγέλιον κατὰ Ματθαῖον ἐτελέσθη, ἄρχεται Εὐαγγέλιον κατὰ Ἰωάννην: “The Gospel according to Matthew has been completed; the Gospel according to John begins.”] THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO JOHN BEGINS.

THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO JOHN BEGINS.

[Col. 0353]

CODEX VERCELLENSIS.

[Col. 0353]

CHAPTER ONE.

[Col. 0353]

1. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. 2. This one was in the beginning 3. with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made. What was made 4. was life in him [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐστίν, “is”], and the life was the light of humankind. 5. And the light shines in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. [Col. 0353] 6. There was a man sent from God, whose name was 7. John. He came as a witness, to bear witness concerning the light, so that all might believe through 8. him. He was not the light, but came to bear witness concerning the light. 9. There was the true light, which enlightens every person coming into this world. 10. In this worl . . . . . [Col. 0355] and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him. 11. He came into his own, and his own did not receive him. 12. But to all who received him, he gave authority to become children of God, to those who believe in his name: 13. who were born not of bloods, nor of the will of flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God. 14. And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us; and we saw his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth. 15. John testifies concerning him [Note: Gat.: “testifies from himself . . . was made, who was before.” Mm.: “and I did not know him, because.” Vulgate: “testifies concerning him . . . was made, because he was before.”], and cries out, saying, “This is he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has been made before me, because he was before me.’” 16. Because [Note: So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὅτι, “because.” From this point—that is, from ἐλάβομεν, “we received”—through the words Ῥαββὶ, ὅς, “Rabbi, who,” in chapter III, verse 26, all is absent in Codex Cantabrigiensis Greek, and in Codex Cantabrigiensis Latin through verse 16.] from his fullness [Col. 0355] we all received grace for 17. grace. For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. 18. No one has ever seen God [Note: Gat.: “ever, except the only-begotten.” Mm.: “ever; except the only-begotten [Col. 0356] Son alone, who is.” Vulgate: “ever; the only-begotten Son, who is.”]: the only Son alone, in the Father’s bosom, has himself made him known. 19. And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to him to ask him, 20. “Who are you?” And he confessed and did not deny; indeed, he confessed: “I am not the Christ.” 21. And they questioned him again: “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “What then? Are you the Prophet?” And he answered, “No.” 22. Then they said to him, “Tell us, then: who are you, so that we may give an answer [Col. 0357] to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?” 23. He answered, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.” 24. And those who had been sent were from the Pharisees [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “And those who had come from the Pharisees questioned him.” Vulgate: “And those who had been sent were from the Pharisees. And they questioned him.”]. 25. The disciples and Levites said to him, “Why, then, do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” 26. John answered them, saying, “I baptize you in water unto repentance [Note: Gat.: “I baptize you in.” Vulgate: “I baptize in.”]; but one stands in your midst whom you do not know. 27. He comes after me and has been made before me; I am not worthy to loosen the strap of his sandal [Note: Gat.: “worthy to loosen the strap of his sandals.” Mm.: “worthy that I should loosen the strap of his sandal.” Vulgate: “worthy that I should loosen the strap of his sandal.”].” 28. These things happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

29. On the next day he saw [Col. 0357] Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God; behold, he who takes away the sin of the world. 30. This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who has been made before me, because he was before me’ [Note: Gat.: “who was before.” Vulgate: “because he was before.”]. 31. And I did not know him; but in order that he might be revealed in Israel [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “that he might be revealed in Israel.” Vulgate: “that he might be revealed in Israel.”], I therefore came baptizing in water.” 32. And John bore testimony, saying, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it remained upon him. 33. And I did not know him; but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘He upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining, he is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ 34. And I have seen and borne testimony [Col. 0359] that this is the chosen Son of God.”

35. The next day John was again standing with two of his disciples. 36. And looking upon Jesus as he walked, he said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, behold, he who takes away the sin of the world.” 37. The two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus. 38. Jesus turned and, seeing them following him [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “seeing them following, he says.” Vulgate: “seeing them following him, he says.”], said to them, “What do you seek?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which translated means “Teacher”), “where are you staying?” 39. He said to them, “Come and see.” Therefore they came and saw where he was staying, and remained with him that day; now it was about the tenth hour. 40. Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who had heard [Col. 0359] John and followed him. 41. He first found his own brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which translated is “Christ”) [Note: Mm.: “he first found his brother . . . Messiah, which is called Christ.” Vulgate: “he first found his brother . . . Messiah (which translated is Christ).”]. 42. And he brought him to Jesus. Looking upon him, Jesus said, “You are Simon, son of John [Note: Gat.: “son of Johna.” Mm.: “son of John.” Vulgate: “son of Jona.”]; you will be called Cephas,” which translated is “Peter.” 43. On the next day he wished to go out into Galilee and found Philip. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.” 44. Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. 45. Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found him of whom Moses wrote in the law, and the Prophets [Note: Gat.: “and the Prophecies.” Mm.: “and the Prophets.” Vulgate: “and the Prophets.”]: Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth.” 46. Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said to him [Col. 0361], “Come and see.” 47. Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him and said of Nathanael, “Behold, truly an Israelite [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “Behold, an Israelite.” Vulgate: “Behold, truly an Israelite.”], in whom there is no deceit.” 48. Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered and said to him, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.” 49. Nathanael answered him and said, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel.” 50. Jesus answered and said to him, “Because I said to you, ‘I saw you when you were under the fig tree,’ do you believe? You will see greater things than these.” 51. And he said to them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man [Note: Cat. and Mm.: “descending to the Son of Man.” Vulgate: “descending upon the Son of Man.”].

CHAPTER II.

1. And on the third day [Col. 0361] a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee [Note: Gat.: “In Chanaan.” Vulgate: “In Cana.”], and Jesus’ mother had been invited there. 2. Jesus and his disciples too had been invited to the wedding. 3. And they had no wine, because the wine for the wedding had been exhausted. Then his mother said to Jesus, “They have no wine.” 4. Jesus said to her, “What is that to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.” 5. His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he tells you, do it.” 6. Now there were six stone water-jars there, according to the Jewish purification custom, holding two or three measures each. 7. Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim. 8. Jesus said to them, “Draw some out and carry it to the master of the banquet.” So they drew it out and brought it. [Col. 0363] 9. When the master of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine—and did not know where it had come from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew—and saw what had been done, he marvelled and called the bridegroom. 10. He said to him, “Every person puts out the good wine first; and when people have become drunk, that which is inferior. But you have kept the good wine until now.” 11. Jesus performed this as the beginning of signs [Note: Mm.: “the first of signs.” Vulgate: “the beginning of signs.”] in Cana of Galilee; he revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.

12. After this he went down to Capernaum, he and his mother and brothers; and they remained there not many days [Note: So also the Greek text: οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας, “not many days”]. 13. The Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem [Col. 0363]. 14. He found in the temple those selling sheep, oxen, and doves, and money-changers seated there. 15. Making something like a whip of cords, he drove them all out of the temple, including the sheep, oxen, and doves; he poured out the money [Note: So the Ethiopic version and Origen: τὰ κέρματα, “the coins”] of the money-changers and overturned their tables. 16. To those who sold doves he said, “Take these things away from here, and do not make my Father’s house a house of trade.” 17. Then his disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house has consumed me.” 18. Therefore the Jews answered and said to him, “What sign do you show us, since you do these things?” 19. Jesus answered and said to them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it again.” [Note: St Ambrose, in *On the Institution of a Virgin*, book 1, chapter 12, p. 266, reads as Vercelli: “Destroy the temple, and in three days I will raise it again.” So also in *On Faith*, book 3, chapter 2, p. 499, and *Letters*, class 2, p. 1098. See also St Augustine, *City of God*, book 16, chapter 41.] [Col. 0365] 20. The Jews said, “This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it again in three days?” 21. But he spoke about the temple of his body. 22. Therefore, after he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus had spoken.

23. While Jesus was in Jerusalem at the Passover, on the feast day, many believed in his name, seeing the signs that he was doing. 24. But Jesus did not entrust himself to them, because he knew all persons, 25. and because he did not need anyone to testify concerning a person [Note: Gat.: “that anyone should testify.” Mm.: “that testimony.” Vulgate: “that someone should testify.”], for he himself knew what was in a human being.

CHAPTER III.

1. There was [Col. 0365] a man from the Pharisees whose name was Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. 2. He came to Jesus by night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; for no one can do these signs which you do unless God is with him.” 3. Jesus answered and said to him, “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless someone is born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” [Note: Gat.: “unless one has been born.” Mm.: “unless one has been born again.” Vulgate: “unless anyone has been born again.”] 4. Nicodem . . . said to him, “How can a person be born when old? Can a person enter again into his mother’s womb and be born?” [Note: Gat.: “into his mother’s womb . . . and be born again.” Mm.: “into the mother’s womb and be born.” Vulgate: “into his mother’s womb . . . and be born again.”] 5. Jesus answered, “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless someone is born again of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot en . . . . . . . . . . . ter into the kingdom [Col. 0367] 6. of God. What is born of flesh is fle . . h, because it is born of flesh; and what is born of the Spirit [Note: After *Spiritu*, “Spirit,” *sancto*, “holy,” is absent also in the Greek text] is spirit, because God is spirit, and is born from God. 7. Do not marvel that I told you: you must be born again. 8. The Spirit blows where he wills, and you hear his voice, but you do not know whence he comes or where he goes. So is everyone who is born again of water [Note: Mm.: “born of water, the Holy Spirit.” Vulgate: “born of the Spirit”] and the Spirit.” 9. Nicodemus answered and said to him, “How can these things happen?” 10. Jesus answered and said, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and do not know these things? 11. Amen, amen, I tell you: we speak what we know, and testify to what we have seen [Note: Mm.: “we testify to what we see.” Vulgate: “we testify to what we have seen”], yet you do not receive our testimony. 12. If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? How [Col. 0367] if I say: 13. No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in 14. heaven. And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness [Note: Mm.: “in the solitude.” Vulgate: “in the desert”], so must the Son 15. of Man be lifted up, that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life. 16. For God so loved this world [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “this world . . . that everyone.” Vulgate: “the world . . . that everyone”] that he gave his only Son, that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life. 17. For God did not send his Son into the world [Note: Gat.: “into this world, to judge.” Mm.: “into this world.” Vulgate: “into the world, to judge”] to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him. 18. Therefore the one who believes in him is not judged [Note: Mm.: “will not be judged.” Vulgate: “is not judged”]; but the one who does not believe has already been judged [Col. 0369], because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God. 19. And this is the judgment: that the light came into this world, and people loved darkness rather than light, for their works were evil. 20. Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his works be exposed. 21. But the one who does the truth comes to the light, that his work may be made manifest, because it has been done in God.

22. After these things Jesus and his disciples went out into the land of Judea, and he stayed there with them and baptized. 23. John also was baptizing in Aenon near Salim [Note: Gat.: “in Aenon . . .” Mm.: “in Aenon near Salim beyond the Jordan.” Vulgate: “in Aenon near Salim.”], because there was much water there; and people came and were baptized. 24. For John had not yet been put into prison [Col. 0369]. 25. Therefore a dispute arose between Jews and John’s disciples concerning purif. . . . . 26. And they came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you bore testimony—behold, he is baptizing, and all are coming to him.” 27. John answered and said, “A person cannot receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven. 28. You yourselves bear witness to me that I sa . . . . vo . . . ‘I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him.’ 29. He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the bridegroom’s friend, who stands and hears him, rejoices with joy because of the bridegroom’s voice. This joy of mine, therefore, has been fulfilled. 30. He must increase, but I must decrease. 31. He who comes from above [Col. 0371] is above all. But he who is from the ear . . . . is from the earth and speaks from the earth. 32. He who comes from heaven [Note: After *venit*, “comes,” *super omnes est, et*, “is above all, and,” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis], testifies [Note: Before *testatur*, “testifies,” *hoc*, “this,” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis] to what he has seen and heard, and no one receives his testimony. 33. Whoever has received his testimony has certified that God is true. 34. For he whom God sent speaks God’s words; for God does not give the Spirit by measure. 35. The Father loves the Son: . . . . . nia has given [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “into his hands.” Vulgate: “into his hand”] into his hand. 36. He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who is disobedient to the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.

CHAPTER IV.

1. Therefore, when Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that [Col. 0371] Jesus had more disciples and baptized [Note: [Col. 0372] Gat.: “was making [disciples], and baptizing.” Vulg.: “makes [disciples], and baptizes.”] more than 2. John—although Jesus [Note: [Col. 0372] Gat. and Mm.: “Jesus himself.” Vulg.: “Jesus.”] himself [Note: [Col. 0371] Adds “himself,” as does the Greek text, αὐτός (“himself”).] did not baptize, but his disci- 3. . . ples did—he left [Note: [Col. 0371] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: γῆν (“land”).] [Note: [Col. 0372] Gat. and Mm.: “the land of Judaea, and.” Vulg.: “Judaea, and.”] the land + of Judaea and went again into Galilee. 4. Now he had to [Note: [Col. 0372] Mm.: “go through.” Vulg.: “pass through.”] pass through Samaria. 5. Therefore he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the field which Jacob gave to his son Joseph. 6. Now Jacob’s spring was there. Therefore Jesus, wearied by the journey, [Note: [Col. 0372] Gat.: “was sitting upon.” Mm.: “was sitting above.” Vulg.: “was thus sitting above.”] sat by the spring. It was about the sixth 7. hour. And a Samaritan woman came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me 8. something to drink.” (For his disciples had gone into the city to buy food.) 9. Therefore the Samaritan woman [Note: [Col. 0371] After “woman,” “that” is absent, as also in the Greek text.] said + to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, [Col. 0373] ask me for a drink, when I am a Samaritan?” [Note: [Col. 0373] Gat. and Mm.: “when I am a woman?” Vulg.: “who am a woman?”] 10. Jesus answered and said to her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would ask him, and he would give you living water.” 11. The woman said to him, “Sir, you have nothing with which to draw, and the well is deep: [Note: [Col. 0373] Therefore is wanting after ‘whence,’ also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] whence + do you have living water? 12. Are you greater than our father Jacob, who [Note: [Col. 0373] Gat.: “this well.” Vulg.: “the well.”] gave us this well, and himself drank from it, as did his sons and his livestock?” 13. Jesus answered and said to hi . . . “Everyone who [Note: [Col. 0373] Gat. and Mm.: “drinks from.” Vulg.: “drinks from.”] drinks from this wat . . . will thir . . . . . . but whoever drinks of the water which I shall give him shall not thirst . . . . . . etern . . .: 14. but the wat . . . which I shall give . . . . . . will become in him a spring of water leaping up to eternal life.” 15. . . . the woman said to him, “Sir, give me [Col. 0373] this water, so that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw.” 16. He said to her, “Go . . . call your husband . . . and come.” 17. . . . the woman answered and said to him, [Note: [Col. 0373] Gat. and Mm.: “I do not have a husband.” Vulg.: “I do not have a husband.”] “I do not . . . a husband.” . . . “You have spoken well . . . husband . . . you have not . . . 18. . . . for you have had five husbands . . . [Note: [Col. 0374] Gat.: “and now the one whom you have.” Mm.: “and this one whom you have.” Vulg.: “and now, the one whom you have.”] and now the one whom you have is not your husband; in this you spoke truly.” 19. Th . . . the woman said, “L . . . , I see that you are a 20. prophet.” [Note: [Col. 0373] After “are,” “you” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] “Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say th . . . [Note: [Col. 0373] Adds “in,” as does the Greek text, ἐν.] in + Jer . . usalem is the place where it is necessary . . . . . . 21. Jesus said to . . . . . . “Believe . . . . . . that the hour is coming when neither on this mou . . . nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father. 22. You worship what . . . do not know; we wor . . . what . . . . . . because [Col. 0375] we know that salvation is from the Jews. 23. But the hour is coming, and now is, . . . when [Note: [Col. 0375] Gat.: “true worshippers.” Mm.: “men worshippers.” Vulg.: “true [Col. 0376] worshippers.”] true wor . . . pers will wor . . ship the Father . . . in spirit . . . . . . . . . . . for the Fa . . . seeks . . . . . . those who wor . . . him 24. in spirit. God is Spirit, and those who worship him must worship in sp . . rit and tru . . . . . . . . . . . .” 25. The wo . . . said to him, “I know that Messiah is coming (who is called Christ). When he comes, he will proclaim all things to us.” 26. Jesus said to her, “I am he, who speak with you.” 27. And at that moment . . . his disciples came, and they marvelled that he was speaking with a wom . . . . Yet no one said [Note: [Col. 0375] Adds “to him,” as also Codex Cantabrigiensis, αὐτῷ.] to him +, “What are you seeking?” or, “Why are you speaking with her?” 28. Therefore the woman left her water jar and went into the city, and said [Note: [Col. 0375] Before “men,” “to them” is absent, likewise in the Greek text.] to the men +, 29. “Come, see [Col. 0375] a man who told me everything that I . . . did. Is this . . . the Christ?” 30. They . . . out of the city and came 31. . . . to him. Meanwhile the disciples were urging him, saying, “Master, eat.” 32. But he said to them, “I have food to eat which you do not know.” 33. Therefore his disciples said to one another, “Has anyone brought him something to eat?” 34. Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to complete his work. 35. Do you not say, ‘There are still four months, and then the harvest comes’? Behold, I tell yo . . . Lift up your eyes and see the fields, for they are white [Note: [Col. 0375] After “are,” “already” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] + for harvest. 36. He who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit [Col. 0377] for eternal life, so that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. 37. For in this is the true saying: one is the sower, and anoth . . . 38. the reaper. I sent you to reap that for which you did not labour; others have laboured, and you have entered into their labour.” 39. From that city many Samaritans believed because of the word of the wom . . ., who bore wit . . . ness, saying, “He told me . . . . . . everything . . . . . . . . . . . .” 40. When . . . therefore the Sam . . . ritans came to him, [Note: [Col. 0377] So also the Greek text, ἠρώτων (“they were asking” or “begging”).] they begged + . . . . . . that he might re- . . . . . . with th . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 41. . . . many believed because of his word. 42. And they said to the woman, “We believe not because of your speech; for we ourselves have heard, and we know that this is truly the Saviour of the wor- 43. . . . After tw . . . days, however, [Note: [Col. 0377] Before “he departed,” “he went out” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] . . . . . . . . 44. [Note: [Col. 0377] Gat. and Mm.: “and came into.” Vulg.: “and went into.”] Galilee. For Jesus himself te . . . fied . . . that a prophet has no honour in his own country. 45. Therefore, when he had come . . . Galilee, . . . the Galilaeans received . . . , having seen all the things he did at Jerusalem during the feast-day; for they too had come to the feast. 46. Therefore he came again to C . . . of Galilee, where [Note: [Col. 0377] Gat. and Mm.: “made water wine.” Vulg.: “made the water wine.”] he made water wine. And there was a certain royal official (*basiliscus*), whose son was sick [Note: [Col. 0377] Adds “in,” as does the Greek text, ἐν.] in + Capernaum. 47. When this man [Note: [Col. 0378] Gat.: “when he had heard that the Lord.” Vulg.: “when he had heard that Jesus.”] heard that Jesus had co . . . from Ju . . . into Galil . . ., he came to him and begged him to come down and heal [Col. 0379] his son, for he was about to die. 48. Jesus therefore said to him, “Unless you see signs and won- . . . , you will not . . . .” 49. The roy . . . official said to him, “Sir, co . . . down before . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .” 50. Jesus said . . . [Note: [Col. 0379] Gat.: “come down” (in a later hand, “Go”), “your son . . .”; “the man believed the word which . . .” Mm.: “come down,” “your son . . .”; “the man believed the man whom . . .” Vulg.: “Go,” “your son . . .”; “the man believed the word which . . .”] “. . . Go; your son lives.” [Note: [Col. 0379] Adds “and,” as does the Greek text, καί (“and”).] And + the man believed the word which Jesus spoke to him, 51. and went. While he was now . . . going down, his servants met . . . him and reported [Note: [Col. 0379] Adds “to him,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis, αὐτῷ.] to him +, saying that [Note: [Col. 0379] So also the Greek text, ὁ παῖς σου ζῇ (“your child lives”).] “your son lives” +. 52. He then asked th . . . at what hour he became better. And they said, “Yesterday [Note: [Col. 0379] Gat.: “at about the seventh hour.” Vulg.: “at the seventh hour.”] at the seventh hour . . . the fever left him.” 53. Therefore the father knew that it was [Note: [Col. 0379] “That hour,” in the ablative case, with the verb *erat* omitted. So too the Greek text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ (ἐν ᾗ) (“in that hour,” “in which”).] that hour [Col. 0379] in which + Jesus said, “Your son lives”; and he himself believed, as did his whole 54. household. This was again the second sign Jesus performed, [Note: [Col. 0379] Gat. and Mm.: “when he came.” Vulg.: “when he had come.”] coming from Judaea into Galilee.

## CHAPTER V

1. After this there was a fe . . . of the Jud . . . , and . . . . . . Jesus went up to Jerusalem. 2. Now at Jerusalem, in the lower quarter, there is a pool called in Hebrew Belzatha, having five porticoes. 3. In these [Note: [Col. 0379] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: κατέκειντο (“were lying”). In the same Cantabrigiensis, “many” is absent.] lay + crowds of sick people—blind, lame, withered, [Note: [Col. 0379] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: παραλυτικῶν (“paralytics”).] paralytics +—waiting for the movement of the water. 4. [Note: [Col. 0379] Gat.: “But an angel came down and moved the water. And whoever first went down into the pool became well, whatever disease held him.” Mm.: “But an angel [Col. 0380] of the Lord . . . and moved the water. And whoever first went down into the pool after the movement of the water . . . whatever disease held him.” Vulg.: “But an angel of the Lord came down at a certain time into the pool, and the water was moved. And he who first went down into the pool after the movement of the water became well from whatever illness held him.”] But an angel of the Lord came dow . . ., and [Note: [Col. 0381] So also the Greek text, ἐτάραττε (“was stirring”).] stirred + the water. And whoever first went down into the pool became well, whatever illness held him. 5. Now there was there [Note: [Col. 0381] After “man,” “a certain” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] a man + who had been ill for thirty-eight years. 6. When Jesus saw him lying there, knowing that he had already been so for a long time, he said to him, “Do you wish to become well?” 7. The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one who, when the water has . . . been stirred, will put me into the pool; for while . . . I am coming, another goes down before me.” 8. Jesus said to him, “Rise, take up your pallet, 9. and walk.” . . . Immediately the man became well [Note: [Col. 0381] Gat.: “was made well, and took up.” Mm.: “the man was made well, and took up.” Vulg.: “that man was made well, and took up.”]: [Note: [Col. 0381] Adds “and rose,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis, καὶ ἐγερθείς (“and having risen”).] and rose +, took up his pallet, and walked. Now it was the Sab- [Col. 0381] bath on that day. 10. Therefore the Jews said to the man who [Note: [Col. 0381] Mm.: “had become well.” Vulg.: “had been healed.”] had been healed, “It is the Sabbath, [Note: [Col. 0381] Adds “and,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis, καί.] and + it is not lawful for you to carry your pallet.” 11. . . . He answered them, “He who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your pallet and walk.’” 12. They asked him, “Wh . . . is the man who said to you, ‘Take up your pallet, 13. and walk’?” But the man who had been hea . . . did n . . . know who . . . , for Jesus had withdrawn from the crowd gathered in that place. 14. Afterwards Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Behold, you have become well; sin no longer, lest something worse happen to you.” 15. The man went away and told the Jews that Jesus was the one who made him 16. well. Because of this the Jews persecuted Jesus, [Col. 0383] because he did these things on the Sabbath. 17. But Jesus answered them, “My Father is working until now, and I am working.” 18. [Note: [Col. 0383] So also the Greek text, διὰ τοῦτο (“because of this”). In the same place, “therefore” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Because of this + the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal to God. They answered: “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them: [Note: [Col. 0413] So also the Greek text, εἰ τέκνα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἦτε, τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἐποιεῖτε ἄν, “If you were children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham.”] “If you were children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham

40. +. But now you seek to kill me, a man who spoke to you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham

41. did not do this, which [Note: [Col. 0413] Mm.: “which you do.” Vulg.: “which you do.”] you do: the works of your father.” [Col. 0413] They said to him: “We were not born from fornication; we have one Father, God.”

42. [Note: [Col. 0413] After *said*, *therefore* is absent also in the Gothic version.] Jesus said + to them: “If God were your Father, you would love me. For I came forth from God and came; for I did not come from myself, but he

44. You are of the father, the devil, and you wish to do the desires of your father. He … a murderer from the beginning, and did not stand in the truth, because truth is not in him. When he speaks falsehood, he speaks from his own [store], because he is a liar, as also [his] father.

45. [Note: [Col. 0413] After *I*, *but* is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] I +, because I speak the truth, you do not believe [Col. 0415] me.

46. Which of you convicts me of sin? If I speak truth, why do you not believe

51. Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he shall not see death for ever.”

52. The Jews said to him: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, [Note: [Col. 0415] Gat.: “and the prophets died; yet you.” Vulg.: “and the prophets? Yet you.”] and the prophets; and you [Col. 0415] say: ‘If anyone hears and keeps my word, he shall not taste death for ever.’

55. [Note: [Col. 0416] Gat. and Mm.: “our [God].” Vulg.: “your [God].”] your God, and you have not known him. But I know him; and if I say that I do not know him, I shall be a liar like you. But I know him, [Note: [Col. 0416] Mm.: “and his commandments.” Vulg.: “and his word.”] and keep his word.

56. Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day; [Note: [Col. 0415] Adds *and*, also in the Greek text, καί.] and + he saw it and was glad.”

[Col. 0417]

57. Therefore the Jews said to him: “You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?”

58. Jesus said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: [Note: [Col. 0417] So also the Codex of Canterbury, Latin and Greek, πρὶν Ἀβραὰμ, ἐγώ εἰμι, “before Abraham, I am.”] before Abraham, I am +.”

59. Therefore the Jews took stones [Note: [Col. 0417] Gat. and Mm.: “to throw.” Vulg.: “to cast.”] to … throw at him; but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.

## CHAPTER IX

1. And as he passed by, [Note: [Col. 0417] Before *saw*, *Jesus* is absent also in the Greek text.] he saw + a man blind from his birth.

2. And his disciples asked him, saying: “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”

3. Jesus answered them: “Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but that the works of God might be manifested in

4. him. I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day; night comes, when [Col. 0417] no one can

5. work. While I am in this world, I am the light of this world.”

6. Having said these things, he spat on the ground, made mud from the spittle, and anointed his eyes [with it].

7. And he said: “Go to the pool of [Note: [Col. 0417] So also the Greek text, Σιλωάμ, “Siloam.”] Siloam + (which is translated, ‘Sent’).” He went, washed, and came seeing.

Therefore his neighbours, and those who had seen him [Note: [Col. 0417] Gat.: before *that …*, “[who had seen] … Is this not he?” Others: “By no means.” Vulg.: “previously, that … Is this not he who sat and begged?” Others said, “It is he”; others, “By no means.”] before as blind and a beggar, said: “Is this not the man who sat and begged?” Some said, “This is he.”

11. But he [Note: [Col. 0417] So also the Greek text, ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπος.] answered them and said: “A man + who is called Jesus touched [Col. 0419] my eyes and said: ‘Go to Siloam and wash.’ And I went, washed, and see.”

12. Therefore they said to him: “And where is he?” He said: “I do not know.”

13. They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been

14. blind. Now it was [Note: [Col. 0419] Mm.: “It was Sabbath on that day when …” Vulg.: “It was Sabbath when …”] the Sabbath on the day when Jesus made mud and opened his eyes.

16. Therefore some of the Pharisees said: “This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath thus.” [Note: [Col. 0419] After *others*, *but* is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] Others + said: “How can a sinful person perform [Note: [Col. 0419] So also the Greek text, τοιαῦτα, “such things.”] such + signs?” And there were divisions [Col. 0419] among them.

17. They said + therefore to the blind man [Note: [Col. 0419] After *to him*, *again* is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] to him +: “What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes?” But he said: “That he is a prophet.”

18. The Jews did not [Note: [Col. 0419] After *believed*, *therefore* is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] believe + that he had been blind and now sees, until they called his parents [Note: [Col. 0419] Gat.: “who saw.” Mm.: “who saw him.” Vulg.: “who had seen.”]:

[Col. 0421]

22. His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already resolved that, if anyone confessed him [Note: [Col. 0421] Before *Christ*, *to be* is absent likewise in the Greek text.] [to be] Christ +, he should be put out of the synagogue.

24. Therefore [Note: [Col. 0421] Gat.: “therefore the man who was blind … because [this] man.” Mm.: “who was blind.” Vulg.: “therefore again the man who had been blind … because this man.”] they again called the man who had been blind and said to him: “Give honour to God; we know that this man is a sinner.”

25. [Note: [Col. 0421] Before *he*, *to them* is absent also in the Greek text.] He + said: “If he is a sinner, I do not know; one thing I know: that I was blind and now see.”

26. They said to him: “What did he do to you? How did he open [Note: [Col. 0421] Gat. and Mm.: “your eyes.” Vulg.: “your eyes.”] your eyes?”

27. He answered them: “I told you, [Note: [Col. 0421] Gat.: “and you did not hear.” Vulg.: “and you heard.”] and you did not hear; why do you want to hear again? Do you also wish to become his disciples?”

28. But they [Col. 0421] reviled him and said: “You be his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses.

29. We know that God spoke to Moses; but as for this man, we do not know where he is from.”

31. We know that God [Note: [Col. 0421] Gat.: “God did not hear [sinners], but whoever is his worshipper … [Col. 0422] him he heard.” Mm.: “God did not hear, but whoever is his worshipper.” Vulg.: “God does not hear, but if anyone is a worshipper of God … him he hears.”] does not hear sinners; but if anyone worships God and does his will, God hears that person.

34. They answered … him and … said: [Note: [Col. 0422] Gat. and Mm.: “You were born in sin.” Vulg.: “You were born in sins.”] “You were born wholly in sins; [Col. 0423] and do you teach us?” And they cast him out.

35. Jesus heard that they had cast … him out; [Note: [Col. 0423] So also the Codex of Canterbury, καὶ εὗρεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν, “and he found him and said.”] and found him, and said + to him: “Do you believe in the Son of God?”

## CHAPTER X

1. “Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever does not enter through the door [Note: [Col. 0423] Mm.: “but climbs up in another part, that man.” Vulg.: “but climbs up [Col. 0424] from elsewhere, that man.”] into the sheepfold is

2. a thief. But he who enters through the door is shepherd of the sheep.

3. To him [Note: [Col. 0424] Gat.: “door-keeper.” Vulg.: “doorkeeper.”] the doorkeep… opens, and the … hear his voice; … calls his own sheep by name and leads

4. them. And when he has brought out all [Note: [Col. 0423] Adds *all*, also the Codex of Canterbury, πάντα.] all + his own, he goes before … them, and … follow him, because … know … his voice.

5. … they will not follow a stranger, but flee from him, because they do not know his voice.”

6. Jesus spoke this figure of speech to them; but they did not understand what he was saying to them.

8. sheep. All who [Note: [Col. 0425] Gat.: “came before me, [they] are thieves … but they did not hear them.” Vulg.: “came, [they] are thieves … and they did not hear them.”] came are thieves and robbers; [Note: [Col. 0425] So also the Greek text, ἀλλά, “but.”] but + the sheep did not hear them.”

10. The thief comes only to steal and destroy. But I came that they may have life, and may have it more abundantly.

11. I am the good shepherd. But the good sheph… lays down his life [Note: [Col. 0425] Mm.: “hands over [his life] for.” Vulg.: “gives [his life] for.”] for the sheep.

12. He who is a hired man and is not a shepherd, … whose … sheep are not his own, sees the wolf coming, abandons the sheep, and flees; and the wolf snatches them and scatters the shee…:

[Col. 0425]

13. but the hired man … flees, because … he is a hired man and has no concern for the shee….

14. I am the good shepherd; and I know my sheep … and they know me …,

15. as … the Father knows [me], and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.

16. And I have other little sheep which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, so that they may hear my voice; and there shall be one flock and one

17. shepherd. For this reason the Father loves me: because I lay down my life for the sheep, that I may again [Note: [Col. 0425] Gat.: “receive it.” Vulg.: “take it.”] take it up.

18. No one takes it from me; but … I lay it down of myself. I have authority to lay it down; and I have authority [Col. 0427] to take it up again. For I received this command from [Note: [Col. 0427] After *Father*, *my* is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] the Father +.”

20. And many of them said: “He has a demon and is mad; why do you listen to him?”

21. Others said: “These … words are not [the words] of one who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”

25. Jesus answered them: “I told you, and you do not believe. The works which I do in the name [Col. 0427] of my Father bear witness concerning

26. me; but you do not believe, for you are not of my sheep, as I told

27. you. Those who are … of my sheep hear my voice; and I know them, and they follow me;

29. What the Father gave me is greater than all; and no one can snatch it from my Father’s hand.

31. Therefore the Jews took up stones to stone him.
