42. But everything John said concerning this man was tru….” And many believed … him.

## CHAPTER XI

1. Now a certain man, Lazarus by name, was sick, from Bethany, the vill… of Mary and Martha, [Note: [Col. 0429] Gat. and Mm.: “his sisters.” Vulg.: “his sister.”] his sister.

2. (Now Mary was the one who had anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair; her brother Lazarus was sick.)

3. Therefore his sisters sent to hi…, saying: “… is sick.”

4. When Jesus heard [it], he said to them: “This sickness [Col. 0431] is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

5. For Jesus loved Lazarus and his sisters.

6. Therefore, when he heard [Note: [Col. 0431] Gat.: “that Lazarus is sick.” Mm.: “that [he] is sick.” Vulg.: “that he was sick.”] that [Note: [Col. 0431] So also the Greek text, ἀσθενεῖ, “is sick.”] he is sick +, he then remained in the same place

7. two days. Then after this he said to the disciples: “Let us go again … into Judaea.”

8. His disciples said to him: “Rabbi, [Note: [Col. 0431] Gat.: “this man.” Vulg.: “now.”] just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?”

9. Jesus answered them: “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in daytime, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.

10. But if anyone walks at night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.”

11. He said these things, and af… these [Note: [Col. 0431] So also the Greek text, λέγει, “he says.”] said +: “… Lazarus, our fri…d, has fallen asleep; but I am going to awaken him.”

12. Therefore his disciples said to him: “Lord, if he sleeps, he shall be saved.”

13. But Jesus had spoken of his death; but they … supposed that he was speaking of sleep in slumber.

14. Then he said plainly: “Lazarus is dead;

15. and I am glad … for your sake … that I was not … there …. But let us go to him.”

16. Thomas, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples: “Let us also go, that we may die with him.”

17. Therefore Jesus came and found him already four days in the tomb.

18. Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.

19. But many [Col. 0433] of the Jews had come to … Martha and Mary, to comfort them concerning their brother.

20. Therefore Martha, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet him; but Mary sat in the house.

21. Therefore Martha said to Jesus: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother

22. would not have died; but even now I know that whatever [Note: [Col. 0433] Gat.: “ask of God.” Vulg.: “request of God.”] you ask of God, God will give you.”

23. … Jesus said to her: “Your brother shall rise again.”

24. Martha said: “I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection on the last day.”

25. Jesus said to her: “I am the resurrect…; he who believes in me, even if he has died,

26. shall live; [Note: [Col. 0433] Mm.: “and everyone who believes in me.” Vulg.: “and everyone who lives and believes in me.”] and everyone who sees and will believe in me shall not die for ever. Do you believe this?”

27. Martha said to him: “Certainly, Lord, I have believed [Col. 0433] that you are the Christ, the Son [Note: [Col. 0433] After *God*, *living* is absent also in the Greek text.] [Note: [Col. 0433] Gat.: “Son of God, who …” Vulg.: “Son of the living God, who …”] of God +, who comes into this worl….”

28. Having said this, she went and secretly called her sister Mary, saying: [Note: [Col. 0434] Gat.: “The Teacher has come, and …” Vulg.: “The Teacher is present, and …”] “The Teacher has come and calls you.”

29. When she heard this, she rose quickly and came to him;

30. for Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.

31. But the Jews who were with he… in the hous… and consoling her, when they saw Mary rise quickly [Note: [Col. 0434] Gat.: “and went … Because she will go to.” Vulg.: “and went out … Because she goes to.”] and go out, followed her, saying: “She is going to the tomb, to weep

32. there.” Therefore Mary, when she came where Jesus was and saw him, fell at his feet, saying: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”

[Col. 0435]

33. But Jesus, [Note: [Col. 0435] Mm.: “when he heard her … he groaned.” Gat.: “[the Jews] who were with [her] … he groaned.” Vulg.: “when he saw her … who had come with [her] … groaned deeply.”] when he saw her weeping and the Jews weeping who had come with her, groaned in spirit and troubled himself,

34. and said: “Where have you laid him?” They said to him: “Lord, come

35. and see.” And Jesus wept.

36. And the Jews said: “See how he loved him.”

37. But some of them said: “Could not this man, who opened the eyes [Note: [Col. 0435] After *blind*, *born* is absent also in the Greek text.] of the blind +, cause this man not to die?”

38. Therefore Jesus, groaning within himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay upon

39. it. Jesus said: “Take away the ston….” Martha, Lazarus’s sister, said to him: “Lord, [Note: [Col. 0435] Mm.: “he already stinks.” Vulg.: “he already smells foul.”] he already smells foul, for he has been dead four days.”

40. Jesus said: “Did I not tell you that if you believe, [Col. 0436] you will see the majesty

41. of God?” And they took away the stone. But Jesus, lifting his eyes upward to hea…en, said: “Father, I thank you that you heard

42. me. And I knew that you always hear me; but [Note: [Col. 0435] Gat. and Mm.: “because of the crowd which …” Vulg.: “because of the people who …”] because of the crowd standing around, I said [this], that they may believe that you

43. sent me.” And having said these things, he cried out with a loud voice: “Lazarus, come out.”

44. And [Note: [Col. 0435] Before *came out*, *immediately* is absent also in the Greek text.] came out + the one who had died, his feet and hands bound with strips of cloth [Note: [Col. 0435] Gat.: “his hands and feet bound with strips … and let [him] go.” Mm.: “his feet and hands bound with strips.” Vulg.: “his feet and hands bound with strips … and permit [him] to go.”], and his face was bound with a napkin. Jesus said: “Untie him and let him go.”

45. Therefore many of the Jews who had come to [Note: [Col. 0436] After *Mary*, *and Martha* is absent also in the Greek text.] Mary +, seeing [Note: [Col. 0436] Gat. and Mm.: “what [he] did, believed.” Vulg.: “what Jesus did, believed.”] what Jesus did, believed in

46. him. But some of them went away [Col. 0437] to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

47. Therefore the chief priests and Pharisees assembled a council and said: “What shall we do, since this man performs many signs?

48. If we let him go on thus, all will believe in him; and the Romans will come and take away both our place and nation.”

49. But one of them, Caiaphas by name, who was high priest that year, said to them: “You know nothing,

50. nor do you consider that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people and that the whole nation should not perish.”

51. But he did not say this from himself; rather, because he was high priest that year, he prophesied [Col. 0437] that Jesus was going to die for the nation,

52. and not only for the nation, but so that the Son of God might also gather the dispersed [ones] into one.

53. Therefore from that day they took counsel to kill him.

54. Therefore Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went away into the region near the wilderness, to the city called [Note: [Col. 0437] Gat.: “Ephraim, and he remained there.” Mm.: “he remains.” Vulg.: “Ephraim, and he remained there.”] Ephraim, and remained there with his disciples.

55. At that time the Jewish Passover was approaching; and many went up to Jerusalem from that region before the Passover, in order to purify themselves.

56. Therefore they sought Jesus and said among themselves, standing in the temple: [Note: [Col. 0438] Gat.: “What do you think?” Vulg.: “What do you think?”] “Do you think [Col. 0439] that he is not coming to the festival?” But the chief priests and Pharisees gave an order that, if anyone knew where … was, he should report it, so that they might seize him.

## CHAPTER XII
1. Now six days before the Passover Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, . . . whom he had raised . . . from the dead.

> [Note: Col. 0439. So also the Greek text: ἦν Λάζαρος ὁ τεθνηκώς, “Lazarus who had died.”]

2. . . . made him a supper; and Martha was serving; . . . one of . . . They made him supper, and Martha was serving, while Lazarus was one of those reclining at table.

> [Note: Col. 0439. Gat.: “they made him a supper, and Martha was serving … one of.” Vulg.: “They made him a supper there, and Martha was serving … was one of.”]

3. Mary took a pound of ointment of nard and anointed Jesus’ feet, and wip . . . with her hair his feet; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.

4. One of his disciples said, Simon + Judas Iscariot, . . . who was about to betray him:

> [Note: Col. 0439. Adds “Simon,” as does the Greek text: Σίμωνος, “of Simon.”]

> [Note: Col. 0439. Gat.: “did not come [to three hundred denarii].” Mm.: “did not sell [it].” Vulg.: “was not sold.”]

6. He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief and had the money-box . . . and used to take away what was put into it.

> [Note: Col. 0439. So also the Greek text: εἶχε, “he had.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0439. Mm.: “he had it, and took away what was put in.” Vulg.: “having it, he carried what was put in.”]

7. Jesus said, “Let . . . her keep it for the day of my burial.

> [Note: Col. 0439. So also the Greek text: ἄφες, “let [her].”]  
> [Note: Col. 0440. Mm.: “Leave her.” Vulg.: “Leave her.”]

8. For you always have the poor with you; but you do not always have me.”

> [Note: Col. 0440. Gat. and Mm.: “you will have … you will always have.” Vulg. and S.: “you have … you always have.”]

9. A great crowd of the Jews heard + that he was there; and they came, not for Jesus’ sake alone, but that they might see Lazar . . . whom . . . he had raised . . . from the dead.

> [Note: Col. 0439. Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἤκουσαν, “they heard.”]

10. But the chief priests planned also to kill Lazarus,

11. because many of the Jews +, on account of him, were going away and believing in Jesus.

> [Note: Col. 0441. So also the Greek text: τῶν Ἰουδαίων, “of the Jews.”]

12. On the next day, the great crowds which had come for the feast, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,

13. took palm blossoms and went out . . . to meet him, . . . crying, “Hosanna, Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, King of Israel!”

14. Jesus found a donkey and sat upon it, as it is writ-

15. ten: “Do not fear, daughter of Zion; behold, your king comes, gentle, seated upon a donkey’s colt.”

> [Note: Col. 0441. Mm.: “comes to you seated.” Vulg.: “your king comes seated.”]

16. His disciples did not understand these things at first; but when Jesus had been glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written concerning him and that they had done these things to him.

17. Therefore the crowds which were with him bore witness, because he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead.

> [Note: Col. 0441. Mm.: “the crowd concerning him when.” Vulg.: “the crowd that was with him when.”]

18. For this reason the crowd went to meet him, because they had heard that he had performed this sign.

> [Note: Col. 0441. So also the Greek text: ὠφελεῖτε, “you profit / accomplish.”]

20. There were certain Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.

21. They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, “Sir, we wish to see Jes . . .”

22. Philip came and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip came [Col. 0443] and told Jesus.

23. But he answered them, saying, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be honoured.

24. Truly, truly, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat falling into the earth dies,

25. it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit. Whoever loves his life will lose it; and whoever hates his life in this world will preserve it for eternal life.

> [Note: Col. 0443. Mm.: “and whoever has lost his life.” Vulg.: “and whoever hates his life.”]

26. If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there my servant also will be. If anyone serves me, my Father has honoured him.

28. Father, honour your name.” Then a voice came from heaven, saying, “I have honoured it, and I will honour it again.”

> [Note: Col. 0443. Mm.: “Glorify your Son.” Vulg.: “Glorify your name.”]

29. The crowd which stood and heard said, “Thunder has occurred.” Others said, “An angel has spoken to him.”

> [Note: Col. 0444. Gat.: “has occurred; for an angel [has spoken] to him.” Vulg.: “has occurred. Others said: An angel [has spoken] to him.”]

30. Jesus answered and said to them, “This voice came not for my sake, but for

31. yours. Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world is cast

32. out. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself.”

33. (He said this to signify by what death he was about to die.)

34. The crowd answered him, “We have heard written in the law that + the Christ remains forever. How then do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who [Col. 0445] is this Son of Man?”

> [Note: Col. 0443. Adds *quia*, “that,” as does the Greek text: ὅτι.]

35. Jesus said to them, “For a little [while] + the light is among you. Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you; whoever walks in darkness does not

36. know where he goes. While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be children of light.” Jesus spoke these things, and went away and hid himself.

> [Note: Col. 0445. Adds *tempus*, “time,” as does the Greek text: χρόνον. Codex Brixianus has *habet temporis*, “has [a time] of time.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0445. Gat.: “does not know where he goes.” Mm.: “you do not know where you go.” Vulg.: “does not know where he goes.”]

37. Though he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him,

38. so that the saying of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he said: “Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

39. For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah said again:

40. “He has blinded [Col. 0445] their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they may not see with their eyes and may not understand with their heart, and turn, and I may heal them.”

> [Note: Col. 0445. Gat. and Mm.: “and understand with the heart.” Vulg.: “and not understand with the heart.”]

41. Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory and spoke

42. concerning him. Nevertheless, many even of the rulers believed in him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, lest they should be expelled from the synagogue.

43. For they loved human glory more than the glory of God.

44. But Jesus cried out, saying, “Whoever believes in me believes not in me, but in him who sent

45. me. And whoever sees me sees him who [Col. 0446] sent me.

> [Note: Col. 0445. So also Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Greek text: ἔκραζε καὶ ἔλεγεν, “was crying out and saying.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0446. Gat.: “who sent me. I [am] light.” Vulg.: “who sent me.”]

46. I came as light into this world, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness.

47. And if anyone hears my words and keeps them +, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge this world, but to save this world.

> [Note: Col. 0447. “Not” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]  
> [Note: Col. 0447. Gat.: “that I may make [it] safe.” Vulg.: “that I may save [it].”]

48. Whoever rejects me and does not receive my words has one who judges him. The word which I spoke . . . to them, that . . . will judge him on the last

49. day. For I have not spoken from myself; but the Father who sent me himself gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak.

50. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. Therefore what I speak, I speak just as the Father told me.

## CHAPTER XIII

1. Now before the feast day of the Passover, Jesus knew that his hour had come [Col. 0447] for him to pass from this world to the Father. Having loved his disciples who were in this world, he loved them to the end.

2. And when supper had been prepared, the devil having already inserted himself into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, so that he should betray him—

> [Note: Col. 0447. Gat.: “when the disciple had already put into [his] heart, that … Simon Iscariot.” Vulg.: “when the devil had already put into [his] heart, that … of Simon Iscariot.”]

3. knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come forth from God and was going to God,

4. rose from supper, laid aside his garments, took a towel, and girded

5. himself. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.

6. So he came to Simon Peter. Peter said to him, “Lord, are you washing my feet?”

7. Jesus answered and said to him, “What I am doing, you do not . . . [lacuna].” [Col. 0449] . . . Simon Peter said, “You shall never wash my feet.” Jesus answered him, “Unless I wash . . . your feet, you have + no share with me.”

> [Note: Col. 0449. So also the Greek text: ἔχεις, “you have.”]

9. Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, not only [my] feet +, but also my hands, my head, and my whole body.”

> [Note: Col. 0449. After “feet,” *my* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

10. Jesus said to him, “He who has bathed does not need washing except . . . [lacuna] . . . you are clean, but not

11. all.” For he knew who was about to betray . . . him; therefore he said . . . “You are not all . . . clean.”

> [Note: Col. 0449. Gat.: “does not need to wash, but is.” Mm.: “he who has been washed once does not need to wash again, but is.” Vulg.: “he who has been washed does not need except to wash his feet, but is.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0449. Gat.: “he said: And you are clean, but not all.” Vulg.: “he said: You are not all clean.”]

12. Therefore, after he had . . . their feet, he took his garments, reclined again, and said to them, “Do you understand what I have done to you?

13. You call me Teacher and Lord, and you speak rightly, [Col. 0449] for I am.

> [Note: Col. 0450. Mm.: “and I am.” Vulg.: “for indeed I am.”]

14. If therefore I, who am Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, how much more . . . you ought . . . to wash one another’s

15. feet. For I have given . . . you an example, that as I have done to you, you also may do.

> [Note: Col. 0450. Gat.: “therefore I washed.” Vulg.: “therefore I myself washed.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0450. Mm.: “how much more ought you also.”]

16. Truly, truly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his lord, nor an apostle greater + than the one who sent

17. him. If you know these things, blessed are you + if you do them.

> [Note: Col. 0449. After *major*, “is” is absent also in the Greek text.]  
> [Note: Col. 0449. So also the Greek text: ἐστέ, “you are.”]

18. I do not speak of all of you. I know whom I have chosen; but that the Scripture may be fulfilled: “He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.”

20. Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever receives . . . him [Col. 0451] whom I send . . . receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.

> [Note: Col. 0450. Gat.: “whoever receives him, if [one] whom.” Mm.: “whoever receives him whom.” Vulg.: “whoever receives, if [one] whom.”]

21. Having spoken these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit and testified, saying, “Truly, truly, I say to you, one of you will betray me.”

22. His disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to whom

23. he meant. One of his disciples was reclining at Jesus’ bosom, the one whom Jesus loved.

24. Simon Peter therefore motioned to him, saying, “Ask who it is of whom he speaks.”

25. He therefore, reclining upon Jesus’ breast, said to him, “Lord, who is it?”

26. Jesus answered, “It is he to whom I shall give the dipped bread.” So he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas Iscariot. [Col. 0451]

27. And when he received the bread, Satan entered into him. Jesus said to him, “What you are doing, do more quickly.”

> [Note: Col. 0451. Gat.: “And then [Satan] entered.” Mm.: “And after the morsel had been received, [Satan] entered.” Vulg.: “And after the morsel, [Satan] entered.”]

28. But none of those reclining understood what

29. he had said to him. For many supposed, because Judas had the money-box, that Jesus had said to him, “Buy what was necessary for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.

31. night. When therefore he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man has been honoured, and God has been honoured in him.

33. Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will seek me; and as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I [Col. 0453] am, you cannot come,’ so now I say . . .

34. . . . a new . . . I give you, that you love one another, just as + I + loved you; so also you should love one another.

> [Note: Col. 0453. Gat.: “just as I also loved you, so you also.” Mm.: “just as I also loved you, that you also.” Vulg.: “just as I loved you, that you also.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0453. Adds *ego*, “I,” also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐγώ.]

35. By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have true love among yourselves.

> [Note: Col. 0453. Mm.: “people will know.” Vulg.: “all will know.”]

36. Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered, “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; but afterward you will follow.”

> [Note: Col. 0453. Gat.: “you cannot follow me.” Vulg.: “you cannot follow me now.”]

37. Peter said to him, “Lord +, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”

> [Note: Col. 0453. Adds “Lord,” as does the Greek text: κύριε.]

38. Jesus answered, “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I say to you, the cock will not crow until you have denied me three times.” And he said to his disciples:

## CHAPTER XIV

1. “Let not your [Col. 0453] heart be troubled. Believe in God, and you believe in me.

> [Note: Col. 0453. Gat. and Mm.: “Believe in God.” Vulg.: “You believe in God.”]

4. be. And [the] way where + I am going, you know.”

> [Note: Col. 0454. Gat.: “shall have prepared … and where I am, you also may be.” Vulg.: “shall have prepared … that where I am, you also may be.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0453. Before *vado*, “I” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

> [Note: Col. 0455. So also the Greek text: πιστεύετέ μοι, “believe me.”]

> [Note: Col. 0455. Gat.: “whom this world … does not know him.” Mm.: “because whoever does not see him does not know him.” Vulg.: “whom the world … because it neither sees nor knows him.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0455. So also the Greek text: μένει, “remains.”]

20. On that day you will know that I + am in my Father, and you in me, and I [Col. 0457]

21. in you. Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. Whoever loves me will be loved by my Father; and I will love him and reveal myself to him.”

> [Note: Col. 0455. After *ego*, “am” is absent also in the Greek text.]

> [Note: Col. 0457. Gat.: “you may believe that I am. Now.” Vulg.: “you may believe. Now.”]

> [Note: Col. 0457. Mm.: “With you. For he is coming.” Vulg.: “with you. For he is coming.”]

## CHAPTER XV

1. “I am the true vine, and my Father is the cultivator.

2. Every branch in me which does not bear fruit, he takes away +; and every fruitful branch he cleanses, that it may bear more fruit.

> [Note: Col. 0459. Gat. and Mm.: “not producing fruit.” Vulg.: “not bearing fruit.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0459. So also the Greek text: αἴρει, “takes away.”]

3. You are already clean because of the word which I have spoken

4. to you. Remain in me, and I in you. Just as a branch of the vine cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so also you cannot unless you remain in me.

> [Note: Col. 0459. Gat. and Mm.: “so also you.” Vulg.: “so neither you.”]

5. For I am the vine; you are the branches. If anyone remains in me and I in him, he will bear [Col. 0459] abundant fruit; for apart from me you can do nothing, unless anyone remains in me.

> [Note: Col. 0459. Mm.: “but you are branches; whoever.” Vulg.: “you [are] branches; whoever.”]

6. But if anyone does not remain in me, he is cast out like branches and will wither; and they will gather them and throw them into the fire, and they will burn.

> [Note: Col. 0459. Gat.: “*aruat* [materially uncertain; perhaps ‘it withers’], and they will gather them … they throw [them in], and they burn.” Mm.: “they will wither, and [it is] cast out, and they will gather it … they throw [it in], and it burns.” Vulg.: “it will wither, and they will gather it … they will throw [it in], and it burns.”]

9. disciples. As the Father loved me, I also loved you. Remain in my love.

11. I have spoken these things [Col. 0461] to you, that my joy may be in you and your joy may be fulfilled.

12. This is my commandment: that you love one another, as I loved

13. you. No one has greater love than this: to lay down his life + for his friends.

> [Note: Col. 0461. After *ponat*, “anyone” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek, and Latin.]

14. You are my friends if you receive what I command you.

15. I no longer call + you servants, but friends . . . for a servant does not know what his master does. But I have called you friends, because I have made known to you all that I heard from my Father.

> [Note: Col. 0461. So also the Greek text: λέγω, “I say / call.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0461. Gat.: “I call you … servants, but friends, because … what he will do.” Mm.: “I call you servants, but friends, because … what he does.” Vulg.: “I shall call you servants, because … what he does.”]

16. You did not choose me; but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.

> [Note: Col. 0462. Gat. and Mm.: “you ask my Father in.” Vulg.: “you ask the Father in.”]

17. I command you these things, that you may love one another.

18. If this world [Col. 0461] hates you, know that it hated me before + you.

> [Note: Col. 0461. After *prius*, “than you” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

19. If you were of this world, the world would love you as its own; but because you are not of this world, and I chose you out of this world, therefore the world hates you.

20. Remember the saying which I spoke to you: “A servant is not greater than his lord, nor an apostle greater than the one who sent him.” If you know these things, you are blessed if you do them. I do not speak of all of you; I know whom I have chosen. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you also; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.

21. But they do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know him who sent me.

22. If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; [Col. 0463] but now they have no excuse for their sin.

23. Whoever hates me hates my Father also.

24. If I had not done among them works which no one else did, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.

25. But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: “They hated me without cause.”

26. When that Paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from my Father, he will bear witness concerning me;

27. and you bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.

## CHAPTER XVI

1. I have spoken these things to you, that you may not be scandalized.

> [Note: Col. 0465. Adds *ea*, “them,” also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτά.]

> [Note: Col. 0465. Gat.: “he speaks … he will speak these things, and the things that are coming.” Vulg.: “he speaks … he will speak, and the things that are coming.”]

> [Note: Col. 0465. Mm.: “his disciples … this, what.” Vulg.: “some of his disciples … this which.”]

> [Note: Col. 0465. So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τί ἐστι τοῦτο τὸ μικρόν, “What is this little [while]?” The words *dicebant ergo*, “therefore they said,” are omitted.]  
> [Note: Col. 0465. Mm.: “this? What does he say?” Vulg.: “this which he says?”]

> [Note: Col. 0465. Before “Jesus,” *autem*, “but,” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]  
> [Note: Col. 0466. Gat.: “he said: Concerning this.” Vulg.: “he said to them: Concerning this.”]

20. Truly, truly, I say to you, you will weep and lament, while the world will rejoice. You + will be sorrowful, but your sorrow [Col. 0467] will be turned into joy.

> [Note: Col. 0465. After “you,” *autem*, “but,” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]  
> [Note: Col. 0467. Mm.: “will be transformed.” Vulg.: “will be turned.”]

21. A woman, when she is in labour, has sorrow because her day + has come; but when she has borne a child, she no longer remembers the distress because of joy that a human being has been born into this world.

> [Note: Col. 0467. So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἡμέρα, “day.”]

22. So you also now will have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy

23. from you. But on that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I say to you, if you ask the Father in my name, he will give

> [Note: Col. 0467. Gat.: “my Father in.” Mm.: “to my Father in.” Vulg.: “the Father in.”]

25. I have spoken these things to you [Col. 0467] in figures. The hour is coming when I shall no longer speak to you in figures, but shall announce to you openly concerning the Father.

26. On that day ask in my name, and I will ask on behalf of

27. you. For the Father himself loves you; you have loved me and have believed that I came forth from God.

29. His disciples said to him, “Behold, now you speak openly and use no figure.

30. Now we know that you know all things and have no need that anyone should question you. By this we believe that you came from God.”

31. Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?

32. Behold, the hour is coming—indeed, it has already come—when each of you will be scattered to his own region, [Col. 0469] and leave me alone; but I shall not be alone, because the Father is with me.

> [Note: Col. 0469. Mm.: “that you may leave [me]; and I am not alone.” Vulg.: “and … leave [me]; and I am not alone.”]

33. I have spoken these things to you, that you may have peace in me. In this world you will have affliction; but be of good cheer, for I have conquered the world.”

## CHAPTER XVII

1. Jesus spoke these things and, lifting his eyes to heaven, said: “Father, the hour has come. Honour your Son, that your Son may honour you,

2. just as you gave him authority over all flesh, that he may give eternal life to all whom you gave him.

3. And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus

4. Christ whom you sent. I have honoured you on earth; I have completed the work which you gave me [Col. 0469] to do;

5. and now, Father, honour me in your own presence with the glory which I had in your presence before the world

6. existed. I have made your name known to the people whom you gave me out of this world. They were yours, and you gave them to me; and they kept your word.

> [Note: Col. 0469. Gat. and Mm.: “my word.” Vulg.: “your word.”]

7. Now I have known + that everything which you gave me

8. is from you, because . . . I gave them the words which you gave me; and they themselves truly received them, because they came forth from you [the Greek is ambiguous and may also mean “I came forth”]; and . . . believed that you

9. sent me. I pray for them. I do not pray for this world, but for those whom you gave me, because

10. they are yours; and all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine; and [Col. 0471] I have been honoured in them.

> [Note: Col. 0469. So also the Gothic: ἔγνωκα, “I have known.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0470. Mm.: “they themselves received … truly believed that.” Vulg.: “they themselves received … believed that.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0469. The Greek text has ἐξῆλθον, which can signify both “I came forth” and “they came forth.”]

11. And these are in this world, and I am coming to you, and am no longer in this world, but they are in this world. Holy Father, keep them in your name; and while I was with them in this world,

12. I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me I guarded; and none of them perishes except the son of perdition, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.

> [Note: Col. 0471. Mm.: “and we are one. Father, while.” Vulg.: “and we. While.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0471. Mm.: “will perish, except.” Vulg.: “perished, except.”]

13. But now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in this world, that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves.

14. I gave them your word, and this world hates them because they are not of this world, just as I am not of this world.

15. I do not ask that you take them out of the world.

> [Note: Col. 0471. Gat.: “from evil.” Mm.: “because I do not ask … from evil.” Vulg.: “I do not ask … from evil.”]

16. They are not of this world, just as + I am not of this world.

> [Note: Col. 0471. Before *ego*, “and” is absent also in the Greek text.]

17. Sanctify them into truth. Your word is true.

18. Just as + you sent me into + this + world, I also sent them into this world.

> [Note: Col. 0471. Before “me,” *you* is absent likewise in the Greek text.]  
> [Note: Col. 0471. Adds “this,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τοῦτον.]

19. And for their sake I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified in truth.

20. I do not pray for these only, but also for those . . . who will believe through their word

21. in me: that all may be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be in us +, that the world may thus believe that you sent me.

> [Note: Col. 0472. Mm.: “that all may be one, just as we are one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they may be one in us.” Vulg.: “that all may be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be one in us.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0471. Before *sint*, “one” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

22. And the glory which you gave me, I have given them; that they may be one, just as we are one.

> [Note: Col. 0472. Mm.: “I give them.” Vulg.: “I gave them.”]

23. I in them, [Col. 0473] and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that this world may know that . . . you sent me and that I loved . . . them as you loved me.

> [Note: Col. 0473. So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἠγάπησα, “I loved.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0473. Gat.: “you loved them.” Vulg.: “you loved them.”]

24. Father, those whom you gave me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me, that they may see my glory which you gave me; because you loved me before the foundation . . . of the world.

25. Righteous Father, this world did not know you; but I knew you, and these knew that you

26. sent me. And I made your name known to them, and will make it known, that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.

## CHAPTER XVIII
1. After he had said these things, Jesus went out with his disciples across the torrent of the Kidron, where there was a garden [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek: τοῦ Κέδρου, “of the Kidron.”], into which he entered with his disciples. 2. Judas too knew that place, because Jesus had often met there with his disciples. 3. Judas therefore, having received a cohort from the chief priests and attendants from the Pharisees, came there with lanterns, lamps, and weapons. [Note: Mm.: “The attendants sent from the chief priests and Pharisees came there.” Vulgate: “and attendants from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there.”] 4. But Jesus, knowing all that was about to come upon him, went out and said to them: “Whom do you seek?” [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “What do you seek?” Vulgate: “Whom do you seek?”] 5. They answered him: “Jesus the Nazarene.” He said to them: “I am he.” Jesus was standing there, and Judas, who was about to betray him, with them. 6. Therefore, when he said to them, “I am he,” they drew back and fell to the ground. 7. Again he asked them: “Whom do you seek?” And they said to him: “Jesus the Nazarene.” 8. “I told you that I am he. Therefore, if you seek me, let these go,” [Note: Gat.: “I have already said.” Vulgate: “I said.”] 9. so that the word which he had spoken might be fulfilled: “Of those whom you gave me, I lost none.” [Note: Gat.: “might be fulfilled.” Mm.: “the saying which I spoke might be fulfilled.” Vulgate: “the saying which he spoke might be fulfilled.”] 10. Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the servant of the chief priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus. 11. Jesus therefore said to Peter: “Put the sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup which the Father has given me?” [Note: After “sword,” “your” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic.]

12. Therefore the cohort, the tribune, and the Jewish attendants seized Jesus, bound him, 13. and led him first to Annas; for he was father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was chief priest that year. 14. This was Caiaphas, who had advised the Jews: “It is expedient that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish.” [Note: Mm.: “had given.” Vulgate: “had given [this advice].”]

15. Simon Peter followed Jesus, and another disciple. That disciple was known to the chief priest and entered together with Jesus into the court of the chief priest. [Note: So also the Greek text: συνεἰσῆλθε, “entered with.”] 16. But Peter stood outside at the door. Therefore the other disciple, who was known to the chief priest, went out, spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in. 17. The servant-girl who kept the door therefore said to Peter: “Are you also one of that man’s disciples?” He said: “I am not.” 18. Now the servants and attendants were standing by coals, because it was cold; and Peter too was standing with them, warming himself.

19. The chief priest therefore questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching. 20. Jesus answered: “I have spoken openly to this world. I have always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews assemble; and I have said nothing in secret. 21. Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them; behold, they know what I said.” 22. When he had said these things, one of the attendants standing by struck Jesus on the face, saying: “Do you answer the chief priest thus?” 23. Jesus answered him: “If I spoke wrongly, testify concerning the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike me?” [Note: Mm.: “I bear witness concerning.” Vulgate: “bear witness concerning.”] 24. Annas therefore sent him bound to Caiaphas the chief priest.

25. Simon Peter was standing and warming himself by the fire. They therefore said to him: “Are you also one of his disciples?” But he denied it and said: “I am not.” 26. One of the servants of the chief priest, a kinsman of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said: “Did I not see you in the garden with him?” 27. Again Peter denied it, and immediately a cock crowed.

28. They therefore brought Jesus, sent from Caiaphas the chief priest, into the praetorium. It was morning; and they themselves did not enter the praetorium, lest they should be defiled, but so that they might eat the Passover. 29. Pilate therefore went outside to them and said: “What accusation do you bring against this man?” 30. The Jews answered and said to him: “If this man were not an evildoer, we would never have delivered him to you.” 31. Pilate said to them: “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.” The Jews said to him: “It is not permitted to us to put anyone to death,” [Note: Gat.: “Therefore the Jews [said]: To us.” Mm.: “Therefore they said to him: To us.” Vulgate: “Therefore the Jews said to him: To us.”] 32. so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which he had spoken, signifying by what death he was to die. [Note: Mm.: “that he was to die a death.” Vulgate: “by what death he was to die.”]

33. Pilate therefore entered the praetorium again, summoned Jesus, and said to him: “Are you the King of the Jews?” 34. Jesus answered: “Do you say this of yourself, or did others tell you about me?” 35. Pilate answered: “Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests delivered you to me. What have you done?” 36. Jesus answered: “My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my attendants would fight, lest I be delivered to the Jews; but now my kingdom is not from here.” [Note: Gat.: “from the world … lest I be delivered.” Vulgate: “from this world … that I might not be delivered.”] 37. Pilate said: “Then are you King of the Jews?” Jesus answered: “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into this world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.” 38. Pilate said to him: “What is truth?” And when he had said this, he again went outside to the Jews and said to them: “I find no charge in him. [Note: Gat.: “went out to the Jews and says to them … I find no cause of death in him.” Mm.: “outside to the Jews, and says to them: I …” Vulgate: “went out to the Jews and said to them: I find no charge in him.”] 39. But you have a custom that I should release one man to you. Do you therefore wish me to release the King of the Jews?” [Note: Mm.: “You have among yourselves a custom, that I should release to you one prisoner at Passover.” Vulgate: “You have a custom, that I should release one to you at Passover.”] 40. But they all cried out, saying: “Not this man, but Barabbas.” Now Barabbas was a robber.

## Chapter XIX

[Col. 0481]

1. Pilate therefore took Jesus and scourged him. 2. The soldiers, plaiting a crown of thorns, placed it upon his head; and they clothed him in a purple garment. 3. They came up to him, saying: “Hail, King of the Jews!” And they struck him on the face. 4. Pilate went outside again and said to them: “Behold, I bring him out to you, so that you may know that I find no charge in him.” [Note: Gat.: “He went out again.” This verse is absent in Mm. Vulgate: “Therefore he went out again.”] 5. Jesus therefore went outside, wearing the thorny crown and the purple robe. [Note: “outside” is added, as likewise in the Greek text, ἔξω.] 6. When the priests and attendants saw him, they cried out: “Crucify him!” Pilate said to them: “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no guilt in him.” [Note: Mm.: “I find no charge.” Vulgate: “I find no charge in him.”] 7. The Jews answered: “We have a law, and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.”

8. When Pilate heard this word, he was more afraid. 9. He entered the praetorium again and said to Jesus: “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer. 10. Pilate therefore said to him: “Do you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you and authority to release you?” 11. Jesus answered him and said: “You would have no authority over me at all, unless it had been given you from above. Therefore he who delivered me to you has the greater sin.” [The manuscript is damaged: “Non haberes potestatem . . me nullam, nisi data tibi fuisset de sus . . . Propter hoc, qui me tibi tradidit, magnum peccatum . . - bet.”] 12. From that point Pilate sought to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying: “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend; for everyone who makes himself king opposes Caesar.”

13. When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat upon the judgment seat at the place called Lithostrotus, but in Hebrew Gennaesa. [Note: So also the Greek text: εἰς τόπον, “into a place.” Gat.: Lithostratus. Mm.: Lithosstrotus. Vulgate: Lithostrotos.] 14. Now it was the preparation of the Passover, about the sixth hour; and he said to the Jews: “Behold your king.” [Note: Gat.: “he says to them: Behold.” Mm.: “he says to the Jews.” Vulgate: “he says to the Jews: Behold.”] 15. But they cried out: “Away! Away! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them: “Shall I crucify your king?” The priests answered: “We have no king but Caesar.” [Note: So also the Greek text: ἐκραύγασαν, “they cried out.”] 16. Then he delivered him to them to be crucified. They therefore took Jesus, [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis and Greek οὖν, “therefore.”] 17. and, bearing his cross for himself, he came to the place called the Place of Calvary, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha, 18. where they crucified him, and with him two other robbers, one on either side, Jesus in the middle. [Note: Gat.: “Golgotha, and with him.” Vulgate: “Golgotha, where they crucified him, and with him.”]

19. Pilate also wrote a title and placed it above the cross. It was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews.” 20. Many Jews therefore read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin. 21. The chief priests and rulers of the Jews therefore said to Pilate: “Do not write, ‘King of the Jews,’ but, ‘He himself said, I am King of the Jews.’” 22. Pilate answered them: “What I have written, I have written.”

23. Therefore, when the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took his garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier. Now the tunic was from above, but woven in one piece [uncertain; manuscript damaged]. 24. They therefore said to one another: “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be,” so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “They divided my garments among themselves, and cast a lot upon my clothing.” [Note: Mm.: “and upon the garment.” Vulgate: “and upon my garment.”] 25. But beside the cross of Jesus stood his mother Mary, and his mother’s sister, Mary of Cleophas. 26. When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing by, he said to his mother: “Woman, behold your son.” [Note: So also the Greek text: παρεστῶτα, “standing by.”] 27. Then he said to the disciple: “Behold your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own household. [Note: Gat.: “Behold my mother.” A recent hand: “your.” Vulgate: “Behold your mother.”]

28. After this, Jesus, seeing that all things were completed, so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled, said: “I thirst.” [Note: Mm.: “that already all things … says.” Vulgate: “that all things … said.”] 29. A vessel full of vinegar was set there. Having put it around hyssop, they offered it to his mouth. 30. When he had received the vinegar, he said: “It is finished.” And bowing his head, he gave up his spirit.

31. Therefore, because it was the pure supper [probably OCR corruption for *parasceve*, “Preparation”], the Jews asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken down from the cross, lest the bodies should remain on the cross on the Sabbath—for that Sabbath day was great. [Note: Gat.: “and that they might take [them] away.” Vulgate: “and that they might be taken away.”] 32. Therefore the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man, and likewise of the other who had been crucified with him. [Note: According to the Greek text: συσταυρωθέντος, “one crucified together with [him].”] 33. But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs. [Note: Gat.: “and they saw … and did not break.” Vulgate: “when they saw … they did not break.”] 34. But one of the soldiers struck his side with a spear, and immediately blood 35. and water came out. He who saw it bears witness, and his testimony is true. He himself knows that he speaks what is true, so that you too may believe. [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “that he truly speaks.” Vulgate: “that he speaks true things.”] 36. For these things happened to him, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “You shall not break a bone of him.” [Manuscript damaged.] 37. And again another Scripture says: “They saw him whom they pierced.”

38. After these things Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus but hidden because of fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body; and Pilate permitted it. They therefore came and took him away. [Manuscript damaged.] 39. Nicodemus also came—he who had formerly come to Jesus by night—bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds. [Manuscript damaged.] 40. They took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the Jewish custom of burial. [Note: Gat.: “him in linen cloths … as is the custom.” Vulgate: “it in linen cloths … as is the custom.”] 41. Now in the place where he had been crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new tomb [the remainder is substantially lost]. 42. There they placed Jesus, because of the Jewish Preparation. [Note: Gat.: “because of the pure supper.” Mm.: “where they placed [him].” Vulgate: “because of the Jewish Preparation … they placed [him].”]

## Chapter XX

1. But on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came to the tomb while it was still dark, and saw the stone removed from the tomb. [Note: Gat.: “while it was still dark, and she saw.” Vulgate: “while it was still dark, to the tomb, and she saw.” At the same place Mm.: “the stone removed from the entrance of the tomb.” Vulgate: “the stone removed from the tomb.”] 2. And she ran and came to Simon [name damaged], and [to] the [other] disciple [text damaged] … where they had placed him. 3. Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out and were going to the tomb. 4. The two were running together; but that disciple ran ahead more quickly than Peter and came first to the tomb. 5. And stooping down, he saw the linen cloths lying there, yet he did not enter. 6. Simon Peter followed him and entered the tomb, and saw the linen cloths 7. lying there, and the napkin, which had been set apart, rolled up in one place. 8. Then the other disciple also entered, who had come first to the tomb; he saw 9. and believed. For they did not yet know the Scripture, that he had to rise from the dead. [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “and the other disciple.” Vulgate: “and that disciple.”] 10. Therefore the disciples went away to their own homes.

11. But Mary stood weeping beside the tomb; and as she wept, she looked into the tomb. 12. There she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where Jesus had lain. 13. They said to the woman: “Why do you weep?” She said to them: “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have placed him.” [Note: Gat.: “my Lord, and we do not know.” Mm.: “my Lord from the tomb, and I do not know.” Vulgate: “my Lord, and I do not know.”] 14. Having said these things, she turned back and saw [Jesus; text damaged], but did not know that it was Jesus. 15. Jesus said to her: “Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek?” Thinking that he was the gardener, she said to him: “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have placed him, and I will take him away.” [Note: Gat.: “What? Whom?” Vulgate: “Why do you weep? Whom?”] 16. Jesus said to her: “Mary.” She stood and said to him: “Rabboni” [Ῥαββουνί], which means “Master.” [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “And she rushed (or ran) to touch him. Jesus says to her.” Vulgate: “Jesus says to her.”] 17. Jesus said to her: “Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and tell them: ‘I ascend to my Father and your Father, my God and your God.’” 18. Mary Magdalene came announcing to the disciples: “I have seen the Lord,” and that he had said these things to her.

19. But when evening had come on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were because of fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in their midst and said to them: “Peace to you.” [Note: “The disciples because of … in their midst, and he said to them: Peace to you.” Vulgate: “the disciples gathered together because of … in their midst, and he said to them: Peace to you.”] 20. Having said this, he showed them his hands and side; and the disciples rejoiced. [Note: Gat.: “and his side.” Vulgate: “and his side.”] 21. Jesus therefore said to them again: “Peace to you. As the Father sent me, I also send you.” 22. He breathed upon them and said: “Receive the Holy Spirit. 23. If you forgive anyone’s sins, they shall be forgiven him; if you retain anyone’s, they shall be retained.” [Note: Gat.: “they shall be forgiven them; and those whose sins you have retained are retained.” Vulgate: “they are forgiven them; and those whose sins you have retained are retained.”]

24. Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called Didymus, was not with them when 25. Jesus came. The other disciples therefore said to him: “We have seen the Lord.” But he said to them: “Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, put my finger into the place of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I shall not believe.” 26. Eight days later the disciples were again inside together, and Thomas with them. Jesus came while the doors were shut, stood in the midst, and said: “Peace to you.” [Note: Mm.: “Peace to you.” Vulgate: “Peace to you.”] 27. Then he said to Thomas: “Put forth your finger here and see my hands; put your hand into my side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.” [Note: Gat.: “then to Thomas: put forth your finger.” Vulgate: “then he says to Thomas: put in your finger.”] 28. Thomas answered and said to him: “You are my Lord and 29. my God.” Jesus said to him: “Because you have seen, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.” [Note: Gat.: “You have seen me and believed; blessed are those who have not seen me.” Vulgate: “You have seen me, Thomas, and believed; blessed are those who have not seen.”]

30. Jesus indeed performed many other signs in the presence of his disciples which are not written in this book. 31. But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that, believing, you may have life in his name. [Note: Gat.: “that Jesus … that, believing, you may have eternal life in.” Vulgate: “that Jesus … that, believing, you may have life in.”]

## Chapter XXI

1. After these things Jesus showed himself again to his disciples at the Sea of Tiberias. [Note: “his” is added, also by Codex Cantabrigiensis and Greek αὐτοῦ.] 2. Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples of his were together. [Note: Gat.: “from Channan.” Vulgate: “from Cana.”] 3. Simon Peter said to them: “I am going fishing.” They said to him: “We too are coming with you.” They went out and got into the boat; and that night they caught nothing. 4. But when morning had come, Jesus stood on the shore; yet the disciples did not know that it was Jesus. [Note: Gat.: “But when morning had already come, he stood on.” Vulgate: “But when morning had come, Jesus stood on.”] 5. He said to them: “Have you anything to eat?” They answered him: 6. “No.” But he said to them: “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it, and they were no longer able to draw the net because of the multitude of fish. [Note: The word “side” is added, also in Greek μέρη. Gat.: “Cast the net on the ship, and you will find. Therefore they cast it, and now … because of the multitude.” Mm. contains a divergent passage: “You will find. They said: Master, having laboured all night, we caught nothing; but at your word we shall cast the net. Therefore they cast the nets, and now …” Vulgate: “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find. Therefore they cast it, and now … because of the multitude.”] 7. Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter: “It is the Lord.” Simon Peter, hearing that it was the Lord, girded his tunic around himself, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea. 8. But the other disciples came in the boat, for they were not far from land, about twenty cubits [reading damaged], dragging the net of fish. [Note: Mm.: “into the sea; for they were not …” Vulgate: “for they were not …”]

9. When they came down to land, they saw glowing coals, fish laid upon them, and bread. 10. Jesus said to them: “Bring some of the fish which you have caught.” 11. Simon Peter went up and drew the net onto land, full of one hundred and fifty-three large fish. And although there were so many, the net was not torn. [Note: Gat.: “though there were so many.” Vulgate: “though there were so many.”] 12. Jesus said to them: “Come, eat breakfast.” And none of his disciples dared ask him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord. [Note: Mm.: “ask him, ‘You …’ [knowing] that he was Lord.” Vulgate: “ask him, ‘You …’ [knowing] that he is Lord.”] 13. Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them, and likewise the fish. [Note: Before “came,” “and” is absent, also in the Greek text. Gat.: “took bread and gave it to them.” Mm.: “took bread, blessed it, and gave it to them.” Vulgate: “takes bread and gives it to them.”] 14. This was now the third time Jesus showed himself to his disciples after he rose from the dead. [Note: Gat.: “Jesus showed himself with the disciples.” Mm.: “he was manifested with the disciples.” Vulgate: “Jesus was manifested to the disciples.”]

15. Therefore, when they had breakfasted, Jesus said to Peter: “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He said to him: “Certainly, Lord.” He said to him: “Feed my sheep.” [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “But he said: Certainly … Jesus said to him.” Vulgate: “He said to him: Certainly … He said to him.” Codex Cantabrigiensis and Greek πρόβατα: “sheep.”] 16. Again he said to him: “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He said to him: “Certainly, Lord.” 17. He said to him: “Feed my sheep.” He said to him a third time: “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because he said to him a third time, “Do you love me?” He said to him: “Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you.” He said to him: “Feed my sheep.” [Note: Gat. and Mm.: “He says to him: Feed my lambs.” Vulgate: “He said to him: Feed my sheep.”]

18. “Amen, amen, I say to you: when you were … younger, you girded yourself, … where you wished; but when you have grown old, you will stretch out … hands, … will gird you … where … [you do not wish].” [The manuscript is severely damaged.] 19. He said this, signifying by what death he was to glorify God. Then he said to him: “Follow me.” [Note: Gat.: “would glorify the Lord.” Vulgate: “would glorify God.”]

20. Peter turned and saw the disciple [whom] Jesus loved following, who had also reclined at supper upon Jesus’ breast and had said: “Lord, [who] is it who 21. [will betray] you?” Seeing this man, Peter said [to Jesus]: “Lord, what [will] this man [do]?” [Text damaged.] 22. “[If] I will [that he] remain until I come, what is it to you? Meanwhile, you follow me.” 23. This saying therefore went out among the brothers that that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say, “He does not die”; rather, “Thus I will that he remain until I come.” [Note: Gat.: “The saying therefore went out … that he would not die … what is that to you? You, follow me.” Vulgate: “The saying therefore went out … that he does not die … what is that to you?” The Greek has ἔρχομαι, “I come.”]

24. This is the disciple who bears witness concerning Jesus and who wrote these things; and we know that his testimony is true. [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis and Greek καὶ ὁ γράψας, “and the one who wrote.”] 25. Jesus also did many other things, which, if they were written down one by one, I suppose that not even the world itself could contain the books that would be written. [Note: Gat.: “And many other things, which are not written, which, if they were written … [the world could not] contain those books which are to be written. The Gospel according to John ends.” Vulgate: “And many other things which Jesus did, which, if they were written … [the world could not] contain the books which are to be written.”]

The Gospel according to John ends. The Gospel according to Luke begins. [Note: According to the order of Codex Cantabrigiensis: Εὐαγγέλιον κατὰ Ἰωάννην ἐτελέσθη, ἄρχεται Εὐαγγέλιον κατὰ Λουκᾶν: “The Gospel according to John has been completed; the Gospel according to Luke begins.”]

# Codex Veronensis

[Col. 0354]

## Chapter I

[Col. 0354]

1. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. [Text damaged at the end.] 2. This was in the beginning 3. with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made. What was made 4. in him was life, and the life was the light of human beings. [Note: (a) So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐστίν, “is.” Note: Variant readings of Codex no. 8 of the Church of St Gatianus at Tours, and no. 87 of Marmoutier Abbey. The former is believed to have been copied a thousand years ago, the latter eight hundred years ago. We shall designate the Codex of St Gatianus by Gat., and that of Marmoutier by Mm.] 5. And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.

6. There was a man sent from God, whose name was 7. John. He came for testimony, to bear testimony concerning the light, so that all might believe through 8. him. He was not the light, but came to bear testimony concerning the light. 9. For there was the true light, which enlightens every human being coming into this world. 10. He was in this world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him. 11. He came into his own possessions, and his own did not receive him. 12. But to all who received him, he gave authority to become children of God—to those believing in his name—13. who was born not from blood, nor from the will of the flesh, nor from the will of a man, but from God. 14. And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us; and we saw his honour, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. 15. John bears witness and cries out: “This is he of whom I said: He who comes after me has been made before me, because he was before me.” [Note: After “cries out,” “saying” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

16. Because from his fullness we all received grace for 17. grace. For the law was given through Moses; but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. 18. No one has ever seen God; except the only-begotten Son, who is in the Father’s bosom—he has made him known. [Note: So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὅτι, “because.” From this point, namely from ἐλάβομεν, “we received,” through the words Ῥαββί, “Rabbi,” in chapter III, verse 26, everything is absent in the Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis; and in the Latin Cantabrigiensis through verse 16.]

19. And this is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him: “Who are you?” 20. He confessed and did not deny; he confessed: “I am not the Christ.” 21. They asked him again, saying: “Are you Elijah?” He said: “I am not.” “What then? Are you the Prophet?” And he answered: “No.” 22. They said: “Tell us, then, so that we may give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?” 23. He said to them: “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Make straight the way of the Lord.’” 24. And those who had been sent were from the Pharisees. They asked him and said 25. to him: “Why then do you baptize, if you are neither the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” 26. John answered them, saying: “I indeed baptize you in water for repentance; but one stands in your midst whom you do not know. 27. He is the one who comes after me, whose sandal-strap I am not worthy to untie.” 28. These things happened in Bethany across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

29. On the next day John saw Jesus coming to him and said: “Behold, the Lamb of God; behold, the one who takes away the sin of the world. 30. This is he of whom I said: ‘After me comes a man who has been made before me, because he was before me.’ 31. And I did not know him; but in order that he might be revealed to Israel, for this reason I came baptizing in water.” 32. John bore witness, saying: “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and remaining upon him. 33. And I did not know him; but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me: ‘He upon whom you see the Spirit of the Lord descending and remaining, he is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ 34. And I saw, and bore witness that he is the chosen Son of God.”

35. On the next day John again stood with two of his disciples. 36. Looking at Jesus walking, he said: “Behold, the Lamb of God.” 37. The two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus. 38. Jesus turned, saw them following him, and said: “What do you seek?” They said to him: “Rabbi”—which is translated “Teacher”—“where are you staying?” 39. He said to them: “Come and see.” They came, saw where he was staying, and remained with him that day; for it was about the tenth hour. 40. Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who had heard John and followed him. 41. In the morning he found his brother Simon and said to him: “We have found the Messiah,” which is translated “Christ.” 42. He brought him to Jesus. Looking at him, Jesus said: “You are Simon, son of John; you shall be called Cephas,” which is translated “Peter.”

43. On the next day he wished to go into Galilee and found Philip. Jesus said to him: “Follow 44. me.” Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and 45. Peter. Philip found Nathanael and said to him: “We have found Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth—the one of whom Moses wrote in the law, and the prophets also.” 46. Nathanael said to him: “Can anything good be from Nazareth?” Philip said to him: “Come and see.” 47. Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him and said of him: “Behold, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.” 48. Nathanael said to him: “How do you know me?” Jesus answered and said to him: “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I knew you.” 49. Nathanael answered him: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the king of Israel.” 50. Jesus answered and said to him: “Because I said to you, ‘I saw you under the fig tree,’ do you believe? You shall see greater things than these.” 51. And he said to him: “Amen, amen, I say to you: you shall see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.”

## Chapter II

1. On the third day a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee, and Jesus’ mother was there. 2. Jesus too, with his disciples, was invited to the wedding. 3. They had no wine, because the wedding wine had run out. Jesus’ mother said to him: “They have no wine.” 4. Jesus said to her: “What is that to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.” 5. His mother said to the servants: “Whatever he says to you, do it.” 6. There were stone water-jars set there for the Jewish purification, each holding two or three measures. 7. Jesus said to them: “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the top. 8. Jesus said to them: “Draw some now and take it to the steward of the feast.” And they took it. 9. When the steward tasted the water that had become wine and did not know where it came from—though the servants who had drawn the water knew, and, seeing what had happened, marvelled—the steward called the bridegroom 10. and said to him: “Every person first sets out the good wine, and, when they have become drunk, then the inferior wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.” 11. Jesus performed this first sign in Cana of Galilee; he revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.

12. After these things he went down into Capernaum, he and his mother and his brothers; and they remained there not many days. [Note: “into” is added, also in the Greek εἰς. Note: So also the Greek οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας, “not many days.”] 13. The Passover of the Jews was near, 14. and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. In the temple he found sellers of oxen, sheep, and doves, and money-changers sitting there. 15. Making something like a whip from cords, he drove them all out of the temple, including the sheep and oxen; he poured out the money of the money-changers and overturned their tables. [Note: So the Ethiopic version and Origen: τὰ κέρματα, “coins.”] 16. He said to those selling doves: “Take these things away from here. Do not make my Father’s house a house of trade.” 17. His disciples remembered that it was written: “Zeal for your house has consumed me.” 18. The Jews answered him and said: “What sign do you show us, that you do these things?” 19. Jesus answered and said to them: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” 20. The Jews therefore said: “This temple has been built forty-six years, and will you raise it in three days?” 21. But he spoke of the temple of his body. 22. Therefore, when he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus had spoken.

23. But while he was in Jerusalem at the Passover feast, many believed in his name, seeing the signs which he was doing. [Note: “in” is added, with the Greek ἐν.] 24. But Jesus did not entrust himself to them, because he knew all people, 25. and because he had no need that anyone should bear testimony about a person; for he himself knew what was in a person.

## Chapter III
1. Now there was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. 2. He came to him by night and said to him: “Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; for no one can do these signs which you do unless God is with him.” 3. Jesus answered and said to him: “Amen, I say to you, unless someone has been born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” 4. Nicodemus said to him: “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?” 5. Jesus answered: “Amen, amen, I say to you, unless someone has been born of water and Spirit, he cannot be born into the kingdom of God. 6. What is born of flesh is flesh, because it is born of flesh; and what is born of spirit [Note: [Col. 0367] After *Spirit*, *holy* is lacking, also in the Greek text.] is spirit. 7. Do not marvel that I said to you: You must be born again. 8. The Spirit breathes where it wills, and you hear its sound, but you do not know whence it comes or where it goes; so it is with everyone who is born of water and Spirit.” 9. Nicodemus answered and said to him: “And how can these things happen?” 10. Jesus answered and said to him: “Are you the teacher of Israel [Note: [Col. 0367] So too the Greek text: τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ‘of Israel.’], and do not know these things? 11. Amen, amen, I say to you: we speak what we know and testify to what we have seen, yet you do not receive our testimony. 12. If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? 13. No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven. 14. And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, 15. so that everyone who believes in him may not perish, but may have eternal life. 16. For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life. 17. For God did not send his Son into this world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him. 18. Whoever believes in him is not judged [Note: [Col. 0367] So also the Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis.]; but whoever does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God. 19. And this is the judgment: that light came into this world, and people loved darkness rather than light, for their works were evil. 20. For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his works be exposed. 21. But whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be made manifest, because they have been done in God.

22. After these things Jesus and his disciples went into the land of Judaea, and he remained there with them. 23. Now John was baptizing at Aenon, near Salim, because there was much water there; and people came and were baptized. 24. For John had not yet been cast into prison. 25. Then a dispute arose between John’s disciples and Jews concerning purification. 26. And they came to John and said to him: “Rabbi, the one who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you bore testimony—behold, he is baptizing, and all are coming to him.” 27. John answered, saying: “A person cannot receive anything unless it has been given him from above. 28. You yourselves bear me witness that I said: I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him. 29. He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. This joy of mine, therefore, is complete. 30. He must increase, but I must decrease. 31. He who comes from above is above all. But he who is from the earth is earthly and speaks from the earth. He who comes from heaven [Note: [Col. 0371] After *comes*, *is above all* is lacking, as is *and*, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] testifies [Note: [Col. 0371] Before *testifies*, *this* is lacking also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] to what he has seen and heard, and no one receives his testimony. 33. But whoever receives his testimony has sealed this: that God is true. 34. For he whom God sent speaks the words of God; for he gives the Spirit not by measure. 35. The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hands. 36. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; but whoever does not believe the Son shall not see eternal life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.

## Chapter IV

1. Therefore, when Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making [Col. 0372] more disciples than John, and 2. baptizing—although Jesus himself [Note: [Col. 0371] Adds *himself*, also the Greek text: αὐτός.] did not baptize, but his disciples did—3. he left Judaea [Note: [Col. 0371] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: γῆν, “land.”] and went again into Galilee. 4. Now he had to pass through Samaria. 5. Therefore he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the estate which Jacob gave to his son Joseph. 6. Jacob’s spring was there. Jesus therefore, wearied by the journey, sat down by the spring. It was about the sixth hour.

7. A woman from Samaria came to draw water. 8. Jesus said to her: “Give me a drink.” For his disciples had gone into the city to buy food. 9. Therefore the Samaritan woman said to him [Note: [Col. 0371] After *woman*, *that* is lacking, also in the Greek text.]: “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask a drink from me, since I am a Samaritan woman?” 10. Jesus answered and said to her: “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would rather have asked him, and he would have given you living water.” 11. The woman said to him: “Sir, you have neither a vessel for drawing water, and the well is deep. Whence [Note: [Col. 0373] *Therefore* is wanting after *whence*, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] do you have living water? 12. Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and himself drank from it, as did his sons and his livestock?” 13. Jesus answered and said to her: “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again; but whoever drinks of the water which I shall give him will never thirst. 14. Rather, the water which I shall give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into eternal life.” 15. The woman said to him: “Sir, give me this water, so that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw it.” 16. Jesus said to her: “Go, call your husband, and come here.” 17. The woman answered and said to him: “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her: “You have spoken well in saying, ‘I have no husband’ [Note: [Col. 0373] So also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔχεις, “you have.”]; 18. for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband. This you have spoken truly.” 19. The woman said to him: “Sir, I see that you are a prophet [Note: [Col. 0373] After *are*, *you* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]. 20. Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that in Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 0373] Adds *in*, likewise the Greek text: ἐν.] is the place where one must worship.” 21. Jesus said to her: “Believe me, woman: the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. 22. You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from Judaea. 23. But the hour is coming, and now is, when true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. Indeed, the Father seeks such persons to worship him 24. in spirit. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.” 25. The woman said to him: “I know that Messiah is coming—the one called Christ. When he comes, he will announce all things to us.” 26. Jesus said to her: “I am he, the one speaking with you.”

27. And immediately his disciples came, and they marvelled that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said to him [Note: [Col. 0375] Adds *to him*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτῷ.], “What do you seek?” or, “Why are you speaking with her?” 28. Therefore the woman left her water jar, went into the city, and said to the people [Note: [Col. 0375] Before *people*, *to them* is lacking, likewise in the Greek text.]: 29. “Come and see a man who told me everything that I did. Could this be the Christ?” 30. And [Note: [Col. 0375] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καί, “and.”] they went out of the city and came to him.

31. Meanwhile the disciples urged him, saying: “Rabbi, eat.” 32. But he said to them: “I have food to eat which you do not know.” 33. Therefore the disciples said to one another: “Has anyone brought him something to eat?” 34. Jesus said to them: “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work. 35. Do you not say, ‘There are still four months, and then the harvest comes’? Behold, I say to you: lift up your eyes and look upon the fields, because they are white for harvest [Note: [Col. 0375] After *are*, *already* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]. 36. Already [Note: [Col. 0375] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἤδη, “already.”] the reaper receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. 37. For in this the saying is true: one sows and another reaps. 38. I sent you to reap that for which you did not labour; others have laboured, and you have entered into their labour.”

39. Now many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the testimony of the woman who declared: “He told me everything that I did.” 40. Therefore, when the Samaritans came to him, they asked [Note: [Col. 0377] So also the Greek text: ἠρώτων, “they were asking.”] him to remain with them. 41. And he remained there two days. And many more believed because of his word. 42. They said to the woman: “We no longer believe because of your testimony [Note: [Col. 0377] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: μαρτυρίαν, “testimony.”]; for we ourselves have heard, and know that this man is truly the Saviour of the world.”

43. After the two days he departed [Note: [Col. 0377] Before *departed*, *went out* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] from there into Galilee. 44. For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honour in his own country. 45.
