When he came into Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen everything which he did in Jerusalem at the feast; for they too had come to the feast.

46. Therefore he came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made water into wine. There was [Note: [Col. 0377] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but/and.”] a certain royal official whose son was sick at Capernaum. 47. When he heard that Jesus had come from Judaea into Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, for he was beginning to die. 48. Jesus said to him: “Unless you see signs and wonders, you do not believe.” 49. The royal official said to him: “Sir, come down before my child dies” [Note: [Col. 0379] After *child*, *my* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]. 50. Jesus said to him: “Go; your son lives.” And [Note: [Col. 0379] Adds *and*, likewise the Greek text: καί.] the man believed the word which Jesus spoke to him, and went away. 51. As he was already going down, his servants met him and announced to him [Note: [Col. 0379] Adds *to him*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτῷ.] that your son lives [Note: [Col. 0379] So also the Greek text: ὁ παῖς σου ζῇ, “your child lives.”]. 52. Therefore he asked them at what hour he had become better. And they said: “Yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him.” 53. Then the father knew that it was at that hour [Note: [Col. 0379] *That hour* is in the ablative case, with the verb *was* omitted. So too the Greek text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ (ἐν ᾗ), “at that hour [in which].”] when Jesus said to him, “Your son lives”; and he himself believed, with his entire household. 54. This Jesus again performed as his second sign, when he came from Judaea into Galilee.

## Chapter V

1. After these things there was a feast day of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem, to the lower part 2. of the pool called in Hebrew Bethzatha, having five porticoes. 3. In these lay [Note: [Col. 0379] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: κατέκειντο, “were lying.” In that same Codex Cantabrigiensis, *many* is lacking.] crowds of sick people—blind, lame, withered, paralysed [Note: [Col. 0379] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: παραλυτικῶν, “paralytics.”]—waiting for the movement of the water. 4. For an angel came down and stirred [Col. 0382] the water [Note: [Col. 0381] So also the Greek text: ἐτάραττε, “was stirring.”]. Whoever first descended into the pool became well, whatever disease held him. 5. There was there a man [Note: [Col. 0381] After *man*, *a certain* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] who had been in his infirmity for thirty-eight years. 6. When Jesus saw him lying there, knowing that he had already been there a long time, he said to him: “Do you wish to become well?” 7. The sick man answered him and said: “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water has been stirred; for while I am coming, another goes down before me.” 8. Jesus said to him: “Rise, take up your mat, and walk.” 9. Immediately that man became well; and he rose [Note: [Col. 0381] Adds *and rose*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἐγερθείς.], took up his mat, and walked. Now it was the Sabbath on that day. 10. Therefore the Jews said to the man who had been healed: “It is the Sabbath, and [Note: [Col. 0381] Adds *and*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καί.] it is not lawful for you to carry your mat.” 11. He answered them: “The one who made me well said to me: ‘Take up your mat and walk.’” 13. But the sick man [Note: [Col. 0381] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ δὲ ἀσθενῶν, “but the sick man.”] did not know who he was. For Jesus had withdrawn immediately, because there was a crowd in that place. 14. Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: “Behold, you have become well. Sin no more, lest something worse happen to you.” 15. And [Note: [Col. 0381] Adds *and*, also the Greek text: καί.] the man went away and told the Jews that Jesus was the one who had made him well. 16. For this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the Sabbath.

But Jesus answered them, saying: 17. “My Father is working until now, and I am working.” 18. For this reason [Note: [Col. 0383] So also the Greek text: διὰ τοῦτο, “for this reason.” In the same place, *therefore* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] the Jews sought all the more to kill him: because he not only was breaking the Sabbath, but also said that God was his Father, making himself equal to God. Jesus answered and said to them: 19. “Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son can do nothing of himself except what he sees the Father doing; for whatever things that one does, the Son likewise does these same things. 20. For the Father loves the Son and shows him all things which he himself does; and he has shown him greater works, so that you may marvel. 21. For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wills. 22. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, 23. so that all may honour the Son just as they honour the Father. Whoever does not honour the Son does not honour the Father who sent him. 24. Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life. 25. Amen, amen, I say to you: the hour is coming when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. 26. For as the Father has life in himself, so he has granted the Son also to have life in himself; 27. and he has given him authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man. 28. Do not marvel at this, because the hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs shall hear his voice [Note: [Col. 0385] So also the Greek text: αὐτοῦ, “his.”], 29. and shall arise: those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; but those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment. 30. I can do nothing of myself. As I hear, so I judge; and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will, but the will of him who sent me—the Father [Note: [Col. 0385] Adds *Father*, also the Greek text: πατρός.].

31. “If I bear testimony about myself, my testimony is not true. 32. Another is the one who testifies concerning me, and I know that the testimony which he bears concerning me is true [Note: [Col. 0385] *His* is added in Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτοῦ.]. 33. You sent to John, and he bore testimony to the truth. 34. But I do not receive testimony from a human being; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved. 35. He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing for an hour to rejoice in his light. 36. But I have testimony greater than John’s. For the works which the Father has given me to accomplish—the very works which I do [Note: [Col. 0385] Before *do*, *I* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]—bear testimony concerning me that the Father sent me. 37. And the Father who sent me himself bears testimony concerning me. You have never heard his voice, nor seen his form, 38. and you do not have his word abiding in you, because you do not believe the one whom he sent. 39. Search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and they are those which bear testimony concerning me. In them you think you have life; these are what testify concerning me. 40. Yet you are unwilling to come to me so that you may have life. 41. I do not receive honour from human beings. 42. But I have known you: you do not have the love of God in yourselves. 43. I have come in my Father’s name, and you did not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you receive him. 44. How can you believe, when you receive honour from one another and do not seek the honour of him who alone is? 45. Do not think that I shall accuse you before the Father [Note: [Col. 0387] So also the Greek text: κατηγορήσω, “I shall accuse.”]. There is one who accuses you: Moses, in whom you have hoped [Note: [Col. 0387] According to the Greek text: εἰς ὃν ὑμεῖς ἠλπίκατε, “in whom you have hoped.”]. 46. For if you believed Moses, perhaps you would believe me also, for he wrote concerning me. 47. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”

## Chapter VI

1. After these things Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee, into the region [Note: [Col. 0387] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰς τὰ μέρη, “into the parts/region.”] of Tiberias. 2. A great crowd followed [Note: [Col. 0387] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but/and.”] him because they saw the signs which he performed on the sick. 3. Therefore Jesus went up on the mountain and sat there with his disciples. 4. Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.

5. Therefore, lifting up his eyes and seeing that a great crowd was coming to him, Jesus said to Philip: “Where shall we buy bread for these people to eat?” 6. He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was going to do. 7. Philip answered him: “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough for them, for each to receive even a little” [Note: [Col. 0389] After *little*, *something* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]. 8. One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him: 9. “There is a boy here [Note: [Col. 0389] After *boy*, *one* is omitted, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] who has five barley loaves and two fish; but what are these among so many?” 10. But [Note: [Col. 0389] So also the Greek text: δέ.] Jesus said: “Make the people recline.” There was much grass in that place. So the men reclined, about five thousand in number. 11. Then [Note: [Col. 0389] So also the Greek text: δέ.] Jesus took the loaves and, having given thanks, distributed them [Note: [Col. 0389] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ηὐχαρίστησε καὶ ἔδωκε, “and he gave thanks and gave.”] to those reclining; likewise also the fish, as much as they wished. [Note: [Col. 0389] Adds: “to his disciples, and the disciples [gave]”; likewise the Greek text: τοῖς μαθηταῖς, οἱ δὲ μαθηταί. Erasmus, Zeger, and Grotius long ago observed that these words had been added from the other Gospels.] 12. When they had been filled, he said to the disciples: “Gather the fragments left over, so that none of them may perish” [Note: [Col. 0389] So also the Greek text: ἵνα μή τι … ἀπόληται, “that nothing may perish”; Codex Cantabrigiensis adds ἐξ αὐτῶν, “of them.”]. 13. Therefore they gathered them [Note: [Col. 0389] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ.], and filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley loaves, left over by those who had eaten. 14. Therefore, when those people saw the sign which he had done [Note: [Col. 0389] After *done*, *Jesus* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.], they said: “This is truly the prophet who is to come into the world.” 15. Jesus, knowing that the crowds were about to come and seize him in order to make him king [Note: [Col. 0389] So also the Greek text: καὶ ἁρπάζειν αὐτὸν ἳνα ποιήσωσιν, “and seize him in order that they might make [him].”], withdrew [Note: [Col. 0389] So also the Greek text: ἀνεχώρησε, “withdrew.”] again to the mountain alone.

16. When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea. 17. They embarked in a boat and were going across the sea to Capernaum. Darkness had already fallen, and Jesus had not yet come to them. 18. The sea was rising because a very strong wind was blowing. 19. When they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were greatly afraid. 20. But he said to them: “It is I; do not be afraid.” 21. Therefore they wished [Note: [Col. 0391] So also the Greek text: ἤθελον, “they wished.”] to take him into the boat; and immediately the boat came to the land toward which they were going.

22. On the next day the crowd standing on the other side of the sea saw that no other boat had been there except that one [Note: [Col. 0391] Adds *that*, likewise the Greek text: ἐκεῖνο.], and that Jesus had not entered the boat with his disciples, but his disciples had gone away alone. 23. But when other boats had arrived [Note: [Col. 0391] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐλθόντων, “having come/arrived.”] from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread which the Lord had blessed, 24. the crowds saw that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there. They themselves took boats [Note: [Col. 0391] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔλαβον ἑαυτοῖς πλοιάρια, “they took boats for themselves.”] and came to Capernaum seeking him. 25. When they found him across the sea, they said to him: “Rabbi, when did you come here?” 26. Jesus answered them and said: “Amen, amen, I say to you: you seek me not because you saw signs and wonders [Note: [Col. 0391] Adds *and wonders*, also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ τέρατα. The Gothic version also has it, apparently drawn from John 4:48.], but because you ate of the loaves and were filled. 27. Work not for food which perishes, but for food which remains unto eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For God the Father has sealed him.”

28. Therefore they said to him: “What shall we do, that we may work the works of God?” 29. Jesus answered and said to them: “This is the work of God: that you believe in him whom he has sent.” 30. Therefore they said to him: “What sign, then, do you perform, that we may see and believe you? What work do you do? 31. Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’” 32. Jesus said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: Moses did not give you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. 33. For the bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” [Note: [Col. 0393] The Greek text has διδοὺς, “giving.” I think the translator rendered *giving* as *gives* for no reason other than that the article ὁ is lacking before διδοὺς. Although it stands before καταβαίνων, “coming down,” it is omitted before διδοὺς because of the conjunction καί, “and.” The translator, therefore, taking account of the conjunction *and*, rendered it “gives.” Many similar examples of this translation occur in the Psalms.] 34. Therefore they said to him: “Lord, always give us this bread.” 35. Jesus said to them: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst. 36. But I told you that you have even seen, yet do not believe. 37. Everything which the Father gives me will come to me; and whoever comes to me I will not cast out [Note: [Col. 0393] After *cast out*, *outside* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]. 38. For I came down from heaven not to do my own will, but the will of the Father [Note: [Col. 0393] Adds *Father*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πατρός.] who sent me. 39. And this is the will of him who sent me [Note: [Col. 0393] After *me*, *Father* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]: that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me [Note: [Col. 0395] Adds *anything*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: μηδέν.], but should raise it up on the last day. 40. For this [Note: [Col. 0395] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: γάρ, “for.”] is the will of my Father [Note: [Col. 0395] After *my*, *who sent me* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life; and I will raise him up on the last day.”

41. Therefore the Jews murmured about him because he had said: “I am the bread [Note: [Col. 0395] After *bread*, *living* is lacking in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] that came down from heaven.” 42. And they said: “Is this not the son of Joseph, whose father we know? How then does he say, ‘I came down from heaven’?” 43. Jesus answered and said to them: “Do not murmur among yourselves. 44. No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I will raise him up on the last day. 45. For it is written in the Prophets: ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’ Everyone who hears [Note: [Col. 0395] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ ἀκούων, “the one hearing.”] from the Father and has learned comes to me. 46. Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God: this one sees God [Note: [Col. 0395] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τὸν θεόν, “God.”]. 47. Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life. 48. I am the bread of life. 49. Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died. 50. This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that whoever eats of it may not die, but may live. 51. I am the living bread that came down from heaven. 52. If anyone eats of this bread, he shall live forever; and the bread which I shall give is my flesh for the life of this world.”

53. Therefore the Jews disputed among themselves, saying: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?” [Note: [Col. 0397] So also the Greek text: φαγεῖν, “to eat.”] 54. Jesus said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in yourselves. 55. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood will have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. 56. For my flesh is truly food and my blood is truly drink. 57. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him. 58. As the living Father sent me, and I live through the Father, so also whoever eats my flesh lives [Note: [Col. 0397] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ζῇ, “lives.”] through me. 59. This is the bread which came down from heaven—not as your fathers ate manna and died. But whoever eats this bread lives forever.” 60. He said these things while teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.

61. Therefore many of his disciples said: “This saying is hard; who can hear it?” 62. Jesus, knowing [Note: [Col. 0397] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οὖν, “therefore.”] in himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, said to them: “Does this offend you? 63. What if you see the Son of Man ascending where he was before? 64. It is the Spirit that gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words which I have spoken to you are spirit [Note: [Col. 0399] So also the Greek text: ἐστί; Greek syntax.] and life. 65. But there are some among you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who it was that would betray him. 66. And he said: “For this reason I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been given him by the Father [Note: [Col. 0399] After *Father*, *my* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.].” 67. From this time [Note: [Col. 0399] Adds *therefore*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οὖν.] many of his disciples went back and no longer walked with him. 68. But [Note: [Col. 0399] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ.] Jesus said to the Twelve: “Do you also wish to go away?” 69. Simon Peter answered him: “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. 70. And we have believed and have known that you are the Son of God.” 71. Jesus answered: “Did I not choose you twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.” 72. Now he spoke of Judas Simon Iscariot, for he was about to betray him, being one of the Twelve.

## Chapter VII
## Chapter VII

1. After these things Jesus was walking in Galilee; for he did not have the power to walk in Judaea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.

[Note: [Col. 0399] After “these things,” *but* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

[Note: [Col. 0399] Thus also the Greek text: *ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ*, “in Galilee.”]

2. Now the Jewish festival-day, the Feast of Tabernacles, was near. 3. Therefore his brothers said to him: “Leave here and go into Judaea, so that your disciples also may 4. see the works that you do.

[Note: [Col. 0399] Thus also the Greek text: *οὖν*, “therefore.”]

[Note: [Col. 0401] After “works,” *your* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

For no one does anything in secret while seeking to be publicly known. If you do these things, reveal yourself to the world.” 5. For not even his brothers then believed in him.

[Note: [Col. 0401] Adds “then,” also the Codex of Canterbury.]

6. Jesus therefore said to them: “My time has not yet come; but your time is always ready. 7. The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I testify concerning it that its works are evil. 8. Go up yourselves to the feast; I will not go up to the feast, because my time has not yet been fulfilled.”

[Note: [Col. 0401] After “feast,” *this* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

9. Having said these things, he himself remained in Galilee.

[Note: [Col. 0401] Thus also the Codex of Canterbury: *εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν*, “in/to Galilee.”]

10. But when his brothers went up, then he also went up to the feast, not openly but secretly.

[Note: [Col. 0401] Before “secretly,” *as it were* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

11. The Jews, then, were seeking him at the feast and saying, “Where 12. is he?” And there was much murmuring about him among the crowd. Some said, “He is good.” Others said, “No; rather, he leads 13. the people astray.” Yet no one spoke openly about him, for fear of the Jews.

14. When the feast was already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and taught. 15. The Jews were astonished, saying: “How does this man know letters, when he has not learned?” 16. Jesus answered and said: “My teaching is not mine, but belongs to him who sent me.

[Note: [Col. 0401] Before “Jesus,” *to them* is absent, also in the Gothic version.]

17. If anyone wills to do his will, he will know concerning the teaching whether it is from God, or whether I speak 18. from myself. Whoever speaks from himself seeks his own glory; but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and there is no unrighteousness in him. 19. Did not Moses give you the Law? Yet none of you keeps the Law. 20. Why do you seek to kill me?”

21. Jesus answered and said to them: “I did one work, and you all marvel at it. 22. For this reason Moses gave you circumcision—not because it is from Moses, but from your fathers—and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath. 23. If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the Law of Moses is not broken, are you angry with me because I made the whole man sound on the Sabbath? 24. Do not judge by appearance, but render righteous judgment.”

25. Therefore some of the inhabitants of Jerusalem said: “Is this not the man whom they seek to kill? 26. And see, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Have the rulers truly recognized that he is the Christ? 27. Yet we know where this man is from; but when the Christ comes, no one knows where he is from.”

28. Therefore Jesus cried out in the temple, teaching and saying: “You know both me and where I am from. Yet I have not come of myself; but he who sent me is true, whom you do not know. 29. But I know him, because I am from him and he sent me.”

[Note: [Col. 0403] Adds *but*, as does the Greek text: *δέ*.]

30. Therefore they sought to seize him, but no one laid hands upon him, because his hour had not yet come. 31. But many from the crowd believed in him and said: “When the Christ comes, will he perform more signs than this man has done?”

[Note: [Col. 0405] Thus also the Greek text: *ἐποίησεν*, “did.”]

32. The chief priests and Pharisees heard the people murmuring these things about him, and they sent officers to seize him.

[Note: [Col. 0405] After “about him,” *these things* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

33. Jesus said: “I am with you yet a little while, and I go to him who sent me.

[Note: [Col. 0405] Before “Jesus,” *to them* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

34. You will seek me and will not find me; and where I am, you cannot 35. come.” Therefore the Jews said to one another: “Where is this man going, that we shall not find him? Is he going to go among the Dispersion of the Greeks and teach 36. the Greeks?

[Note: [Col. 0406] Thus also the Greek text: *τῶν Ἑλλήνων*, “of the Greeks.”]

[Note: [Col. 0406] *τοὺς Ἕλληνας*, “the Greeks.”]

What is this saying that he spoke: ‘You will seek me and will not find me; and where I am, you cannot come’?”

37. But on the last, great and solemn day, Jesus stood and cried out, saying: “If anyone thirsts, let him come and 38. drink. Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.”

[Note: [Col. 0406] After “come,” *to me* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

[Note: [Col. 0406] Thus also the Greek text: *εἶπεν*, “said.”]

39. Now he said this concerning the Spirit, whom they were going to receive; for the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

40. Therefore, hearing these words, some of the people said: “This is truly the Prophet.” 41. Others said: “Does the Christ then come from Galilee? 42. Does not Scripture say that the Christ comes from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the town where David was?” 43. Therefore a division arose in the crowd because of him. 44. But some of them wished to seize him; but no one … [lacuna in the source.]

[Note: [Col. 0407] Two erased pages are lacking; their edges still appear in the codex. In Book II, chapter 7, of *On Adulterous Marriages*, addressed to Pollentius, St Augustine says that it came about that certain persons of little faith—or rather, as I believe, enemies of the true faith—fearing that impunity for sin might be granted to their wives, removed from their codices the passage concerning the Lord’s pardon of the adulteress, as though he who said, “From now on, do not sin,” had granted permission to sin.]

## Chapter VIII

[Col. 0410]

12. Again, when they had assembled, Jesus spoke to them, saying: “I am the light of this world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.” 13. The Pharisees said to him: “You bear witness concerning yourself; your testimony is not true.” 14. Jesus answered and said to them: “Even if I bear witness concerning myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or 15. where I am going. You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.

[Note: [Col. 0409] Thus also the Greek text: *οὐδένα*, “no one.” Greek syntax.]

16. Yet if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent me. 17. It is also written in the Law that the testimony of two persons is true. 18. I am he who bears witness concerning myself, and the Father who sent me bears witness concerning me.”

19. Therefore they said to him: “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered and said to them: “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.”

[Note: [Col. 0410] Adds “and said to them,” also the Codex of Canterbury: *καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς*.]

20. He spoke these words in the treasury, teaching in the temple; and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come.

[Note: [Col. 0410] After “spoke,” *Jesus* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

21. Again he said to them: “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

[Note: [Col. 0410] After “to them,” *Jesus* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

22. Therefore the Jews said: “Will he kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?” 23. Again he said to them: “You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world. 24. Therefore I told you that you will die in your sin; for unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sin.”

25. They said to him: “Who are you?” Jesus said to them: “Primarily, that which I speak to you; 26. though I have much to say and to judge concerning you. But he who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him, these things I speak in this 27. world.” They did not understand that he was speaking to them of God the Father.

[Note: [Col. 0411] According to the Codex of Canterbury, *τὸν Θεόν*, “God”; the Canterbury Latin adds *his own*.]

28. Jesus said to them: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and that I do nothing from myself; but as the Father taught me, I speak these things. 29. And he who sent me is with me and has not left me alone, because I always do the things pleasing to him.” 30. As he spoke these things, many believed in him.

31. Jesus said to those Jews who had believed him: “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples;

[Note: [Col. 0411] Thus also the Greek text: *ἐστέ*, “you are.”]

32. and you will know the truth, and the truth itself will set you free.” 33. The Jews answered, saying: “We are Abraham’s seed and have never been enslaved to anyone. How do you say, ‘You will become free’?”

[Note: [Col. 0411] “Abraham.” Thus also the Greek text: *Ἀβραάμ*.]

34. Jesus answered: “Amen, amen, I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave.

[Note: [Col. 0411] After “is,” *of sin* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

35. Now the slave does not remain in the house forever; but the Son remains forever. 36. Therefore, if the Son sets you free, you will truly be free. 37. I know that you are Abraham’s seed; yet you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in 38. you.

[Note: [Col. 0413] Thus also the Greek text: *σπέρμα*, “seed.”]

What I have seen with my Father, that I speak; therefore do what you have seen with your father.”

[Note: [Col. 0413] Thus also the Greek text: *οὖν*, “therefore.”]

39. They answered and said: “Abraham is our father.” Jesus said to them: “If you were Abraham’s children, you would certainly do his works.”

[Note: [Col. 0413] Thus also the Greek text: *εἰ τέκνα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἦτε, τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἐποιεῖτε ἄν*: “If you were children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham.”]

40. “But now you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken to you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this. 41. But you do the works of your father.” They said to him: “We were not born of fornication; we have one Father, God.”

[Note: [Col. 0413] Adds *but*, also the Codex of Canterbury: *δέ*.]

42. Jesus said to them: “If God were your Father, you would certainly love me. For I proceeded from God and came; for I have not come from myself, but he sent me.

[Note: [Col. 0413] After “says,” *therefore* is absent, also in the Gothic version.]

43. Why do you not understand my speech? Because you cannot hear my word. 44. You are from your father the devil, and you desire to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and did not stand in the truth, because truth is not in him. Whenever he speaks falsehood, he speaks from his own resources, because he is a liar, as is also his father. 45. But because I tell you the truth, you do not believe me.

[Note: [Col. 0413] After “I,” *but* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

46. Which of you convicts me of sin? If I speak truth, why do you not believe me? 47. Whoever is from God hears the words of God. For this reason you do not hear, because you are not from God.”

48. The Jews answered and said to him: “Do we not rightly say that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?” 49. Jesus answered: “I do not have a demon, but I honour my Father, and you dishonour me.

[Note: [Col. 0415] Thus also the Greek text: *ἀτιμάζετε*, “you dishonour.”]

50. But I do not seek my own honour; there is one who seeks it and judges. 51. Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he shall never see death.”

52. The Jews said to him: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets; yet you say, ‘If anyone keeps my word, he will not taste death.’ 53. Are you greater than Abraham, who died? And the prophets died. Whom, then, do you make yourself?”

54. Jesus answered: “If I honour myself, my honour is nothing. My Father is he who honours me, whom you say is 55. your God; yet you do not know him. But I know him. If I said that I did not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I know him and keep his word. 56. Abraham, your father, rejoiced that he might see my day; and he saw it and rejoiced.”

[Note: [Col. 0415] Adds *and*, also in the Greek text: *καί*.]

57. Therefore they said to him: “You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?” 58. Jesus said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: before Abraham, I am.”

[Note: [Col. 0417] (a) Thus also the Canterbury Latin and Greek codex: *πρὶν Ἀβραὰμ, ἐγώ εἰμι*, “before Abraham, I am.”]

59. Therefore they took stones to throw at him; but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.

## Chapter IX

1. And as he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.

[Note: [Col. 0417] (b) Before “saw,” *Jesus* is absent also in the Greek text.]

2. And his disciples asked him: “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?” 3. Jesus answered and said to them: “Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but that the works 4. of God might be manifested in him. I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day; for night is coming, when no one can 5. work. While I am in this world, I am the light of the world.”

6. Having said these things, he spat upon the ground, made mud with the spittle, and smeared the mud upon the eyes of the blind man. 7. He said to him: “Go to the pool of Siloam”—which is translated “Sent.” So he went, washed himself, and came seeing.

[Note: [Col. 0417] (c) Thus also the Greek text: *Σιλωάμ*, “Siloam.”]

8. Therefore his neighbours, and those who had previously seen him—for he was a beggar and blind—said: “Is this not the man who sat and begged?” 9. Some said, “He is.” Others said, “He is not; he merely resembles him.” But he said: “I am he.” 10. Therefore they said to him: “How were your eyes opened?”

[Note: [Col. 0417] Thus also the Codex of Canterbury: *εἶπον*, “they said.”]

[Note: [Col. 0417] Thus also the Greek text: *σοῦ*, “your.”]

11. He answered and said: “The man called Jesus made mud and smeared me with it, and said to me, ‘Go to Siloam and wash yourself.’ So I went, washed myself, and began to see.”

[Note: [Col. 0417] Thus also the Greek text: *ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπος*, “that man answered and said: ‘A man …’”]

[Note: [Col. 0419] Thus also the Codex of Canterbury: *εἰς τὸν Σιλωάμ*, “to Siloam.”]

12. They said to him: “Where is he?” He said to them: “I do not know.”

[Note: [Col. 0419] Adds *to them*, also the Codex of Canterbury: *αὐτοῖς*.]

13. They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind. 14. Now it was the Sabbath on the day Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes. 15. Therefore the Pharisees again asked him, saying: “How do you see?” And he said to them: “He made mud, put it upon my eyes; I washed myself in Siloam, and see, I see.” 16. Some of the Pharisees said: “This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath in this manner.” Others said: “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” And there was division among them.

[Note: [Col. 0419] After “others,” *but* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

[Note: [Col. 0419] Thus also the Greek text: *τοιαῦτα*, “such.”]

17. Therefore they said to the blind man: “What do you say concerning him who opened your eyes?” But he said: “He is a prophet.”

[Note: [Col. 0419] Thus also the Codex of Canterbury: *ἔλεγον*, “they said.”]

[Note: [Col. 0419] After “to him,” *again* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

18. The Jews did not believe concerning the man who had been blind until they summoned 19. his parents and asked them: “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”

[Note: [Col. 0419] After “believed,” *therefore* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

20. His parents answered them and said: “We know that this is our son and that he was 21. born blind. But how he now sees, we do not know; nor do we know who opened his eyes. He is of age; let him speak for himself.” 22. His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that, if anyone confessed him to be Christ, he should be 23. put out of the synagogue.

[Note: [Col. 0421] Before “Christ,” *to be* is absent, likewise in the Greek text.]

Therefore his parents said: “He is of age; ask him.”

24. Therefore they summoned again the man who had been blind and said to him: “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.” 25. He said: “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. One thing I know: though I was blind, now I see.”

[Note: [Col. 0421] Before “he,” *to them* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

26. Therefore they said to him: “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?” 27. He answered them: “I have already told you, and you heard. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also wish to become his disciples?”

28. They reviled him and said: “You may be that man’s disciple; we are disciples of Moses. 29. We know that God spoke to Moses; but we do not know where this man is from.” 30. The man answered and said to them: “This is indeed remarkable: you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes.

[Note: [Col. 0421] After “said,” *to them* is lacking, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

31. We know that God does not hear sinners; but if anyone is a worshipper of God and does his will, God hears him. 32. Since the beginning of time it has never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a man born blind. 33. Unless this man were from God, he could do nothing.” 34. They answered and said to him: “You were altogether born in sin, and do you teach us?” And they cast him out.

35. Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and he found him and said to him: “Do you believe in the Son of God?”

[Note: [Col. 0423] Thus also the Codex of Canterbury: *καὶ εὗρεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν*, “and he found him and said.”]

36. He answered and said: “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?” 37. Jesus said to him: “You have both seen him, and he who speaks with you is he.” 39. “For judgment I have come into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.” 40. Some Pharisees who were with him heard this and said to him: “Are we also blind?”

[Note: [Col. 0423] Before “from the Pharisees,” *some* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

41. Jesus said to them: “If you were blind, you would not have sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Your sin remains in you.”

## Chapter X

1. “Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever does not enter the sheepfold through the door, but climbs in elsewhere, is a thief and a robber. 2. But whoever enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep. 3. The gatekeeper opens to him; the sheep hear his voice; he calls his own sheep by name and leads 4. them out. When he has sent out all his sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice.

[Note: [Col. 0423] Adds “all,” also the Codex of Canterbury: *πάντα*.]

5. But they do not follow a stranger; rather, they flee from him, because they do not know his voice.” 6. Jesus spoke this proverb to them; but they did not understand what he was saying to them.

7. Therefore Jesus said to them again: “Amen, amen, I say to you: I am the door of the sheep. 8. All who came are thieves and robbers; but the sheep did not hear them.

[Note: [Col. 0425] Before “all who,” *all* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

[Note: [Col. 0425] Thus also the Greek text: *ἀλλά*, “but.”]

9. I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved; he will enter and go out and find pasture. 10. The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and have it more abundantly. 11. I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep. 12. But the hired hand, who is not a shepherd and whose sheep are not his own, sees the wolf coming and abandons the sheep and flees, because he is a hired hand; and the wolf snatches and scatters the sheep. 13. The hired hand flees because he is a hired hand and is not concerned for the sheep.

14. I am the good shepherd; I know my own, and my own know me. 15. Just as the Father knows me, and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for my sheep. 16. I have other sheep that are not from this fold; I must bring them also, and they will hear my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd. 17. For this reason the Father loves me: because I lay down my life, that I may take it up again. 18. No one takes it from me; rather, I lay it down of myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. This commandment I received from the Father.”

[Note: [Col. 0427] (a) After “Father,” *my* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

19. Again a division arose among the Jews because of these words. 20. Many of them said: “He has a demon and is mad; why do you listen to him?” 21. Others said: “These are not the words of one who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”

22. The Feast of Dedication took place at Jerusalem … 23. And Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s Portico. 24. Therefore the Jews surrounded him and said to him: “How long do you take away our life? If you are the Christ, tell us openly.” 25. Jesus answered them: “I speak to you, and you do not believe. The works which I do in my Father’s name bear witness 26. concerning me; but you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I told 27. you. Those who are of my sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. 28. I give them eternal life; they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them from my hand. 29. What the Father has given me is greater than all, and no one can snatch it from my Father’s hand. 30. I and the Father are one.”

31. Therefore the Jews took up stones to stone him. 32. Jesus answered them: “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of these works do you stone me?” 33. The Jews answered him: “We do not stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy: because you, being a man, make yourself God.” 34. Jesus answered: “Is it not written in your Law: ‘I said, You are gods’?

[Note: [Col. 0429] After “Law,” *your* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

35. If he called those gods to whom the word of God came—and Scripture cannot be broken—36. do you say to him whom the Father sanctified and sent into this world, ‘You blaspheme,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’? 37. If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me. 38. But if I do them, even if you do not wish to believe me, believe the works, and know that the Father is in me and I in him.”

[Note: [Col. 0429] After “you will know,” *and believe* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.]

39. Therefore they sought to seize him, but he escaped from their hands. 40. And again he went across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and he remained there. 41. Many came to him and said: “John indeed performed no sign. 42. But everything John said about this man was true.” And many believed in him.

## Chapter XI

1. Now there was a certain sick man named Lazarus, from Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha. 2. Mary was the woman who anointed Jesus with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair; her brother Lazarus was ill. 3. Therefore they sent to Jesus, saying: “Lord, behold, he whom you love is sick.”

[Note: [Col. 0429] Thus also the Codex of Canterbury: *πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν*, “to Jesus.”]

4. Jesus heard it and said: “This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” 5. Now Jesus loved Martha, her sister Mary, and Lazarus. 6. Therefore, when he heard that Lazarus was sick, he nevertheless remained two days in the same place.

[Note: [Col. 0431] Thus also the Greek text: *ἀσθενεῖ*, “is sick.”]

[Note: [Col. 0431] Adds “Jesus,” also the Codex of Canterbury: *ὁ Ἰησοῦς*.]

[Note: [Col. 0431] Thus also the Greek text: *ἡμέρας*, “days.”]

7. Then after these things he said to his disciples: “Let us go again into Judaea.” 8. His disciples said to him: “Rabbi, the Jews were just seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?” 9. Jesus answered: “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks by day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world. 10. But if anyone walks at night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.” 11. He said these things, and afterwards said to them: “Lazarus our friend is asleep; but I am going to awaken him.”

[Note: [Col. 0431] Thus also the Greek text: *λέγει*, “he says.”]

12. The disciples said to him: “Lord, if he is asleep, he will be safe.” 13. But Jesus had spoken of his death; they thought that he was speaking to them about the sleep of slumber. 14. Then Jesus said to them plainly: “Lazarus is dead. 15. But I am glad for your sakes, that you may believe, because I was not there. But let us go to him.” 16. Therefore Thomas, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples: “Let us also go, that we may die with him.”

17. Therefore Jesus came and found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days. 18. Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away. 19. Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother. 20. Therefore, when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she met him; but Mary remained sitting at home. 21. Martha then said to Jesus: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. 22. But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.” 23. Jesus said to her: “Your brother will rise.” 24. Martha said to him: “I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.” 25. Jesus said to her: “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he has died, lives; 26. and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never die. Do you believe this?” 27. Martha said to him: “Certainly, Lord; I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who came into this world.”

[Note: [Col. 0433] After “God,” *living* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

28. And after she had said these things, she went away and secretly called her sister Mary, saying: “The Teacher is here and is calling you.” 29. When she heard this, she arose quickly and came to him. 30. For Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him. 31. The Jews who were with her in the house, consoling her, saw that Mary had risen quickly and gone out; they followed her, saying, “She is going to the tomb to weep there.”

[Note: [Col. 0433] According to the Gothic: *ἐν οἰκίᾳ, παραμυθούμενοι*, “in the house, consoling [her].”]

32. When Mary came where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 33. Therefore, when Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, he groaned in spirit and troubled himself. 34. And he said: “Where have you laid him?” They said to him: “Lord, come 35. and see.” And Jesus wept. 36. Therefore the Jews said: “See how he loved him.” 37. But some of them said: “Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have prevented this man also from dying?”

[Note: [Col. 0435] After “blind,” *born* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

38. Therefore Jesus, groaning within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it. 39. Jesus said: “Remove the stone.” Martha said to him: “Lord, by now he smells, for it is the fourth day.” 40. Jesus said to her: “Did I not tell you that, if you believed, you would see the glory of God?” 41. Therefore they removed the stone. Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: “Father, I thank you that you heard me.

[Note: [Col. 0435] Thus also the Greek text: *ᾖρε*, “lifted.”]

[Note: [Col. 0435] Adds *his*, also the Codex of Canterbury: *αὐτοῦ*.]

42. And I knew that you always hear me; but I said this because of the crowd standing around, that they might believe that you sent me.” 43. Having said these things, he cried out with a loud voice: “Lazarus, come 44. forth!” And the man who had been dead came out, his feet and hands bound with strips of cloth, and his face bound about with a napkin. Jesus said to them: “Untie him, and let him go.”

[Note: [Col. 0435] Before “came out,” *immediately* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

45. Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, seeing what he had done, believed in him.

[Note: [Col. 0435] After “Mary,” *and Martha* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

[Note: [Col. 0435] The Vulgate adds “Jesus”; it is nevertheless absent in the Alexandrian, Gothic, and Coptic.]

46. But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

[Note: [Col. 0437] Thus also the Greek text: *ὅ*, “that which.”]

47. Therefore the chief priests and Pharisees assembled a council and said: “What are we to do? For this man performs such signs. 48. If we leave him alone in this way, everyone will believe in him; and the Romans will come and take away our place and nation.” 49. But one of them, named Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them: “You know nothing at all, 50. nor do you consider that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people and that the whole nation should not perish.” 51. Now he did not say this from himself; but because he was high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation, 52. and not for the nation only, but also that he might gather into one the children of God who were scattered abroad. 53. Therefore from that day they planned to kill him.

54. Thus Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but departed into a region near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim; and there he remained with his disciples. 55. Now the Passover of the Jews was near. Therefore many went up from the country to Jerusalem before the Passover, to purify themselves.

[Note: [Col. 0437] Thus also the Codex of Canterbury: *οὖν*, “therefore.”]

56. Therefore they sought Jesus and spoke with one another while standing in the temple, saying: “What do you think—that he will not come to the feast?” 57. Now the chief priests and Pharisees had given a command that, if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, so that they might seize him.

## Chapter XII
1. Therefore Jesus, six days before the Passover, came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, who had died, whom he had raised up.  
[Note: [Col. 0439] So also the Greek text: ἦν Λάζαρος ὁ τεθνηκώς, “Lazarus who had died.”]

2. Therefore they made him a supper there; and Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with him. 3. Mary therefore took a pound of pure ointment and anointed Jesus’ feet, and wiped his feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.  
[Note: [Col. 0439] Before *pistici* (“pure”), *nardi* (“of nard”) is absent, also in the Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

4. And one of his disciples, Judas, son of Simon, Iscariot, who was about to betray him, said: 5. “Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”  
[Note: [Col. 0439] Adds *Simon*, likewise the Greek text: Σίμωνος, “of Simon.”]

6. But he said this not because the poor mattered to him, but because he was a thief and kept the money-box, and carried away what was put into it.  
[Note: [Col. 0439] So also the Greek text: εἶχε, “he kept/had.”]

7. Therefore Jesus said to him: “Leave her, that she may keep it for the day of my burial. 8. For you always have the poor with you, but me you do not always have.”  
[Note: [Col. 0439] So also the Greek text: ἄφες, “leave [her].”]

9. Then a great crowd of the Jews heard that he was there; and they came, not on account of Jesus, but that they might see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.  
[Note: [Col. 0439] Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἤκουσαν, “they heard.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0439] After *Jesus*, *tantum* (“only”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

10. But the chief priests planned to kill Lazarus also, [Col. 0442] 11. because many of the Jews were going away on account of him and believing in Jesus.  
[Note: [Col. 0441] So also the Greek text: τῶν Ἰουδαίων, “of the Jews.”]

12. On the following day, when the crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jeru- 13. salem, they took palm branches and went out to meet him, crying: “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel.” 14. And Jesus found a young ass and sat upon it, as it is written: 15. “Do not fear, daughter of Zion: behold, your King comes, sitting upon an ass’s colt.”

16. His disciples did not understand these things at first; but when Jesus was glorified, they remembered [Col. 0442] that these things had been written concerning him, and that they had done these things to him. 17. Therefore the crowd which was with him, when he called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead, bore witness. 18. For this reason the crowd went out to meet him, because they had heard that he had done this sign. 19. Therefore the Pharisees said among themselves: “You see that you gain nothing? Behold, the whole world has gone after him.”  
[Note: [Col. 0441] So also the Greek text: ὠφελεῖτε, “you profit/gain.”]

20. Now there were certain Greeks among those who had gone up to worship at the feast. 21. These therefore approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying: “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.” 22. Philip came and told Andrew; and Andrew and Philip in turn [Col. 0444] told Jesus. 23. But Jesus answered them, saying: “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. 24. Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, 25. it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit. He who loves his life in this world loses it; and he who hates his life in this world preserves it for eternal life. 26. If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also shall my servant be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.

27. “Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say? Father, save me, Father, from this hour? Yet for this very reason [Col. 0444] I came to this hour. 28. Father, glorify your name.” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.” 29. Therefore the crowd standing by and hearing said: “There has been thunder.” Others said: “An angel has spoken to him.”  
[Note: [Col. 0443] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: βροντὴ γέγονεν, “there has been thunder.” The Vercelli manuscript supports this.]

30. Jesus answered and said: “This voice came not for my sake, but for yours. 31. Now is the judgment of the world; now the ruler of this world will be cast down. 32. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all things 33. to myself.” But he said this, signifying by what death he was going to die. 34. The crowd answered him: “We have heard from the law that the Christ remains for ever; and how do you say, ‘The Son of Man must be lifted up’? Who [Col. 0446] is the Son of Man?”  
[Note: [Col. 0443] Adds *quia* (“that”), likewise the Greek text: ὅτι.]

35. Therefore Jesus said to them: “For a little while longer the light is among you. Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you; and he who walks in darkness does not know where he is going. 36. While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be children of light.” Jesus spoke these things, and went away and hid himself from them.  
[Note: [Col. 0445] Adds *tempus* (“time”), as also the Greek text: χρόνον. The Brixian codex has *temporis*, “of time.”]

37. But though he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in 38. him, so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he said: “Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?” 39. Therefore they could not believe, because Isaiah said again, [Col. 0446] 40. “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they may not see with their eyes, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I should heal them.”  
[Note: [Col. 0445] Before *understand*, *not* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

41. Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory and spoke of him. 42. Nevertheless, even many of the rulers believed in him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, lest they should be expelled from the synagogue. 43. For they loved human glory more than the glory of God.

44. But Jesus cried out and said: “He who believes in me believes also in him who sent me. 46. I came as light into this world, that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness. 47. And [Col. 0448] if anyone hears my words and keeps them, I do not judge him; for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.  
[Note: [Col. 0445] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔκραζε καὶ ἔλεγεν, “he cried out and said.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0447] *Not* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

48. He who rejects me and does not receive my words has one who judges him: the word which I have spoken will judge him on the last day. 49. For I have not spoken from myself; but the Father who sent me himself gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak. 50. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. Therefore the things which I speak, I speak as the Father told me.”

## CHAPTER XIII

1. Now before the feast day of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour had come to pass from this world to the Father, having loved his disciples who were in the world, loved them unto the end. 2. And supper having taken place, when the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon, Iscariot, to betray him, 3. Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come forth from God and was going to God, 4. rose from supper and laid aside his garments; and, having taken a linen cloth, girded 5. himself. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet, and to wipe them with the linen cloth with which he was girded.  
[Note: [Col. 0447] Adds *Jesus*, likewise the Greek text: ὁ Ἰησοῦς, “Jesus.”]

6. He came to Simon. And he said to him: “Lord, do you wash my feet?” 7. Jesus answered and said to him: “What I am doing, you do not know now; [Col. 0450] you will know afterward.” 8. Peter said to him: “You shall never wash my feet.” Jesus answered: “Unless I wash you, you have no share with me.”  
[Note: [Col. 0449] After *answered*, *to him* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]  
[Note: [Col. 0449] So also the Greek text: ἔχεις, “you have.”]

9. Simon Peter said to him: “Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and head.”  
[Note: [Col. 0449] After *feet*, *my* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

10. Jesus said to him: “He who has bathed needs only to wash his feet, but is wholly clean. And you are clean, but not all.” 11. For he knew who was to betray him; therefore he said: “You are not all clean.” 12. And after he had washed their feet, he took his garments and, when he had reclined again, said to them: “Do you know what I have done to you?”  
[Note: [Col. 0449] After *garments*, *his* is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

13. “You call me Teacher and Lord; and you speak rightly, for I am so. [Col. 0450] 14. Therefore, if I, the Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. 15. For I have given you an example, that as I do to you, you also may do. 16. Amen, amen, I say to you: a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is an apostle greater than him who sent 17. him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.  
[Note: [Col. 0449] So also the Greek text: Κύριος, “Lord.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0449] After *greater*, *is* is absent, also in the Greek text.]  
[Note: [Col. 0449] So also the Greek text: ἐστέ, “you are.”]

18. “I do not speak of all of you: I know whom I have chosen; but that the Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.’ 19. From now on I tell you before it happens, that when it has happened you may believe that I am he. 20. Amen, amen, I say to you: he who receives one whom [Col. 0452] I send receives me; and he who receives me receives him who sent me.”

21. When Jesus had said these things, he was troubled in spirit, and solemnly declared: “Amen, amen, I say to you, that one of you will betray me.” 22. Therefore the disciples looked at one another, uncertain of whom he spoke. 23. Now one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was reclining in Jesus’ bosom. 24. Therefore Simon Peter made a sign to him and said: “Tell who it is.” 25. So, reclining upon Jesus’ breast, he said to him: “Lord, who 26. is it?” Jesus answered: “It is he to whom I shall give the dipped bread.” And, having dipped the bread, he gave it to Judas, son of Simon, Iscariot. 27. And when [Col. 0452] he received the bread, Satan entered into him. Therefore Jesus said to him: “What you are doing, do more quickly.”  
[Note: [Col. 0451] So also the Greek text: οὖν, “therefore.”]

28. But none of those reclining knew what he had said to him. 29. For some supposed that, because Judas had the money-box, Jesus was saying to him: “Buy the things which are needed by you for the feast,” or that he should give something to the needy. 30. Therefore, having received the bread, he went out immediately. And it was night.

31. Therefore, when he had gone out, Jesus said: “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified 32. in him. And God has glorified him in himself, and immediately will glorify him. 33. Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You seek me; and, as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I go [Col. 0454] you cannot come,’ so now I say to you. 34. A new commandment I give you: that you love one another, as I have loved you, that you also may love one another.  
[Note: [Col. 0453] Adds *I*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐγώ.]

35. By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another. 36. Simon Peter said to him: “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered: “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; but you will follow me afterward.”  
[Note: [Col. 0453] Adds *me*, likewise the Greek text: μοὶ.]  
37. Peter said to him: “Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.” Jesus answered him: “Will you lay down your life for me?”  
[Note: [Col. 0453] Adds *Lord*, likewise the Greek text: κύριε.]

## CHAPTER XIV

1. “Amen, amen, I say to you: the cock will not crow until you have denied me three times. Let not [Col. 0454] your heart be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in me. 2. In my Father’s house are many dwelling-places; otherwise I would have told you, because I go to prepare a place for you. 3. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I come again and receive you to myself, that where I am, you also may be. 4. And you know where I am going, and you know the way.”  
[Note: [Col. 0453] Before *I go*, *I* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

5. Thomas said to him: “Lord, we do not know where you are going; how do we know the way?”  
[Note: [Col. 0453] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οἴδαμεν, “we know.”]

6. Jesus said to him: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. 7. If you have known me, you have known my Father also; and from now on you know him and have seen him.”

8. Philip said to him: “Lord, show us the Father, and it suffices us.” 9. Jesus said to him: “Have I been with you for so long a time [Col. 0456] and you have not known me? Philip, he who has seen me has seen the Father. How do you say, ‘Show us the Father’? 10. Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words which I speak to you, I do not speak from myself. But the Father remaining in me, he speaks and does the works which I do. 11. Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father in me; 12. otherwise, believe me on account of the works themselves. Amen, amen, I say to you: he who believes in me will himself do the works which I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.  
[Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Greek text: πιστεύεις, “you believe.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Greek text: πιστεύετέ μοι, “believe me.”]

13. And whatever you ask of him in my name, [Col. 0456] I will do, that the Father may be honored in the Son. 15. If you love me, keep my commandments. 16. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, that he may be with you for ever: 17. the Spirit of truth, whom this world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You see him and know him, because he remains with you and is with you.  
[Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Greek text: μένει, “remains.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0455] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐστίν, “is.”]

18. “I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to 19. you. Yet a little while, and this world sees me no longer. But you will see me; because I live, you also will live. 20. On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.  
[Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Greek text: ἔρχομαι, “I am coming.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0455] After *you will know*, *you* is absent, also in Codex Alexandrinus.]  
[Note: [Col. 0455] After *I*, *am* is absent, likewise in the Greek text.]

[Col. 0458] 21. He who hears my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father; and I will love him and reveal myself to him.” 22. Judas—not the Iscariot, but another—said to him: “Lord, what has happened that you are about to reveal yourself to us and not to this world?” 23. Jesus answered and said to him: “If anyone loves me, he has kept my word, and my Father will love him; and we shall come to him and make our dwelling with him. 24. He who does not love me does not keep my words. And the word which you have heard is not mine, but the Father’s, who sent me.”

[Col. 0458] 25. “These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you. 26. But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, whatever I shall say. 27. Peace I give you; my peace I leave with you. Not as this world gives do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid. 28. You heard that I said to you, ‘I am going away and am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would rejoice because I am going to the Father; for the Father is greater than I. 29. And now I have told you before it happens, that when it has happened 30. you may believe. I shall no longer speak much with you; for the ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in me. 31. But that this world may know that I love [Col. 0460] the Father, I do as the Father commanded me. Rise, let us go from here.

## CHAPTER XV

1. “I am the true vine, and my Father is the cultivator. 2. Every branch in me which does not bear fruit, the Father removes; and every one that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit.  
[Note: [Col. 0459] So also the Greek text: αἴρει, “removes/takes away.”]

3. You are already clean because of the word which I have spoken to you. 4. Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so too [is] one who has not remained in me. 5. I am the vine; you are the branches. He who remains in me, and I in him, bears much [Col. 0460] fruit; because apart from me you can do nothing. 6. But if anyone does not remain in me, he is cut off like a branch, cast out, and withered; and they gather them and throw them into the fire, and they burn.  
[Note: [Col. 0459] So also the Greek text: ἐβλήθη . . . ἐξηράνθη . . . αὐτὰ . . . βαλλουσι, “was cast out . . . withered . . . them . . . they throw.”]

7. If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you will, and it will be done for you.  
[Note: [Col. 0459] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αἰτήσασθε, “ask.”]

8. In this my Father is glorified: that you bear much fruit and become my disciples. 9. As the Father loved me, I also loved you. Remain in my love. 10. If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, as I have kept the Father’s commandments and remain in his love. 11. I have spoken these things to you [Col. 0462] that my joy may be in you and your joy may be fulfilled.

12. This is my commandment: that you love one another as I loved 13. you. No one has greater love than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.  
[Note: [Col. 0461] After *lay down*, *anyone* is absent, also in the Greek and Latin Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

14. You are my friends if you do what I command you. 15. I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, because I have made known to you all things whatsoever I heard from my Father.  
[Note: [Col. 0461] So also the Greek text: λέγω, “I call.”]

16. You did not choose me; but I chose you and appointed you, that you may go and bear fruit, and that your fruit may remain, so that whatever you ask from the Father in my name he may give you. 17. These things I command you: that you love [Col. 0462] one another.

18. If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.  
[Note: [Col. 0461] After *before*, *you* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

19. If you were of the world, the world would love what was its own; but because you are not of the world, and I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. 20. Remember the word which I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will persecute you also; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also. 21. But they will do all these things to you on account of my name, because they do not know him who sent me.  
[Note: [Col. 0461] Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰς ὑμᾶς, “against/to you.”]

22. If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but [Col. 0464] now they have no excuse for their sin. 23. He who hates me hates my Father also. 24. If I had not done among them works which no other has done, they would not have had sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father. 25. But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’ 26. Therefore, when the Paraclete comes, whom I shall send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from my Father—he will bear witness concerning 27. me; and you also will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.

## CHAPTER XVI

1. “I have spoken these things to you so that you may not be caused to stumble. 2. They will put you out of the synagogues; indeed, the hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he is rendering service to God. [Col. 0464] 3. But they will do these things because they have known neither the Father nor me. 4. But I have spoken these things to you, so that when their hour comes you may remember that I told you.

5. “I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you; but now I am going to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you 6. going?’ But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.  
[Note: [Col. 0463] So also the Greek text: δέ, “but.”]

7. But I tell you the truth: it is expedient for you that I go away; if I do not go away, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go away, I will send him to you. 8. And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment: 9. concerning sin, indeed, because they do not believe [Col. 0466] in me; 10. concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father and you will see me no longer; 11. and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has already been judged.  
[Note: [Col. 0465] So also the Greek text: πιστεύουσιν, “they believe.”]

12. “I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. 13. But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will lead you into all truth. For he will not speak from himself, but he will speak what he hears, and will announce to you the things that are to come.  
[Note: [Col. 0465] Adds *them*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτά.]  
[Note: [Col. 0465] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πάσῃ, “he will lead you in all truth.”]

14. He will glorify me, because he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you. 15. All things whatsoever the Father has are mine. Therefore I said that he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.

[Col. 0466] 16. “A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me.” 17. Therefore his disciples said to one another: “What is this that he says to us, ‘A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me’; and, ‘Because I am going to the 18. Father’?” “What is this little while? We do not know what he is saying.”  
[Note: [Col. 0465] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, τί ἐστι τοῦτο τὸ μικρόν, “What is this little while?” omitting the words *therefore they said*.]

19. Jesus knew that they wished to question him, and said to them: “Are you asking one another about this, because I said, ‘A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me’?  
[Note: [Col. 0465] Before *Jesus*, *but* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

20. Amen, amen, I say to you: you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow [Col. 0468] will be turned into joy.  
[Note: [Col. 0465] After *you*, *but* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

21. A woman, when she is giving birth, has sorrow because her day has come; but when she has borne the child, she remembers the distress no longer, because of the joy that a human being has been born into this world.  
[Note: [Col. 0467] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἡμέρα, “day.”]

22. And you indeed now will have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy from you. 23. And on that day you will ask me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask anything of the Father in my name, he will give it to 24. you. Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be complete.  
[Note: [Col. 0467] So also the Greek text: αἴρει, “takes away.”]

25. “I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. [Col. 0468] The hour is coming when I shall no longer speak to you in figures of speech, but shall openly make known to you concerning the Father. 26. In that day you will ask in my name; and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father for you, 27. for the Father himself loves you, because you love me 28. and believe that I came forth from God and came into this world. Again I leave the world and go to the Father.”  
[Note: [Col. 0467] After *I came forth*, *again* is absent: “I came forth from the Father,” also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

29. His disciples said to him: “Behold, now you speak openly and use no figure of speech. 30. Now we know that you know all things and have no need that anyone should question you. By this we believe that you came forth from God.” 31. Jesus answered them: “Do you now believe? 32. Behold, the hour is coming—and has now come—when each of you will be scattered to his own region, [Col. 0470] and you will leave me alone; yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. 33. I have spoken these things to you that in me you may have peace. In this world you will have affliction; but take courage: I have overcome the world.”

## CHAPTER XVII

1. Jesus spoke these things and, lifting up his eyes to heaven, said: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, that your Son may glorify 2. you, as you have given him authority over all flesh, that he may give eternal life to all whom you have given him. 3. And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent. 4. I glorified you upon the earth, having completed the one work [Col. 0470] which you gave me to do. 5. And now, Father, glorify me with yourself, with the glory which I had with you before the world existed. 6. I have made your name known to the people whom you gave me out of this world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.

7. And now I know that all things whatsoever you have given me are from you; 8. because I gave them the words which you gave me, and they received them and truly knew that they came forth from you; and they believed that you sent me.  
[Note: [Col. 0469] So also the Gothic: ἔγνωκα, “I have known.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0469] The Greek text has ἐξῆλθον, which can mean both “I came forth” and “they came forth.”]

9. I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, because 10. they are yours. And all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine; [Col. 0472] and I have been glorified 11. in them. And I am no longer in this world, but they are in this world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name. While I was with them, I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me I guarded, and none of them perished except the son of perdition, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.  
[Note: [Col. 0469] After *mine*, *are* is absent, also in the Greek text.]

13. But now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in this world, that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves. 14. I gave them your word, and the world hated them, because they are not of the world. 15. I do not pray that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from evil. 16. They are not of this world, just as I [Col. 0472] am not of this world.  
[Note: [Col. 0471] Before *I*, *also* is absent, likewise in the Greek text.]

17. Sanctify them in truth. Your word is truth. 18. As you sent me into this world, I also sent them into this world; 19. and for their sake I sanctify myself, that they too may be sanctified in truth.  
[Note: [Col. 0471] Before *me*, *you* is absent, likewise in the Greek text.]  
[Note: [Col. 0471] Adds *this*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τοῦτον.]

20. “I pray not for these only, but also for those who believe in me through their word, 21. that all may be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be in us, that the world may believe that you sent me.  
[Note: [Col. 0471] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τῶν πιστευόντων, “of those believing.”]  
[Note: [Col. 0471] Before *may be*, *one* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

22. And I have given them the glory which you gave me, that they may be one, as we also are one: 23. I in them [Col. 0474] and you in me, that they may be made perfect into one, and that the world may know that you sent me and loved them as you loved me.  
[Note: [Col. 0473] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἠγάπησα, “I loved.”]

24. Father, those whom you gave me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me, that they may behold my glory which you gave me, because you loved me before the foundation of the world. 25. Righteous Father, the world did not know you; but I knew you, and these knew that you sent me. 26. And I made your name known to them, and will make it known, that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

## CHAPTER XVIII

1. When Jesus had said these things, he went out with his disciples across the torrent of the river Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.  
[Note: [Col. 0473] So also the Latin and Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis: τοῦ Κέδρου, “of Kidron.”]

2. And Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with his disciples. [Col. 0474] 3.
