Therefore Judas, having received a cohort and attendants from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons. 4. But Jesus, knowing all things that were coming upon him, went forward and said to them: “Whom do you seek?”  
[Note: [Col. 0473] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”]

5. They answered him: “Jesus the Nazarene.” Jesus said to them: “I am he.” And Judas, who betrayed him, was standing with 6. them. Therefore, when he said to them, “I am he,” they went backward and fell to the ground. 7. Again Jesus asked them: “Whom do you seek?” And they said: “Jesus the Nazarene.” 8. Jesus answered: “I told you that I am he. Therefore, if you seek me, let these go,” 9. that the word which he had spoken might be fulfilled: “Of those [Col. 0476] whom you gave me, I lost none.”

10. Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the servant of the chief priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus. 11. Therefore Jesus said to Peter: “Put your sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup which the Father has given me?”  
[Note: [Col. 0475] After *sword*, *your* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic.]

12. Therefore the cohort, the tribune, and the Jewish attendants seized Jesus and bound him, 13. and brought him first to Annas; for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was chief priest that year. 14. Now Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews: “It is expedient that one man die for the people.”

15. Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. [Col. 0476] That disciple was known to the chief priest, and entered with Jesus into the chief priest’s courtyard.  
[Note: [Col. 0475] So also the Greek text: συνεισῆλθε, “entered with [him].”]

16. But Peter was standing outside at the door. Therefore the other disciple, who was known to the chief priest, went out, spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in. 17. Then the maid who kept the door said to Peter: “Are you not also one of this man’s disciples?” He said: “I am not.” 18. The servants and attendants were standing around coals, because it was cold; and Peter too was standing with them and warming himself.

19. Therefore the chief priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching. 20. Jesus answered: “I have spoken openly to the [Col. 0478] world. I have always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather; and I have spoken nothing in secret. 21. Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them. Behold, they know what I said.” 22. When he had said this, one of the attendants standing by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying: “Do you answer the chief priest thus?” 23. Jesus answered him: “If I have spoken wrongly, bear witness concerning the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike me?” 24. Therefore Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.

25. Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. Therefore they said to him: “Are you not also one of his disciples?” He denied it and said: “I am not.” [Col. 0478] 26. One of the servants of the high priest, a kinsman of him whose ear Peter had cut off, said: “Did I not see you with 27. him in the garden?” Therefore Peter denied it again, and immediately the cock crowed.

28. They led Jesus from Caiaphas into the praetorium. It was morning; and they themselves did not enter the praetorium, lest they should be defiled, but might eat the Passover.  
[Note: [Col. 0477] After *but*, *that* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic.]

29. Therefore Pilate went out to them and said: “What accusation do you bring against this man?” 30. They answered and said to him: “If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you.” 31. Pilate said to them: “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your [Col. 0480] law.” Therefore the Jews said to him: “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death,” 32. that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which he had spoken, signifying by what death he would die.

33. Therefore Pilate entered the praetorium again, called Jesus, and said to him: “Are you the King of the Jews?” 34. Jesus answered: “Do you say this from yourself, or have others told you about me?”  
[Note: [Col. 0479] Adds *you*, likewise the Greek text: σύ.]

35. Pilate answered: “Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?” 36. Jesus answered: “My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would fight, that I should not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom [Col. 0480] is not from here.” 37. Pilate therefore said to him: “Then are you a king?” Jesus answered: “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into this world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.” 38. Pilate said to him: “What is truth?” And when he had said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them: “I find no ground of accusation in him. 39. But it is your custom that I release one person to you at the Passover. Therefore, shall I release to you the King of the Jews?” 40. Then all cried out: “Not this man, but Barabbas.” Now Barabbas was a robber.

## CHAPTER XIX

[Col. 0482]

1. Then Pilate took Jesus and scourged him. 2. And the soldiers placed upon his head a crown plaited of thorns, and clothed him in a purple robe. [Note: [Col. 0481] So also the Greek text: ἱμάτιον πορφυροῦν, “a purple garment.”] 3. And they came to him and said, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and struck him with their hands. 4. Therefore Pilate went out [Note: [Col. 0481] Before “Pilate,” “again” is absent, also in the Gothic version.] and said to them, “Behold, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no charge against him.” 5. Therefore Jesus came out, [Note: [Col. 0481] It adds “outside,” as does the Greek text, ἔξω.] wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment; and he said to them, “Behold the man.” 6. Therefore, when the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, “Crucify him, crucify him!” Pilate said to them: [Col. 0482] “Take him yourselves and crucify him; for I find no charge against him.” 7. The Jews answered: “We have a law, and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.” 8. Therefore, when Pilate heard this statement, he was more afraid. 9. And he entered [Note: [Col. 0481] It adds “into,” as does the Greek text, εἰς.] the praetorium again and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer. 10. Pilate therefore said to him, “Will you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you and authority to release you?” 11. Jesus answered, “You would have no authority at all over me unless it had been given you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.” 12. [Note: [Col. 0481] Before *exinde* (“thereupon”), “and” is absent, likewise in the Greek text.] Thereupon he sought to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying: [Col. 0484] “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.” 13. Therefore Pilate, when he heard these words, brought Jesus out and sat upon the judgment seat, [Note: [Col. 0483] So also the Greek text: εἰς τόπον, “into a place.”] in the place called Lithostrotus, but in Hebrew Gennetha. 14. Now it was the Preparation of the Passover, about the sixth hour; and he said to the Jews, “Behold your King.” 15. [Note: [Col. 0483] So also the Greek text: ἐκραύγασαν, “they cried out.”] They therefore cried out, “Away with him, away with him; crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.” 16. Then therefore he handed him over to them to be nailed to the cross. They took [Note: [Col. 0483] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οὖν, “therefore.”] Jesus; 17. and, bearing his cross for himself, he went out to the place called the Place of Calvary, in Hebrew 18. Golgotha, where they crucified him, and with him two others, one on either side, and Jesus in the middle. 19. Pilate also wrote a title and placed it upon the cross. And it was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews.” 20. Therefore many of the Jews read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin. 21. Therefore the chief men of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘King of the Jews,’ but, ‘He said, I am King of the Jews.’” 22. Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”

[Col. 0486]

23. Therefore, when the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took his garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier. But the tunic was seamless, woven throughout from the top. 24. Therefore they said to one another, “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, to determine whose it shall be,” so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast a lot.” And the soldiers indeed did these things. 25. But standing beside Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. 26. When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple [Note: [Col. 0485] So also the Greek text: παρεστῶτα, “standing by.”] standing near, whom he loved, he said [Col. 0486] to his mother, “Woman, behold your son.” 27. Then he said to the disciple, “Behold your mother.” And from that hour the disciple received her into his own home. 28. After this, Jesus, knowing that all things had been accomplished, in order that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, 29. “I thirst.” A vessel full of vinegar stood there. Therefore, placing a sponge full of vinegar around a reed, they offered it to his mouth. 30. Therefore, when Jesus had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished.” And, bowing his head, he gave up his spirit. 31. Therefore the Jews, because it was the pure supper [i.e. the Preparation], in order that the bodies might not remain upon the cross on the Sabbath—for that Sabbath day was a great one—asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away. 32. Therefore the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first [Note: [Col. 0485] Here the ancient translator renders the Greek prefixed article.] and of the other, [Col. 0488] [Note: [Col. 0487] According to the Greek text: συσταυρωθέντος, “who had been crucified together.”] who had been crucified with him. 33. But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs. 34. But one of the soldiers pierced [Note: [Col. 0487] So also the Greek text: ἔνυξε, “pierced.”] his side with a spear, and immediately blood 35. and water came out. And he who saw it has borne witness, and his testimony is true. And he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe. 36. For these things took place in order that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “You shall not break a bone of him.” 37. And again another Scripture says: “They shall look upon him whom they pierced.” 38. After these things Joseph of Arimathea, [Col. 0488] who himself also was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly because of fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body; and Pilate permitted it. 39. They came and took him away. Nicodemus also came, who had first come to Jesus by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds. 40. Therefore they took Jesus’ body and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the Jewish custom in burial. 41. Now in the place where he had been crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been laid. 42. Therefore, because of the Preparation, since the tomb was nearby, [Col. 0490] they laid Jesus there.

## CHAPTER XX

1. But on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came to the tomb while it was still dark, and saw that the stone had been removed from the tomb. 2. Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him.” 3. Therefore Peter and that other disciple went out and came to the tomb. 4. The two of them ran together, but that other disciple ran ahead faster than Peter and came first to the tomb. 5. And when he had bent down [Col. 0490] and looked in, he saw the linen cloths lying there; yet he did not enter. 6. Therefore Simon Peter came, following him, and entered the tomb; and he saw the linen cloths 7. lying there, and the face-cloth that had been upon his head, not lying with the linen cloths but rolled up separately in one place. 8. Then that disciple also entered, the one who had come first to the tomb; and he saw and believed. 9. For they did not yet know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead. 10. Therefore the disciples went away again to their own homes. 11. But Mary sat at the tomb, weeping; and as she wept, she bent down and looked into the tomb. 12. And she saw two angels sitting in white, one [Col. 0492] at the head and one at the feet, where Jesus’ body had lain. 13. They said to her, “Woman, why do you weep?” She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.” 14. When she had said these things, she turned backward and saw Jesus standing there, but did not know that it was the Lord. 15. Jesus said to her, “Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek?” Supposing that he was the gardener, [Note: [Col. 0491] So also the Greek text: ἐστίν, “he is.”] she said to him, “Sir, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.” 16. Jesus said to her, “Mary.” [Note: [Col. 0491] It adds “and,” as does Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ.] And she turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabboni” (which is interpreted, “Teacher”). 17. Jesus said to her, “Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to [Note: [Col. 0491] After “Father,” “my” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] the Father; but go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father [Col. 0492] and your Father, [Note: [Col. 0491] It adds “and,” likewise the Greek text: καί.] and my God and your God.’” 18. Mary Magdalene came, announcing to the disciples that she had seen Jesus and that he had said these things. 19. Therefore, when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were enclosed because of fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in their midst and [Note: [Col. 0491] Thus from the Greek text: λέγει, “he says.”] said to them, “Peace be with you.” 20. And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and side. [Note: [Col. 0491] It adds “his,” as does the Greek text: αὐτοῦ.] And the disciples rejoiced when they saw Jesus. 21. Therefore Jesus [Note: [Col. 0491] It adds “Jesus,” likewise the Greek text: ὁ Ἰησοῦς.] said to them again, “Peace be with you. As the Father sent me, I also send you.” 22. [Note: [Col. 0491] So also the Greek text: τοῦτο, “this.”] Having said this, he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit. 23. Whose sins you forgive are forgiven them; and whose sins you retain are retained.”

[Col. 0494]

24. But Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. 25. Therefore the other disciples said to him, “We have seen the Lord.” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the place of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.” 26. After eight days the disciples were again indoors, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came while the doors were shut, stood in the midst, and said, “Peace be with you.” 27. Then he said to Thomas, “Bring your finger here and see my hands; bring your hand and put it into my side. And do not be unbelieving, but believing.” 28. Thomas answered and said to him, “My Lord and my God.” [Col. 0494] 29. Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.” 30. Jesus indeed performed many other signs in the presence of his disciples which are not written in this book. 31. But these have been written so that you may believe that [Note: [Col. 0493] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς υἱός ἐστιν τοῦ Θεοῦ, “Jesus Christ is the Son of God.”] Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and so that, believing, you may have eternal life [Note: [Col. 0493] It adds “eternal,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αἰώνιον.] in his name.

## CHAPTER XXI

1. After this Jesus manifested himself again to his disciples [Note: [Col. 0493] It adds “his,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτοῦ.] by the Sea [Note: [Col. 0493] Greek text: ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης, “upon the sea.”] of Tiberias. And he manifested himself in this way: 2. Simon Peter, Thomas who was called Didymus, Nathanael, who was from Cana of Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples of his were together. 3. Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing.” They said to him, “We are coming with you also.” [Col. 0496] They went out and entered the boat, and that night they caught nothing. 4. But when morning had already come, [Note: [Col. 0495] It adds “already,” as does the Greek text: ἤδη.] Jesus stood on the shore; but the disciples did not know that it was Jesus. 5. Jesus therefore said to them, “Children, do you have anything to eat?” They answered him, “No.” 6. He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side [Note: [Col. 0495] It adds “side,” also the Greek text: μέρη.] of the boat, and you will find some.” Therefore they cast it, and because of the multitude of fish they were not even able to draw in the net. 7. Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said, “It is the Lord.” Simon [Note: [Col. 0495] It adds “therefore,” likewise the Greek text: οὖν.] Peter, when he heard that it was the Lord, girded his tunic about himself—for he was naked—and [Col. 0496] threw himself into the sea. 8. But the other disciples came in the boat—for they were not far from land, but about [Note: [Col. 0495] So also the Greek text: ἀπό, “from.”] two hundred cubits away—dragging the net of fish. 9. Therefore, when they went down onto the land, they saw burning coals, fish placed upon them, and bread. 10. Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have caught.” 11. Simon Peter went up and dragged the net to land, full of one hundred and fifty-three large fish; and although there were so many, the net was not torn. 12. Jesus said to them, “Come, dine.” Yet none of the disciples [Note: [Col. 0495] Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but/yet.”] dared ask him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord. 13. [Note: [Col. 0495] Before “Jesus came,” “and” is absent, also in the Greek text.] Jesus came, [Col. 0498] took the bread, and gave it to them, and likewise the fish. 14. This was already the third time Jesus manifested himself to his disciples after he had risen from the dead. 15. Therefore, after they had dined, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He said to him, “Certainly, Lord; you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed [Note: [Col. 0497] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πρόβατα, “sheep.”] my sheep.” 16. Again he said to him, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed 17. my little sheep.” He said to him a third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because he said to him a third time, “Do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know all things; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep. 18. Truly, truly, I tell you: when [Col. 0498] you were younger, you girded yourself and walked; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not 19. wish to go.” He said this to signify by what death Peter would glorify God. And when he had said this, he said to him, 20. “Follow me.” Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following, who also reclined at the supper upon his breast and said, “Lord, who is the one who will 21. hand you over?” Therefore, when Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, “Lord, but what of this man?” 22. Jesus said to him, “If I wish him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.” 23. Therefore this saying went out among the brothers, that that disciple [Col. 0500] would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him, “He will not die,” but, “If I wish him to remain until [Note: [Col. 0499] So also the Greek text: ἔρχομαι, “I come.”] I come, what is that to you?” 24. This is the disciple who bears witness concerning these things [Note: [Col. 0499] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ὁ γράψας, “and the one who wrote.”] and who wrote these things; and we know that [Col. 0500] his testimony is true. 25. There were indeed many other things which Jesus did, which are not written in this book; if they were written down individually, I suppose that not even the world itself could contain the books that would be written.

**THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO JOHN ENDS, IN GOD. THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE BEGINS.**

**CODEX BRIXIANUS**

[Col. 0353]

[Col. 0353] In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. This was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing that has been made was made. What was made in him was life. [Note: [Col. 0353] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐστίν, “is.”] And the life was the light of human beings. And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.

There was [Col. 0354] a man sent from God, whose name was John. He came for testimony, to bear testimony concerning the light, so that all might believe through him. He was not the light, but came in order to bear testimony concerning the light. Now the true light was that which enlightens every human being coming into this world.

He was in this world, [Col. 0355] and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him. He came into his own, and his own did not receive him. But as many as received him, he gave them power to become children of God: to those who believe in his name, who were born not of bloods, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.

And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. John bears testimony concerning him and cries out, saying: “This is he of whom I told you: He who comes after me has been made before me, because he was before me.” And from his fullness we all received, [Col. 0356] even grace for grace. For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known.

And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to him, that they might question him: “Who are you?” And he confessed and did not deny; he confessed: “I am not the Christ.” And they questioned him: “What then? Are you Elijah?” And he said: “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” And he answered: “No.” Therefore they said to him: “Who then are you, that we may give an answer [Col. 0357] to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?” He answered: “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”

And those who had been sent were from the Pharisees. And they questioned him and said to him: “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” John answered them, saying: “I baptize in water; but one stands in your midst whom you do not know. He is the one who comes after me, who has been made before me, whose sandal-strap I am not worthy to untie.” These things took place in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

The next day John saw Jesus coming [Col. 0358] toward him and said: “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world. This is he of whom I said: ‘After me comes a man who has been made before me, because he was before me.’ And I did not know him; but in order that he might be made manifest to Israel, for this reason I came baptizing in water.” And John bore testimony, saying: “I saw the Spirit descending as a dove from heaven, and it remained upon him. And I did not know him; but he who sent me to baptize in water himself told me: ‘He upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining—this is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ And I saw and bore testimony [Col. 0359] that this is the Son of God.”

The next day again John was standing there, with two of his disciples. And, looking at Jesus as he walked, he said: “Behold, the Lamb of God.” The two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus. Jesus turned and, seeing them following, said to them: “What are you seeking?” They said to him: “Rabbi”—which translated means “Teacher”—“where are you staying?” He said to them: “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and remained with him that day; for it was about the tenth hour.

Now Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who had heard from John and followed him. He first found [Col. 0360] his own brother Simon and said to him: “We have found the Messiah,” which translated means “Christ.” And he brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said: “You are Simon, son of John; you shall be called Cephas,” which is translated “Peter.”

The following day he wished to depart for Galilee and found Philip. And Jesus said to him: “Follow me.” Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. Philip found Nathanael and said to him: “We have found Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth, of whom Moses wrote in the law and the Prophets.” Nathanael said to him: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said to him: [Col. 0361] “Come and see.”

Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him: “Behold, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.” Nathanael said to him: “How do you know me?” Jesus answered and said to him: “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.” Nathanael answered him and said: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the king of Israel.” Jesus answered and said to him: “Because I told you, ‘I saw you under the fig tree,’ do you believe? You shall see greater things than these.” And he said to him: “Amen, amen, I say to you: you shall see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.”

And on the third day a wedding took place in [Col. 0362] Cana of Galilee, and Jesus’ mother was there. Jesus and his disciples had also been invited to the wedding. When the wine failed, Jesus’ mother said to him: “They have no wine.” And Jesus said to her: “What is that to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.” His mother said to the servants: “Whatever he tells you, do.”

Now six stone water-jars were standing there, according to the purification rite of the Jews, each holding two or three measures. Jesus said to them: “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim. And Jesus said to them: “Draw some now and carry it to the master of the feast.” And they carried it.

[Col. 0363] When the master of the feast tasted the water made wine, and did not know where it came from—though the servants who had drawn the water knew—the master of the feast then called the bridegroom and said to him: “Every person puts out the good wine first, and when people have become drunk, then what is inferior. But you have kept the good wine until now.” This Jesus performed as the first beginning of signs, in Cana of Galilee; and he manifested his glory, and his disciples believed in him.

After this Jesus went [Note: [Col. 0363] It adds *in*, as also the Greek text, εἰς, “into.”] into Capernaum, with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; and they remained there not many days. The Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. He found in the temple those selling [Col. 0364] sheep, oxen, and doves, and money-changers sitting there. Making something like a whip out of cords, he drove all of them from the temple, together with the sheep and oxen; he poured out the money-changers’ coins and overturned the tables. And to those selling doves he said: “Take these things away from here; do not make my Father’s house a house of trade.” His disciples remembered that it was written: “Zeal for your house has consumed me.”

Then the Jews answered and said to him: “What sign do you show us, since you do these things?” Jesus answered and said to them: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” [Col. 0365] The Jews therefore said: “This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it in three days?” But he was speaking of the temple of his body. When therefore he had risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

Now while he was in Jerusalem at the feast, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he was doing. But Jesus did not entrust himself to them, because he himself knew everyone, and because he had no need for anyone to bear testimony concerning a human being; for he himself knew what was in a human being.

Now there was a man of the Pharisees, [Col. 0366] Nicodemus by name, a ruler of the Jews. He came to Jesus by night and said to him: “Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; for no one can do these signs that you do unless God is with him.” Jesus answered and said to him: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” Nicodemus said to him: “How can a person be born anew when old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?” Jesus answered and said: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born of water and Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom [Col. 0367] of God. What is born of flesh is flesh, and what is born of [Note: [Col. 0367] After *Spirit*, *holy* is absent, likewise in the Greek text.] spirit is spirit. Do not wonder that I told you: ‘You must be born anew.’ The Spirit blows where it wills, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”

Nicodemus answered and said to him: “How can these things happen?” Jesus answered and said to him: “Are you the teacher [Note: [Col. 0367] So also the Greek text: τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, “of Israel.”] of Israel, and do not know these things? Amen, amen, I say to you: what we know we speak, and what we have seen we testify to; yet you do not receive our testimony. If I told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? [Col. 0368] No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven. And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.

“For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into this world in order to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him. Whoever believes in him is not judged; but whoever does not believe has already been judged, [Col. 0369] because he does not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of God. And this is the judgment: that light came into this world, and people loved darkness rather than light, because their works were evil. For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his works be exposed. But whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be made manifest, because they have been done in God. . . .

After these things Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea; and there he remained with them and baptized. John too was baptizing in the wilderness near Salim, because there was much water there; and people came and were baptized. For John had not yet been put into prison.

[Col. 0370] Therefore a dispute arose between John’s disciples and Jews concerning purification. They came to John and said to him: “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you bore testimony—behold, he baptizes, and all are coming to him.” John answered and said: “A human being cannot receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven. You yourselves bear me testimony that I said: ‘I am not the Christ,’ but rather, ‘I have been sent before him.’ He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. This joy of mine, therefore, has been fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.

“He who comes from above [Col. 0371] is above all. He who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks from the earth. But he who comes from heaven is above all, and what he has seen and heard, this he testifies to; yet no one receives his testimony. Whoever receives his testimony has sealed this: that God is true. For he whom God sent speaks the words of God; for he gives the Spirit not by measure. . . . The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; but whoever does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.”

When therefore the Lord learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing [Col. 0372] more disciples than John—although Jesus [Note: [Col. 0371] It adds *himself*, as also the Greek text, αὐτός.] himself did not baptize, but his disciples did—he left Judea and went again into Galilee. . . . But he had to pass through Samaria.

He came, then, to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the estate that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. Jacob’s spring was there. Jesus, therefore, weary from the journey, was sitting thus by the well. It was about the sixth hour. A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her: “Give me a drink.” For his disciples had gone into the city to buy food.

The Samaritan woman said to him: “How is it that you, being a Jew, [Col. 0373] ask a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” For Jews do not associate with Samaritans. Jesus answered and said to her: “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ perhaps you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.” The woman said to him: “Sir, you have nothing with which to draw, and the well is deep; from where then do you have living water? Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and himself drank from it, as did his sons and his livestock?” Jesus answered and said to her: “Everyone who drinks from this water will thirst again; but whoever drinks from the water that I shall give him will never thirst, but the water that I shall give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into eternal life.”

The woman said to him: “Sir, give me this [Col. 0374] water, so that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw.” Jesus said to her: “Go, call your husband, and come here.” The woman answered and said: “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her: “You have spoken well in saying, ‘I have no husband’; for you have had five husbands, and the one you now have is not your husband. In this you have spoken truly.” The woman said to him: “Sir, I see that you are a prophet. Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that [Note: [Col. 0373] It adds *in*, likewise the Greek text, ἐν.] in Jerusalem is the place where one ought to worship.”

Jesus said to her: “Woman, believe me: an hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because [Col. 0375] salvation is from the Jews. But an hour is coming, and now is, when true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and truth; for indeed the Father seeks such people to worship him. God is Spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

The woman said to him: “We know that Messiah is coming, who is called Christ; when he comes, he will announce everything to us.” Jesus said to her: “I am he, the one speaking with you.”

Immediately his disciples came and wondered that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said: “What are you seeking?” or, “Why are you speaking with her?” Therefore the woman left her water-jar and went into the city, and said to the people: “Come, see a man [Col. 0376] who told me everything I have done. Is he perhaps the Christ?” They went out from the city and came to him.

Meanwhile his disciples were asking him, saying: “Rabbi, eat.” But he said to them: “I have food to eat that you do not know.” The disciples therefore said to one another: “Has anyone brought him something to eat?” Jesus said to them: “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work. Do you not say that four months still remain and then the harvest comes? Behold, I say to you: Lift up your eyes and see the fields, because they are already white for harvest. And the reaper receives wages and gathers [Col. 0377] fruit for eternal life, so that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. For in this the saying is true: ‘One is the sower and another the reaper.’ I sent you to reap that for which you did not labor. Others labored, and you have entered into their labors.”

Many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the word of the woman, who bore testimony: “He told me everything I have done.” Therefore, when the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to remain there with them; and he remained there two days. And many more believed because of his word. And they said to the woman: “We no longer believe because of your speech, for we ourselves have heard [Col. 0378] and know that this is truly the Savior of the world, Christ.”

After two days [Note: [Col. 0377] Before *departed*, *went out* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] he departed from there into Galilee. For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country. When therefore he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen everything he had done in Jerusalem at the feast; for they too had come to the feast.

Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made water wine. There was [Note: [Col. 0377] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but/now.”] now a certain royal official whose son was ill [Note: [Col. 0377] It adds *in*, as also the Greek text, ἐν.] in Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, he went to him and asked him to come down and heal [Col. 0379] his son, for he was beginning to die. Jesus therefore said to him: “Unless you see signs and wonders, you do not believe.” The royal official said to him: “Sir, come down before my son dies.” Jesus said to him: “Go; your son lives.” [Note: [Col. 0379] It adds *and*, likewise the Greek text, καί.] And the man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and went away.

As he was going down, his servants met him and announced: “Your son lives.” Therefore he asked them at what hour he had begun to improve. They said to him: “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.” The father therefore knew that it was [Col. 0380] [Note: [Col. 0379] “At that hour,” in the ablative case, the verb *was* being omitted. So also the Greek text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ (ἐν ᾗ), “at that hour [in which].”] at that hour when Jesus said to him: “Your son lives.” And he himself believed, and his whole household. This Jesus again performed as the second sign, when he came from Judea into Galilee.

After these things there was a feast-day of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. Now in Jerusalem, by the Sheep Pool, there is a pool called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porticoes. In these lay a great multitude of sick persons, blind, lame, and withered, awaiting the movement of the water.

[Col. 0381] There was a certain man there who had been in infirmity [Note: [Col. 0381] After *infirmity*, *his* is absent, likewise in the Greek text.] thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had already been there a long time, he said to him: “Do you wish to become well?” The sick man answered and said: “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water has been stirred; for while I am coming, another goes down before me.” Jesus said to him: “Rise, take up your mat, and walk.” And immediately that man became well, took up his mat, and walked. Now it was the Sabbath on that day. Therefore the Jews said to him who had been healed: “It is the Sabbath; it is not lawful for you to carry your mat.”

[Col. 0382] But he answered them: “He who made me well himself said to me: ‘Take up your mat and walk.’” Then they asked him: “Who is that man who said to you, ‘Take up your mat and walk’?” But the one who had been healed did not know who he was, for Jesus had withdrawn from the crowd assembled in the place. Later Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: “Behold, you have become well; sin no more, lest something worse happen to you.” [Note: [Col. 0381] It adds *and*, as also the Greek text, καί.] And the man went away and reported to the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. For this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him, [Col. 0383] because he did these things on the Sabbath.

But Jesus answered them: “My Father works until now, and I work.” For this reason the Jews sought to kill him, because he was not only breaking the Sabbath but was also calling God his own Father, making himself equal to God.

Jesus answered and said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son cannot do anything of himself, except what he sees the Father doing. For whatever things he does, these the Son likewise does. For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he himself does; and he will show him greater works than these, so that you may marvel. For just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wills. For the Father [Col. 0384] judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him. . . .

“Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life. Amen, amen, I say to you: an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear shall live. For just as the Father has life in himself, so he gave the Son also to have life in himself; and he gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man. [Col. 0385] Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs shall hear his [Note: [Col. 0385] So also the Greek text: αὐτοῦ, “his.”] voice and shall come forth: those who have done good, to a resurrection of life; but those who have done evil, to a resurrection of judgment.

“I cannot do anything of myself. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will but the will of him who sent me. If I bear testimony concerning myself, my testimony is not true. Another bears testimony concerning me, and I know that the testimony which he bears concerning me is true. You sent to John, and he bore testimony to the truth. [Col. 0386] But I do not receive testimony from a human being; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved. He was a burning and shining lamp, and you wished to rejoice for an hour in his light. But I have testimony greater than John’s. For the works that the Father gave me to complete—the very works that I [Note: [Col. 0385] Before *I do*, *I* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] do—bear testimony concerning me that the Father sent me. And the Father who sent me himself bears testimony concerning me. You have never heard his voice nor seen his form; and you do not have his word abiding in you, because you do not believe him whom he sent.

[Col. 0387] “Search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they that bear testimony concerning me. Yet you do not wish to come to me in order that you may have life. I do not receive glory from human beings. But I have known you: that you do not have the love of God in yourselves. I came in my Father’s name, and you do not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. How can you believe, receiving glory from one another and not seeking the glory that is from God alone? Do not suppose that I [Note: [Col. 0387] So also the Greek text: κατηγορήσω, “will accuse.”] will accuse you [Col. 0388] before the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, in whom you hope. For if you believed Moses, perhaps you would believe me also; for he wrote concerning me. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”

After these things Jesus went away across the Sea of Galilee, that of Tiberias. And great crowds followed him because they had seen the signs that he was performing upon the sick. Jesus therefore went up the mountain and sat there with his disciples. Now the Passover, the feast-day of the Jews, was near.

[Col. 0389] Jesus lifted up his eyes and, seeing that a great crowd was coming to him, said to Philip: “Where shall we buy bread for these people to eat?” But he said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was about to do. Philip answered him: “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough for them, for each to receive even a little.” One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him: “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish; but what are these among so many?” Jesus said: “Make the people recline.” Now there was much grass in that place. Therefore the men reclined, about five thousand in number.

[Col. 0390] Jesus then took the loaves and, having given thanks, distributed them to those reclining; likewise also from the fish, as much as they wanted. When they had been filled, he said to his disciples: “Gather the fragments left over, [Note: [Col. 0389] So also the Greek text: ἵνα μή τι … ἀπόληται, “lest anything … perish”; Codex Cantabrigiensis adds ἐξ αὐτῶν, “of them.”] lest anything of them perish.” Therefore they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley loaves, which were left over by those who had eaten.

Then those people, seeing the sign that Jesus had performed, said: “This is truly the prophet who comes into this world.” But Jesus, knowing that they were about to come and seize him and make him king, [Note: [Col. 0389] So also the Greek text: ἀνεχώρησε, “withdrew.”] withdrew again to the mountain by himself alone.

[Col. 0391] When evening had come, his disciples went down to the sea. Boarding a boat, they went across the sea to Capernaum; darkness had already fallen, and Jesus had not yet come to them. The sea was rising because a strong wind was blowing. When therefore they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking upon the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid. But he said to them: “It is I; do not be afraid.” [Note: [Col. 0391] So also the Greek text: ἤθελον, “they wished.”] They wished, therefore, to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat came to the land toward which they were going.

The next day, the crowd which stood on the far side of the sea saw that no other boat [Col. 0392] was there except one, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with his disciples, but that his disciples had gone away alone. Other boats, however, came from Tiberias near the place where they had eaten the bread which the Lord blessed. Therefore, when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they immediately boarded boats and came to Capernaum seeking Jesus. When they found him across the sea, they said to him: “Rabbi, when did you come here?”

Jesus answered them and said: “Amen, amen, I say to you: you seek me, not because you saw signs [Note: [Col. 0391] It adds *and wonders*, as also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek: καὶ τέρατα, “and wonders”; likewise the Gothic version, apparently from John 4:48.] and wonders, [Col. 0393] but because you ate from the loaves and were filled. Work not for food that perishes, but for food that endures unto eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For God the Father has sealed him.”

They said therefore to him: “What shall we do, that we may work the works of God?” Jesus answered and said to them: “This is the work of God: that you believe in him whom he sent.” They said to him: “What sign then do you perform, so that we may see and believe you? What work do you do? Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’” Jesus therefore said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: Moses did not give you bread from heaven, but my Father [Col. 0394] gives you bread from heaven. For the bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to this world.”

Therefore they said to him: “Lord, always give us this bread.” Jesus said to them: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst. But I told you that you have seen me and do not believe. Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I shall not cast out; because I came down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of him who sent me. And this is the will of him who [Note: [Col. 0393] After *me*, *the Father’s* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] sent me: that of everything he gave me [Col. 0395] I should lose [Note: [Col. 0395] It adds *anything*, as also Codex Cantabrigiensis: μηδέν, “nothing.”] nothing of it, but raise it up on the last day. For this [Note: [Col. 0395] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: γάρ, “for.”] is the will of my Father who sent me: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him has eternal life; and I shall raise him up on the last day.”

The Jews therefore murmured about him because he said: “I am the [Note: [Col. 0395] After *bread*, *living* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] bread that came down from heaven.” And they said: “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say, ‘I came down from heaven’?” Jesus therefore answered and said to them: “Do not murmur among yourselves. No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I shall raise [Col. 0396] him up on the last day. For it is written in the Prophets: ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me. Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God—he has seen the Father. Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life.

“I am the bread of life. Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died. This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that if anyone eats of it, he may not die. I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he shall live forever. For this bread which I shall give [Col. 0397] is my flesh, which I shall give for the life of this world.”

The Jews therefore disputed with one another, saying: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?” Jesus said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you do not have life in yourselves. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I shall raise him up on the last day. For my flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood [Col. 0398] abides in me, and I in him. As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so also whoever eats me shall live because of me. This is the bread that came down from heaven—not as your fathers ate manna and died. But whoever eats this bread shall live forever.”

He said these things in the synagogue, teaching in Capernaum. Therefore many of his disciples, hearing this, said: “This saying is hard; who can hear it?” But Jesus, knowing in himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, said to them: “Does this cause you to stumble? What then if you see [Col. 0399] the Son of Man ascending to where he was before? It is the Spirit that gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life. But there are some among you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who those were who did not believe in him, and who it was that would betray him. And he said: “For this reason I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been given to him by my Father.”

From this [Note: [Col. 0399] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “then/but.”] time, therefore, many of his disciples went back and no longer walked with him. Jesus therefore said to the Twelve: “Do you also wish to go away?” Simon Peter answered him: “Lord, [Col. 0400] to whom shall we go? You have words of eternal life. And we have believed and known that you are the Christ, the Son of God.” Jesus answered them: “Did I not choose you twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.” He spoke of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot; for he was about to betray him, though he was one of the Twelve.

After [Note: [Col. 0399] After *these things*, *but* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] these things Jesus walked in Galilee, for he did not wish to walk in Judea because the Jews were seeking to kill him. Now the Jewish feast of Tabernacles was near. Therefore [Note: [Col. 0399] So also the Greek text: οὖν, “therefore.”] his brothers said to him: “Leave here [Col. 0401] and go into Judea, so that your disciples too may see the works that you do. For no one does anything in secret while he himself seeks to be publicly known. If you do these things, make yourself manifest to this world.” For not even his brothers [Note: [Col. 0401] It adds *then*, as also Codex Cantabrigiensis.] then believed in him.

Jesus therefore said to them: “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready. This world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I bear testimony concerning it that its works are evil. Go up yourselves to this feast. I do not yet go up to this feast, because my time has not yet been fulfilled.” Having said these things to them, he remained [Note: [Col. 0401] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, “in Galilee.”] in Galilee.

But when [Col. 0402] his brothers had gone up, then he too went up to the feast, not openly but as if in secret. Therefore the Jews sought him at the feast and said: “Where is that man?” And there was much murmuring concerning him among the people. Some said: “He is true.” But others said: “No; rather, he deceives the crowds.” Yet no one spoke openly concerning him, for fear of the Jews.

When the feast was already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and taught. The crowds marvelled, saying: “How does this man know letters, when he has not learned?” But [Note: [Col. 0401] Before *Jesus*, *them* is absent, also in the Gothic version.] Jesus answered and said: “My teaching is not mine, but that of him who sent me. If anyone wills to do his will, [Col. 0403] he shall know concerning this teaching whether it is from God or whether I speak from myself. Whoever speaks from himself seeks his own glory; but whoever seeks the glory of him who sent him, that one is true, and there is no unrighteousness in him. Did not Moses give you
the law, and none of you keeps the law. Why do you seek to kill me?” The crowd answered and said, “You have a demon. Who seeks to kill you?” Jesus answered and said to them, “I did one work, and you all marvel. For this reason Moses gave you circumcision—not because it is from Moses, but from the fathers—and on the Sabbath you circumcise a man. If, then, a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be broken, why are you angry with me because I made the whole man well on the Sabbath? Do not judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.”

Then some of the Jerusalemites said, “Is this not he whom they seek to kill? And behold, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Have the rulers perhaps truly recognized that this is truly the Christ? Yet we know where this man is from; but when the Christ comes, no one knows where he is from.” Therefore Jesus cried out while teaching in the temple and saying, “You know me, and you know where I am from; and I have not come of myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you do not know. But I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”  
[Note: Col. 0403. Adds *autem* (“but”), as also the Greek text, δέ.]

Therefore they sought to seize him, but no one laid hands upon him, because his hour had not yet come. But many of the crowd believed in him and said, “When the Christ comes, will he do more signs than those which this man has done?”  
[Note: Col. 0405. So also the Greek text, ἐποίησεν, “did.”]

The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him, and the chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to seize him. Therefore Jesus said, “I am still with you a little while, and I go to him who sent me. You will seek me and will not find me; and where I am, you cannot come.”  
[Note: Col. 0405. Before *Jesus*, *eis* (“to them”) is absent, also in the Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

Therefore the Jews said to one another, “Where will this man go, so that we shall not find him? Will he go into the Dispersion among the Gentiles and teach the Gentiles? What is this saying that he spoke: ‘You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am you cannot come’?”

But on the last, great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. He who believes in me, as Scripture said, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly.”  
[Note: Col. 0405. So also the Greek text, εἶπεν, “said.”]

But he said this concerning the Spirit, whom those believing in him were to receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet in them, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

But many from that crowd, hearing these words, said, “This is truly the Prophet.” Others said, “This is the Christ.” But some said, “Does the Christ come from Galilee? Does not Scripture say that the Christ comes from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the town where David was?” Therefore a division arose in the crowd because of him. Some of them wished to seize him, but no one laid hands upon him.

Then the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said to them, “Why have you not brought him?” The officers answered, “Never has any man spoken as this man speaks.” Therefore the Pharisees answered them, “Have you also been deceived? Has any one of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed in him? But this crowd, which does not know the law, is accursed.” Nicodemus said to them—he who had come to him by night, being one of them—“Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him and knows what he does?” They answered and said to him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see, because no prophet arises from Galilee.”

Then Jesus again spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” Therefore the Pharisees said to him, “You bear witness concerning yourself; your testimony is not true.” Jesus answered and said to them, “Even if I bear witness concerning myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going. You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one. And if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent me. For it is also written in your law that the testimony of two men is true. I am he who bears witness concerning myself, and the Father who sent me bears witness concerning me.”

Therefore they said to him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered, “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, perhaps you would know my Father also.” These words he spoke in the treasury, teaching in the temple; and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come.  
[Note: Col. 0409. After *locutus est* (“spoke”), *Jesus* is absent, also in the Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

Therefore Jesus again said to them, “I go away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I go, you cannot come.” Therefore the Jews said, “Will he kill himself, because he says, ‘Where I go, you cannot come’?” And Jesus said to them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world. Therefore I told you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins.”

Therefore they said to him, “Who are you?” And Jesus said to them, “The beginning, which I also speak to you. I have much to say and to judge concerning you; but he who sent me is true, and what I heard from him I speak in this world.” They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.

Therefore Jesus said to them, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and that I do nothing of myself; but as my Father taught me, these things I speak. And he who sent me is with me; the Father has not left me alone, because I always do the things pleasing to him.” As he spoke these things, many believed in him.

Then Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him, “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples; and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.”  
[Note: Col. 0411. So also the Greek text, ἐστέ, “you are.”]

They answered him, “We are Abraham’s seed, and have never been slaves to anyone. How do you say, ‘You shall become free’?” Jesus answered them, “Amen, amen, I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin. But the slave does not remain in the house forever; the Son remains forever. Therefore, if the Son makes you free, you shall truly be free. I know that you are Abraham’s seed; but you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in you. I speak what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”  
[Note: Col. 0413. So also the Greek text, σπέρμα, “seed.”]

They answered and said to him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.”  
[Note: Col. 0413. So also the Greek text: *εἰ τέκνα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἦτε, τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἐποιεῖτε ἄν*—“If you were children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham.”]

“But now you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken to you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this. You do the works of your father.” Therefore they said to him, “We were not born of fornication; we have one Father, God.” Jesus therefore said to them, “If God were your Father, you would surely love me, because I proceeded from God and came; for I did not come of myself, but he sent me. Why do you not understand my speech? Because you cannot hear my word. You are of your father the devil, and you desire to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and did not stand in the truth, because truth is not in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, because he is a liar and its father. But because I have spoken the truth to you, you do not believe me. Which of you convicts me of sin? If I speak truth, why do you not believe me? He who is of God hears God’s words. Therefore you do not hear, because you are not of God.”

Therefore the Jews answered and said to him, “Do we not rightly say that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?” Jesus answered, “I do not have a demon, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.  
[Note: Col. 0415. So also the Greek text, ἀτιμάζετε, “you dishonor.”]

“But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges. Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he shall never see death.” Therefore the Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets; yet you say, ‘If anyone keeps my word, he shall never taste death.’ Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets died. Whom do you make yourself?” Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, he whom you say is our God; and you do not know him. But I know him; and if I said that I do not know him, I should be a liar like you. But I know him and keep his word. Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day; and he saw it and rejoiced.”  
[Note: Col. 0415. Adds *and*, as also in the Greek text, καί.]

Therefore the Jews said to him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?” Jesus said to them, “Amen, amen, I say to you: before Abraham came to be, I am.” Therefore they took up stones to stone him; but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple, passing through their midst, and went on.

And as he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.  
[Note: Col. 0417. Before *vidit* (“saw”), *Jesus* is absent also in the Greek text.]

His disciples asked him, saying, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?” Jesus answered, “Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but that the works of God might be manifested in him. I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day; night is coming, when no one can work. As long as I am in this world, I am the light of the world.”

Having said these things, he spat upon the ground, made clay from the spittle, and spread it upon the blind man’s eyes. And he said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam,” which is interpreted “Sent.” Therefore he went, washed, and came back seeing.

Then his neighbors and those who had seen him before, because he was a beggar, said, “Is this not the man who sat and begged?” Others said, “It is he.” Others said, “He is like him.” But he said, “I am he.” Therefore they said to him, “How were your eyes opened?” He answered and said, “The man called Jesus made clay and spread it on my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go, wash in the pool of Siloam.’ So I went, washed, and see.”  
[Note: Col. 0417. So also the Greek text: *ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπος*—“that man answered and said, ‘A man …’”]

They said to him, “Where is he?” He said, “I do not know.”

They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind. Now it was a Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes. Therefore the Pharisees again asked him how he had received sight. And he said to them, “He put clay on my eyes; I washed, and I see.” Therefore some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath.” Others said, “How can a sinful man do such signs?”  
[Note: Col. 0419. After *alii* (“others”), *autem* (“but”) is absent also in the Codex Cantabrigiensis. The reading is *talia*, “such,” as also in the Greek text, τοιαῦτα.]

And there was division among them. Therefore they again said to the blind man, “What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?” And he said, “He is a prophet.”

The Jews did not believe concerning him that he had been blind and had received sight, until they called the parents of him who had received sight.  
[Note: Col. 0419. After *credebant* (“believed”), *ergo* (“therefore”) is absent, also in the Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

They asked them, saying, “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?” His parents answered and said, “We know that this is our son and that he was born blind. But how he now sees we do not know, nor do we know who opened his eyes. Ask him; he is of age. Let him speak for himself.” His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that, if anyone confessed him to be the Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.  
[Note: Col. 0421. Before *Christum*, *esse* (“to be”) is absent, likewise in the Greek text.]

For this reason his parents said, “He is of age; ask him.”

Therefore they again called the man who had been blind and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.” He answered, “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. One thing I know: that whereas I was blind, now I see.” Therefore they again said to him, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?” He answered them, “I told you already, and you did not hear. Why do you wish to hear it again? Do you also wish to become his disciples?” Then they reviled him and said, “You are his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses. We know that God spoke to Moses; but this man, we do not know where he is from.”

The man answered and said to them, “For this is remarkable: that you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes. But we know that God does not hear sinners; rather, if anyone worships God and does his will, him he hears. Since the world began, it has not been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind. Unless this man were from God, he could do nothing.” They answered and said to him, “You were wholly born in sins, and do you teach us?” And they cast him out.

Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he found him, he said to him, “Do you believe in the Son of God?” He answered and said, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?” Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and he who speaks with you is he.” Then he said, “I believe, Lord”; and falling down, he worshipped him.

And Jesus said, “For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and that those who see may become blind.”  
[Note: Col. 0423. Before *ex Pharisaeis* (“from the Pharisees”), *quidam* (“some”) is absent, also in the Greek text.]

Some Pharisees who were with him heard these things and said to him, “Are we also blind?” Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would not have sin; but now you say, ‘We see’; your sin remains.

“Amen, amen, I say to you: he who does not enter the sheepfold through the door, but climbs in by another way, is a thief and a robber. But he who enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the gatekeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice; and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out. And when he has brought out his own sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice. But they will not follow a stranger; rather, they flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.”

Jesus spoke this figure to them, but they did not understand what he was saying to them. Therefore Jesus again said to them, “Amen, amen, I say to you: I am the door of the sheep. All who came are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them.  
[Note: Col. 0425. So also the Greek text, ἀλλά, “but.”]

“I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he shall be saved, and shall enter and go out and find pasture. The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it more abundantly. I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. But the hireling, who is not a shepherd and whose own sheep they are not, sees the wolf coming, abandons the sheep, and flees; and the wolf seizes them and scatters the sheep. The hireling flees because he is hired and has no care for the sheep.

“I am the good shepherd; I know my sheep, and my sheep know me, as the Father knows me and I know the Father. And I lay down my life for my sheep. I also have other sheep, which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one flock and one shepherd. For this reason the Father loves me: because I lay down my life, that I may take it again. No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again. This commandment I received from my Father.”

Again a division arose among the Jews because of these words. Many of them said, “He has a demon and is mad; why do you listen to him?” Others said, “These are not the words of one who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”

Then the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem, and it was winter. Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s portico. Therefore the Jews surrounded him and said to him, “How long do you keep our soul in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us openly.” Jesus answered them, “I speak to you, and you do not believe. The works which I do in my Father’s name bear witness concerning me; but you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I told you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. And I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them from my hand. What my Father has given me is greater than all, and no one can snatch it from my Father’s hand. I and the Father are one.”

Therefore the Jews again took up stones to stone him. Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father; for which of those works do you stone me?” The Jews answered him, “We do not stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God.” Jesus answered them, “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, You are gods’? If he called those gods to whom the word of God came—and Scripture cannot be broken—do you say to him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You blaspheme,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’? If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me. But if I do them, even if you do not wish to believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in me and I in him.”

Therefore they again sought to seize him, but he escaped from their hands. And he went away again beyond the Jordan, to the place where John had first been baptizing, and remained there. Many came to him and said, “John indeed performed no sign, but everything that John said about this man was true.” And many believed in him there.

Now there was a certain sick man named Lazarus, of Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha. Mary was the one who had anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair; her brother Lazarus was sick. Therefore his sisters sent to him, saying, “Lord, behold, he whom you love is sick.” But Jesus, hearing it, said, “This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

Jesus loved Martha, her sister Mary, and Lazarus. Therefore, when he heard that Lazarus was sick, he nevertheless remained two days in the same place.  
[Note: Col. 0431. So also the Greek text, ἀσθενεῖ, “is sick.”]

Then after this he said to his disciples, “Let us go into Judaea again.” The disciples said to him, “Rabbi, the Jews were just seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?” Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks by day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world. But if anyone walks by night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.” Having said these things, afterward he said to them, “Lazarus our friend sleeps, but I am going in order to awaken him.”  
[Note: Col. 0431. So also the Greek text, λέγει, “says.”]

Therefore his disciples said, “Lord, if he sleeps, he will be well.” But Jesus had spoken of his death; they, however, thought that he was speaking about sleep in the ordinary sense. Then Jesus said to them plainly, “Lazarus is dead; and I rejoice for your sake, that you may believe, because I was not there. But let us go to him.” Then Thomas, called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, that we may die with him.”

Therefore Jesus, coming, found that Lazarus had already been four days in the tomb. Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away. Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother.

Therefore, when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet him; but Mary remained seated at home. Martha then said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that whatever you ask from God, God will give you.” Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.” Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day.” Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me, though he has died, shall live; and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never die. Do you believe this?” She said to him, “Certainly, Lord. I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who came into this world.”  
[Note: Col. 0433. After *Dei* (“of God”), *vivi* (“living”) is absent, also in the Greek text.]

Having said this, she went away and secretly called Mary her sister, saying, “The Teacher is here and calls you.” When she heard this, she rose quickly and came to him. For Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him. The Jews who were with her in the house, consoling her, saw that Mary rose quickly and went out, and followed her, saying, “She goes to the tomb, to weep there.”

Therefore Mary, when she came where Jesus was, saw him and fell at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” Therefore Jesus, when he saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, was deeply moved in spirit and troubled himself. He said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to him, “Lord, come and see.” And Jesus wept. Therefore the Jews said, “See how he loved him.” But some of them said, “Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind, have caused this man also not to die?”  
[Note: Col. 0435. After *caeci* (“blind”), *nati* (“born”) is absent, also in the Greek text.]

Therefore Jesus, again deeply moved within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it. Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, “Lord, he already smells, for it is the fourth day.” Jesus said to her, “Did I not tell you that, if you believe, you will see the glory of God?” Therefore they took away the stone from where he lay.

Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven and said, “Father, I thank you because you heard me. I indeed knew that you always hear me; but I said it because of the people standing around, that they may believe that you sent me.” Having said these things, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” Immediately the dead man came out, bound hand and foot with grave-cloths, and his face was wrapped in a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Loose him, and let him go.”

Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, seeing what Jesus did, believed in him.  
[Note: Col. 0435. After *Mariam*, “Mary,” *et Martham*, “and Martha,” is absent, also in the Greek text.]

But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done. Therefore the chief priests and Pharisees assembled a council and said, “What are we to do? For this man performs many signs.
