If we let him go on thus, all will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and nation.” But one of them, named Caiaphas, high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all, nor do you consider that it is expedient for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish.” But he did not say this of himself; rather, because he was high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation, and not only for the nation, but also to gather into one the children of God who were scattered abroad.

Therefore from that day the Jews planned to kill him. But Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews; rather, he went away from there into the region near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and remained there with his disciples.

Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up from the country into Jerusalem before the Passover, to purify themselves. Therefore they sought Jesus and said to one another, as they stood in the temple, “What do you think? Surely he will not come to the feast?” Now the chief priests and Pharisees had given an order that, if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, that they might seize him.

But Jesus, six days before the Passover, came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, who had died, whom Jesus raised from the dead.  
[Note: Col. 0439. So also the Greek text, ἦν Λάζαρος ὁ τεθνηκώς, “Lazarus was [there], the one who had died.”]

Therefore they made him a supper there, and Martha served; Lazarus was one of those reclining with him. Mary therefore took a pound of costly genuine nard ointment, anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.

Then one of his disciples, Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, who was about to betray him, said, “Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”  
[Note: Col. 0439. Adds *Simon*, as likewise the Greek text, Σίμωνος.]

But he said this, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief and had the money-box; he carried what was put into it.  
[Note: Col. 0439. So also the Greek text, εἶχε, “had.”]

Therefore Jesus said, “Leave her; she has kept it for the day of my burial.  
[Note: Col. 0439. So also the Greek text, ἄφες, “leave [her].”]

“For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.” Therefore a great crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there, and they came, not because of Jesus alone, but also that they might see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead. But the chief priests planned to kill Lazarus also, because many of the Jews were coming on his account and believing in Jesus.

On the following day, the great crowd that had come to the feast, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him. They cried, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!” Jesus found a young ass and sat upon it, as it is written: “Do not fear, daughter of Zion; behold, your King comes, seated upon a colt of an ass.”

At first his disciples did not understand these things; but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written concerning him and that they had done these things to him. Therefore the crowd that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead bore witness. For this reason the crowd also came out to meet him, because they had heard that he had done this sign. Therefore the Pharisees said to one another, “You see that we gain nothing; behold, the whole world has gone after him.”

Now there were certain Gentiles among those who had gone up to worship at the feast. These came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and requested him, saying, “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.” Philip came and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip in turn told Jesus. Jesus answered them, saying, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit. He who loves his life loses it, and he who hates his life in this world keeps it for eternal life. If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also shall my servant be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.

“Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this hour’? But it was for this reason that I came to this hour. Father, glorify your name.” Therefore a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.” Therefore the crowd that stood by and heard it said that thunder had occurred. Others said, “An angel has spoken to him.” Jesus answered and said, “This voice came not for my sake, but for yours. Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world shall be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, shall draw all things to myself.” But he said this, signifying by what death he was about to die.

The crowd answered him, “We have heard from the law that the Christ remains forever; how then do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”  
[Note: Col. 0443. Adds *quia* (“that”), also in the Greek text, ὅτι.]

Therefore Jesus said to them, “The light is still among you for a little while.  
[Note: Col. 0445. Adds *tempus* (“time”); the Greek text likewise has χρόνον. The Codex Brixianus reads *temporis*, “of time.”]

“Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you. He who walks in darkness does not know where he goes. While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become children of light.” Jesus spoke these things, then went away and hid himself from them.

Although he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him, so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: “Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?” Therefore they could not believe, because Isaiah said again: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, lest they see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I heal them.” Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory and spoke concerning him.

Nevertheless, many even of the rulers believed in him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, lest they be put out of the synagogue. For they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.

But Jesus cried out and said, “He who believes in me does not believe in me, but in him who sent me. And he who sees me sees him who sent me. I have come as light into the world, that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness. And if anyone hears my words and believes, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.”  
[Note: Col. 0447. *Non* (“not”) is absent, also in the Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

“He who rejects me and does not receive my words has one who judges him: the word which I spoke, that shall judge him on the last day. For I have not spoken of myself; but the Father who sent me has himself given me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. Therefore the things I speak, I speak as the Father told me.”

Before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour had come for him to pass from this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end. And supper having taken place, when the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, that he should betray him, Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God, rose from supper, laid aside his garments, and, taking a towel, girded himself.  
[Note: Col. 0447. Adds *Jesus*, also in the Greek text, ὁ Ἰησοῦς.]

Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the feet of his disciples and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded. Therefore he came to Simon Peter. Peter said to him, “Lord, do you wash my feet?” Jesus answered and said to him, “What I do, you do not understand now, but afterward you will understand.” Peter said to him, “You shall never wash my feet.” Jesus answered him, “Unless I wash your feet, you have no share with me.” Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.” Jesus said to him, “He who has bathed has no need except to wash his feet, but is wholly clean. And you are clean, but not all.” For he knew who was about to betray him; therefore he said, “Not all of you are clean.”

Therefore, after he had washed their feet, taken his garments, and reclined again, he said to them, “Do you know what I have done to you? You call me Teacher and Lord, and you speak rightly, for I am. Therefore, if I, the Lord and Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that as I have done to you, you also should do. Amen, amen, I say to you: a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is an apostle greater than the one who sent him.  
[Note: Col. 0449. After *major* (“greater”), *est* (“is”) is absent, also in the Greek text.]

“If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them. I do not speak of all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But this is so that Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.’ From now on I tell you before it happens, so that when it has happened, you may believe that I am. Amen, amen, I say to you: he who receives whomever I send receives me; and he who receives me receives him who sent me.”

Having said these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit, testified, and said, “Amen, amen, I say to you: one of you will betray me.” Therefore the disciples looked at one another, uncertain of whom he spoke. One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was reclining in Jesus’ bosom. Therefore Simon Peter made a sign to him and said, “Ask who it is of whom he speaks.” Then that disciple, reclining upon Jesus’ breast, said to him, “Lord, who is it?” Jesus answered, “It is he to whom I shall give the dipped morsel.” And when he had dipped the morsel, he gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. And after he received the morsel, Satan then entered into him. Jesus said to him, “What you do, do more quickly.” But none of those reclining understood why he said this to him. For some thought that, because Judas had the money-box, Jesus had said to him, “Buy what we need for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor. Therefore, having received the morsel, he went out immediately. And it was night.

Therefore, when he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now he has been glorified.”

The Son of Man, and God has been glorified in him. If, then, God has been glorified in him, God also has glorified him in himself, and immediately has glorified him. Little children, I am with you yet a little while. You seek me; and, as I said to the Jews, “Where I am going, [Col. 0453] you cannot come,” so I say to you now. I give you a new commandment: that you love one another, just as [Note: [Col. 0453] The word *I* is added also by the Codex of Canterbury: ἐγώ ("I").] I + have loved you, that you also may love one another. By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another. Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered, “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; but you will follow later.” Peter said to him, [Note: [Col. 0453] *Lord* is added, likewise in the Greek text: κὺριε (“Lord”).] “Lord, + why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.” Jesus answered him, “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I tell you: the cock will not crow until you have denied me three times.

“Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me. In my [Col. 0454] Father’s house are many dwellings. Otherwise, I would have told you: I am going to prepare a place for you. And if I go to prepare a place for you, I am coming again and will receive you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be. And you know where I am going, and you know the way.” Thomas said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going; and how can we know the way?” Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you had known me, certainly you would also have known my Father; and from now on you know him and see him.” Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.” Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you so long, [Col. 0455] and have you not known me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. And how do you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Do you not [Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Greek text: πιστεύεις (“you believe”).] believe + that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak from myself; but the Father, who remains in me, himself does these works. [Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Greek text: πιστεύετέ μοι (“believe me”).] Believe me + that I am in the Father and the Father in me; otherwise, believe because of the works themselves. Truly, truly, I tell you: whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father. And whatever you ask in my name, I will do, so that the Father may be honoured in the [Col. 0456] Son. If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it. If you love me, keep my commandments. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, that he may be with you for ever: the Spirit of truth, whom this world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, because he remains [Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Greek text: μένει (“remains”).] with you + and is [Note: [Col. 0455] So also the Codex of Canterbury: ἐστίν (“is”).] in you +. I will not leave you orphans; I will come to you. Yet a little while, and this world will no longer see me; but you will see me, because I live and you will live. On that day you will know that [Note: [Col. 0455] After *I*, *am* is absent also in the Greek text.] I + am in my Father, and you in me, and I [Col. 0457] in you. Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me; and whoever loves me is loved by my Father, and I will love him and reveal myself to him.”

Judas—not Iscariot—said to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are going to reveal yourself to us and not to this world?” Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word; and my Father will love him, and we shall come to him and make our dwelling with him. But whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word which you heard is not mine, but the Father’s who sent me. I have spoken these things to you while remaining with you. But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the [Col. 0458] Father is going to send in my name, will teach you all things and remind you of all things that I have said to you. Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as this world gives. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid. You heard that I said to you, ‘I am going away and I am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would surely rejoice that I am going to the Father, because my Father is greater than I. And now I have told you before it happens, so that, when it has happened, you may believe. I will no longer speak much with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he will find nothing in me. But so that this world may know that I love [Col. 0459] my Father, and that I do as the Father commanded me: rise, let us go from here.

“I am the true vine, and my Father is the cultivator. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit, [Note: [Col. 0459] So also the Greek text: αἴρει (“removes”).] he removes +; and every branch that bears fruit he cleanses, so that it may bear much fruit. You are already clean because of the word which I have spoken to you. Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in me. I am the vine and you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing. Whoever does not [Col. 0460] remain in me will be cut off like a branch, thrown outside, and wither; and they gather them and [Note: [Col. 0459] So also the Greek text: ἐβλήθη . . . ἐξηράνθη . . . αὐτὰ . . . βαλλουσι (“was cast . . . withered . . . them . . . they cast”).] cast + them into the fire, and they burn. But if you remain in me and my words remain in you, whatever you wish to ask will be done for you. In this my Father has been glorified: that you bear much fruit and may become my disciples. As the Father loved me, so I loved you. Remain in my love. If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love. I have spoken these things [Col. 0461] to you so that my joy may remain in you and your joy may be made full. This is my commandment: that you love one another as I loved you. No one has greater love than this: that someone lay down his life for his friends. You are my friends, if you do what I command you. I no longer [Note: [Col. 0461] So also the Greek text: λέγω (“I say”).] call + you servants, because a servant does not know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I heard from my Father. You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, so that you also may bear fruit and your fruit may remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you. I command you these things: that you love [Col. 0462] one another.

“If this world hates you, know that it hated me before you. If you were of this world, the world would certainly love what was its own; but because you are not of this world, and I chose you out of this world, therefore this world hates you. Remember the word which I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will persecute you also; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also. But they will do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know him who sent me. If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; [Col. 0463] but now they have no excuse for their sin. Whoever hates me also hates my Father. If I had not done among them works which no one else has done, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father. But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’ But when the Paraclete comes, whom I shall send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father—he will bear witness concerning me. And you too bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning. I have spoken these things to you so that you may not be caused to stumble. They will expel you from the synagogue; indeed, the hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he has offered a sacrifice [Col. 0464] to God. But they will do these things to you because they have not known either the Father or me. Yet I have spoken these things to you so that, when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you. I did not tell you these things from the beginning because I was with you; but now [Note: [Col. 0463] So also the Greek text: δέ (“but”).] I + am going to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’ But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart. Yet I tell you the truth: it is advantageous for you that I go away, for if I do not go, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go, I shall send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment: concerning [Col. 0465] sin, because they did not believe in me; concerning righteousness, because I am going to my Father and you will no longer see me; and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been condemned. I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all truth. For he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak; and he will announce to you the things that are coming. He will glorify me, because he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you. Everything that the Father has is mine. Therefore I said to you, ‘He will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.’ Yet a little while, and you will not see [Col. 0466] me; and again a little while, and you will see me, because I am going to the Father.”

His disciples therefore said to one another, “What is this that he says to us: ‘A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me’; and, ‘Because I am going to the Father’?” They were therefore saying, “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We do not know what he is saying.” But Jesus knew that they wished to ask him, and said to them, “Are you questioning among yourselves about this, because I said, ‘A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me’? Truly, truly, I tell you: you will weep and lament, but this world will rejoice. [Note: [Col. 0465] After *you*, *but* is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] You + will be sorrowful, but your sorrow [Col. 0467] will become joy. When a woman gives birth, she has sorrow, because her hour has come; but when the child has been born, she no longer remembers the distress, because of joy that a human being has been born into the world. So you also now indeed have sorrow; but I shall see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one [Note: [Col. 0467] So also the Greek text: αἴρει (“takes away”).] takes + your joy from you. And on that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I tell you: if you ask the Father anything in my name, he will give it to you. Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete. I have spoken these things to you in figurative sayings. But the hour is coming when I shall no longer speak to you in figurative sayings, [Col. 0468] but shall openly announce to you concerning the Father. On that day you will ask in my name; and I do not say to you that I shall ask the Father concerning you. For the Father himself loves you, because you love me and have believed that I came forth from God. I came forth from the Father and came into this world; again I leave this world and go to the Father.” His disciples said to him, “See, now you speak openly and use no figurative saying. Now therefore we know that you know all things, and have no need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came from God.” Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe? Look: the hour is coming, and now has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own place, [Col. 0469] and will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. I have spoken these things to you so that in me you may have peace. In this world you will have tribulation; but be steadfast, because I have conquered this world.”

Jesus spoke these things, lifted his eyes to heaven, and said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son may glorify you, just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that he may give eternal life to all that you have given him. And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent. I glorified you upon the earth; I completed the work which you gave me to [Col. 0470] do. And now, Father, glorify me beside yourself with the glory which I had beside you before the world existed. I revealed your name to the people whom you gave me out of this world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word. Now [Note: [Col. 0469] So also the Gothic: ἔγνωκα (“I have known”).] I have known + that all things which you gave me are from you, because I gave them the words which you gave me, and they received them and truly knew that I came forth from you, and they believed that you sent me. I pray for them. I do not pray for this world, but for those whom you gave me, because they are yours. And all that is mine is yours, and what is yours [Note: [Col. 0469] After *mine*, *are* is absent also in the Greek text.] is mine +; [Col. 0471] and I have been glorified in them. And I am no longer in this world, but they are in this world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, preserve in your name those whom you gave me, so that they may be one as we also are one. While I was with them in this world, I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me I guarded, and none of them perished except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled. But now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in this world so that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I gave them your word, and this world hated them because they are not of this world, just as I am not of this world. I do not ask you to take them out of this world, but that you [Col. 0472] preserve them from the evil one. They are not of this world, just as I am not of this world. Sanctify them in truth: your word is truth. Just as you sent me into [Note: [Col. 0471] *This* is added; likewise the Codex of Canterbury: τοῦτον (“this”).] this + world, I also sent them into this world. And for them I sanctify myself, so that they too may be sanctified in truth. I do not pray only for these, but also for those who will believe in me through their word: that they all may be one. As you, Father, are in me and I in you, so may they also be one in us, so that this world may believe that you sent me. And I have given them the glory which you gave me, so that they may be one, as we are one: I in them, [Col. 0473] and you in me, so that they may be perfected into one, and so that this world may know that you sent me and loved them as you loved me. Father, those whom you gave me—I desire that, where I am, they also may be with me, so that they may see my glory, which you gave me because you loved me before the foundation of this world. Righteous Father, this world did not know you; but I did not know you, and these knew that you sent me. And I made your name known to them, and I shall make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

When Jesus had said these things, he went out with his disciples across the brook Cedron, where there was a garden, into which he himself and his disciples entered. Judas, who was betraying him, also knew the place, because Jesus often met [Col. 0474] there with his disciples. Judas therefore, having received a cohort of soldiers and attendants from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons. But Jesus, [Note: [Col. 0473] So also the Codex of Canterbury: δέ (“but”).] knowing + all that was coming upon him, went out and said to them, “Whom do you seek?” They answered him, “Jesus the Nazarene.” Jesus said to them, “I am he.” Judas, who was betraying him, was also standing with them. When therefore he said to them, “I am he,” they went backward and fell to the ground. Again therefore he asked them, “Whom do you seek?” They said, “Jesus the Nazarene.” Jesus answered them, “I told you that I am he. If therefore you seek me, let these go,” so that the word which he spoke might be fulfilled: “Of those whom [Col. 0475] you gave me, I lost none of them.” Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the servant of the chief priest, cutting off his right ear. That servant’s name was Malchus. Jesus therefore said to Peter, “Put [Note: [Col. 0475] After *sword*, *your* is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury and the Gothic.] the sword + into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup which the Father gave me?” The cohort, then, and the tribune and the Jewish attendants seized Jesus, bound him, and brought him first to Annas. For he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was chief priest that year. Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it was expedient for one man to die for the people.

Simon Peter followed Jesus, as did another disciple. [Col. 0476] That disciple was known to the chief priest and [Note: [Col. 0475] So also the Greek text: συνεισῆλθε (“entered with”).] entered together + with Jesus into the court of the chief priest. But Peter stood outside at the door. Therefore the other disciple, who was known to the chief priest, went out, spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in. The maidservant who was the doorkeeper said to Peter, “Are you not also one of this man’s disciples?” He said, “I am not.” The servants and attendants stood around a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and were warming themselves. Peter also was standing with them and warming himself. The chief priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching. Jesus answered him, “I have spoken openly to this world. I always taught in synagogue [Col. 0477] and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I spoke nothing in secret. Why do you question me? Question those who heard me, what I spoke to them. Look, these know what I said.” When he had said these things, one of the attendants standing nearby struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, “Is this how you answer the chief priest?” Jesus answered him, “If I spoke wrongly, bear witness concerning the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike me?” Annas therefore sent him, bound, to Caiaphas the chief priest.

Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said to him, “Are you not also one of his disciples?” But he denied it and said, “I am not.” One of the servants of the chief priest, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, [Col. 0478] “Did I not see you in the garden with him?” Peter therefore denied it again, and immediately the cock crowed. They then brought Jesus to Caiaphas, into the praetorium. It was morning; and they themselves did not enter the praetorium, so that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover. Pilate therefore went outside to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?” They answered and said to him, “If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you.” Pilate therefore said to them, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to [Col. 0479] your law.” The Jews said to him, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death,” so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which he spoke, indicating by what death he was to die. Pilate therefore entered the praetorium again, summoned Jesus, and said to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “Do you say this of yourself, or did others tell you about me?” Pilate answered, “Am I a Jew? Your nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?” Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my attendants would surely fight, so that I might not be handed over to the Jews. But now [Col. 0480] my kingdom is not from here.” Pilate therefore said to him, “Then are you a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: that I might bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.” Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” And when he had said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them, “I find no charge in him. But you have a custom that I should release one person to you at the Passover. Do you therefore wish that I release to you the King of the Jews?” They all cried out again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.

Pilate therefore took Jesus and scourged him. The soldiers wove a crown of thorns, put it on his head, clothed him in a purple garment, and said, “Hail, King of the Jews!” And they struck him with their palms. Pilate went outside again and said to them, “Look, I bring him outside to you, so that you may know that I find no charge in him.” Jesus therefore went out [Note: [Col. 0481] *Outside* is added, likewise in the Greek text: ἔξω.] outside +, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. And he said to them, “Look: the man!” When the chief priests and their attendants saw him, they cried out, saying, “Crucify, crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no charge in him.” The [Col. 0482] Jews answered, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.” When Pilate heard this statement, he was more afraid. He entered the praetorium again and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer. Pilate therefore said to him, “Will you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you and authority to release you?” Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over me unless it had been given you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.” From that point Pilate sought to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, [Col. 0483] “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. For everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.” When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat upon the judgment seat [Note: [Col. 0483] So also the Greek text: εἰς τόπον (“into a place”).] in the place + called Lithostrotos, and in Hebrew Gennesar. It was the Preparation of the Passover, about the sixth hour. And he said to the Jews, “Look: your King!” But they [Note: [Col. 0483] So also the Greek text: ἐκράυγασαν (“they cried out”).] cried out +, “Away, away! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king except Caesar.” Then therefore he handed him over to them to be crucified. They took Jesus and led him away; and, carrying his cross himself, he went out to the place [Col. 0484] called the Place of the Skull, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha. There they crucified him, and with him two others, one on either side, with Jesus in the middle. Pilate also wrote an inscription and placed it upon the cross. It was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews.” Many of the Jews therefore read this inscription, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin. Therefore the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘King of the Jews,’ but, ‘He said, “I am King of the Jews.”’” Pilate answered them, “What I have written, I have written.”

The soldiers therefore, after they crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier, and also the tunic. The tunic was seamless, woven from above throughout. They therefore said to one another, “Let us not tear this tunic, but cast lots for it to determine whose it shall be,” so that the Scripture might be fulfilled which says, “They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast a lot.” These things, then, the soldiers did. But standing beside Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple [Note: [Col. 0485] So also the Greek text: παρεστῶτα (“standing nearby”).] standing nearby + whom he loved, he said to his mother, “Woman, behold your son.” [Col. 0486] Then he said to that disciple, “Behold your mother.” And from that hour the disciple received her into his own home.

After this, Jesus, knowing that all things were now completed, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, “I thirst.” A vessel full of vinegar was standing there. They filled a sponge with vinegar, put it around hyssop, and offered it to his mouth. Therefore, when Jesus had received the vinegar, he said, “It is completed.” And, bowing his head, he gave up his spirit. Since it was the Preparation, the Jews therefore asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be removed, so that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the Sabbath; for that Sabbath day was a great day. The soldiers therefore came and [Note: [Col. 0485] Thus this ancient translator renders the Greek prepositive article.] broke the legs of the former + [Col. 0487] and likewise of the other [Note: [Col. 0487] According to the Greek text: συσταυρωθέντος (“having been crucified with”).] who had been crucified together + with him. But when they came to Jesus, they found him already dead and did not break his legs. Instead, one of the soldiers opened his side with his spear, and immediately blood and water came out. The one who saw it has borne witness, and his testimony is true. He knows that he speaks truth, so that you also may believe. For these things happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “You shall not break a bone of it.” And again another Scripture says, “They will look upon him whom they pierced.” After this Joseph of [Col. 0488] Arimathea, who was also a disciple of Jesus—but secretly, because of fear of the Jews—asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus; and Pilate permitted it. He came and took the body of Jesus. Nicodemus also came, the one who had first come to Jesus by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds. They therefore took Jesus’ body and bound it in linen cloths with spices, as is the Jewish custom of burial. Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been placed. There therefore, because of the Jewish Preparation, [Col. 0489] since the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus.

On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came early to the tomb, while it was still dark, and saw the stone rolled away from the entrance of the tomb. She ran therefore and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and we do not know where they have put him.” Peter therefore went out, and the other disciple, and they came to the tomb. Both were running together, but the other disciple ran faster ahead of Peter and came first to the tomb. And when he had bent down, he saw the linen cloths lying there, [Col. 0490] but did not enter. Simon Peter therefore came, following him, and entered the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there, and the face-cloth, which had been upon his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up separately in one place. Then the other disciple, who had come first to the tomb, also entered; and he saw and believed. For they did not yet know the Scriptures, that Jesus had to rise from the dead. The disciples therefore went away again to their own homes.

But Mary stood outside by the tomb, weeping. While she wept, she bent down and looked into the tomb, and saw two angels in white sitting, one [Col. 0491] at the head and the other at the feet, where Jesus’ body had been lying. They said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “Because they have taken my Lord, and I do not know where they have put him.” When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but did not know that it was Jesus. Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom do you seek?” She, supposing that he was the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have put him, and I will take him away.” Jesus said to her, “Mary.” [Note: [Col. 0491] *And* is added, likewise in the Codex of Canterbury: δέ (“and”).] And + she turned and said to him, “Rabboni,” which means “Teacher.” Jesus said to her, “Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and say to them: ‘I am ascending to [Col. 0492] my Father and your Father, my God and your God.’” Mary Magdalene came, announcing to the disciples that she had seen the Lord and all the things that he had said to her.

When it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where his disciples had gathered for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and said to them, “Peace to you.” When he had said this, he showed them his hands and side. The disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord. Therefore he said to them [Note: [Col. 0491] *Jesus* is added, likewise in the Greek text: ὁ Ἰησοῦς (“Jesus”).] Jesus + again, “Peace to you. As the Father sent me, I also send you.” And when he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone’s sins, they are forgiven him; if you retain anyone’s sins, they are retained.”

[Col. 0493] But Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord.” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the place of the nails, and put my finger into the openings of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.” After eight days his disciples were again inside, and Thomas with them. Jesus came, though the doors were shut, stood in the midst, and said, “Peace to you.” Then he said to Thomas, “Bring your finger here and see my hands; bring your hand and put it into my side; and do not be unbelieving, but believing.” Thomas answered and said to him, “My Lord [Col. 0494] and my God.” Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.” Jesus indeed performed many other signs in the presence of his disciples which have not been written in this book. But these have been written so that you may believe that [Note: [Col. 0493] So also the Codex of Canterbury: Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς υἱός ἐστιν τοῦ Θεοῦ (“Jesus Christ is the Son of God”).] Jesus Christ is the Son of God +, and that, believing, you may have [Note: [Col. 0493] *Eternal* is added, also in the Codex of Canterbury: αἰώνιον (“eternal”).] eternal + life in his name.

After this Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples [Note: [Col. 0493] *His* is added, likewise in the Codex of Canterbury: αὐτοῦ (“his”).] his + at the Sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself in this way. Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael, who was from Cana of Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together. Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing.” They said to him, “We also will come [Col. 0495] with you.” They went out and entered the boat, but in that night they caught nothing. When morning had [Note: [Col. 0495] *Already* is added, also in the Greek text: ἤδη (“already”).] already + come, Jesus stood on the shore; yet his disciples did not know that it was Jesus. Jesus therefore said to them, “Children, do you have anything to eat?” They answered him, “No.” He said to them, “Cast the net on the right [Note: [Col. 0495] *Side* is added, also in the Greek text: μέρη (“parts”).] side + of the boat, and you will find some.” Therefore they cast it, and they were unable to draw it because of the multitude of fish. The disciple whom Jesus loved therefore said to Peter, “It is the Lord.” Simon Peter, when he heard that it was the Lord, girded his tunic around himself, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea. But the other disciples [Col. 0496] came in the boat, for they were not far from land, but about [Note: [Col. 0495] So also the Greek text: ἀπό (“from”).] two hundred cubits + away, dragging the net of fish. When they came down upon land, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, with fish placed upon it and bread. Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.” Simon Peter went up and drew the net to land, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three. And although there were so many, the net was not torn. Jesus said to them, “Come, eat breakfast.” Yet no one [Note: [Col. 0495] Codex of Canterbury: δέ (“but”).] however + of the disciples dared to ask him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord. Jesus therefore came, took the bread, [Col. 0497] and, blessing, gave it to them, and likewise the fish. This was now the third time Jesus revealed himself to his disciples after he rose from the dead.

When they had eaten, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.” Again Jesus said to him, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed my sheep.” Jesus said to him a third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because he said to him the third time, “Do you love me?” And he said to him, “Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep. Truly, truly, I tell [Col. 0498] you: when you were young, you girded yourself and walked where you wished; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not wish to go.” He said this to indicate by what kind of death Peter would glorify God. And when he had said this, he said to him, “Follow me.”

Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following, the one who had also reclined at supper upon Jesus’ breast and said, “Lord, who is the one betraying you?” When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?” Jesus said to him, “If I wish him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.” This saying therefore went out among the brethren that that disciple [Col. 0499] would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him, “He will not die,” + but, “If I wish him to remain until [Note: [Col. 0499] So also the Greek text: ἔρχομαι (“I come”).] I come.” This is the disciple who bore witness concerning these things and wrote them; and we know that his testimony is true. [Col. 0500] There are also many other things which Jesus did; if they were written one by one, I suppose that not even this world itself could contain the books that would have to be written. AMEN.

The Gospel according to John ends. The Gospel according to Luke begins.

**Codex Corbeiensis**, marked no. 195.

[Note: Col. 0353: We present here a most ancient codex of the monastery of Corbie, no. 195, written in the sixth century in Roman letters. In it words are very frequently not separated by any distinction, and correct rules of writing are little observed. This codex contains the four Gospels as they were formerly read before they were corrected, or translated, by St Jerome. Since, however, this codex was used in church for chanting the Gospel at Mass, it often happens—especially in Matthew—that interpolations occur by which the codex was made very similar to the Vulgate from Jerome’s version. Yet these corrections are readily recognized, both from the ink and from the form of the letters. The four Gospels preserve in it an order altogether different from that in our copies: I, Matthew, of which the first eleven chapters have perished; II, John; III, Luke, or *Lucanus*, as it is called in it; IV, Mark. We have collected from this codex the principal differences of readings. Whoever wishes to transcribe everything must transcribe the whole codex; for differences occur in almost every verse, if one considers the order and force of the words. With the aid of this codex and of our own, which we found in ancient libraries, there can be no doubt that the Old Italian version in the Gospels can be restored. Lucas of Bruges mentions an old codex from the monastery of Malmedy containing the old Vulgate. Martianay, a Benedictine monk of the Congregation of St Maur, published an old text of Matthew (reprinted above) from two ancient codices, one of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, the other Corbie; but his Corbie codex is altogether different, both in age and in letter-form. Martianay’s Corbie codex is not older than eight hundred years and is written in Saxon or Merovingian letters; our no. 195 is written in square Roman majuscule letters and belongs, in the judgment of the most learned scholars, to the sixth century. Martianay’s codex contains Matthew alone from the Old Italian version; ours contains all four Gospels. When we compare our codex with Martianay’s edition of Matthew, this one seems to agree more closely with the codex of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, from which Martianay extracted variant readings and entered them in the margin of his edition. On comparing these variants, you will find altogether true what Jerome says in his Preface to the Four Gospels: “If faith is to be placed in Latin copies, let them answer—which ones? For there are almost as many copies as codices,” says the Reverend Father Dom Augustin Calmet after his literal Commentary on the Acts of the Apostles.]

## Chapter V

[Col. 0380]

2. Now there is at Jerusalem, in the lower part [Note: Col. 0380: *Gat.* and *Mm.*: “by the Sheep Gate.”], a pool called in Hebrew Berzeta.

4. But an angel [Col. 0381] came down and stirred the water; and whoever first went down into the pool was made well.

6. Because he had already spent much time in illness.

7. The sick man answered him … “to put me into the pool.”

[Col. 0382]

9. And rising, he took up his pallet and walked.

13. [Note: Col. 0382: *Gat.*: “But Jesus withdrew.” *Mm.*: “But Jesus withdrew himself.”] But Jesus withdrew.

[Col. 0383]

23. Whoever does not honour the Father does not honour the Father who sent the Son. In a later hand: “Whoever does not [Col. 0384] honour the Son.”

24. From death [Note: Col. 0384: *Gat.* and *Mm.*: “to life,” omitting “eternal.”] to eternal life.

[Col. 0385]

28. “For I say to you: Do not marvel at this.”

32. Another is he who bears witness concerning me; it omits what follows: “and I know that the witness which he bears concerning me is true.”

[Col. 0386]

33. You yourselves sent to me; and John bore witness concerning me.

37. Nor have you seen his appearance.

[Col. 0387]

**The Gospel of Eusebius of Vercelli, collated with various codices of the Old Italian version. Part Two.**

[Col. 0499]

## The Preface Begins

[Col. 0499]

Luke was indeed a Syrian of Antioch, a physician by profession, a disciple of the apostles. Later he followed Paul as far as Paul’s confession, serving the Lord without reproach. He never had a wife and never begot children; he died in his seventy-fourth year, full of the Holy Spirit. Therefore, since Gospels had already been written—by Matthew indeed in Judea, by Mark in Italy—Luke, stirred by the Holy Spirit, wrote this Gospel in the regions of Achaia. By its beginning he indicates that others had been written before his own; but he also indicates that a very great necessity lay upon him: to set forth with the utmost diligence, for Greek believers, the entire arrangement by means of his narrative.

[Col. 0500]

For this reason, lest they should be held fast by a longing for Jewish fables, or lest, deceived by heretical fables and foolish … solicitations, they should depart from the truth, [Note: Col. 0499: It should be read: “Therefore he adopted a most necessary beginning of the Gospel from the birth of John, who was sent beforehand—or was the forerunner—of our Lord Jesus Christ, and who was a companion,” etc.] he immediately adopted at the beginning a most necessary beginning from John’s birth, which is the beginning of the Gospel: [John], sent beforehand by our Lord Jesus Christ, was a companion for the perfection of the people, and likewise for the introduction of baptism and of the Passion. But he certainly recalls an example of this ordering from Malachi, [Note: Col. 0500: He seems to allude to Malachi 3:1: “Behold, I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face.”] the last prophet of the Twelve.

Afterward the apostle John wrote the Apocalypse on the island of Patmos, and then the Gospel in Asia. Likewise Luke wrote the Acts of the Apostles.

## CHAPTER III

1. Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, with Pontius Pilate governing Judea, and Herod tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and the regions of Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene [Note: [Col. 0523] The Cantabrigian manuscript has Ἀβιλλιανῆς; the Cantabrigian Latin, *Abillianetis*], 2. under the chief priests + [Note: [Col. 0523] So also the Greek text: Θεοῦ (“of God”).] Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God + came [Col. 0523] upon John the son of Zacharias in the desert.

3. And he came into the whole region of the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance, 4. as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “The voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight. 5. Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked ways shall become straight, and the rough ways into smooth roads; 6. and every flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

7. Therefore he said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him: “Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the coming wrath? 8. Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance. Do not be willing to say: ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham. 9. For already indeed the axe has been placed at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree not producing fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

10. And the crowds asked him, saying: “What then [Note: [Col. 0523] *Gat.* “What shall we do, that we may live?” *Vulg.* “What shall we do?”] shall we do?” 11. And answering, he said to them: “Let the one who has two tunics give to the one who has none; and let the one who has food do likewise.”

12. Tax collectors too came to be baptized, and said to him: “Teacher, 13. what shall we do?” To them he said: “Exact nothing more than what has been appointed for you [Note: [Col. 0525] *Gat.* “than what has been appointed for you, exact.” *Vulg.* “than what has been appointed for you, do.”]

14. And soldiers also asked him, saying: “And what shall we do?” And he said to them: “Violently extort no one, and accuse no one falsely; and be satisfied with your wages.”

15. As the people were expecting, and all were reasoning in their hearts about John, whether perhaps he himself were the Christ, 16. he answered them all, saying: “I indeed baptize you with water [Note: [Col. 0525] The Cantabrigian manuscript also adds *in repentance*, εἰς μετάνοιαν (“for repentance”).] for repentance + [Note: [Col. 0525] *Gat.* “you in repentance; but he comes.” *Vulg.* “you; but he will come.”]; but one stronger than I is coming [fragmentary: *…us non sum dignus calciamenta portare*], whose sandal I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire. 17. He has a winnowing fork in his hand, to cleanse his threshing floor; and he gathers the wheat into his granary, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”

18. And exhorting the people + with many other words [Note: [Col. 0525] So also the Greek text: τὸν λαόν (“the people”).], he evangelized them [fragmentary: *… evangelizab…*].

19. But Herod the tetrarch, when he was reproved by him concerning Herodias, the wife of his brother, and concerning all the evil things that Herod did [Note: [Col. 0526] *Gat.* “that Herod was doing.” *Vulg.* “that Herod did.”], 20. added this above all, and shut John up in prison.

21. Now it came to pass, when all the people had been baptized, and Jesus had been baptized and was praying, that heaven was opened, 22. and the Holy Spirit descended in bodily form, like a dove, upon him [Note: [Col. 0526] *Gat.* “upon him, and a voice came, saying: ‘You are … in whom I am well pleased.’” *Vulg.* “upon him, and a voice came from heaven: ‘You are … with you I am well pleased.’”], and a voice came from heaven: “You are my Son; [Col. 0527] today I have begotten you +” [Note: [Col. 0527] The Cantabrigian manuscript also adds: ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε (“today I have begotten you”).]

23. And Jesus himself was about thirty years old, beginning, son, as was supposed, of Joseph, who was of Heli, who was of Mattheae [Note: [Col. 0527] *Gat.* “Melchi.” *Vulg.* “Matthat.”], 24. who was the son of Levi, who was the son of Melchi, who was the son of Janna, who was the son of Joseph, 25. who was the son of Nahum, who was the son of Esli, who was the son of Nagge, who was the son of Maath, 26. who was the son of Mattathias, who was the son of Semei, who was the son of Joseph, who was the son of Judah, 27. who was the son of Joanna [Note: [Col. 0527] *Gat.* “Manathae.” *Vulg.* “Joanna.”], who was the son of Rhesa [fragmentary: *… qui Resae…*], who was the son of Zerubbabel, who was the son of Salathiel [fragmentary: *… babel, qui S…atiel,*], who was the son of Neri, 28. who was the son of Melchi, who was the son of Addi, who was the son of Cosam, who was the son of Elmadam, who was the son of Er, 29. who was the son of Jesus, who was the son of Eliezer, who was the son of Jorim, who was the son of Matthat, 30. who was the son of Levi, who was the son of Simeon, who was the son of Judah, who was the son of Joseph, who was the son of Jonam, 31. who was the son of Eliakim, who was the son of Melea [Note: [Col. 0527] *Gat.* “Mecha … Mathathia.” *Vulg.* “Melea … Mathatha.”] [fragmentary: *… qui Enam*], who was the son of Mattatha + [Note: [Col. 0527] Greek text: Ματταθά (“Mattatha”).], who was the son of Nathan, 32. who was the son of David, who was the son of Jesse, who was the son of Obed, who was the son of Boaz, who was the son of Salmon, who was the son of Nahshon, 33. who was the son of Amminadab, who was the son of Aram, who was the son of Hezron, who was the son of Perez, who was the son of Judah, 34. who was the son of Jacob, who was the son of Isaac, who was the son of Abraham, who was the son of Terah, who was the son of Nahor, 35. who was the son of Seruch + [Note: [Col. 0527] So also the Cantabrigian manuscript: Σερούκ.
