## CHAPTER IV

1. And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit [Note: [Col. 0529] So also the Cantabrigian manuscript: ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ (“in the desert”).] in the desert + 2. for forty days, being [Note: [Col. 0529] *Gat.* “is tempted.” *Vulg.* “was tempted.”] tempted by the devil, and he ate nothing during those days; and when they were completed, he was hungry.

3. And the devil said to him: “If you are the Son of God, say to these stones [fragmentary: *… fiant pan…*] that they become bread.” 4. And Jesus answered him [Note: [Col. 0529] The Cantabrigian manuscript also adds “and said,” καὶ εἶπεν; the Brixian manuscript has “saying.”], saying +: “It is written: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”

5. The devil led him [Note: [Col. 0529] *Gat.* “the devil, and …” *Vulg.* “the devil …”] to Jerusalem, set him upon the pinnacle of the temple, and showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in a moment of time, 6. and the devil said to him: “I will give you all this power and their glory, because it has been handed over to me [fragmentary: *… mi…i tradita est,*], and I give it to whomever I wish [Note: [Col. 0530] *Gat.* “to him … to whom I shall wish.” *Vulg.* “to him … to whom I wish.”]. 7. Therefore, if you fall down and worship before me, all these things will be yours.”

8. And Jesus answered and said to him: “It is written + [Note: [Col. 0529] So also the Cantabrigian manuscript: γέγραπται (“it is written”)]: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.’”

9. And he led him to Jerusalem and set him upon the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him: “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here. 10. For it is written that he has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you; 11. they will lift you up in their hands, lest you perhaps strike your foot against a stone.”

12. And Jesus answered and said to him: “It is written: ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’” 13. And when every temptation had been completed, the devil departed from him until an appointed time.

14. And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and fame went out [Col. 0531] through the whole neighboring region concerning him. 15. And he himself taught in the synagogues + [Note: After “synagogues,” *eorum* (“their”) is absent, also in the Cantabrigian manuscript], receiving honor from all.

16. And he came into [Note: The Greek text also adds *in*, εἰς (“into”).] Nazareth +, where he had been brought up, and he entered the synagogue according to his custom on the Sabbath day, and he stood up to read. 17. And the book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him; and when he had unrolled the book, he found the place where it was written:

18. “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; because [Note: [Col. 0531] *Gat.* “because of which.” *Vulg.* “because.”] he anointed me, sent me to evangelize the humble; 19. to proclaim + release to captives and sight to the blind, to send the broken into rest, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of redemption.” [Note: [Col. 0531] Before “to proclaim,” the phrase “to heal the brokenhearted” is absent, also in the Cantabrigian manuscript and in the Coptic, Ethiopic, and Saxon versions, as well as in Origen, Ambrose, and Augustine. Grotius says it is more probable that interpreters added it from Isaiah than that other copyists omitted it.]

20. And when he had rolled up the book and returned it to the attendant, he sat down. And the eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed upon him. 21. And he began to say to them: “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.”

22. And all bore witness to him, and they marveled at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth, and they said: “Is this not Joseph’s son?” 23. And he said to them: “Perhaps you will say to me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself. Whatever we have heard was done in Capernaum, do also here in your native place.’”

24. But he said: “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his native place.

25. In truth I tell you: There were many widows in the days of Elijah, when heaven was shut up for three years and six months; thus a great famine came upon the whole land; 26. and Elijah was sent to none of them except to a widow woman at Sarepta of Sidon.

27. And there were many lepers in Israel under Elisha the prophet [Note: [Col. 0533] *Gat.* “in Jerusalem under … Naaman.” *Vulg.* “in Israel under … Naaman.”]; yet none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.”

28. And all in the synagogue were filled with anger when they heard these things. 29. And they rose up and drove him outside the city, and led him to the brow of the mountain upon which their city had been built. 30. But passing through the midst of them, he went away.

31. And he came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and he was teaching them on the Sabbaths. 32. And they were astonished at his teaching, because his word was with authority.

33. And in the synagogue there was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice, 34. saying: “What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God.”

35. And Jesus rebuked him, saying: “Be silent, and come out of him.” And when the demon had thrown him down, it came out of him [Note: [Col. 0533] *Gat.* “it came out from the man.” A later hand has “from him.” *Vulg.* “it came out from him.”], harming him not at all.

36. And fear came upon everyone, and they spoke to one another [Note: [Col. 0534] *Gat.* “great fear among all, and they spoke together.” *Vulg.* “fear among all, and they spoke together.”], saying: “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out.” 37. And his fame went out into every neighboring region.

38. And rising + [Note: After “rising,” Jesus is absent, likewise in the Greek text.] from the synagogue, he entered Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was held by a great fever, and they appealed to him for her. 39. And standing over her, he rebuked the fever, and it left her. Immediately rising, she served them.

40. Now when the sun had set, all who had the sick suffering from various diseases brought them to him. He healed each one of them by laying his hands upon them. 41. And [Note: [Col. 0535] *Gat.* “demons also from many.” *Vulg.* “demons from many.”] demons also came out from many, crying out and saying: “You are the Son of God.” And rebuking them, he did not allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.

42. And when day had dawned, he went out and departed into a deserted place, and the crowds sought him. They came as far as he was and held him back, so that he would not depart from them. 43. He said to them: “I must evangelize the kingdom of God to other cities also, because for this I have been sent.” 44. And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.

## CHAPTER V
1. And it came to pass, while the crowd was pressing upon him to hear the word of God, and he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret [Note: [Col. 0535] So also the Greek text, Γεννησαρέτ, “Gennesaret.”] [Note: [Col. 0536] Gat.: *Genesar*. Vulg.: *Genesareth*.] +, 2. that he saw two little boats [Col. 0537] standing by the shore; the fishermen, having gone out from them, were washing [Note: [Col. 0537] Gat.: “their nets in the sea.” Vulg.: “their nets.”] their nets. 3. And getting into one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, he asked him to put out a little way from the land. Then, sitting down, he taught the crowds from the boat. 4. And when he had ceased speaking, he said to Simon: “Put out into the deep, and [Note: [Col. 0537] Gat.: *relaxate*, “let down.” Vulg.: *laxate*, “let down.”] spread out your nets for a catch.” 5. And Simon answered and said to him: “Master, though we have laboured the whole night, we have caught nothing; yet at your word I will spread out the net.” 6. And when they had done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish; but [Col. 0537] their nets were breaking. 7. And [Note: [Col. 0537] Gat.: “they signalled … that they might sink.” Vulg.: “they signalled … that they might nearly sink.”] they signalled to their partners in the other boat … that they might come … and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that [Note: [Col. 0537] Before *mergerentur*, “they might sink,” *pene*, “nearly,” is absent, also in the Greek text.] they were sinking 8. +. Seeing this, [Note: [Col. 0537] After *Simon*, *Petrus*, “Peter,” is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] Simon + fell at Jesus’ knees, saying: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.” 9. For terror had seized him, and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which 10. they had taken; likewise James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners. And Jesus said to Simon: [Note: [Col. 0538] Gat.: “Do not fear,” plural. Vulg.: “Do not fear,” singular.] “Do not fear. From now on you will be catching men alive.” 11. And when they had brought the boats to land, leaving all things behind, they followed him.

12. And it came to pass, [Col. 0539] while he was in one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy; and, falling on his face, he implored him, saying: “If you will, you are able to cleanse me.” 13. And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying: “I will; be cleansed.” And immediately the leprosy departed 14. from him; and he commanded him to tell no one, but said: “Go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing as Moses commanded, [Note: [Col. 0539] So also the Codex of Canterbury: ἵνα εἰς μαρτύριον ἦν ὑμῖν τοῦτο, “that this might be a testimony to you.”] that this may be a testimony to you.” + 15. But the report about him spread abroad still more; and great crowds came together to hear and to be healed of their infirmities. 16. But he [Note: [Col. 0539] Gat.: “was withdrawing into the wilderness.” Vulg.: “was withdrawing into a wilderness.”] was withdrawing into desert places and praying.

17. And it came to pass on one of the days, [Col. 0539] that he [Note: [Col. 0539] So also the Greek text, ἦν, “was.”] was + teaching. And there were … Pharisees … and teachers … who had come together from every town of Galilee, and from Judaea and Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was present to heal them. 18. And behold, men were bringing on a bed a man who was paralysed; and they sought to bring him in and set him before him. 19. And, because they could not … bring him in … on account of the crowd, they went up upon the roof and lowered him through the tiles, with his little bed, into Jesus’ presence. 20. And when he saw their faith, he said to the man: “Your sins are forgiven you.” 21. And the scribes and Pharisees began to reason, saying: “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? [Col. 0541] Who can forgive sins except God alone?” 22. But Jesus, knowing … their thoughts, [Note: [Col. 0541] Before *dixit*, “he said,” *respondens*, “answering,” is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.] said + to them: “What are you reasoning in your hearts? 23. Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’? 24. But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth [Note: [Col. 0541] Gat.: “to forgive sins.” Vulg.: “of forgiving sins.”] to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—“I say to you, rise, take up your little bed … and go to your house.” 25. And immediately, rising before them all, he took up the pallet on which he had lain … and went away to his house, glorifying God. 26. And fear seized them all. And they were filled with awe, saying: “For we have seen … [Col. 0541] wondrous things …”

27. And … he went out and saw a tax collector … named [Note: [Col. 0541] Gat.: “Lewin … at the *thiloneum*.” Vulg.: “Levi … at the *telonium*.”] Levi sitting at the tax-office, and said to him: “Follow 28. me.” And leaving all things behind, he rose and followed him. 29. And Levi made him a great dinner in his house; and there was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who … were reclining with them at … 30. But the Pharisees and their scribes murmured, saying to his disciples: “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?” [Note: [Col. 0541] So also the Ethiopic version: ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει, “eats and drinks,” taken from Matthew.] + 31. And Jesus answered and said to them: “Those who are well do not need physicians, but those who are ill. 32. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” 33. And they said to him: “Why do John’s [Col. 0543] disciples fast often and offer prayers, as do those of the Pharisees, while yours eat and drink?” 34. And he said to them: “Can [Note: [Col. 0543] So also the Codex of Canterbury: δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος νηστεύειν ἐφ᾽ ὅσον, “can the sons of the bridechamber fast so long as …”] [Note: [Col. 0543] Gat.: *possum*, “I am able,” in a recent hand; “can you fast.” Vulg.: “can you … make [them] fast.”] the sons of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them? 35. + But days will come; and when the bridegroom has been taken away from them, then they will fast in those days. 36. And he also spoke a parable to them: “No one sews a patch from an unshrunk garment upon an old garment; otherwise the new garment will tear, and the patch from the new will not match the old. 37. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise [Col. 0543] the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be poured out, and the wineskins will perish. 38. But they put new wine into new wineskins [Note: [Col. 0543] So also the Codex of Canterbury: βάλλουσιν, “they put.” In the same place, “both.” I do not know whether this is the translator’s or the scribe’s fault; for the Greek text has ἀμφότεροι, “both,” namely *οἶνος*, “wine,” and *ἀσκός*, “wineskin,” both masculine nouns.] +, and both are preserved.

## CHAPTER VI

1. [Note: [Col. 0543] The whole of verse 39 is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] And it came to pass on the second-first Sabbath, as he was passing through the grainfields, that his disciples were plucking ears of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating. 2. But certain Pharisees … said: “Why … on the Sabbaths what is not lawful?” 3. And Jesus answered and said to them: “Have you not even read what David did, when he himself and those who were with 4. him were hungry? How he entered the house of God, and took the loaves of presentation and ate, and gave to [Col. 0545] those who were with him; which [Note: [Col. 0545] Gat.: “it was not lawful for them to eat, except for priests alone. Or have you not read in the law that the priests in the temple violate the Sabbath and are without blame? And he said.” Vulg.: “it is not lawful to eat except only for priests? And he said.”] it is not lawful to eat … except [Note: [Col. 0545] So also the Greek text: μόνους, “alone.”] for priests alone? And he said to them: “For the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

6. And it came to pass on another Sabbath that he entered the synagogue and taught. And there was a man there whose right hand was withered. 7. But the scribes and Pharisees were watching … [Note: [Col. 0545] Before *sabbato*, “Sabbath,” *in*, “on,” is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.] on the Sabbath + … whether he would heal … that [Note: [Col. 0546] Gat.: “to accuse him.” Vulg.: “that they might accuse him.”] they might accuse 8. him. But he knew their thoughts. And he said to the man who had the withered hand: “Rise and stand [Note: [Col. 0545] So also the Codex of Canterbury: ἐν μέσῳ, “in the midst.”] in the midst.” + [Note: [Col. 0546] Gat.: “he stood, and rising.” Vulg.: “and rising, he stood.”] And rising, he stood. 9. Then Jesus said to them: “I ask you whether it is lawful [Col. 0545] on the Sabbaths to do good, … evil …” 10. Looking around at them all [Note: [Col. 0545] It adds *illis*, “them,” as does also the Greek text, αὐτούς. The Vercelli and Brescia manuscripts likewise support it.] +, being [Note: [Col. 0545] It adds *in ira*, “in anger,” also in the Codex of Canterbury: ἐν ὀργῇ, “in anger,” from Mark.] in anger +, he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored. 11. But they were filled with astonishment and discussed with one another what they might do to J… [Jesus].

12. And it came to pass … he spent the night in prayer to 13. God. And when day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve from among them, whom he also named apostles: 14. Simon, whom he also surnamed Peter, and Andrew his brother, [Col. 0547] [Note: [Col. 0547] Wherever the Verona, Vercelli, and Brescia manuscripts add *and*, the Codex of Canterbury adds καί, “and,” as well.] and + James, and John, and Philip, … Bar… 15. … and Mat… and Thomas, and James of Alphaeus +, and Simon who is called 16. the Zealot, and Judas of James, and Judas, who was the traitor.

17. And coming down with them, he stood in a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judaea and Jerusalem, and from across the sea, and from the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon, 18. who had come to hear him and to be healed of their infirmities. Those who were troubled by unclean spirits were healed. 19. And the whole crowd sought to touch him, because power went out from him and healed [Col. 0547] all.

20. And lifting up his eyes toward his disciples, he said: “Blessed are [Note: [Col. 0547] Gat.: “the poor in spirit; for.” Vulg.: “the poor; for.”] the poor in spirit, for yours is the kingdom of God. 21. Blessed are you who hunger now and thirst, for you shall be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you shall laugh. 22. Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they separate you, and cast you out, and reproach your name as evil, on account of the Son of Man. 23. Rejoice in that hour and exult; for behold, your reward [Note: [Col. 0547] Gat.: “is great, abundant in heaven; according to these things they did.” Vulg.: “is great in heaven; for according to these things they did.”] is abundant in heaven; for in the same way their fathers did to the prophets. 24. But woe to you rich persons, [Note: [Col. 0548] Gat.: “who have.” Vulg.: “because you have.”] because you have [Col. 0549] your consolation. 25. Woe to you who are full, because you shall hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, because you shall mourn and 26. weep. Woe when all people speak well of you; for in the same way [Note: [Col. 0549] *Enim*, “for,” is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] their fathers did to the false prophets.

27. “But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies; do good to those who hate you. 28. Bless [Note: [Col. 0549] So also the Greek text: καταρωμένους, “those cursing [you].”] those who curse + you; [Note: [Col. 0549] Before *orate*, “pray,” *et*, “and,” is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.] pray + for those who malign 29. you. To one striking you on the cheek, [Note: [Col. 0549] Gat.: *percussit*, “struck,” in a recent hand, *percusserit*, “shall strike.” Vulg.: *percutit*, “strikes.”] offer [Note: [Col. 0549] *Ei*, “to him,” is added in the Codex of Canterbury and the Gothic version also: αὐτῷ.] to him + the other also. And from one who takes away your garment, do not withhold your cloak. 30. Give to everyone who asks you; and from one who takes what is yours, do not demand it back. 31. And as you wish people to do to you, [Col. 0549] do likewise to them. 32. And if you love those who love you, what favour is there to you? For even sinners love those who love them. 33. And if you do good to those who do good to you, what favour is there to you? For sinners also do this. 34. And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what favour is there to you? For sinners lend to sinners in order that they may [Note: [Col. 0549] After *recipiant*, “they may receive,” *aequalia*, “equal things,” is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] receive +. 35. Nevertheless, love your enemies, do good, and lend, [Note: [Col. 0549] *Desperantes*, “despairing of nothing.” The Greek text: ἀπελπίζοντες.] despairing of nothing +; and your reward will be great in heaven, and you shall be sons of the Most High; for he is kind toward the ungrateful and wicked. 36. [Note: [Col. 0549] After *estote*, “be,” *ergo*, “therefore,” is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury and the Gothic version.] Be + merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

[Col. 0551] 37. “Do not judge, lest you be judged; do not condemn, that you may not be condemned. Forgive, and you shall be forgiven. 38. Give, and it shall be given to you: a good measure, [Note: [Col. 0551] The threefold conjunction *and* is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.] shaken, [Note: [Col. 0551] Gat.: *confestam*, “compressed,” and *supereffluentem*, “overflowing.” Vulg.: *confertam*, “packed,” and *coagitatam*, “shaken together,” and *supereffluentem*, “overflowing.”] heaped up, overflowing +, they shall give into your bosom. With the same measure with which you measure, it shall be measured back to you.” 39. And he also spoke a parable to them: “Can a blind person lead a blind person? Will not both fall into a pit? 40. A disciple is not above his teacher; but everyone will be perfected if he is like his teacher. 41. Why do you see the speck in your [Col. 0551] brother’s eye, but do not consider the beam which is in your own eye? 42. Or how can you say to your brother: [Note: [Col. 0551] Before *sine*, “allow,” *frater*, “brother,” is absent, also in the Codex of Canterbury.] ‘Allow + me to take the speck out of your eye,’ [Note: [Col. 0551] So also the Codex of Canterbury: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ ὑπόκειται, “and behold, the beam lies in your own eye.”] while behold, a beam lies in your own eye +? Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then [Note: [Col. 0551] Gat.: “you will see clearly to cast out the speck.” Vulg.: “you will see clearly, so that you may take out the speck.”] you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s 43. eye. For there is no good tree producing bad fruit, nor a bad tree producing 44. good fruit. Every tree is known by its own fruit. For [Note: [Col. 0551] So also the Codex of Canterbury: λέγονται ἐξ ἀκανθῶν, “they gather from thorns.”] they do not gather figs from thorns +, nor do they harvest grapes from a bramble. 45. A good man brings forth good from the good [Note: [Col. 0552] Gat.: “treasure of his heart brings forth evil.” Vulg.: “treasure brings forth evil.”] treasure of his heart; and the wicked [Note: [Col. 0551] After *malus*, “wicked,” *homo*, “man,” or *nequam*, “wicked,” is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] [Col. 0553] + brings forth evil from evil. For the mouth [Note: [Col. 0553] It adds *ejus*, “his,” as does also the Greek text, αὐτοῦ.] speaks + from the abundance of the heart.

46. “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do [Note: [Col. 0553] Gat.: “what I say to you?” Vulg.: “what I say?”] what 47. I say? Everyone who comes to me, hears my words, and does them—I will show you to whom he is like: 48. he is like a man building [Note: [Col. 0553] Gat.: “his house, who.” Vulg.: “a house, who.”] a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation upon rock. When a storm arose, [Note: [Col. 0553] According to the Greek text: προσέρρηξεν, “burst against.”] the flood burst + against that house and could not move it, because it had been founded upon rock. 49. But one who hears and does not act is like a man building a house [Note: [Col. 0553] Gat.: “upon sand without … the fall of his house was great.” Vulg.: [Col. 0554] “upon earth without … the fall of that house was great.”] upon the ground without a foundation. The flood burst against that house, and it fell, and the ruin of [Col. 0553] that house was great.”

## CHAPTER VII

1. [Note: [Col. 0553] So also the Codex of Canterbury: καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν, “and it came to pass when he had finished.”] And it came to pass, when he had finished + all these words in the hearing of the people, that he entered Capernaum. 2. Now a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was ill and beginning to die. 3. Hearing about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and heal his servant. 4. When they came, they earnestly entreated Jesus, saying: “He is worthy for you to grant him 5. this, for he loves our nation, and he himself built our synagogue 6. for us.” So Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far [Col. 0555] from the house, the [Note: [Col. 0555] Gat.: “The centurion [either ‘asking’ or ‘saying’; likewise either ‘Master’ or ‘Lord’ in the Gat. manuscript are variant readings brought from the margin [Col. 0556] into the text] sent friends, saying to him: ‘Lord, do not trouble yourself’ [‘Master’].” Vulg.: “The centurion sent friends, saying: ‘Lord, do not trouble yourself.’”] centurion sent friends to him, saying: “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; [Note: [Col. 0555] Gat.: “enter; but speak the word.” Vulg.: “enter. Therefore I did not think myself worthy to come to you; but speak the word.”] [Note: [Col. 0555] Before *sed dic*, “but speak,” the words “therefore I did not think myself worthy to come to you” are absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] but speak + the word, and my servant will be healed. 8. For I also am a man subject to authority, having soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and [Note: [Col. 0556] Gat.: “I say to my servant, ‘Do [it].’” Vulg.: “to my servant, ‘Do [it].’”] to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.” 9. Hearing these things, Jesus marvelled; and turning to the crowd following him, he said: “Amen, I say to you, I have found such great faith in no one in Israel.” 10. And those who had been sent returned home and found the [Col. 0555] servant [Note: [Col. 0556] Gat.: “who was ill.” Vulg.: “who had been ill.”] well.

11. And it came to pass afterward that Jesus went into a city called Nain; and his disciples and a large crowd went with him. 12. And it came to pass as he drew near + to the gate of the city that [Note: [Col. 0555] It adds *et*, “and,” as does the Greek text, καί.] and + behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother; and she was a widow, and a large crowd of the city was 13. with her. And when [Note: [Col. 0556] Gat.: “Jesus saw her.” Vulg.: “the Lord saw her.”] the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her: “Do not weep.” 14. And coming near, he touched the bier—and those who carried it stood still—and he said: [Note: [Col. 0556] Gat.: “To the young man: ‘I say to you.’” Vulg.: “Young man, I say to you.”] “Young man, young man, I say to you, arise.” 15. And the dead man sat up, [Col. 0557] and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother. 16. Then fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying: “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and, “God has visited his people for good.” 17. And this report about him went out through all Judaea and throughout the whole surrounding region.

18. And his disciples reported these things to John. 19. And John, calling to himself two certain men from among his disciples, sent them to the Lord, saying: “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to expect another?” 20. And the men came to him and said: “John the Baptist sent us to you, saying: ‘Are you the one who is to come, or are we to expect another?’” 21. In that hour [Note: [Col. 0557] So also the Codex of Canterbury: ἐθεράπευε, “he was healing.”] he was healing + many [Col. 0557] of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits; and he granted sight to many blind persons. 22. And answering, he said to them: “Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: blind persons see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, the poor receive the gospel; 23. and blessed is whoever is not offended by me.”

24. And when John’s messengers had departed, he began to speak to the crowds concerning John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind? 25. [Note: [Col. 0557] Gat.: “But did you go out?” Vulg.: “But what did you go out?”] But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold, those who abound in costly dress and luxury [Col. 0559] are in kings’ houses. 26. But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you: among those born of women no one is greater than John the Baptist, [Note: [Col. 0559] Mm.: “and certainly … and more than a prophet.” Vulg.: “Certainly … and more than a prophet.”] and more than a prophet. 27. This is he of whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who prepared your way.’ 28. But I say to you: among those born of women, no one is greater than John the Baptist. Yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than 29. he.” And [Note: [Col. 0559] Gat.: “all the people, and.” Mm.: “all peoples hearing, and.” Vulg.: “all the people hearing, and.”] all the people, when they heard, and the tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized with [Note: [Col. 0559] So also the Greek text: τὸ Βάπτισμα, “the baptism”; Greek syntax.] John’s baptism +. 30. But the Pharisees and doctors of the law rejected God’s purpose [Col. 0559] for themselves, since they had not been baptized.

31. [Note: [Col. 0559] Before *cui*, “to whom,” *ait autem Dominus*, “but the Lord said,” is absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] “To whom + then shall I compare the people of this generation? And to what are they like? 32. They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling to one another, [Note: [Col. 0559] So also the Codex of Canterbury: λέγοντες, “saying.”] saying +: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang laments for you, and you did not mourn.’ 33. For John the Baptist came neither eating [Note: [Col. 0559] *Bread and wine* are absent also in the Codex of Canterbury.] bread nor drinking + wine, and you say: ‘He has a demon.’ 34. The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say: ‘Behold, a man [Note: [Col. 0560] Gat.: *voratur*, “is devoured.” Mm.: *vorator*, “a devourer.” Vulg.: *devorator*, “a glutton.”] a glutton and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax collectors.’ 35. And wisdom has been justified [Note: [Col. 0560] Mm.: “by all, by her children.” Vulg.: “by all her children.”] by all her children.”

36. [Note: [Col. 0559] So also the Codex of Canterbury: ἠρώτησεν, “asked.”] A certain Pharisee asked + him [Col. 0561] to dine with him. And entering the Pharisee’s house, he reclined at table. 37. Since they had nothing with which to repay, he forgave both. Which of them, then, [Note: [Col. 0562] Mm.: “will love him more.” Vulg.: “will love him more.”] will love him more?” 43. And it came to pass thereafter that he went about [Note: [Col. 0563] Mm. “through city and village.” Vulg. “through cities, [Col. 0564] and villages.”] through cities and villages, preaching and proclaiming [Col. 0563] the kingdom of God; and the twelve disciples were with him, 2. and certain women who had been healed of [Note: [Col. 0564] Mm. “unclean spirits.” Vulg. “evil spirits.”] unclean spirits: Mary, who is called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out; and Joanna, wife of [Note: [Col. 0564] Gat. “of Chuszia … to them from.” Mm. “of Chusia.” Vulg. “of Chuza … to him from.”] Chuza, Herod’s procurator; and Susanna; and many others, who also ministered to him from their own resources.

[Note: [Col. 0564] Gat. and Mm. “Behold, he went out.” Vulg. “He went out.”] “Behold, the sower went out to sow his seed; and while he sowed, some fell beside the road, was trampled underfoot, and the birds [Note: [Col. 0563] After “birds,” “of heaven” is absent, also in the Codex Cantabrigiensis.] + [Note: [Col. 0564] Gat. “devour.” Vulg. “devoured.”] devoured it. He said.” Vulg. “a calm. He said.”] a calm. 25. Then you shall begin to say: ‘We ate and drank in thy presence, and thou didst teach in our streets.’ 27. And he shall say to you: ‘I do not know whence you are; depart from me, [Note: [Col. 0625] Gat.: “all [who] work iniquities.” Mm.: “all, who work iniquities.” Vulg.: “all workers of iniquity.”] all workers of iniquity.’ 28. [Note: [Col. 0626] Gat. and Mm.: “Where there shall be”; in a later hand, “there.” Vulg.: “There shall be.”] There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets of God entering into the kingdom of God, [Col. 0625] but yourselves cast out. 29. And they shall come from east and west and from north and south, and shall recline at table in the kingdom of 30. God. And behold, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who were last.”

31. On that same day some Pharisees came, saying to him: “Depart and go hence, for Herod wishes to kill thee.” 32. And he said to them: “Go and tell that fox: ‘Behold, I cast out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am perfected.’ 33. Jerusalem, [Col. 0627] Jerusalem, thou who killest the prophets and stonest those sent to thee, how often I wished to gather thy children, as a hen [gathers] her nest under her wings, and ye would not! 35. Behold, your house is left to you desolate. For I say [Note: [Col. 0627] Gat.: “unto you: you shall not see me.” Mm.: “unto you: you shall not see me from now on until you say: Blessed.” Gat.: “when you say.” Vulg.: “unto you, because you shall not see me until the time comes when you say.”] unto you, you shall not see me until the day comes when you say: ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

He therefore [Note: [Col. 0628] Gat.: “having taken hold of the man, he healed [him].” Mm.: “having taken hold of John, he healed him.” Vulg.: “having taken hold [of him], he healed him.”] took hold of his hand, healed him, and dismissed him. 5. And [Note: [Col. 0627] Before *said*, *answering* is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] he said + to them: “Whose ass or ox among you, if it falls into a pit on the sabbath, will not immediately draw it out on the day of the sabbath?” 6. And they were unable to answer him concerning these things.

7. 12. ## CHAPTER XV
1. [...di], let him hear. Now all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.  
2. And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying: “Why does this man receive sinners and eat with them?”  
3. And he spoke to them this parable, saying:  
4. “What man among you, having one hundred sheep, if one of them has perished, does he not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost, seeking it until he finds it?  
5. And when he has found it, he lays it upon his shoulders rejoicing;  
6. and when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them: ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep which had perished.’  
7. I tell you that thus there will be joy in heaven over one sinner doing penance, more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who have no need of repentance.

10. Thus, I tell you, there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner doing penance.

14. And when he had spent everything, a severe famine arose throughout that region; and he began  
15. to be in want. And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that region, who sent him into his field to feed swine.  
16. And he desired to fill his belly with the husks which the swine ate; and no one  
17. gave him anything. But coming to himself, he said: ‘How many hired servants of my father have bread in abundance, while I here  
18. perish with hunger! I will rise and go to my father, and I will say to him: “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before  
19. you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired  
20. servants.”’ And rising, he came to his father. And while he was still far off, his father saw him; and, moved with compassion, he ran forward, fell upon his neck, and kissed him.  
21. And the son said to him: ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’  
22. But the father said to his servants: ‘Quickly bring out the best robe and put it on him; give him a ring for his hand and sandals for his feet;  
23. bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat and feast;  
24. for this my son was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’ And they began to feast.  
25. Now his elder son was in the field; and as he came and approached the house, he heard music and  
26. dancing. He called one of the servants and asked what these things might be.  
27. He said to him: ‘Because your brother has come, your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and sound.’  
28. But he became angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and began to plead with him.  
29. But he answered and said to his father: ‘Behold, for so many years I have served you, and I have never transgressed your command; yet you never gave me even a kid, that I might feast with my friends.  
30. But when this son of yours, who consumed all his wealth living with prostitutes, came, you killed the fattened calf for him.’  
31. But he said to him: ‘You have always been with me, and you are; and all that is mine  
32. is yours. But it was fitting for us to feast and rejoice, because this your brother was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’”

## Chapter XVI

1. And he also said to his disciples: “There was a certain rich man who had a steward; and this man had been accused before him of squandering his goods.  
2. And his master called him and said to him: ‘What is this that I hear about you? Render an account of your stewardship, for you will no longer be able to manage my affairs.’  
3. But the steward said within himself: ‘What shall I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not able to dig; I am ashamed to beg.  
4. I know what I shall do, so that, when I have been removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.’  
5. And, having called each of his master’s debtors, he said to the first: ‘How much do you owe my master?’  
6. He said: ‘One hundred baths of oil.’ And he said to him: ‘Take your bond, sit down, and quickly write fifty.’  
7. Then he said to another: ‘And how much do you owe my master?’ He said: ‘One hundred cors of wheat.’ And he said to him: ‘Take your bond and write eighty.’  
8. And the master praised the steward of unrighteousness because he had acted shrewdly. And he said to … [serv…] … I tell you … [child]ren of this age are more shrewd than the children of light in this generation.  
9. And I tell you: Make friends for yourselves from unrighteous mammon (*mamona*, Greek Μαμωνᾶ), so that, when it fails you, they may receive you into eternal dwellings.  
10. He who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much; and he who is unrighteous in the least is unrighteous also in much.  
11. If, therefore, you have not been faithful in unrighteous mammon, who will give you that which is with you?  
12. And if you have not been faithful in what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?  
13. No servant can serve two masters. For either he will hate one and love the other; or he will hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.’  
14. When the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things, they mocked him.  
15. And he said to them: ‘You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among men is an abomination before God.  
16. The Law and the Prophets were until John; from then on the kingdom of God is proclaimed, and everyone presses into it.  
17. But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the Law to fail.  
18. Everyone who dismisses his wife and marries another commits adultery; and whoever marries a woman dismissed by her husband commits adultery.  
19. There was a certain rich man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen and feasted splendidly every day.  
20. And a certain poor man named Lazarus lay at the gate of that rich man, full of sores;  
21. and he desired to be filled with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. But dogs also came and licked his wounds.  
22. And it happened that the poor man died and was carried by angels into Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried in hell.  
23. And lifting up his eyes from hell, while he was in torments, he saw Abraham far off and Lazarus in his bosom.  
24. And he cried out and said: “Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.”  
25. But Abraham said to him: “Son, remember that you received good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise evil things; but now he is comforted, while you are tormented.  
26. And besides all these things, a great gulf of earth has been fixed between us and you, so that those who would pass from here to you cannot do so, nor may any cross from there to here.”  
27. And he said: “Then I beg you, Father, that you send him to my father’s house,  
28. for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they too come into this place of torment.”  
29. But Abraham said to him: “They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them.”  
30. But he said: “No, Father Abraham; but if someone should rise from the dead, they will do penance.”  
31. He said to him: “If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they believe even if someone should go to them from the dead.”’

## Chapter XVII

1. And he said to his disciples: “It is difficult that stumbling blocks should not come; nevertheless, woe to him through whom they come.  
2. It would be better for him not to have been born, or for a millstone to have been placed around his neck and for him to have been cast into the sea, than for him to cause one of these little ones to stumble.  
3. Take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he does penance, forgive  
4. him. And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times turns to you, saying, ‘I repent,’ forgive him.”  
5. And the apostles said to the Lord: “Increase our faith.”  
6. To them he said: “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree: ‘Be rooted up and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.  
7. But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding sheep, when he returns from the field, will immediately say to him: ‘Come forward and recline at table’?  
8. Will he not rather say to him: ‘Prepare something for me to dine upon; and, girded, serve me until I eat and drink; afterward you shall eat and  
9. drink’? Does he thank the servant because he did what was commanded  
10. him? So you also, when you have done what was commanded, say: ‘We are unprofitable servants; we have done what we ought to do.’  
11. And it happened, while he was going to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria, Galilee, and Jericho.  
12. And as he entered a certain village, behold, ten leprous men stood  
13. at a distance. They raised their voices, saying: “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.”  
14. And when he heard them, he said to them: “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And it happened, while they were going, that they were cleansed.  
15. But one of them, seeing that he was healed, returned, glorifying God with a loud voice;  
16. and he fell on his face at his feet, giving thanks to him; and he was a Samaritan.  
17. And Jesus answered and said: “Were not these ten cleansed? Where are the nine?  
18. Of these, none has been found who returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner.”  
19. And he said to him: “Rise and go; your faith has made you whole.”  
20. And when he was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, he said to them: “The kingdom does not come with observation;  
21. nor will they say: ‘Behold, here,’ or ‘Behold, there.’ For behold, the kingdom of God is within you.”  
22. And he said to his disciples: “Days will come when you will desire to see one day of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.  
23. And they will say to you: ‘Behold, here,’ or ‘Behold, there.’ Do not go, nor follow.  
24. For as lightning flashes, so will the Son of Man be.  
25. But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.  
26. And as it happened in the days of Noah, so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.  
27. They were eating, drinking, marrying, and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered  
28. the ark; and the flood came and destroyed them all.  
28. Likewise it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, and building;  
29. but on the day Lot went out from Sodom, fire rained from heaven and destroyed them all.  
30. It will be the same on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.  
31. In that hour, whoever is on the roof and whose goods are in the house must not go down to take them away; likewise, whoever is in the field must not turn back.  
32. Remember Lot’s wife.  
33. Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it; and whoever loses it will preserve it.  
34. I tell you: on that night there will be two in one bed; one will be taken and the other left.  
35. There will be two women grinding together; one will be left and the other taken; two in the field: one will be taken and the other left.”  
36. And they answered and said to him: “Where, Lord?”  
37. He said to them: “Wherever the body may be, there the eagles gather.”

## Chapter XVIII

1. And he spoke to them a parable to show that they ought always to pray and not  
2. lose heart, saying: “There was a certain judge in a certain city, who did not fear God and did not respect  
3. man. Now there was a certain widow in that city, and she came to him saying: ‘Vindicate me against my adversary.’  
4. And for a time he was unwilling. But afterward he said within himself: ‘Though I do not fear God or respect man,  
5. yet because this widow troubles me, I will vindicate her, lest by continually coming she wear me out.’”  
6. And the Lord said: “Hear what the unjust judge says.  
7. And will not God bring vindication to his elect who cry out day and night, while he is patient  
8. with them? I tell you that he will bring their vindication speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, do you suppose that he will find faith upon the earth?”  
9. And he also spoke this parable to some who trusted in themselves as though they were righteous and despised others:  
10. “Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a tax collector and the other a Pharisee.  
11. The Pharisee, standing, prayed these things within himself: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like other men—robbers, unrighteous persons, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.  
12. I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of everything that I possess.’  
13. But the tax collector, standing far off, was unwilling even to lift his eyes to heaven, but struck his breast, saying: ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner.’  
14. I tell you that this man went down justified to his house rather than that Pharisee; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.  
15. And they brought infants to him, that he might touch them; but the disciples, seeing this, rebuked them.  
16. But Jesus commanded them, saying: ‘Allow the children to come to me and do not prevent them; for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.  
17. Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child shall not enter into it.’  
18. And a certain man asked him, saying: ‘Good Master, what must I do to possess eternal life?’  
19. But Jesus said to him: ‘Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.  
20. You know the commandments.’ He said: ‘Which?’ ‘You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; honor your father and mother.’  
21. He said: ‘I have kept all these things from my youth.’  
22. When Jesus heard this, he said to him: ‘One thing still lacks for you: sell everything you have to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow  
23. me.’ When he heard these things, he became sad, for he was very rich.  
24. And Jesus, seeing him saddened, said: ‘How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!  
25. For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.’  
26. Those who heard said: ‘Then who can be  
27. saved?’ And he said to them: ‘What is impossible with men is possible with God.’  
28. Then Peter said: ‘Behold, we have left all our possessions and followed  
29. you.’ He said to them: ‘Amen, I tell you: there is no one who has left house, parents, brothers, wife, or children for the kingdom of  
30. God who shall not receive sevenfold in this time, and in the age to come possess eternal life.’  
31. And having summoned the twelve disciples, he said to them: ‘Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all things written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be fulfilled.  
32. For he will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, and spat upon;  
33. and after scourging him they will kill him, and on the third day  
34. he will rise.’ But they understood none of these things; the saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was said to them.  
35. And it happened, as he approached Jericho, that a certain blind man sat by the road begging.  
36. Hearing a crowd passing by, he asked what  
37. this was. They told him that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by.  
38. And he cried out, saying: ‘Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on  
39. me.’ Those who were passing by rebuked him, that he should be silent. But he cried out all the more: ‘Son of David, have mercy on me.’  
40. And Jesus stood still and commanded him to be brought. When he had drawn near, he asked  
41. him, saying: ‘What do you wish me to do for you?’ He said: ‘That I may see.’  
42. And Jesus answered and said to him: ‘Receive sight; your faith has made you whole.’  
43. And immediately he began to see; and he followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

## Chapter XIX

1. And having entered, he passed through  
2. Jericho. And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus; he was chief of the tax collectors, and he was  
3. wealthy. He sought to see who Jesus was, but could not because of the crowd, for he was short in  
4. stature. And running ahead, he climbed a sycamore tree to see him, because he was going to pass that way.  
5. And when Jesus passed by, he saw him; and looking up, he said to him: “Zacchaeus, come down quickly, for today I must stay in your house.”  
6. And he came down quickly and received him joyfully.  
7. And when they all saw it, they murmured because he had entered to lodge with a sinful man.  
8. But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord: “Behold, Lord, I give half of my goods to the poor; and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.”  
9. And Jesus said to them: “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of  
10. Abraham. For the Son of Man came to save and seek what was lost.”  
11. As they heard these things, he added and spoke a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and because they thought that the kingdom of God would immediately appear.  
12. Therefore he said: “A certain householder went into a far country to receive a kingdom and return.  
13. And having called ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them: ‘Trade until I come.’  
14. But his citizens hated him, and sent an embassy after him, saying: ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’  
15. And it happened, when he returned after receiving the kingdom, that he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to be called, so that he might know what each had gained by trading.  
16. The first came, saying: ‘Lord, your mina has gained ten  
17. minas.’ He said to him: ‘Very good, good servant; because you have been faithful in a very little matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’  
18. And another came, saying: ‘Lord, your mina has made another five  
19. minas.’ He said to him also: ‘And you, be set over five cities.’  
20. And another came, saying: ‘Lord, behold your mina, which I kept laid away in  
21. a cloth; for I feared you, because you are a severe man: you take what you did not put down and reap what you did not sow.’  
22. He said to him: ‘Out of your own mouth I will judge you, faithless and wicked servant. You knew that I am a severe man, taking what I did not put down and reaping what I did not sow;  
23. then why did you not put my money in the bank, so that when I came I might have collected it with interest?’  
24. Then he said to those standing by: ‘Take it from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’  
25. And they said to him: ‘Lord, he has ten minas.’  
26. ‘I tell you: to everyone who has, it shall be given; but from the one who does not have, even what he has shall be taken from him.  
27. Nevertheless, bring here those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, and slaughter them before me.’”  
28. Having said these things, he went on, ascending toward Jerusalem.  
29. And it happened, when he had approached Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, that he sent two of his disciples,  
30. saying: “Go into the village opposite; as you enter it, you will find an ass with a colt tied beside her, on which no one has sat. Untie her and bring her.  
31. And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying her?’ you shall say to him, ‘Because the Lord has need of her service.’”  
32. And those who had been sent went away and found the ass standing, as he had told them.  
33. And while they untied the ass with the colt, its owners said  
34. to them: “Why are you untying the colt?” They said: “Because it is needed by its Lord.”  
35. And they brought it to Jesus; and, spreading their garments upon the colt, they set Jesus upon it.  
36. As he went, they spread their garments in the road.  
37. And as he approached the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole rejoicing multitude began to praise God loudly for all the mighty works which they had seen,  
38. saying: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord: blessed is the King; peace in heaven and glory.”  
39. And some Pharisees from the crowd said to him: “Master, rebuke  
40. them.” He said to them: “I tell you, if these should be silent, the stones will cry out.”  
41. And when he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it, saying:  
42. “Because if you knew—although on this your day—the things pertaining to your peace, they would be hidden from [your] eyes. For days will come upon you when your enemies will cast up an embankment against you, surround you, and hem you in on every side;  
44. and they will level you to the ground, and your children within you, and will not leave one stone upon another  
45. in you, because you did not know the time of your visitation.” And entering the temple, he began to cast out those selling and buying in it; he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves,  
46. saying to them: “It is written: ‘My house is a house of prayer.’ But you have made it a den of robbers.”  
47. And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people sought to destroy him,  
48. yet they did not find what they could do, for all the people hung upon his words, listening to him.

## Chapter XX
1. And it came to pass, on one of the days, while he was teaching the people in the temple and making proclamation, that the chief priests and scribes, with the elders, came forward, 2. saying: “Tell us, by what authority do you do these things? And who is it that gave you this authority?” 3. Answering, he said to them: “I too will ask you a question; 4. and answer me: Was John’s baptism from heaven, or from human beings?” 5. But they reasoned among themselves, saying: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ 6. But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ all the people will stone us; for they know that John 7. was a prophet.” And they answered that they did not know from where it was. 8. And Jesus said to them: “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

9. Then he began to tell this parable: “A man planted a vineyard and leased it to tenants, and he himself went away for a long time. 10. At a certain season he sent a servant to those tenants, that they might give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But they beat him and sent him away empty-handed. 11. And he proceeded to send another servant. They likewise beat that one also and sent him away empty-handed. 12. And he proceeded to send a third. They wounded him also and threw him out. 13. Then the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’ 14. But when the tenants saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir; let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.’ 15. And having thrown him out of the vineyard, they killed him. What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do? 16. He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others.” When they heard this, they said, “May it never be!”

17. Looking at them, he said: “What, then, is this that is written: ‘The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner’? 18. Everyone who falls upon that stone will be shattered; but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him to pieces.”

19. The chief priests and scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but they feared the people; for they knew that he had spoken this parable against them. 20. And, when they had withdrawn, they sent men, pretending [the transmitted text reads *suborfingentes*, sic], in order to catch his words, so as to hand him over to the authority of the governor. 21. They questioned him, saying: “Teacher, we know that you speak rightly and do not show partiality toward persons, but teach the way of God in truth. 22. Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?” 23. But seeing their wickedness, he said to them: “Why do you test me? 24. Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it bear?” They answered, “Caesar’s.” 25. He said: “Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” 26. And they could not catch his statement before the people; and, astonished at his answer, they fell silent.

27. Then some Sadducees approached, who deny that there is a resurrection, and questioned 28. him, saying: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that, if a man’s brother dies having a wife and leaves no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother. 29. There were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died childless. 30. The next took her and also died childless. 31. The third likewise; and all seven, and they left no child and died. 32. Then the woman also died. 33. In the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.”

34. Jesus said to them: “The children of this age beget and are begotten, marry and are given in marriage; 35. but those judged worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage. 36. For they can no longer die; for they are equal to the angels of God, being children of the resurrection. 37. But that the dead rise, Moses showed in the passage concerning the bush, when he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ 38. He is not God of the dead but of the living; for all live to him.”

39. Some of the scribes answered: “Teacher, you have spoken well.” 40. And they no longer dared to ask him anything.

41. He said to them: “How do they say that the Christ is David’s son? 42. For David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, 43. until I place your enemies beneath your feet.’ 44. David therefore calls him Lord; how, then, is he his son?”

45. While all the people were hearing, he said to his disciples: 46. “Beware of the scribes, who wish to walk about in robes and love greetings in the marketplace, the foremost seats in synagogues, and the places of honour at banquets—47. who devour widows’ houses while pretending to make long prayers. These will receive a greater punishment.”

## CHAPTER XXI

1. Looking up, Jesus saw rich persons putting their gifts into the treasury. 2. He also saw a certain poor widow putting in two small coins. 3. And he said: “Truly I tell you that this poor widow has put in more than all of them. 4. For all these gave gifts to God out of what they had in abundance; but she, out of her poverty, put in all the means she had.”

5. And when some were saying concerning the temple that it had been built with excellent and fine stones, he said: 6. “These things that you see: days will come in which not one stone upon another will be left here in the wall that will not be destroyed.” 7. They questioned him, saying: “Teacher, when will these things be? And what will be the sign when these things begin to happen?” 8. He said: “See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not follow them. 9. But when you hear of wars and revolts, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end will not be immediately in them. 10. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. 11. There will also be great earthquakes in various places, plagues and famines; there will be terrors and great signs from heaven, and winters.

12. “But before all these things they will lay their hands upon you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons; you will be brought before kings because of my name, 13. and it will result in testimony for you. 14. Therefore settle it in your hearts not to prepare beforehand how to make your defence; 15. for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand. 16. You will be handed over even by parents, relatives, and friends; and they will put some of you to death. 17. You will be hated by all because of my name. 18. Yet not a hair of your head will perish. 19. By your endurance you will gain your lives.

20. “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has drawn near. 21. Then let those who are in Judaea flee to the mountains; let those in its midst depart; and let those in the surrounding country not enter it. 22. For these are days of judgment, in order that all things written may be fulfilled. 23. Woe to those who are pregnant and those nursing in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people. 24. They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive among all nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled.

25. “There will be signs in sun, moon, and stars; and upon the earth distress of nations in perplexity at the roaring of the sea and its waves, 26. people fainting from fear and expectation of what is coming upon the inhabited world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken. 27. Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with great power and glory. 28. But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your deliverance draws near.”

29. And he told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees. 30. When they put forth leaves of themselves, you know that summer is near. 31. So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near. 32. Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all things take place. 33. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

34. “Take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with indulgence, drunkenness, and worldly anxieties, and that day come upon you suddenly; 35. for like a snare it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth. 36. Keep watch, praying at every time that you may be judged worthy to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”

37. During the days he was teaching in the temple; but at night he went out and stayed on the mountain called Olivet. 38. And all the people rose early at dawn to come to him in the temple to hear him.

## CHAPTER XXII

1. Now the feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was drawing near. 2. And the chief priests and scribes sought how they might kill him; for they feared the people. 3. Then Satan entered Judas, who was surnamed Iscarioth (*Iscarioth*; Origen read the Greek Ἰσκαριώθ, as does the Latin Codex Vercellensis; the Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis has Ἰσκαριώδ; other readings are *Scarioth* and *Isariotes*), one of the number of the twelve. 4. He went and conferred with the chief priests and scribes about how he might hand him over. 5. They rejoiced and promised to give him money. 6. And he sought an opportunity to hand him over without a crowd.

7. Then came the day of Passover. 8. And he sent Peter and John, saying: “Go and prepare the Passover for us to eat.” 9. They said to him: “Where do you wish us to prepare it?” 10. He said to them: “Behold, when you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him into the house which he enters. 11. And say to the master of the house: ‘The Teacher says to you, Where is the dining room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’ 12. And he will show you a large furnished upper room (*maedianum*; Greek ἀνώγεον μέγα; Codex Cantabrigiensis reads οἶκον, ‘house’; Cantabrigiensis Latin, ‘upper house’). Prepare it there.” 13. They went and found it as he had told them, and prepared the Passover.

14. When the hour came, he reclined at table, and the apostles with him. 15. He said to them: “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. 16. For I tell you that I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.” 17. And, taking a cup, he gave thanks and said: “Take this and divide it among yourselves. 18. For I tell you that I will not drink from the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.” 19. And, taking bread, he gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying: “This is my body.”

[After “This is my body,” the text lacks: “which is given for you,” and the remainder through verse 21, as also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. Verse 20 is absent. The Gatian text has: “Likewise also the cup after supper, saying: This is the cup of the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.” The Vulgate reads: “Likewise the cup after he had supped, saying: This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which shall be poured out for you.”]

21. “Nevertheless, behold, the hand of my betrayer is with me upon the table. 22. For the Son of Man goes according to what has been determined; but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed.” 23. And they began to inquire among themselves which of them it could be who was about to do this.

24. A dispute also arose among them as to which of them was greater. 25. But he said to them: “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors. 26. But you are not to be so; rather, let the greater among you become as the younger, and the one who presides as one who serves. 27. For who is greater: the one reclining at table or the one serving? Among the nations it is the one reclining; but among you it is not so: I am in your midst as one who serves. 28. But you are those who have remained with me in my trials; 29. and I appoint for you, as my Father appointed for me, a kingdom, 30. that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit upon twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

31. The Lord said to Peter: “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded you, that he may sift you like wheat. 32. But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, when at last you have turned back, strengthen your brothers. And pray that you may not enter into temptation.” 33. Peter said to him: “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death.” 34. He said: “I tell you, Peter, the cock will not crow today before you deny three times that you know me.”

35. And he said to them: “When I sent you without purse, bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?” They said, “Nothing.” 36. He therefore said: “But now, let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag; and let the one who does not have a sword sell his tunic and buy one. 37. For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘And he was reckoned with the unrighteous.’ And what concerns me is coming to its end.” 38. They said: “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” He said to them: “It is enough.”

39. Going out, he went according to his custom to the Mount of Olives; and his disciples followed him. 40. When he was at the place, he said to them: “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.” 41. And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw; and, kneeling, 42. he prayed, saying: “Father, not my will but yours be done; take this cup away from me.” 43. Then an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him. 44. And being in agony, he prayed more earnestly; and his sweat became like drops of blood running down upon the ground. 45. Rising from prayer, he came to his disciples and found them sleeping from sorrow. 46. He said to them: “Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, that you may not enter into temptation.”

47. While he was still speaking, behold, a crowd came; and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. Coming near, he kissed Jesus. 48. But Jesus said: “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?” 49. When those around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him: “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?” 50. And one of them struck the servant of the chief priest and cut off his right ear. 51. But Jesus said to him: “Permit this much.” And stretching out his hand, he touched him, and his ear was restored.

52. Then Jesus said to those who had come against him—the chief priests, officers of the temple, and elders—“Have you come out with swords and clubs as against a robber? 53. While I was with you daily in the temple, you did not lay hands upon me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”

54. Having arrested him, they led him into the house of the chief priest. But Peter followed at a distance. 55. When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and were sitting together, Peter sat in their midst. 56. A certain maidservant saw him, looked closely at him, and said: “This man also was among those who were with him.” 57. But he denied it, saying: “Woman, I do not know him.” 58. And when he had gone out to the doorway, another saw him and said, “[. . .] This man also was with Jesus the Nazarene.” And he again denied it with an oath. 59. A little later someone saw him and said: “Certainly this man also was with Jesus, for he is a Galilean.” 60. But Peter said: “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” And immediately, while he was still speaking, the cock crowed. 61. And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Peter remembered the word of the Lord, as he had said to him: “Before the cock crows, you will deny three times that you know me.” 63. The men who held him mocked him. 64. Covering his face, they struck him and questioned him, saying: “Prophesy: who is it that struck you?” 65. And blaspheming, they said many other things against him.

66. When day came, the elders of the people, chief priests, and scribes assembled; they led him into their council and questioned him, saying: “If you are the Christ, tell us.” 67. But he said to them: “If I tell you, you will not believe; 68. and if I question you, you will not answer, nor will you release me. 69. But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.” 70. They all said to him: “Are you, then, the Son of God?” He said to them: “You say that I am.” 71. They said: “Why do we still need testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from his mouth.”

## CHAPTER XXIII

1. And the whole multitude of them rose and led him to Pilate. 2. They began to accuse him, saying: “We found this man subverting the nation [. . .] tribute [. . .] to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ, a king.” 3. Pilate questioned him, saying: “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answered him: “You say so.” 4. Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowd: “I find no fault in this man.” 5. But they insisted, saying: “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judaea, beginning from Galilee as far as this place.”

6. When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man was a Galilean. 7. And when he learned that he was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him back to Herod, who himself was also in Jerusalem in those days. 8. Herod, seeing Jesus, rejoiced greatly; for he had long wished to see him, because he had often heard about him, and he hoped to see some sign performed by him. 9. He questioned him at length, but he answered him nothing. 10. The chief priests and scribes stood by, accusing him vehemently. 11. Herod also, with his soldiers, despised him; and, after mocking him and clothing him in a white garment, he sent him back to Pilate. 12. Herod and Pilate became friends with one another that same hour; for previously they had been enemies.

13. Pilate summoned the chief priests and the leaders of the people, 14. and said to them: “You brought this man to me as one who turns the people away; and behold, after examining him before you, I found in this man nothing of the charges which you bring against him. 15. Nor did Herod; for I sent you to him, and behold, nothing deserving death has been done by him. 16. Therefore I will punish him and release him.”

[Verse 17 is absent. Gatian and Marian texts read: “But it was necessary to release one to them at the feast.” The Vulgate: “But he had the necessity, etc.”]

18. But all the people cried out, saying: “Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us”—19. one who had been thrown into prison for a certain revolt made in the city and for murder. 20. Again Pilate addressed them, wishing to release Jesus. 21. But they shouted: “Crucify him!” 22. For the third time he said to them: “Why? What evil has this man done? I have found nothing deserving death in him. Therefore I will punish him and release him.” 23. But they pressed him with loud cries, demanding that he be crucified; and their cries prevailed. 24. Pilate decided that their request should be granted. 25. He released the man who had been thrown into prison for murder and revolt, whom they requested; but Jesus he handed over to their will.

26. As they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene coming from the country and laid the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus. 27. A great multitude of people followed him, and women who were beating themselves and lamenting. 28. Turning to them, he said: “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; rather, weep for yourselves and your children. 29. For days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nurse.’ 30. Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall upon us!’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us!’ 31. For if they do these things in the green wood, what will be done in the dry?”

32. Two other criminals were also being led with him to be put to death. 33. When they came to the place called Calvary, they crucified him there, and the criminals, one at the right and the other at the left. 34. And, dividing his garments, they cast lots.

[Before “dividing,” the text lacks: “But Jesus said, Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing,” as also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

35. The people stood watching. The rulers mocked him among themselves, saying: “He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ of God, the chosen one.” 36. The soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him vinegar, 37. and saying: “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.” 38. There was also an inscription written over him: “This is the King of the Jews.”

39. One of the criminals hanging there blasphemed him, saying: “Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us.” 40. But the other answered, rebuking him, saying: “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment? 41. And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward of what we have done; but this man has done nothing wrong.” 42. And he said to Jesus: “Remember me when you come into your kingdom.” 43. Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”

44. It was about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour. 45. The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in the middle. 46. And Jesus cried out with a loud voice: “Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.” And he gave up his spirit. 47. When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying: “Certainly this man was righteous.” 48. And all the crowds that had gathered for this spectacle, seeing what was taking place, returned, beating their breasts. 49. But all his acquaintances stood at a distance, as did the women who had followed him from Galilee, seeing these things.

50. And behold, there was a man named Joseph, a councillor, a good and righteous man 51. (he had not consented to their counsel and action), from the Judean city of Arimathia, who awaited the kingdom of God. 52. This man went to Pilate and requested the body of Jesus. 53. Taking it down, he wrapped it in a linen cloth and laid it in a hewn tomb, where no one had yet been laid. 54. It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was dawning. 55. Two women who had come with him from Galilee followed; they saw the tomb and how his body was laid. 56. Then they returned and prepared spices and ointments; and on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.

### Additional textual apparatus

The following notes preserve the remaining editorial matter and variant readings of the supplied text.

**Chapter XX.** [Col. 0671] At v. 3, Gat. reads “But,” Mm. “But,” and the Vulgate “But Jesus said.” At v. 4, Gat. and Mm. read, “Whence was John’s baptism? From heaven, or . . . ?”; the Vulgate, “Was John’s baptism from heaven, or . . . ?” [Col. 0672] At v. 5, Gat. reads “among themselves . . .”; Mm., “among themselves . . . he will say to us: Why did you not . . . ?”; Vulg., “within themselves . . . he will say: Why then did you not . . . ?” [Col. 0673] At v. 10, Mm. reads “that they might give to him”; Vulg., “that they might give.” At v. 14, Gat. reads “But when”; Mm., “among themselves”; Vulg., “Whom when . . . among themselves.” [Col. 0675] At v. 23, Mm. reads “But Jesus, seeing their deceit”; Vulg., “But considering their deceit.” At v. 24, Mm. reads “a denarius, that I may see it. Whose does it have . . . ?”; Vulg., “a denarius. Whose does it have . . . ?” At v. 25, “to Caesar” is additional.
