At v. 26, Gat. reads “to answer . . . in their answers”; Mm., “in their answers”; Vulg., “to find fault . . . in his answer.” [Col. 0676] At v. 28, Gat. and Mm. read “saying: Moses . . . if he die without children, that . . .”; Vulg., “saying: Teacher, Moses . . . if he die without offspring, that . . .” [Col. 0677] At v. 29, Gat. and Mm. read “without children”; Vulg., “without a child.” At v. 31, “but” is additional. At v. 32, Gat. and Mm. read “died”; Vulg., “was dead.” At v. 33, Mm. reads “for all had”; Vulg., “indeed the seven had.” At v. 35, Gat. reads “marry . . .”; Mm., “marry, nor take wives”; Vulg., “will neither marry nor take wives.” At v. 36, Gat. and Mm. read: “for they will no longer be able to die; but they are like the angels, and are children of God, because they are children of the resurrection.” [Col. 0678] At v. 37, Gat. reads “But that the dead rise, Moses . . .”; Mm., “But truly, etc.”

**Chapter XXI.** [Col. 0679] At v. 4, Gat. and Mm. read “out of abundance for herself”; Vulg., “out of her abundance for herself.” [Col. 0681] At v. 8, Gat. and Mm. read “I am the Christ, and . . .”; Vulg., “I am, and . . .” At v. 12, Gat. and Mm. read “dragging [you] into their synagogues and prisons, handing [you] over to kings”; Vulg., “handing [you] over to synagogues and prisons, dragging [you] before kings.” [Col. 0682] At v. 14, Gat. reads “therefore in yourselves”; Mm., “how you should answer”; Vulg., “therefore in . . . how you should answer.” [Col. 0683] At v. 17, Gat. reads “by all people because of”; Vulg., “by all because of.” At v. 20, Gat. and Mm. read “its desolation has drawn near”; Gat., in a recent hand, reads “your”; Vulg., “its desolation has drawn near.” The main text has a transmitted gap, “adpropinquavit . . . olatio.” [Col. 0684] At v. 21, Gat. and Mm. read “to the mountains”; Gat. and Mm. read “go down,” while the Vulgate reads “depart.” At v. 23, Gat. reads “Woe to those who have [children] in the womb, and those who give the breast”; Mm., “Woe to you. Those who have [children] in the womb, and those who give the breast.” [Col. 0685] At v. 31, Gat. reads “all these things happening”; Vulg., “these things happening.” At v. 33, Gat. and Mm. read “will not pass away”; Vulg., “will not pass over.” At v. 34, Mm. reads “be hardened”; Vulg., “be weighed down.” At v. 36, the reading *effugere* (“to escape”) agrees with the Greek text, ἐκφυγεῖν; Mm. reads *effugere*, Vulg. *fugere* (“to flee”). The reading *stabitis* (“you shall stand”) agrees with Codex Cantabrigiensis and Greek στήσεσθε. [Col. 0686] At v. 37, Gat. and Mm. read “rested”; at v. 38, Gat. reads “rose early,” Vulg. “rose early [at dawn].”

**Chapter XXII.** [Col. 0687] At v. 2, “him” is supplied from the Greek text, αὐτόν. At v. 3, Origen reads, with Vercellensis, Greek Ἰσκαριώθ; Codex Cantabrigiensis Latin likewise has *Iscarioth*, whereas its Greek has Ἰσκαριώδ. Gat. reads “surnamed Scarioth, one of”; Mm., “Scarioth, one of”; Vulg., “surnamed Isariotes, one of.” At v. 7, *Paschae* (“of Passover”) agrees with Codex Cantabrigiensis and Greek τοῦ πάσχα. At v. 10, after *homo* (“a man”), *quidam* (“a certain”) is absent, also in the Greek text. At v. 12, the Greek text reads ἀνώγεον μέγα, “a large upper room, furnished”; Codex Cantabrigiensis reads οἶκον (“house”) instead of μέγα; Cantabrigiensis Latin has *superiorem domum* (“upper house”). At v. 17, “this” is added, as also in the Greek text, τοῦτο. At v. 19, after “my body,” the words “which is given for you,” etc., through v. 21 are absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis. Verse 20 is absent; Gat. has: “Likewise also the cup after supper, saying: This is the cup of the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you”; Vulg.: “Likewise the cup after he had supped, saying: This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which shall be poured out for you.” At v. 21, Mm. reads “my betrayer with me”; Vulg., “the betrayer of me with me.” After “with me,” *est* (“is”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 22, Gat. reads “as what has been determined . . . is betrayed”; Mm., “as has been determined”; Vulg., “according to what has been determined . . . will be betrayed.” [Col. 0690] At v. 23, Gat. reads “began to inquire among themselves which”; Mm., “to inquire among themselves, which.” After “was,” “of them” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 24, Gat. reads “But this dispute arose”; Mm., “But this dispute having arisen”; Vulg., “And a dispute also arose.” [Col. 0691] After “which,” “of them” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 25, Gat. reads “over them [are called] kindly”; Mm., “over benefits.” At v. 26, Gat. reads “as the younger, and let him who goes before become as the minister”; Mm., “as the younger, and let him who is first become as one who serves”; Vulg., “as the lesser, and he who goes before as the minister.” At v. 27, Gat. likewise reads “Among the nations, indeed, [it is] the one reclining.” [Col. 0692] At v. 30, Mm. reads “thrones. Twelve judging”; Vulg., “thrones, judging twelve.” At v. 31, Gat. and Mm. read “Jesus [said] to Simon: Simon”; Vulg., “The Lord: Simon, Simon.” [Col. 0693] At v. 36, Mm. reads “and he who does not have a sword, let him sell”; Gat., “let him buy himself a sword.” At v. 37, Gat. reads “And that with the unjust”; Mm., “And with the unjust.” At v. 40, “his” is added, also in the Greek text, αὐτοῦ. [Col. 0695] At v. 44, Mm. reads “running down upon”; the common text reads “running down [in the genitive].” At v. 46, Gat. reads “to them: Rise and pray”; Vulg., “to them: Why are you sleeping? Rise, pray.” At v. 49, Gat. and Mm. read “shall we strike?”; Vulg., “do we strike?” [Col. 0696] At v. 51, Gat. and Mm. read “He said to him”; Vulg., “he said.” Gat. and Mm. read “Allow [it].” At v. 52, Gat. and Mm. read “Have you come as against a robber?”; Vulg., “Have you gone out as against a robber?” [Col. 0697] At v. 55, the Greek text likewise reads ἐκάθητο καί (“Peter sat also”); *illis* (“them”) after *circumsedentibus* is omitted, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 57, after “denied,” “him” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis; Mm. reads “said: I am not.” At v. 61, Gat. reads “the word of his Lord, as he said”; Vulg., “the word of the Lord, as he had said.” The wording “he said to him” agrees with the Greek, εἶπεν αὐτῷ. [Col. 0699] At v. 68, after “believe,” “me” is absent, also in the Greek text; after “if,” “but also” is absent in Codex Cantabrigiensis. Gat. reads “you answer me, nor release [me]”; Vulg., “you will answer me, nor release [me].” At v. 70, Mm. reads “Then they all said: But you are”; Vulg., “But they all said: Then you are.” “To them” is added, as also in Codex Cantabrigiensis Greek, αὐτοῖς. At v. 71, before “we have heard,” “we ourselves” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

**Chapter XXIII.** [Col. 0700] At v. 2, Gat. and Mm. read “saying, Christ”; Vulg., “saying himself Christ.” [Col. 0701] At v. 7, Mm. reads “because he also”; Vulg., “who also.” At v. 10, Mm. reads “also the chief priests, vehemently”; Vulg., “but the chief priests and scribes, vehemently.” [Col. 0703] At v. 15, Gat. and Mm. read “I sent him to you”; Vulg., “I sent you to him.” Verse 17 is absent; Gat. and Mm. read: “But it was necessary to release one to them on the feast day”; the Vulgate reads, “But he had the necessity, etc.” At v. 19, Gat. and Mm. read “had been cast into”; Vulg., “had been . . . cast into.” At v. 21, Mm. adds “saying: Crucify him.” [Col. 0704] At v. 22, Gat. reads “this man . . . I have found”; Vulg., “this [man] . . . I find.” At v. 23, Mm. reads “their cries prevailed”; Vulg., “the cries prevailed.” At v. 24, Gat. reads “their requests”; Vulg., “their request.” [Col. 0703] At v. 27, the reading “a great multitude of people” agrees with Codex Cantabrigiensis Greek, πλῆθος λαοῦ; Vercellensis reads *multitudo ingens populi*. [Col. 0705] At v. 28, “for me” is absent three times over, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 29, Mm. reads “for they are coming”; Vulg., “for behold, they will come.” At v. 30, Gat. and Mm. read “Cover us”; Vulg., “Hide us.” At v. 32, Gat. reads “that they might be crucified”; Vulg., “that they might be killed.” At v. 33, Gat. and Mm. read “which is called Calvary”; Vulg., “which is named Calvary.” At v. 34, before “dividing,” “But Jesus said: Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 35, Gat. reads “watching . . . the chief priests with the Sadducees . . . let him save himself”; Mm., “watching . . . Sadducees . . . he does not save himself”; Vulg., “watching . . . the rulers with them . . . let him save himself.” [Col. 0706] At v. 37, Gat. reads “If you are Christ the king, etc.” At v. 39, Gat. reads “of those who was hanging”; Mm., “of those who were hanging.” [Col. 0707] At v. 44, Mm. reads “the third hour”; Vulg., “the sixth hour.” At v. 46, supply “he said.” At v. 50, before “good,” “a man” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 51, *Arimathia* agrees with Codex Cantabrigiensis Greek, Ἀριμαθίας. Gat. and Mm. read “of Judaea. This man came”; Vulg., “of Judaea, who himself also awaited the kingdom of God. This man came.” [Col. 0709] Before “kingdom,” “also himself” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis. At v. 53, “in” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis Greek, ἐν. At v. 55, Gat. reads “had come with him . . . had been”; Mm., “were with him”; Vulg., “had come with him . . . was.” “Two” is added, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis Greek, δύο.

## CHAPTER XXIV
1. But on the first [Col. 0709] day of the week they came very early, before dawn, to the tomb, bringing the things they had prepared. 2. And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb. 3. But when they entered [Note: [Col. 0709] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”] +, they did not find the body [Note: [Col. 0709] After “body,” “of the Lord Jesus” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] +. 4. And it came to pass, while they were bewildered about this, behold, two men stood beside them in shining clothing. 5. And, seized with fear, bowing their faces to the ground, they said to them: “Why do you seek the living among [Note: [Col. 0709] After “the dead,” “he is not here, but has risen” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] + the dead?” 6. Remember how he spoke [Note: [Col. 0710] Mm.: “with you.” Vulgate: “to you.”] to you while he was still in Galilee, 7. saying: “For the Son of Man [Col. 0711] must be handed over, and rise again on the third day.” 8. And they remembered [Note: [Col. 0711] And so Gat.] these words. 9. And when they returned [Note: [Col. 0711] After “returned,” “from the tomb” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] +, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest. 10. Now there were Mary Magdalene, and [Note: [Col. 0711] Gat.: “Mary of James, and Joseph, and the others.” Mm.: “Mary of James, and the others.” Vulgate: “Mary of James, and the others.”] Mary of James, and Joanna, and the other women with them, who told these things to the apostles. 11. But these words seemed to them like delirium, and [Note: [Col. 0711] So also the Greek text: ἠπίστουν, “they disbelieved.”] they did not believe + them [Note: [Col. 0711] The entire verse 12 is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] +.

13. And behold, [Note: [Col. 0711] Mm.: “two men of them.” Vulgate: “two of them.”] two of them were going to a village, sixty stadia from Jerusalem, whose name was [Note: [Col. 0711] St Jerome testifies, in his book *On Hebrew Names*, that certain manuscripts had this reading.] [Note: [Col. 0711] Gat.: “Aemavus.”] Ammaus +. 14. And they [Note: [Col. 0711] Gat.: “were speaking about these things.”] discussed [Col. 0711] all that had happened to them. 15. And it came to pass, while [Note: [Col. 0712] Gat.: “they conversed together.”] they were discussing these matters, Jesus himself came up and went along with them. 16. But their eyes were kept from recognizing him. 17. And he said to them: “What are these words that you are discussing with one another, and are sad?” 18. One of them answered, whose [Note: [Col. 0712] Gat.: “whose name was Cleophas, said to him . . . do you not know all the things which have happened there in these days?” Vulgate: “whose name [was] Cleophas, said to him . . . do you not know the things which have happened there in these days?”] name was Cleophas, and said to him: “Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem? Do you not know what has happened there in these days?” 19. He said to them: “What things?” And they said to him: “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, [Col. 0713] who was a prophet, mighty in deed, [Note: [Col. 0713] Gat.: “and word before God and all the people.” Vulgate: “and speech before God and all the people.”] and word, before God and all the people; 20. [Note: [Col. 0713] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πῶς τοῦτον, “how this man.”] how our chief priests + handed him over [Note: [Col. 0713] Gat.: “Our chief priests and rulers.” Vulgate: “Our high priests and rulers.”] for a sentence of death, and crucified him. 21. But we had hoped that he was the one [Note: [Col. 0713] So also the Greek text: ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι, “the one who was going to redeem.”] who was to redeem + Israel. And now today is the third day since [Note: [Col. 0713] Gat.: “since these things.” Vulgate: “that these things.”] these things occurred. 22. Moreover, some women from among us astonished us: they were at the tomb early in the morning; 23. and when they did not find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, [Col. 0713] [Note: [Col. 0713] Gat. and Mm.: “who were saying.” Vulgate: “who say.”] who say that he is alive. 24. And some of our number went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said; but him they did not [Note: [Col. 0713] So also the Greek text: εἶδον, “saw.”] see +.” 25. And he said to them: “Foolish men, [Note: [Col. 0713] Mm.: “and slow of heart.” Vulgate: “and slow of heart.”] and heavy of heart in believing all that the prophets have spoken! 26. [Note: [Col. 0713] Mm.: “Was it not necessary?” Vulgate: “Was it not necessary for these things?”] Was it not necessary for Christ to suffer these things and enter into his glory?” 27. And [Note: [Col. 0713] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἦν, “was.”] he was + beginning from Moses and all the prophets, [Note: [Col. 0713] Mm.: “interpreting.”] interpreting to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

28. And they approached [Note: [Col. 0714] Gat. and Mm.: “the village to which they were going.” Mm.: “he wished.” Vulgate: “the village to which they were going, and he made as though.”] the village to which they were going; and he made as though to go farther. 29. [Note: [Col. 0714] Mm.: “And they asked him.” Gat.: “And he entered to remain with them.” Vulgate: “And they constrained him. And he entered with them.”] And they constrained him, saying: “Stay with us; [Col. 0715] [Note: [Col. 0715] Gat.: “evening is drawing on, and the day has declined” (a variant reading introduced into the text: “the day is already declining”). Mm.: “because the day is now declining toward evening.”] because [Note: [Col. 0715] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πρὸς ἑσπέραν κέκλικεν ἡ ἡμέρα, “the day has declined toward evening” (ἤδη, “already,” is added in Barb. 1 and in the Vulgate).] the day has now declined toward evening +.” And he went in to remain with them. 30. And it came to pass, when he had reclined at table with them, [Note: [Col. 0715] Mm.: “Jesus took bread.” Vulgate: “he took bread.”] having taken bread, he blessed it and, breaking it, gave it to them. 31. And their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; and he was no longer visible to them. 32. And they said to one another: “Was not our heart [Note: [Col. 0715] Mm.: “burning within us concerning Jesus, while.” Vulgate: “burning within us, while.”] burning within us on the road, while he opened the Scriptures to us?” 33. And rising in that same hour, they returned to Jerusalem and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with [Col. 0715] them, 34. saying: “The Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon.” 35. And they related what had occurred on the road, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread. 36. And while they were saying these things, [Note: [Col. 0715] “To them” is added, also in the Greek text: αὐτῶν, “of them.” The Brixianus supports this. In the same place: “himself,” and so also Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτός.] [Note: [Col. 0715] Gat.: “But Jesus himself stood . . . Peace to you.” Vulgate: “Jesus stood . . . Peace to you.”] he himself + stood in their midst. 37. But terrified and seized with fear, they thought they saw a spirit. 38. He said to them: “Why [Note: [Col. 0716] Gat. and Mm.: “are you troubled?”] are you troubled? And [Note: [Col. 0715] “Why” is added, likewise in the Greek text: διατί.] [Note: [Col. 0716] Gat. and Mm.: “and why do thoughts arise in your heart?” Vulgate: “and thoughts arise in your hearts?”] why + do thoughts arise in your heart? 39. See [Note: [Col. 0716] Gat.: “my feet; for . . . having.” Mm.: “my feet.” Vulgate: “my hands and feet; because . . . to have.”] my hands and feet [Note: [Col. 0715] “My” is added, also in the Greek text: μου.] +, that it is I myself. Touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as [Col. 0717] you see me having [Note: [Col. 0717] Verse 40 is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] +.”

41. But while they still did not believe, for joy, and were amazed, he said: [Note: [Col. 0717] Gat.: “But while they did not believe him for joy and were astonished, he said.” Vulgate: “But while they did not believe and were astonished for joy, he said.”] “Have you anything [Note: [Col. 0717] Mm.: “that I may eat.”] for us to eat 42. here?” They gave him a portion of broiled fish and honeycomb. 43. And taking it, he ate before 44. them; and he said to them: “These are the words that I spoke to you while I was still with you: that all things written concerning me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled.” 45. Then he opened [Note: [Col. 0717] Mm.: “their minds, that.” Vulgate: “their understanding, that.”] their understanding to understand the Scriptures. 46. And he said to them: “For [Note: [Col. 0717] Gat. and Mm.: “thus it is written, that Christ should suffer.” Vulgate: “thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for Christ to suffer.”] thus it is written [Col. 0717] [Note: [Col. 0717] After “written,” “and thus it was necessary” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis; nor does St Irenaeus appear to have read it.] +, that Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third 47. day, and that repentance and the forgiveness of sins should [Note: [Col. 0717] Gat. and Mm.: “be preached.” Vulgate: “be preached.”] be preached in his name among all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. 48. And you are witnesses of these things. 49. And I will send [Note: [Col. 0717] Gat.: “the promise of the Father . . . until you are clothed [Col. 0718] with power from on high.” Mm.: “from the highest.” Vulgate: “the promise of the Father . . . until you are clothed with power from on high.”] the promise of my Father upon you; but remain in the city until you are clothed with [Note: [Col. 0717] So also the Greek text: δύναμιν, “power.”] power + from the highest.”

50. And he led them out [Note: [Col. 0718] Gat.: “out as far as Bethany.” Vulgate: “out to Bethany.”] as far as Bethany; and, lifting up his hands, he blessed [Note: [Col. 0717] So also the Greek text: αὐτούς, “them.”] them +. 51. And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he departed [Note: [Col. 0718] Gat.: “and was carried up into heaven.” Vulgate: “and was borne up into heaven.”] [Note: [Col. 0717] After “from them,” “and was borne up into heaven” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] from 52. them +. And they [Note: [Col. 0717] Before “returned,” “worshipping him” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] [Note: [Col. 0718] Gat.: “worshipping him, they returned.” Mm.: “worshipping, they returned.”] returned + [Col. 0719] to Jerusalem with joy . . . no. 53. And they were always [Col. 0719] in the temple, [Note: [Col. 0719] After “praising,” “and blessing God. Amen” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. The *Amen* is not read in most ancient manuscript codices. Some judge that it was added by the Church, which customarily closed the Gospel narrative with this acclamation.] [Note: [Col. 0719] Gat. omits “blessing God. Amen.” Mm.: “but blessing.” The Vulgate has “praising and blessing God. Amen.”] praising + God.

[Note: [Col. 0719] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἐυαγγέλιον κατὰ Λουκᾶν ἐπληρώθη, ἄρχεται κατὰ Μάρκον: “The Gospel according to Luke has been completed; that according to Mark begins.”] THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE ENDS. THAT ACCORDING TO MARK BEGINS +.

CODEX VERONENSIS.

[Col. 0502]

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0502]

1. Since indeed many have undertaken to arrange an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us, 2. just as those who from the beginning were themselves eyewitnesses and ministers of the word delivered them to us, 3. it seemed good also to me, [Note: [Col. 0501] “And to the Holy Spirit” is added, also in the Gothic: καὶ τῷ Πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, “and to the Holy Spirit,” from Acts of the Apostles 15:28.] and to the Holy Spirit +, [Note: [Col. 0501] Gat.: “having followed from.” Vulgate: “having followed all things from.”] having carefully followed from the beginning [Note: [Col. 0501] According to Greek syntax: πᾶσιν, “all things.”] all things +, to write them to you in order, most excellent Theophilus, 4. that you may know the truth of those words in which you have been instructed.

5. In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zacharias, of the division of Abia; and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth. 6. Now both were [Col. 0502] righteous before the Lord, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of God; and they had no 7. child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both [Note: [Col. 0501] Gat.: “had advanced in age.” Vulgate: “had advanced in.”] had advanced in their days. 8. And it came to pass, while Zacharias was performing priestly service in the order of his division before God, according to the custom of the priesthood, that by lot he went out to offer incense, 9. [Note: [Col. 0501] Gat.: “to offer it, having entered the temple.” Vulgate: “to offer it, having entered [Col. 0502] into the temple.”] having entered the temple 10. of the Lord; and the whole multitude of the people was praying at the hour of incense. 11. Then an angel appeared to him, standing at the right side of [Note: [Col. 0502] Gat.: “the altar of supplication.” Vulgate: “the altar of incense.”] the altar of incense; 12. and Zacharias, seeing him, was troubled, and fear fell [Col. 0504] upon him. 13. [Note: [Col. 0503] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καί, “and.”] And + the angel said to him: “Do not fear, [Note: [Col. 0504] Gat.: “Zacharias, for behold, your prayer has been heard.” Vulgate: “Zachariah, because your prayer has been heard.”] Zacharias, for your supplication has been heard; and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John. 14. And there shall be joy and exultation for you, and many will rejoice at his birth. 15. For he shall be great before the Lord; he shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother’s womb. 16. And he shall turn many sons of Israel to the Lord their 17. God; and he himself shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward children, and the unbelieving toward the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a perfect people.”

[Col. 0504] 18. And Zacharias said to the angel: “How shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in her days.” 19. And the angel answered and said to him: “I am Gabriel, who stand before the Lord; and I was sent to speak to you and to announce these things to you as good news. 20. And behold, you shall be silent and unable to speak until the day when these things come to pass, because you did not believe my words, which shall be fulfilled in their proper time.” 21. And the people were waiting for Zacharias, and they wondered because he delayed . . . in the temple. 22. But when he came out, he could not speak to them; and they recognized that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he kept making signs to them and remained mute.

[Col. 0506] 23. And it came to pass, when the days of his service were completed, that he went home. 24. After these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and concealed herself for five months, 25. saying: “Thus has the Lord dealt with me in the days when he looked upon me to take away my reproach among people.”

26. And at that same time the angel Gabriel was sent by the Lord to a city of Galilee, called Nazareth, 27. to the virgin Mary, betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the VIRGIN’S name was MARY. 28. And the angel entered and addressed her with good news, and said to her: “The Lord is with you; blessed are you among women.” 29. But when she saw him, she was troubled at his entrance and was considering [Col. 0506] that he had thus blessed 30. her. And the angel of the Lord said to her: “Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favor with 31. God. [Note: [Col. 0505] “And” is added, also in the Greek text: καί.] And + behold, you shall conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name 32. Jesus. He shall be great and shall be called Son of the Most High; and the Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father, and he shall reign over the house of Jacob 33. forever, and his kingdom shall have no end.” 34. But Mary said: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; let it happen to me according to your word.” 35. And the angel answered and said to her: “The Holy Spirit comes upon you, and the power of the Most High overshadows you. Therefore the one who [Note: [Col. 0505] After “shall be born,” “from you” is absent, also in the Greek text.] shall be born + holy [Col. 0508] shall be called the Son of God. 36. And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman has herself conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren, 37. because no word is impossible with God.” 38. And the angel departed from her.

39. Then Mary arose in those days and went with haste into the hill country, to a city of Judea. 40. And she entered the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth. 41. And it came to pass, when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, that the child leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit 42. and cried out with a loud voice, saying: [Col. 0508] “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. 43. And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord should come 44. to me? For behold, when the sound of your greeting came into my ears, [Note: [Col. 0507] Gat.: “the child leaped for joy.” Vulgate: “the child leaped.”] the child leaped for joy in my womb. 45. And blessed is she who believed, because the things spoken to you by the Lord shall be fulfilled.”

46. And [Note: [Col. 0507] Origen observes—if he is indeed the author of the homilies on Luke—that in certain copies Mary’s name was omitted; consequently some believed this song to be Elizabeth’s, but wrongly. Moreover, *Elisabeth* is a dative, not a nominative, case.] Elizabeth + said: “My soul magnifies the Lord, 47. and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior, 48. because he has regarded the lowliness of his handmaid. For behold, from this time all generations shall call me blessed, 49. because he who is mighty has done great things for me, [Col. 0510] and holy is his name. 50. And his mercy is unto ages of ages for those who fear him. 51. He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thought of their hearts. 52. He has brought down the mighty from their seat and exalted the lowly. 53. He has filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich away empty. 54. He has taken up Israel his servant, [Note: [Col. 0509] According to the Greek text: μνησθῆναι, “to remember.”] remembering + mercy, 55. as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.”

56. Now Mary remained with her [Note: [Col. 0509] Before “months,” “about” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] for three months + and returned to her own home. 57. But Elizabeth’s time to give birth was fulfilled, and she [Col. 0510] bore a son. 58. And her neighbors and kinsfolk heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy with her, and they rejoiced with her. 59. And it came to pass on the eighth day that they came to circumcise the child, and they called him Zacharias after his father’s name. 60. But his mother answered and said: “No; rather, he shall be called John.” 61. And they said to her: “There is no one in your kindred who is called by this name.” 62. Then they made signs to his father, asking what he wished him to be called. 63. And he received a writing tablet and wrote, saying: “His name is John.” 64. [Note: [Col. 0509] So also the Greek Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἐλύθη ἡ γλῶσσα αὐτοῦ, “and immediately his tongue was loosed.” The Latin Cantabrigiensis, however, agrees with the Vercellensis.] And immediately his tongue [Col. 0512] was loosed +, and all were astonished. Then his mouth was opened, and he spoke, blessing 65. God. And fear [Note: [Col. 0511] “Great” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: μέγας.] great + came upon all their neighbors; and throughout all the hill country [Note: [Col. 0511] So also the Greek text: ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ὀρεινῇ, “throughout all the hill country.”] + of Judea all these things were spoken abroad, 66. and all who heard them laid them up in their heart, saying: “What indeed will this child be?” For the hand of the Lord is with him.

67. And Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying: 68. “Blessed be the God of Israel, because he has visited and accomplished redemption for his people. 69. And he has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant, [Col. 0512] 70. as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets, who have been from of old: 71. and he has delivered us from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us; 72. to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant, 73. the oath which he swore to Abraham our father, to grant 74. us that, delivered from the hand of our enemies, we might serve 75. him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him all our days. 76. And you, child, shall be called prophet of the Most High; for you shall go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways, [Col. 0514] 77. to give to his people knowledge of salvation in the forgiveness of their sins, 78. through the tender mercies of our God, in which the dawn from on high has visited us, 79. to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, and to direct our feet into the way of peace.”

80. And the child grew and was strengthened in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until his day to Israel.

## CHAPTER II

1. And it came to pass in those days that an edict went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be enrolled . . . . . the first enrollment 2. under Quirinius, governor [Col. 0514] of Syria; and 3. all went to enroll themselves, each to his own city. 4. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David, 5. to enroll himself with Mary, his pregnant wife. 6. And it came to pass while they were there that the days were fulfilled for her to 7. give birth. And she bore her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room in the inn.

8. But [Note: [Col. 0513] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”] + there were shepherds in that region, keeping watch and [Col. 0516] guarding the watches of the night over their flock. 9. And behold, an angel of the Lord stood beside them, and [Note: [Col. 0515] After “glory,” “of God” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] glory + shone around them, and they feared with great fear. 10. And he said to them: “Do not fear; for behold, I announce to you great joy, which shall be for all the people, 11. because there has been born to you today a Savior, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David. 12. And this shall be the sign for you: you shall find an infant wrapped in swaddling cloths and laid in a manger.” 13. And suddenly there was a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying: 14. “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among people [Col. 0516] of good will.”

15. And it came to pass, when the angel departed from them into heaven, that the shepherds spoke to one another and said: “Let us go as far as Bethlehem and see this thing which has happened, which the Lord has thus made known to us.” 16. And they came in haste and found Mary and Joseph and the infant laid in a manger. 17. And they made known the word that had been spoken to them concerning this 18. child. And all who heard wondered [Note: [Col. 0515] Before “concerning these things,” “and” is absent, also in the Greek text.] at these things + which had been told them by the shepherds. 19. But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart. 20. And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising . . . . in all things [Col. 0518] which they had heard and seen, as had been spoken to them.

21. And when eight days were completed for his circumcision, his name was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb. 22. . . . when the days of her purification were fulfilled according to the law of Moses, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, 23. as it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”; 24. and to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

25. And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon; and this man was righteous and devout, [Col. 0518] waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. 26. And [Note: [Col. 0517] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”] he had received + an answer from the Holy Spirit that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. 27. And he came in the Spirit into the temple. And when his parents brought in the child Jesus, to do according to the custom of the l. . . . on his behalf, 28. he too received him into his arms, blessed God, and said:

29. “Now dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace;  
30. for my eyes have seen your salvation,  
31. which you have prepared before the face of all peoples,  
32. a light for the revelation of the eyes, and the glory [Col. 0520] of your people Israel.”

33. And [Note: [Col. 0519] So also the Greek text: Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ, “Joseph and his mother.”] Joseph and his mother + were wondering at the things said 34. concerning him. And Simeon blessed [Note: [Col. 0519] So also the Greek text: αὐτούς, “them.”] them + and said to Mary his mother: “Behold, this one is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that shall be opposed; 35. and a sword shall pierce through your own soul also, so that the thoughts [Note: [Col. 0519] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πολλῶν καρδιῶν, “of many hearts.”] of many hearts + may be revealed.”

[Note: [Col. 0519] After “and,” “there was” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] 36. And + Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher—she had advanced in many days and had lived [Note: [Col. 0519] So also the Greek text: ἔτη, “years.”] years + with her husband seven years from her virginity; 37. and she was a widow [Note: [Col. 0519] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐτῶν, “years [old].”] of eighty-four years +—who did not depart from the temple, serving night and day with fastings [Col. 0520] and observances. 38. And she, standing there at that same hour, gave thanks to the Lord and spoke concerning him to all who were awaiting the redemption of Jerusalem. 39. And when they had completed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own city Nazareth. 40. And the child was strengthened and grew and was filled with wisdom; and the grace of God was with him.

41. And Joseph and Mary went every year to Jerusalem for the solemn day of Passover. 42. And when he was [Note: [Col. 0519] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὡς ἐγένετο αὐτῷ ἔτη, “when he became years old.”] twelve years old +, and they had gone up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast day, [Col. 0522] 43. when the days had been completed and they were returning, the boy Jesus remained in Jerusalem; and [Note: [Col. 0521] So also the Greek text: Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ, “Joseph and his mother.”] Joseph and his mother + did not know it. 44. Thinking that he was in the traveling party, they went a day’s journey and sought him among their relatives and acquaintances. 45. And not finding him, they returned to Jerusalem, [Note: [Col. 0521] So also the Greek text: ζητοῦντες, “seeking.”] seeking + him. 46. And it came to pass, after three days, that they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, listening to them and questioning them. 47. And all who heard him were astonished at his understanding and his answers. 48. And when they saw him, they were amazed. His mother said to him: “Child, why have you done [Col. 0522] this to us? In sorrow we have sought you.” And he said to them: “Why is it that you seek me? 49. [Note: [Col. 0521] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οὐκ οἴδατε, “do you not know?”] Do you not know + that I must be in the things of my Father?” 50. But they did not understand the word that he spoke to 51. them. And he went to Nazareth and was subject to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart. 52. And Jesus advanced in age and wisdom and grace before God and people.

## CHAPTER III

1. Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate was governing Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, Philip his brother tetrarch of Iturea and the region of Trachonitis, [Col. 0524] and Lysanias [Note: [Col. 0523] Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἀβιλλιανῆς; Latin Cantabrigiensis: “Abillianetis.”] tetrarch of Abilene +, 2. under Anna and Caiaphas, the high priest [Note: [Col. 0523] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἀρχιερέως, “high priest.”] +, the word [Note: [Col. 0523] So also the Greek text: Θεοῦ, “of God.”] of God + came upon John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness. 3. And he came into all the region of the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance, 4. as it is written in the book of the words . . . . of the prophet: “A voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight. Every 5. valley shall be filled, and every hill shall be made low; the crooked shall become straight, and the rough places smooth ways; 6. and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

7. Therefore he said to the crowds who came out to be baptized [Note: [Col. 0523] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, “before him.”] before him +: “Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come? [Col. 0524] 8. Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance; and do not begin to say, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham. 9. Now [Note: [Col. 0523] So also the Greek text: δέ, “but/now.”] the axe + has been laid at the root of the trees. Every tree not producing good fruit shall be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

10. And the crowds [Note: [Col. 0523] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐπηρώτησαν, “asked.”] asked + him, saying: [Note: [Col. 0523] After “what,” “therefore” is absent in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] “What + shall we do, that we may live?” 11. He answered them: “Whoever has two tunics, let him give to one who has none; and whoever has food, let him do likewise.” 12. And tax collectors also came to be baptized, and said to him: [Col. 0526] “Teacher, what shall we do?” 13. He said: “Exact nothing more than what has been appointed for you.” 14. [Note: [Col. 0525] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐπηρώτησαν, “asked.”] And soldiers asked + him too, saying: “And what shall we do?” He said to them: “Extort from no one, nor make false accusations; and be content with your wages.”

15. But as the people were expecting, and all were reasoning in their hearts concerning John whether perhaps he was the Christ, 16. John answered and said to all: “I indeed baptize you with water [Note: [Col. 0525] “For repentance” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰς μετάνοιαν.] for repentance +; but one stronger than I is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire. 17. His winnowing fan is [Col. 0526] in his hand, and he has cleansed his threshing floor and gathered the wheat into his storehouse; but he shall burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.” 18. And with many other exhortations he proclaimed good news to [Note: [Col. 0525] So also the Greek text: τὸν λαόν, “the people.”] the people +.

19. But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him concerning Herodias, his brother’s wife, and concerning all the evil things Herod had done, added this above all: he shut John up in prison.

21. And it came to pass, when all the people had been baptized, and Jesus also had been baptized and was praying, that heaven was opened 22. and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form, like a dove; and a voice came from heaven: “You are my [Col. 0528] Son; [Note: [Col. 0527] “I have begotten you today” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε.] I have begotten you today +.”

23. And Jesus himself was beginning to be about . . . . years old, being regarded and said [Note: [Col. 0527] “To be” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἶναι.] to be + 24. the son of Joseph, who was of Heli, who was of Matthew, who was of Levi, who was of Melchi, 25. who was of Janna, who was of Joseph, who was of Naum, who was of Sedi, who was of Magga, 26. who was of Mattathias, who was of Semein, who was of Josech, who was of Joda, who was of Jona, who was of Resa, who was of Zerubbabel, who was of Salathiel, who was of Neri, who was of Melchi, 28. who was of Addi, who was of Cosa, who was of Hermadam, 29. who was of Er, who was of Jesus, who was of Eliezer, who was of Jorim, who was of Matthat, 30. who was of Simeon, who was of Joda, who was of Joseph, 31. who was of Jonah, [Col. 0528] who was of Eliakim, who was of Enan, who was of [Note: [Col. 0527] Greek text: Ματταθά, “Matthat.”] Matthat +, who was of Nathan, who was of 32. David, who was of Jesse, who was of Obed, who was of Boaz, who was of Salmon, who was of Nahshon, 33. who was of Amminadab, who was of Aram, who was of Joaram, who was of Hezron, 34. who was of Perez, who was of Judah, who was of Jacob, who was of Isaac, who was of Abraham, who was of . . . . ., 35. who was of N . . . ., who was of [Note: [Col. 0527] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Σερούκ, “Serug.” See the genealogy of the same Codex Cantabrigiensis, p. 154, col. 1, in the notes; in Mill at this passage.] Serug +, who was of Reu, who was of [Note: [Col. 0527] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Φαλέκ, “Peleg.”] Peleg +, who was of Eber, 36. who was of Salec, who was of Cainan, who was of Arphaxad, who was of Shem, who was of Noah, 37. who was of Lamech, who was of Methuselah, who was of Enoch, who was of Jared, 38. who was of Mahalaleel, who was of Enan, who was of Enosh, who was of Seth, who was of Adam, who was the son of God.

## CHAPTER IV
1. But Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned [Col. 0530] from the Jordan, and was led [Note: [Col. 0529] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, “in the wilderness.”] into the wilderness + for forty days, being tempted by the devil. And he ate nothing during those days; and when those days were completed, he was hungry. 3. Then the devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become 4. bread.” And Jesus answered him, [Note: [Col. 0529] It adds “and said,” as does Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ εἶπεν. Codex Brixianus: “saying.”] and said +: “It is written: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.”

9. And he led him to Jerusalem and set him upon the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down from here; 10. for it is written that he will command his angels concerning you, to keep you, and that they will bear you up in their hands, 11. lest perhaps you strike your foot against a stone.” 12. And Jesus answered and said to him, [Note: [Col. 0529] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: γέγραπται, “it is written.”] “It is written +: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.”

5. And the devil led him, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment 6. of time, and said to him, “I will give you all this authority and their glory, because they have been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I will. 7. Therefore, if you fall down and worship before me, all these things shall be yours.” 8. And Jesus answered and said to him, [Note: [Col. 0529] It adds “Get behind me, Satan,” as does the Greek text, ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ, from Matthew.] “Get behind me, Satan +. For it is written +: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.” 13. And when every temptation was completed, the devil departed from him until an appointed time.

14. And Jesus went forth in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and his fame went out through the whole [Col. 0532] region concerning him. 15. And he himself taught in [Note: [Col. 0531] After “synagogues,” “their” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] synagogues +, and was glorified by all. 16. And he came [Note: [Col. 0531] “Into” is added, as also in the Greek text, εἰς.] into + Nazareth, where he had been brought up; and, according to his custom, he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up 17. to read. And the book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him; and, having unrolled the book, he found the place where it was written:

18. “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; therefore he has anointed me . . . to proclaim the gospel to the poor he has sent 19. me, [Note: [Col. 0531] Before “to proclaim,” “to heal the broken-hearted” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis, as likewise in the Coptic, Ethiopic, and Saxon versions and in the Fathers Origen, Ambrose, and Augustine. Grotius says that it is more probable that the words were added from Isaiah by the translators of the Septuagint than that they were omitted by other copyists.] to proclaim + release to the captives, and sight to the blind; to send forth the oppressed in release; to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of recompense.”

[Col. 0532] 20. And when he had folded the book, he gave it back to the attendant and sat down. And the eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed upon him. 21. Then he began to say to them, “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” 22. And all bore witness to him and marvelled at the words of grace which proceeded from his mouth; and they said, “Is this not Joseph’s son?” 23. And he said to them, “Surely you will say to me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself.’ Whatever we have heard done at Capernaum, do here also in your own country.” 24. And Jesus said, “Amen, I say to you: no prophet is accepted in his own country.”

[Col. 0534] 25. “In truth I say to you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when heaven was shut up for three years and six months, when a great famine occurred throughout all the land; 26. and Elijah was sent to none of them except to Zarephath of Sidon, to a widow. 27. And there were many lepers in Israel under Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.” 28. And all in the synagogue were filled with anger when they heard these things. 29. And they rose up and cast him out of the city; and they led him as far as the brow of the hill upon which their city had been built, in order to throw 30. him down. + But he passed through the midst [Col. 0534] of them and went away.

31. And he went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and there he taught them on the Sabbaths. 32. And they were astonished at his teaching, because his word was with authority. 33. And there was in the synagogue a man who had an unclean demon, and he cried out in a loud voice, saying, 34. “What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come before the time to destroy us? I know who you are: you are the Holy One of God.” 35. And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him.” And when the demon had thrown . . . [him] down, it came out of him, harming him in no way. 36. And great fear [Note: [Col. 0533] “Great” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: μέγας.] great + came upon all, and they spoke with one another, [Col. 0536] saying, “What sort of word is this, that with authority and power he commands unclean spirits, and they come out?” 37. And the report concerning him was spread abroad into every place of that region.

38. Rising [Note: [Col. 0535] After “but,” “Jesus” is absent, as likewise in the Greek text.] from the synagogue +, he entered Simon’s house, [Note: [Col. 0535] “And Andrew’s” is added, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ Ἀνδρέου, from Mark.] and Andrew’s +. Now Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a severe fever, and they asked him 39. concerning her. And standing over her, he commanded the fever, and it left her. And immediately she rose and ministered to them. 40. When the sun had set, all who had sick persons afflicted with severe illnesses brought them to him. And he, laying his hand upon each one, healed them. 41. And many demons [Note: [Col. 0535] “Many” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: πολλά.] many + came out, crying [Col. 0536] and saying, “You are the Son of God.” And rebuking them, he did not allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ. 42. And when day came, he went out to a deserted place; and the crowds sought him and came . . . to him, and held him back, that he should not depart from them. 43. But he said to them, “I must proclaim the kingdom of God to other cities also, because for this I was sent.” 44. And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.

## CHAPTER V

1. And it came to pass, when the crowds pressed upon him to hear the word of God, that he was standing beside the lake [Note: [Col. 0535] So also the Greek text: Γεννησαρέτ, Gennesaret.] of Gennesaret +. 2. And he saw two boats standing [Col. 0538] beside the lake; but the fishermen had gone down from them and were washing their nets. 3. And entering one of the boats, which was Simon’s, he asked him to put out a little from the land. And sitting down, he taught the crowds from the boat. 4. And when he had ceased speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and let down your net for a catch.” 5. And Simon answered and said to him, “Master, though we have laboured all night, we have caught nothing; nevertheless, at your word I will let down the net.” 6. And when they had done this, they enclosed a very great multitude of fish; and their nets were breaking. 7. And they signalled to their partners, who [Col. 0538] were in the other boat, that they should come and help them. + And they filled both boats, so that [Note: [Col. 0537] Before “were sinking,” “almost” is absent, also in the Greek text.] they were sinking +. 8. When [Note: [Col. 0537] After “Simon,” “Peter” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Simon + saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.” 9. For astonishment had seized . . . and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which they had taken; 10. and likewise James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners. And Jesus said to Simon, “Do not fear; from now on you will be catching men alive.” 11. And, having brought the boats to land, they left everything and followed him.

12. And it came to pass, [Col. 0540] while he was in one of the cities, that, behold, there was a man full of leprosy; and he, falling upon his face, begged him, saying, “Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me.” 13. And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying, “I will cleanse.” And immediately his leprosy departed 14. from him; and he commanded him to tell no one, but: “Go, show yourself to the priests, and offer a gift for your cleansing, as Moses commanded . . . [Note: [Col. 0539] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἵνα εἰς μαρτύριον ᾖ ὑμῖν τοῦτο, “that this may be a testimony to you.”] that it may be a testimony . . . to you +.” 15. But the report concerning him spread all the more, and great crowds assembled to hear and to be healed of their infirmities. 16. Yet he withdrew into deserted places and prayed.

17. And it came to pass . . . on one of the days, and he [Note: [Col. 0539] So also the Greek text: ἦν, “was.”] was + [Col. 0540] teaching. And Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was present to heal them. 18. And behold, men carrying on a bed a man who was paralysed sought to bring him in and place him before him. 19. But, finding no way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up upon the roof, [Note: [Col. 0539] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἀποστεγάσαντες τοὺς κεράμους, “and having uncovered the tiles.”] and uncovered the roof +, and lowered him with the bed into the midst before 20. Jesus. When he saw their faith, he said to the man, “Your sins are forgiven you.” 21. And the scribes and Pharisees began to reason [Note: [Col. 0539] “In their hearts” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν.] in their hearts +, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? [Col. 0542] Who can forgive sins except God alone?” 22. But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, [Note: [Col. 0541] Before “said,” “answering” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] said + to them, “Why do you reason in your hearts? 23. Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’? 24. But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralysed man—“I say to you, rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.” 25. And immediately he rose before them, took up the bed on which he had lain, and went to his house, glorifying God. 26. And amazement seized them all, and they glorified God. And they were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen marvellous things [Col. 0542] today.”

27. And after these things Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me.” 28. And leaving everything, he rose and followed him. 29. And he made a great feast for him in his house; and there was a great crowd of tax collectors and others reclining with them. 30. And the Pharisees and their scribes murmured, saying to his disciples, “Why does he eat and drink [Note: [Col. 0541] So also the Ethiopic version: ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει, from Matthew.] eat and drink + with tax collectors and sinners?” 31. And Jesus answered and said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do. 32. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

33. But they said to him, [Col. 0544] “Why do John’s disciples fast frequently and make supplications, as do those of the Pharisees, while your [Note: [Col. 0543] “Disciples” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: μαθηταί.] disciples + eat and drink?” 34. And he said to them, “Can the sons of the bridegroom [Note: [Col. 0543] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος νηστεύειν ἐφ᾽ ὅσον, ‘Can the sons of the bridegroom fast so long as.’] fast, so long as + the bridegroom is with them? 35. But days will come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.” 36. And he also spoke to them this parable: “No one puts a patch from a new garment upon an old garment; otherwise the new one tears, and the patch from the new does not match the old. 37. And no one puts new wine into old skins; otherwise the new wine bursts [Col. 0544] the skins, and it will be spilled, and the skins will perish. 38. But they put new wine into new skins, [Note: [Col. 0543] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: βάλλουσιν, “they put.” In the same place, “both.” I do not know whether this is the fault of the translator or of a scribe; for the Greek text has ἀμφότεροι, “both,” namely ὁ οἶνος, “the wine,” and ὁ ἀσκός, “the skin,” both being masculine nouns.] and both + are preserved.” [Note: [Col. 0543] The whole of verse 39 is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

## CHAPTER VI

1. And it came to pass on a Sabbath, as he was passing through grainfields, [Note: [Col. 0543] According to Codex Cantabrigiensis: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν, “and his disciples began to pluck.”] and the disciples began . . . to pluck + ears of grain and eat them, rubbing them in their hands. 2. But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why do you do what is not lawful on the Sabbaths?” 3. And Jesus answered and said to them, “Have you not even read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him? 4. How he entered the house of God and took the loaves of presentation and ate them, and gave them to those [Col. 0546] who were with him, which it was not [Note: [Col. 0545] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐξὸν ἦν, “it was lawful.”] lawful + to eat except [Note: [Col. 0545] So also the Greek text: μόνους, “only.”] for priests alone +?” 5. And he said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord also of the Sabbath.”

6. And it came to pass on another Sabbath that he entered the synagogue and taught. And there was a man whose right hand was withered. 7. And the scribes and Pharisees watched whether he would heal on the [Note: [Col. 0545] Before “Sabbath,” “on” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Sabbath +, so that they might find how to accuse him. 8. But he, [Note: [Col. 0545] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: γινώσκων, “knowing.”] knowing + their thoughts, [Note: [Col. 0545] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: λέγει, “he says.”] said + to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise and stand [Note: [Col. 0545] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν μέσῳ, “in the midst.”] in the midst +.” And he rose and stood. 9. And Jesus said to them, “I ask . . . is it lawful on the Sabbath . . . to do good, [Col. 0546] or to do evil; to save life, or to destroy it?” 10. And having looked around at [Note: [Col. 0545] “At them” is added, also in the Greek text: αὐτούς. Codices Vercellensis and Brixianus also support it.] them + all, [Note: [Col. 0545] “In anger” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν ὀργῇ, from Mark.] in anger +, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, [Note: [Col. 0545] “Like the other” is added—Brixianus: “like the other [hand]”—as also in the Greek text, ὡς ἡ ἄλλη.] like the other +. 11. But they were filled . . . with . . . madness, and spoke with one another about what they might do to Jesus.

12. And it came to pass in those days that he went out into the mountain to pray, and spent the night in prayer to God. 13. And when day came, he called his disciples to himself and chose twelve from among them, whom he also named apostles: 14. Simon, whom he surnamed Peter, and Andrew his brother, [Col. 0548] [Note: [Col. 0547] Wherever the Veronese, Vercellian, and Brixian codices add “and,” Codex Cantabrigiensis likewise adds καί.] and + John, and James, and Philip, and 15. Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James of Alphaeus +, and Simon who was called the Zealot, 16. and Judas of James, and Judas who became his betrayer.

17. And he came down with them and stood in a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and from across the sea, and from the sea-coast . . . of Tyre 18. and Sidon, who had come to hear him and be healed of their diseases. And those troubled by unclean spirits were healed. 19. And all the crowd sought to touch him, because power went out from him and healed all . . . . . . . . . .

[Col. 0548] 20. And lifting up his eyes toward his disciples, he said: “Blessed are the poor, for yours is the kingdom of God. 21. Blessed are you who now hunger and thirst, for you shall be satisfied. Blessed are you who now weep, for you shall laugh. 22. Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you, and when they cast you out and reproach your name as evil, for the sake of the Son of Man. 23. Rejoice in that day and exult; for behold, your reward is great in heaven. For their fathers did the same things to the prophets.

24. “But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation [Col. 0550]. 25. Woe to you who are full, for you shall hunger. Woe to you who mock, for you shall mourn and weep. 26. Woe to you when all . . . men bless you; for their fathers did the same things [Note: [Col. 0549] “For” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] to the false prophets.

27. “But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies; do good to those who hate 28. you. Bless those [Note: [Col. 0549] So also the Greek text: καταρωμένους, “those cursing.”] who curse + you; [Note: [Col. 0549] Before “pray,” “and” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] pray + for those who slander you. 29. To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer [Note: [Col. 0549] “To him” is added, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic version: αὐτῷ.] to him + the other also. And do not withhold your cloak from him who takes away your tunic. 30. Give to everyone who asks you; and from him who takes away what is yours, do not demand it back. 31. And as you wish people to do to you, [Col. 0550] do likewise to them.

32. “And if you love those who love you, what [Note: [Col. 0549] After “to you,” “is” is absent, also in the Greek text.] grace + is there to you? For sinners also love those who love them. 33. And if you do good to those who do good to you, what grace will there be to you? For sinners also do these things. 34. And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what grace is there to you? Do not sinners also lend to sinners, in order that they may receive [Note: [Col. 0549] After “receive,” “equal things” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] in return +?

35. “But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting [Note: [Col. 0549] *Desperantes*. The Greek text: ἀπελπίζοντες, “expecting nothing in return.”] nothing in return +; and your reward shall be great, and you shall be sons of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and evil. 36. [Note: [Col. 0549] After “be,” “therefore” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic version.] Be + merciful, as your Father has mercy.

[Col. 0552] 37. “Do not judge, and you shall not be judged; do not condemn, and you shall not be condemned. Forgive, and you shall be forgiven. 38. Give, and it shall be given to you: a good measure, [Note: [Col. 0551] The threefold conjunction “and” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] pressed down, shaken together, overflowing +, shall they give into your lap. With the same measure with which you measure, [Note: [Col. 0551] So the Gothic version and St Clement, *Epistle to the Corinthians*: μετρηθήσεται, “it shall be measured.”] it shall be measured + to you.”

39. And he also spoke to them this parable: “Can a blind person guide a blind person? Will not both fall into a pit? 40. A disciple is not above his master; but everyone who is perfected shall be like his master. 41. Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye, but do not consider the beam [Col. 0552] that is in your own eye? 42. Or how can you say to your brother, [Note: [Col. 0551] Before “allow,” “brother” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] ‘Allow + me to remove the speck from your eye,’ [Note: [Col. 0551] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ ὑπόκειται, “and behold, the beam lies in your own eye.”] while behold, a beam lies in your own eye +? Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take out the speck from your brother’s eye.

43. “For there is no . . . good tree which bears bad fruit, nor again a bad tree bearing good fruit. 44. For every tree is known by its own fruit. Nor do they gather [Note: [Col. 0551] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: λέγονται ἐξ ἀκανθῶν, “they gather from thorns.”] from thorns + grapes, nor do they harvest grapes from a bramble. 45. The good person brings forth good from the good treasure of his heart; and the evil [Note: [Col. 0551] After “evil,” “person,” or perhaps “thing,” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] one + [Col. 0554] brings forth evil from the evil treasure. For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth [Note: [Col. 0553] “His” is added, also in the Greek text: αὐτοῦ.] speaks +.

46. “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I say? 47. Everyone who comes to me and hears these words of mine and does them—I will show you to whom he is like. 48. He is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation upon the rock. And when a flood came, the stream struck [Note: [Col. 0553] According to the Greek text: προσέρρηξεν, “struck against.”] against + that house and could not move it, for it was founded upon the rock. 49. But he who hears and does not act is like a man building his house upon sand without a foundation. The stream struck against that house, and immediately it fell, [Col. 0554] and the ruin of that house was . . . great.

## CHAPTER VII

1. [Note: [Col. 0553] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν, “and it came to pass when he had completed.”] And it came to pass, when he had completed + all words in the hearing of the people, that he entered Capernaum. 2. Now a certain centurion’s servant, who was precious to him, was ill and at the point of death. 3. And when he had heard about Jesus, he sent . . . of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant. 4. And they came to Jesus and earnestly entreated him, saying, “He is worthy that you should grant this to him, 5. for he loves our nation and himself built the synagogue for us.” 6. And Jesus went with them. But when he was already not far [Col. 0556] from the house, the centurion sent his friends to him, saying, “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; 7. [Note: [Col. 0555] Before “but say,” the words “therefore I did not consider myself worthy to come to you” are absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] but say + the word, and my servant shall be healed. 8. For I too am a man placed under authority, with soldiers under me; and I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.” 9. When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled; and turning to those who followed him, he said, [Note: [Col. 0555] “Amen” is absent, likewise in the Greek text. Also “in no one.” Thus certain Latin codices formerly read, according to the testimony of St Ambrose.] “I say to you: in no one such great faith . . . in Israel.” 10. And those who had been sent, returning home, [Col. 0556] found the servant well.

11. And it came to pass afterward that he went into a city called Nain; and his disciples went with him, [Note: [Col. 0555] “Many” is added, also in the Greek text: ἱκανοί.] many +, and a great crowd. 12. [Note: [Col. 0555] Thus from Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς ἤγγιζεν, “and it came to pass as he drew near.”] And it came to pass . . . as he drew near + the gate of the city; [Note: [Col. 0555] “And” is added, likewise in the Greek text: καί.] and + behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother; and she was a widow, and a great crowd [Note: [Col. 0555] Before “great,” “of the city” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] great + was with her. 13. And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Do not weep.” 14. And he came near and touched the bier; and those carrying it stood still. And he said, “Young man, I say to you, arise.” 15. And he who had been dead sat up [Col. 0558] and began to speak; and he gave him to his mother. 16. And great fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and, “God has visited his people for good.” 17. And this report [Note: [Col. 0557] So also the Greek text: ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ, “throughout all Judea concerning him, and throughout all the surrounding region.” Codex Vercellensis supports it.] concerning him went out into all Judea and throughout all the surrounding region +.

18. And John’s disciples reported to him concerning all these things. 19. And John summoned two of his disciples . . . to Jesus . . . “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to expect another?” 20. And when the men came to him, they said, “John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or are we to expect another?’” 21. In that hour he healed [Note: [Col. 0557] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐθεράπευε, “he was healing.”] many + of diseases, [Col. 0558] afflictions, and unclean spirits; and to many blind persons he granted sight. 22. And answering, he said to them, “Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the dead are raised, and the poor receive the gospel; 23. and blessed is he who is not offended in me.”

24. And when John’s messengers had departed, he began to speak to the crowds concerning John: “What do you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind? 25. But what do you go out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold, those who are in splendid clothing and luxury are in [Col. 0560] royal houses. 26. But what do you go out to see? A prophet? Certainly, I say to you, and more than a prophet. 27. This is he [Note: [Col. 0559] Codex Veronensis adds “for,” with very many Latin and Greek codices. Lucas Brugensis says it was drawn from Matthew.] for + of whom it is written: ‘Behold . . . messeng . . . before your face, who prepared your way before you.’ 28. But I say to you: no one among those born of women is greater than John the Baptist. For the one who is smaller in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”

29. And all the people hearing, and the tax collectors, . . . justified God, having been baptized with [Note: [Col. 0559] So also the Greek text, τὸ βάπτισμα; Greek syntax.] the baptism + of John. 30. But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected God’s purpose for themselves, not having been baptized.

31. [Note: [Col. 0559] Before “to whom,” “but the Lord said” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] “To whom + then shall I compare the people of this generation? 32. They are like children sitting in the marketplace and speaking to one another, [Note: [Col. 0559] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: λέγοντες, “saying.”] saying +: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament for you, and you did not 33. weep.’ For John the Baptist came neither [Note: [Col. 0559] “Bread [and] wine” are absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] eating nor drinking +, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’ 34. The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’ 35. And wisdom has been justified by all her children.”

36. [Note: [Col. 0559] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἠρώτησεν, “asked.”] A certain Pharisee asked + [Col. 0562] him to eat with him. And he entered . . . the Pharisee’s house and reclined at table. 37. And behold, a woman [Note: [Col. 0561] So also the Greek text: ἐν τῇ πόλει ἥτις ἦν, “in the city, who was.”] in the city, who was + a sinner, when she learned that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster vessel of ointment. 38. And standing behind him at his feet, she [Note: [Col. 0561] Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔβρεξεν, “she wetted.”] wet + his feet . . . and wiped them with the hair of her head, and kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment. 39. But the Pharisee who had invited him, seeing this, said within himself: “If this man were a prophet, he would surely know who and what sort of woman it is who touches him, because she is a sinner.”

40. And Jesus answered and said [Col. 0562] to him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” And he said, “Teacher, say it.” [Note: [Col. 0561] Codex Cantabrigiensis adds ὁ δὲ εἶπεν, “and he said.”] Jesus therefore said +: 41. “There were two debtors to a certain moneylender: the one owed five hundred denarii, the other fifty. 42. Since they had nothing [Note: [Col. 0561] “But” is added, also in the Greek text: δέ.] but + with which to repay, he freely forgave them both. Which of them, then, loved him more?” 43. Simon answered and said, “I suppose the one to whom he forgave more.” And he said to him, “You have judged rightly.” 44. And turning toward the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house: you gave me no water for my feet; but she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. 45. You gave me no kiss; [Col. 0564] but from the time I came in, she has not ceased to kiss my feet. 46. You did not anoint my head with oil; but she anointed [Note: [Col. 0563] After “anointed,” the words “my feet” are absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and other witnesses in Mill.] + with ointment. 47. Therefore I say to you, her many sins have been forgiven her, because she loved much. But the one to whom less is forgiven loves less.” 48. And Jesus said to her, “Woman, your sins are forgiven.” 49. And those reclining at table with him began to say within themselves, “Who is this, who even forgives sins?” 50. And Jesus said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

## CHAPTER VIII
1. And it came to pass afterward that he himself was making his way through cities and villages, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God; and the Twelve disciples were with him, 2. and women who had been healed of unclean spirits and infirmities: Mary, who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out; 3. Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others, who ministered to him from their own resources.

4. When therefore a crowd had gathered, and people were coming to him from the cities [Note: [Col. 0563] The Greek text has, “as they were coming to him,” ἐπιπορευομένου.], he spoke to them this parable [Note: [Col. 0563] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: παραβολὴν τοιαύτην πρὸς αὐτούς.]: 5. “Behold, the sower went out to sow his seed. And while he sowed, some fell beside the road; it was trampled down, and the birds [Note: [Col. 0563] After “birds,” “of heaven” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] devoured it. 6. And other seed fell upon the ground; when it sprang up, it withered, because it had no moisture. 7. And other seed fell among thorns; and the thorns, springing up with it, choked it. 8. And other seed fell into good soil; when it sprang up, it produced fruit a hundredfold.” Saying these things, he cried aloud, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

9. His disciples asked him what this parable meant. 10. He said to them, “To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to the rest I speak in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand. 11. Now the parable is this: the seed is the word of God. 12. Those sown beside the road are those who hear the word of God; but the devil comes and takes away … from their … the word, lest, believing, they should be saved. 13. Those upon the rock are those who, when they have heard the word, receive it with joy; yet these have no roots, because they believe for a time, and in a time of temptation fall away. 14. That which fell among thorns: these are those who hear, but as they go their way they are choked by cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bear no fruit. 15. But that in the good soil: these are those who, hearing the word in a good heart [Note: [Col. 0565] After “good,” “and upright” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.], retain it and bear fruit with endurance.

16. “No one lights a lamp and puts it under a measuring-basket, but puts it on a lampstand, so that those entering may see the light. 17. For nothing is hidden that shall not be made manifest, nor concealed except that it may be known and come into public view. 18. Take heed, therefore, how you hear. For whoever has, to him shall be given; and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has shall be taken away from him.”

19. His mother and his brothers came to him, but could not approach him because of … It was reported … to him: 20. [Note: [Col. 0567] Adds “because,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis, ὅτι.] “Because your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wishing to see you.” 21. Answering, he said to them, “My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.”

22. Now it came to pass on one of those days that he entered a boat with his disciples, and he said to them, “Let us cross over the lake.” And they put out [Note: [Col. 0567] In accordance with the Greek text, ἀνήχθησαν.]. 23. While they were sailing, he fell asleep; and a windstorm came down upon the lake, and the boat was filling with waves [Note: [Col. 0567] In accordance with Colbertinus 2, cited here by Mill: συνεπληροῦτο … τὸ πλοῖον.], and they were in danger. 24. They came and woke him, saying, “Master, we are perishing!” But he arose and commanded the wind and the storm of the water; and they ceased [Note: [Col. 0567] So also the Greek text, ἐπαύσαντο.], and there was a calm, a great calm [Note: [Col. 0567] Adds “great,” from Matthew or Mark.]. 25. He said to them, “Where is your faith?” And being afraid, they marvelled and said to one another, “Who is this, that he commands even the sea and the winds, and they obey his command?”

26. They sailed to the country of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee. 27. And when he had gone ashore, a certain man from the city met him [Note: [Col. 0569] Adds “from the city,” also the Greek text, ἐκ τῆς πόλεως.] … who had had a demon for many times, wore no clothing, and did not live in a house but among the tombs. 28. When he saw Jesus, he fell before him and cried out with a loud voice, “What have I to do with you, Jesus [Note: [Col. 0569] Before “Jesus,” “is” is absent, also in the Greek text.] Son of God Most High? I beg you, do not torment me.” 29. For he commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For many times it had seized him; and indeed [Note: [Col. 0569] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, γάρ.] he was kept bound with chains and fetters, but breaking the bonds, he was driven by the demon into desert places.

30. Jesus asked him [Note: [Col. 0569] After “Jesus,” “saying” is absent also in the Gothic version.], “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” because we are many [Note: [Col. 0569] Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὅτι πολλὰ ἦσαν.]. 31. And they begged him not to command them to go into the abyss. 32.
