Now by day he was teaching in the temple; but by night he went out and lodged on the mountain called Olivet. 38. And all the people came early in the morning [Col. 0688] to the temple to hear him.

## CHAPTER XXII

1. [Note: [Col. 0687] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἤγγισεν, “drew near.”] Now the day of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, drew near. + 2. And the chief priests and scribes sought how [Note: [Col. 0687] Thus from the Greek text: αὐτόν, “him.”] they might kill him, + but they feared the people. 3. But Satan entered into Judas, who was surnamed [Note: [Col. 0687] Origen reads, like the Vercelli codex, Ἰσκαριώθ; and so the Latin Cantabrigiensis, *Iscarioth*. But the Greek Cantabrigiensis has Ἰσκαριώδ.] Scarioth, + one of the Twelve. 4. And he went away and spoke with the chief priests and scribes about how . . . . . he might betray him to them. 5. And they agreed to give him money. 6. And he sought an opportunity to betray him [Note: [Col. 0687] So also the Greek text: αὐτοῖς ἄτερ ὄχλου, “to them without a crowd.” The Vercelli and Brescia codices also support this.] to them without a crowd. + 7. Now the day [Col. 0688] of [Note: [Col. 0687] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τοῦ πάσχα, “of the Passover.”] Passover + came, on which it was necessary for the 8. Passover to be killed; and he sent Peter and John . . . . . . . “Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat it.” 9. But they said to him: “Where do you wish us to prepare it?” 10. And he said to them: “Behold, when you enter the city, a man [Note: [Col. 0687] After *man*, *a certain* is absent also in the Greek text.] + carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house into which he enters; 11. and say to the master of the house: ‘The Teacher says to you: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’ 12. And he will show you [Note: [Col. 0687] Greek text: ἀνώγεον μέγα, “a large upper room.” For μέγα Codex Cantabrigiensis reads οἶκον, “house”; the Latin Cantabrigiensis: *superiorem domum*, “upper house”; ἐστρωμένον, “furnished.”] a large furnished upper room +; prepare it there.” [Col. 0690] 13. And they went and found it as he had told them, and prepared the Passover. 14. And when the hour had come, he reclined at table, and the apostles with him. 15. And he said to them: “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. 16. For I tell you that from now on I shall not eat it until . . . . . . . . in the kingdom of God.” 19. And, having taken bread, he gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, 17. saying: “This is [Note: [Col. 0689] After *my body*, “which is given for you,” etc., through verse 21, is absent likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] my body.” + And, having taken the cup, he gave thanks and said: [Col. 0690] “Take [Note: [Col. 0689] *This* is added; so also the Greek text, τοῦτο.] this + and divide it among yourselves. 18. For I tell you that I shall not drink [Note: [Col. 0689] The Greek text has ἀπὸ τοῦ γεννήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου, “of the fruit of the vine.” Elsewhere too, Veronensis frequently renders the articles.] of this fruit of the vine + until the kingdom of God comes. 21. Nevertheless, behold, the hand of him who betrays me is [Note: [Col. 0689] After *with me*, *is* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] with me + at 22. the table. And indeed the Son of Man goes according as it is written; nevertheless, woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed.” 23. And they began to inquire among themselves who [Note: [Col. 0689] After *was*, *of them* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] it was + who would do this. 24. And there arose a dispute among them [Col. 0692] as to which of them [Note: [Col. 0691] After *which*, *of them* is not found also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] + was considered greatest. 25. But he said to them: “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors. 26. But you are not so; rather, let the greater among you become like [Note: [Col. 0691] So also the Greek text: ὁ νεώτερος, “the younger.”] the younger, + and the one who leads like one who serves. 27. For which is greater, the one who reclines at table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves. 28. You are those who have remained with me in temptation . . . . 29. to him . . . . I appoint for you, as my Father appointed a kingdom for me, 30. that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom; and [Note: [Col. 0691] Codex Alexandrinus has καθήσεσθε, as do all Stephanus’s manuscripts. Many others read καθίσεσθε. In the same place, *on twelve seats*, as Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐπὶ δώδεκα θρόνους, “upon twelve thrones,” and many others in Mill.] you shall sit on twelve seats +, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. 31. And the Lord said: “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan . . . . . . . asked, that . . . . . sift you like wheat. 32. But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers; and pray that you may not enter into temptation.” 33. But . . . . . . . Peter said: “Lord, with you [Col. 0694] I am ready to go both to prison and to death.” 34. And he said: “I tell you, Peter, the cock will not crow today until you have denied me three times.” 35. And he said to them: “When I sent you without purse, bag, and sandals, did you lack [Note: [Col. 0693] In accordance with the Greek text: τίνος ὑστερήσατε, “what did you lack?”] anything +?” And they said: “Nothing.” 36. Therefore he said: “But now, let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag; and let the one who does not have one sell his garment and buy a sword. 37. For I tell you that [Note: [Col. 0693] Before *which*, *still* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] that + which is written must be fulfilled in me: ‘And he was [Note: [Col. 0693] So also the Syriac, Persian, and Arabic versions.] numbered + among transgressors.’ [Note: [Col. 0693] So also the Greek text: τὸ περὶ ἐμοῦ, “that concerning me.”] For that which concerns me also . . . . . . . has an end . . . .” 38. And they said to him: “Lord, [Col. 0694] behold, here are two swords.” And he said to them: “It is enough.” 39. And going out, he went, according to his custom, to the Mount of Olives. And his disciples followed him. [Note: [Col. 0693] *His* is added, as also in the Greek text, αὐτοῦ.] + 40. And when he came to the place, he said to them: “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.” 41. And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, and kneeling down, he prayed: 42. “Father, if you will, remove this cup from me; nevertheless, not my will, but yours be done.” 43. And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him. And being in agony, he prayed more earnestly; 44. and his sweat became like drops of blood running down to the ground. [Col. 0696] 45. And when he rose from prayer and came to his disciples, he found them sleeping because of sorrow. 46. And he said to them: “Why do you sleep? Rise and pray, that you may not enter into temptation.” 47. While he was still speaking, [Note: [Col. 0695] *But* is added, as also in the Greek text, δέ.] behold, a crowd; and he who was called Judas, one of the Twelve, went before them. [Note: [Col. 0695] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ἐγγίσας ἐφίλησε τὸν Ἰησοῦν, “and approaching, he kissed Jesus.” For he had given them this sign: Ὅν ἂν φιλήσω, αὐτός ἐστιν, “Whomever I shall kiss, he is the one” (*seize him* is absent). These words may perhaps have been annotated in the margin from the earlier Evangelists, and at length crept into the text of the Cantabrigiensis and Veronensis codices.] And approaching, he kissed Jesus; for he had given them this sign . . . . . . . saying: “Whomever I shall kiss, he is the one; seize him.” + 48. But Jesus said to him: “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?” 49. When those who were about [Col. 0696] him saw this, they said to him: “Lord, do you wish us to strike him with 50. the sword?” And one of them struck the servant of the chief priest and cut off his right ear. 51. But Jesus answered and said: “Let him be, up to this point.” And he touched his ear and healed him. 52. And Jesus said: “Enough of this.” And to those who had come against him—to the chief priests, officers of the temple, and elders—he said: “Have you come out with swords and clubs as against a robber? 53. When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not stretch out your hands against me; but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”

54. And having seized [Col. 0698] him, they led him into the house of the chief priest. But Peter followed him [Note: [Col. 0697] *Him* is added, as also in Codex Cantabrigiensis, αὐτῷ; Brescia: *eum*, “him.”] + at a distance. 55. And when a fire had been kindled in the middle of the courtyard and they had sat down together, [Note: [Col. 0697] So also the Greek text, ἐκάθητο καί, “he was sitting also,” with *they* omitted after *having sat down*; it is absent likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Peter also sat + among them. 56. When a maidservant saw him sitting by the light, she looked intently at him and said: “This man too is one of those who were always with him.” 57. But he [Note: [Col. 0697] After *denied*, *him* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] denied [him] +, saying: “Woman, I do not know him.” 58. And again, after a little while, another saw him and said: “Man, you too were always with . . . . . . . .” But he answered: “I am not.” 59. And after an interval [Col. 0698] of about one hour, another insisted, saying: “Truly this man also was with him, for he too is a Galilean.” 60. And Peter said: “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” And immediately, while he was still speaking, the cock crowed. 61. And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, as [Note: [Col. 0697] So also the Greek text: εἶπεν αὐτῷ, “he said to him.”] he had said to him: + “Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times [Note: [Col. 0697] *Today* is also added by the Coptic, Arabic, Ethiopic, and Saxon versions: σήμερον. The Cantabrigiensis codices and another Greek manuscript cited by Mill add “not to know me,” μὴ εἰδέναι με. Brescia: *te scire*, “to know you.”] today, saying that you do not know me.” + 63. And the men who held him mocked him, saying: “Prophesy to us: who is it that 65. struck you?” And [Col. 0700] uttering many other blasphemies, they spoke against him. 66. And when day came, [Note: [Col. 0699] So also the Greek text: τὸ πρεσβυτέριον, “the council of elders.”] the council of elders + of the people, chief priests, and scribes assembled; and they led him into their council and questioned him, saying: “If you are the Christ, tell us.” 67. He said to them: “If I tell you, you will not [Note: [Col. 0699] After *believe*, *me* is absent also in the Greek text. In the same place, after *if*, *but also* is absent in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] believe +; 68. and if I question you, you will not answer me or release me. 69. But from now on the Son of Man shall be seated at the right hand of the power of God.” 70. And they all said: “Then are you the Son of God?” But he said [Note: [Col. 0699] *To them* is added, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis, αὐτοῖς.] to them: + “You say that I am.” 71. But they said: “Why do we still [Col. 0700] require testimony? For [Note: [Col. 0699] Before *we heard*, *we ourselves* is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] we heard + it from his own mouth.”

## CHAPTER XXIII
1. And the whole multitude of them rose up and led him to Pilate.  
2. They began to accuse him, saying: “We found this man subverting our nation,

> [Note: Col. 0699] It adds, “and abolishing our Law and the Prophets,” with Marcion’s Catholic codex, καὶ καταλύοντα τὸν νόμον καὶ προφήτας.

and abolishing our Law and the Prophets [+], forbidding tribute to be paid to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king.”  
3. Pilate, hearing this, questioned him, saying: “Are you the King of the Jews?” He replied: “You say so.”  
4. Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds: “I find no charge in this man.”  
5. But they persisted, saying: “He stirs up the people [+], teaching throughout all Judaea, beginning from Galilee as far as this place.”

> [Note: Col. 0701] After *the people*, *teaching* is absent, also in Usser. 2, in Mill.

6. Pilate, hearing “Galilee,” asked whether the man was a Galilaean.  
7. And when he learned that he was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was in Jerusalem in those days.  
8. When Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly glad; for he had desired to see him for a long time, because he had heard much concerning him, and he hoped to see some sign performed by him.  
9. He questioned him with many words; but he answered him nothing.  
10. The chief priests and scribes also stood there, vigorously accusing him.  
11. Herod, with his soldiers [+], despised him and mocked him; and, having clothed him in a white garment [+], sent him [+] back to Pilate.

> [Note: Col. 0701] Thus also the Greek text: στρατεύμασιν, “soldiers.”
>
> [Note: Col. 0701] (c) It adds *him* twice, as also the Greek text: αὐτόν.

12. On that very day Herod and Pilate became friends; for previously they had been enemies of one another.  
13. Pilate, having summoned the chief priests and the rulers  
14. of the people, said to them: “You brought this man before me as one who turns the people away; and behold, having examined him in your presence, I find in this man no charge of those on which you accuse him.  
15. Nor did Herod; for I sent you to him, and behold, nothing deserving death has been done by him.  
16. Therefore I shall punish him and release him.  
17. Now he was obliged, according to custom, to release one to them.  
18. But the whole crowd cried out together, saying: “Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us”—  
19. a man who had been put in prison for a certain insurrection made in the city, and for murder.  
20. Pilate again spoke to them, wishing to release  
21. Jesus. But they cried out in response, saying: “Crucify him!”  
22. He said to them a third time: “Why, what evil has this man done? I find in him no cause of death. Therefore I shall chastise him and release him.”  
23. But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that he be crucified; and their voices prevailed.  
24. And Pilate decreed that their request should be carried out.  
25. He released to them the man who had been put in prison for murder and insurrection; but Jesus he delivered over to their will.  
26. And as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, coming in from the country, and laid the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus.  
27. A multitude of people [+] followed him, and of women, who bewailed and lamented him.

> [Note: Col. 0703] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πλῆθος λαοῦ, “a multitude of people.” Vercelli: “a great multitude of people.”

28. But Jesus, turning toward them, said: “Daughters of Israel, be silent; do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and your children [+].

> [Note: Col. 0705] The word *for* is absent three times, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

29. For behold, days are coming in which they will say: ‘Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nurse.’  
30. Then they will begin to say to the mountains: ‘Fall upon us’; and to the hills: ‘Cover us.’  
31. For if these things are done in the green wood, what will be done in the dry?”  
32. And two other criminals were led with him to be crucified.  
33. And when they came to the place called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the two criminals, one on the right and the other on the left. They also divided [+] his garments and cast a lot [+].

> [Note: Col. 0705] Before *dividing*, the words “But Jesus was saying, ‘Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing’” are absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
>
> [Note: Col. 0705] Thus also the Greek text: κλῆρον, “a lot.”

35. And the people stood watching. The rulers mocked him, saying: “He saved others; let him now save himself, if he is the Christ of God, the chosen one.”  
36. The soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him vinegar [+],  
37. saying: “If you are the King of the Jews, … save yourself.”  
38. And there was an inscription written over him in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew letters: “This is the King of the Jews.”

> [Note: Col. 0705] Thus also the Greek text: προσέφερον, “they were offering.” Likewise, after *to him*, *and* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

39. One of the criminals hanging there also reviled him, saying: “Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us.”  
40. But the other answered and rebuked him, saying: “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same condemnation?  
41. And indeed we suffer these things justly, for we receive what our deeds deserve; but this man has done nothing evil.”  
42. And he said to Jesus: “Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”  
43. And Jesus said to him: “Amen, I tell you: today you will be with me in Paradise.”  
44. And it was about the sixth hour of the day, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.  
45. The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in the middle.  
46. Jesus cried out with a loud voice [*supply: said*]: “Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.” And having said this, he gave up his spirit.

> [Note: Col. 0707] Supply *said*.

47. The centurion, seeing what had happened, glorified God, saying: “Truly this man was righteous.”  
48. And the whole crowd … assembled together at this spectacle, seeing [+] what was taking place, beat their breasts and returned.

> [Note: Col. 0707] Greek text: θεωροῦντες, “watching.”

49. But all his acquaintances stood at a distance, together with the women who had followed him from Galilee, seeing these things.  
50. And behold, there was a man named Joseph, a councillor, a good man [+],  
51. and righteous—he had not consented to their counsel and actions—from the city of Arimathaea [+] in Judaea, who was awaiting the kingdom [+] of God.

> [Note: Col. 0707] Before *good*, *man* is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
>
> [Note: Col. 0707] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἀριμαθίας.
>
> [Note: Col. 0709] Before *kingdom*, *he himself also* is absent in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

52. This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.  
53. Having taken it down, he wrapped it [+] in a new linen cloth, and laid him in a rock-hewn tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.

> [Note: Col. 0709] It adds *it*, as also the Greek text: αὐτό.
>
> [Note: Col. 0709] It adds *in*, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν.

54. And it was the day of the pure preparation, and the sabbath was dawning.  
55. The two women [+] who had come with him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb, and how his body had been laid.  
56. And returning, they prepared spices and ointments; but on the sabbath they kept silence according to the commandment.

> [Note: Col. 0709] It adds *two*, also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δύο.

## Chapter XXIV

1. But on the first day of the week, very early, they came to the tomb carrying what they had prepared, and found the stone rolled away.

> [Note: Col. 0709] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”
>
> [Note: Col. 0709] After *body*, “of the Lord Jesus” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

> [Note: Col. 0709] After *dead*, “He is not here, but has risen” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

> [Note: Col. 0711] Thus also the Greek text: ἀπίστουν, “they did not believe.”
>
> [Note: Col. 0711] The entire verse 12 is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

> [Note: Col. 0711] It adds *in*, as also the Greek text: ἐν.
>
> [Note: Col. 0711] Thus also the Greek text: ἀπέχουσαν, “being distant.”
>

14. And they were discussing all these things that had happened.

> [Note: Col. 0711] Before *answered*, *and* is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

19. He said to them: “What things?” And they said: “Those concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet, mighty in deed and word before God and all the people;

> [Note: Col. 0713] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πῶς τοῦτον, “how him.”

> [Note: Col. 0713] Thus also the Greek text: ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι, “the one who was about to redeem.”

> [Note: Col. 0715] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πρὸς ἑσπέραν κέκλικεν ἡ ἡμέρα, “the day has declined toward evening.” ἤδη, “already,” is added in Barb. 1 and in the Vulgate.
>
> [Note: Col. 0715] Thus also the Greek text: τοῦ μεῖναι, “to remain.” Vercelli has “that he might remain with them”; Brixianus, “that he might remain.”

> [Note: Col. 0715] Thus also the Greek text: ἄφαντος ἐγένετο, “he became unseen.”

37. But they were troubled and terrified, thinking that they saw a spirit.

> [Note: Col. 0715] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”
>
> [Note: Col. 0715] It adds *why*, as also the Greek text: διατί.

> [Note: Col. 0715] It adds *my*, as also the Greek text: μου.
>
> [Note: Col. 0717] Verse 40 is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

41. But while they still did not believe for joy and were wondering, he said: “Do you have anything here to eat?”

43. a portion of honeycomb [+]. And, having eaten before them, he said to them:

> [Note: Col. 0717] Thus also the Greek text: ἀπὸ μελίσσου, “of honeycomb.”

46. And he said to them: “For thus it is written [+]: that the Christ should suffer and rise from the dead,

> [Note: Col. 0717] After *is written*, “and thus it was necessary” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis; Saint Irenaeus also appears not to have read it.

47. and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name among every nation, beginning from Jerusalem.  
48. But you are witnesses of these things.  
49. And behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you; but remain in the city until you are clothed with power [+] from on high.

> [Note: Col. 0717] Thus also the Greek text: δύναμιν, “power.”

50. And he led them out as far as Bethany; and, lifting up his hands, he blessed them [+].

> [Note: Col. 0717] Thus also the Greek text: αὐτούς, “them.”

51. And it came to pass, while he was blessing them, that he departed from them [+].

> [Note: Col. 0717] After *from them*, “and was carried up into heaven” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

52. And they returned [+] to Jerusalem with great joy.

> [Note: Col. 0717] Before *returned*, “worshipping him” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

53. And they were continually in the temple, praising [+].

> [Note: Col. 0719] (a) After *praising*, “and blessing God. Amen” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. The *Amen* is not read in most ancient manuscript codices. Some consider it an addition by the Church, which customarily concluded the Gospel narrative with this acclamation.

> [Note: Col. 0719] (b) Thus Codex Cantabrigiensis also: Ἐυαγγέλιον κατὰ Λουκᾶν ἐπληρώθη, ἄρχεται κατὰ Μάρκον: “The Gospel according to Luke is completed; that according to Mark begins.”

**The Gospel according to Luke ends. The Gospel according to Mark begins [+].**

## Codex Brixianus

[Col. 0501]

Since many have undertaken to arrange an account of the events fulfilled among us, just as those who from the beginning were themselves eyewitnesses and ministers of the word delivered them to us, it seemed good also to me, having followed everything carefully from the beginning, to write to you in orderly sequence, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the truth concerning the words in which you have been instructed.

> [Note: Col. 0501] According to Greek syntax, πᾶσιν, “all things.”

In the days of Herod, king of Judaea, there was a certain priest named Zacharias, of the division of Abijah; and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.  
[Col. 0502] Both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord. But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in years.

Now it came to pass, while Zacharias was performing the priestly office before God in the order of his division, according to the custom of the priesthood, that the lot fell to him to offer incense after entering the temple of the Lord. And all the multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of incense. An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. And when Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.

[Col. 0503] But the angel said to him: “Do not fear, Zacharias, because your prayer has been heard; and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John. And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth. For he will be great before the Lord; he will drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb. And he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God. And he himself will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to children, and the uninstructed to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a perfected people.”

And Zacharias said to the angel: [Col. 0504] “How shall I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in years.” The angel answered him: “I am Gabriel, who stand in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you and bring you these good tidings. And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things take place, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their proper time.”

Now the people were waiting for Zacharias, and wondered that he delayed in the temple. When he came out, he could not speak to them; and they perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple. He continued making signs to them and remained mute.

[Col. 0505] And when the days of his service were completed, he went home. After these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and hid herself for five months, saying: “Thus the Lord has dealt with me in the days when he looked upon me, to take away my reproach among people.”

But in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary. The angel entered to her and said: “Hail, full of grace; the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women.” But when she saw him, she was troubled at his word [Col. 0506] and considered what sort of greeting this was, that he had so blessed her.

And the angel said to her: “Do not fear, Mary, for you have found grace with God; and [+] behold, you will conceive in the womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.

> [Note: Col. 0505] It adds *and*, as also the Greek text: καί.

He will be great, and will be called Son of the Most High; and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.”

Mary said to the angel: “How will this be, since I do not know a man?” The angel answered her: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also that which will be born [+] will be called holy, the Son of God.

> [Note: Col. 0505] After *will be born*, *from you* is absent, also in the Greek text.

[Col. 0507] And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman has herself also conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month for her who is called barren, because no word is impossible with God.” Mary said: “Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; let it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.

Mary arose in those days and went with haste into the hill country, to a city of Judaea. She entered the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth. And it came to pass, when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, that the child leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. [Col. 0508] She cried out with a loud voice and said: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And why has this been granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the child in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed are you who believed, because the things spoken to you by the Lord will be fulfilled.”

And Mary said: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior, because he has regarded the lowliness of his handmaid. For behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed, because he who is mighty [Col. 0509] has done great things for me, and holy is his name. His mercy is from generation to generation upon those who fear him. He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts. He has brought down the mighty from thrones and exalted the lowly. He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty. He has protected Israel his servant, remembering [+] his mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his seed forever.”

> [Note: Col. 0509] According to the Greek text: μνησθῆναι, “to remember.”

Mary remained with her about three months and returned to her own house. Elizabeth’s time to give birth was fulfilled, [Col. 0510] and she bore a son. Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy with her, and they rejoiced with her.

On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child and called him Zacharias, after his father’s name. But his mother answered: “No; rather, he shall be called John.” They said to her: “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.” Then they made signs to his father, asking what he wished him to be called. And asking for a writing tablet, he wrote: “His name is John.”

[Col. 0511] And all wondered. Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue released, and he spoke, blessing God. Fear came upon all their neighbors, and throughout all the hill country [+] of Judaea all these words were spread abroad. All who heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying: “What, then, will this child be?” For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him.

> [Note: Col. 0511] Thus also the Greek text: ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ὀρεινῇ, “throughout all the hill country.”

And Zacharias his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, because he has visited and wrought redemption for his people. He has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant, [Col. 0512] as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old: salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us; to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant, the oath that he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us that, delivered from the hand of our enemies, we might serve him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.

“And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways, [Col. 0513] to give knowledge of salvation to his people in the forgiveness of their sins, through the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high has visited us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”

And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and was in the deserts until the day of his manifestation to Israel.

Now in those days an edict went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be enrolled. This was the first enrollment, when Quirinius was governor of Syria. And all went to be enrolled, [Col. 0514] each to his own city. Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and lineage of David, to be enrolled with Mary, his betrothed, who was pregnant.

And while they were there, the days were fulfilled for her to give birth. And she bore her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging.

But [+] shepherds were in the same region, keeping watch and guarding the watches of the night over their flock.

> [Note: Col. 0513] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: δέ, “but.”

[Col. 0515] And behold, an angel of the Lord stood beside them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they feared with great fear. The angel said to them: “Do not fear; for behold, I proclaim to you great joy, which will be for all the people, because today in the city of David there has been born to you a Savior, who is Christ the Lord. And this will be a sign to you: you will find an infant wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”

And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to people of good will.”

When the angels departed from [Col. 0516] them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another: “Let us go as far as Bethlehem and see this thing which has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.” And they came in haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger. On seeing, they learned concerning the saying that had been spoken to them about the child. And all who heard wondered at the things [+] spoken to them by the shepherds.

> [Note: Col. 0515] Before *concerning the things*, *and* is absent, also in the Greek text.

But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart. And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, [Col. 0517] as it had been spoken to them.

When eight days were completed for his circumcision, his name was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb. And when the days of her purification according to the Law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord, as it is written in the Law of the Lord: “Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”; and to offer a sacrifice for him to the Lord, according to what is said in the Law of the Lord: “a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.”

And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem named [Col. 0518] Simeon; and this man was righteous and devout, awaiting the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. He had received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. And he came in the Spirit into the temple. When his parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him according to the custom of the Law, he took him into his arms and blessed God, saying: “Now you dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared before all peoples: a light for revelation to the nations and glory to your people Israel.”

[Col. 0519] Joseph and his mother [+] were wondering at the things said concerning him.

> [Note: Col. 0519] Thus also the Greek text: Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ, “Joseph and his mother.”

Simeon blessed them [+] and said to Mary his mother: “Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that will be opposed. And a sword will pierce through your own soul also, so that thoughts from many hearts may be revealed.”

> [Note: Col. 0519] Thus also the Greek text: αὐτούς, “them.”

And there was Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in many days, having lived with her husband seven years from her virginity. She had been a widow up to eighty-four years, and did not depart from the temple, serving [Col. 0520] with fastings and supplications night and day. At that very hour she stood and gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of him to all who were awaiting the redemption of Jerusalem.

When they had completed everything according to the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own city Nazareth. And the child grew and became strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom; and the grace of God was upon him.

His parents went every year to Jerusalem for the feast day of Passover. When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast. [Col. 0521] When the days were completed and they were returning, the child Jesus remained in Jerusalem; and Joseph and his mother [+] did not know it, supposing him to be in the traveling company. They went a day’s journey and sought him among relatives and acquaintances. When they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem seeking him.

> [Note: Col. 0521] Thus also the Greek text: Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ, “Joseph and his mother.”

And it came to pass after three days that they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, listening to them and questioning them. All who heard him were astonished at his understanding and his answers. And when they saw him, they were amazed.

His mother said to him: “Child, why have you done this to us? Behold, your father and I have been seeking you in distress.” [Col. 0522] And he said to them: “Why were you seeking me? Do you not know [+] that I must be in the things of my Father?”

> [Note: Col. 0521] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οὐκ οἴδατε, “do you not know?”

But they did not understand the word that he spoke to them. And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them. But his mother kept all these words in her heart. And Jesus advanced in wisdom, age, and favor with God and people.

Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate governed Judaea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother tetrarch of Ituraea and the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene [+], under the chief priests Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God [+] came to John, son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.

> [Note: Col. 0523] Codex Cantabrigiensis: Ἀβιλλιανῆς; Latin Cantabrigiensis: *Abillianetis*.
>
> [Note: Col. 0523] Thus also the Greek text: Θεοῦ, “of God.”

And he came into all the region of the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins, as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet:

“A voice crying in the wilderness:  
Prepare the way of the Lord;  
make his paths straight.  
Every valley shall be filled,  
and every mountain and hill brought low;  
the crooked shall become straight,  
and the rough places smooth ways;  
and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

He said therefore to the crowds coming to be baptized by him: “Brood of vipers, [Col. 0524] who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come? Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say within yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you, God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham. Even now the axe is laid at the roots of the trees. Therefore every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire.”

The crowds questioned him, saying: “What then shall we do?” He answered them: “Whoever has two tunics, let him give to one who has none; and whoever has food, let him do likewise.” Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him: “Teacher, [Col. 0525] what shall we do?” He said to them: “Exact nothing beyond what has been appointed for you.” Soldiers also questioned him, saying: “And what shall we do?” He said to them: “Extort no one, make no false accusation, and be content with your pay.”

While the people were expecting, and all were reasoning in their hearts concerning John whether perhaps he himself was the Christ, John answered all of them, saying: “I indeed baptize you with water; but one stronger than I is coming, whose sandal-strap I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.”

[Col. 0526] “He has a winnowing fan in his hand, and he will cleanse his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.” With many other exhortations also he proclaimed good news to the people.

But Herod the tetrarch, when he was reproved by him concerning Herodias, his brother’s wife, and concerning all the evil things that Herod had done, added this also above all: he shut John up in prison.

Now when all the people had been baptized, and Jesus also having been baptized and praying, heaven was opened; and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven, saying: “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

[Col. 0527] And Jesus himself was about thirty years old, being, as was supposed, the son of Joseph:

1. son of Heli, son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Jannai, son of Joseph, son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Nahum, son of Esli, son of Naggai, son of Mahath, son of Mattathias;

2. son of Semei, son of Joseph, son of Judah, son of Johanan, son of Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, son of Neri, son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmadam, son of Er;

3. son of Jesus, son of Eliezer, son of Joram, son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Simeon, son of Judah, son of Joseph, son of Jonah, son of Eliakim, son of Melea, son of Mainan, son of Mattatha [+];

> [Note: Col. 0527] Greek text: Ματταθά, Mattatha.

4. son of Nathan, son of David, son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Salmon, son of Nahshon, son of Amminadab, son of Aram, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah, son of Jacob;

5.
son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor, son of [Note: [Col. 0527] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Σερούκ, Seruch. See the genealogy of the same Cambridge codex, p. 154, col. 1, in the notes; in Mill here.] Seruch, son of Ragau, son of [Note: [Col. 0527] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: Φαλέκ, Phalech.] Phalech, son of Eber, son of Saleh, son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noah,

6

son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalaleel, son of Cainan, son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

[Col. 0527] Now Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan [Col. 0529] and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness for forty days, and was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days; and when those days were ended, afterward he was hungry. The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.” Jesus answered him, [Note: [Col. 0529] It adds “and said,” as does Codex Cantabrigiensis, καὶ εἶπεν. Codex Brixianus: “saying.”] saying, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”

Then he led him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down from here; for it is written, ‘He commanded his angels concerning you, that they should preserve you,’ and ‘they shall bear you up in their hands, lest perhaps you strike your foot against a stone.’” And Jesus answered [Col. 0530] and said to him, [Note: [Col. 0529] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: γέγραπται, “it is written.”] “It is written: ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’”

The devil again led him up a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And he said to him, “I will give you all this power and their glory, because they have been delivered to me, and I give them to whom I will. Therefore, if you fall down and worship me, all shall be yours.” Jesus answered and said to him, “It is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.’” And when every temptation had been completed, the devil departed from him until a time.

Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and a report concerning him went out [Col. 0531] through the whole region. He himself taught in their synagogues and was glorified by all. He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and, according to his custom, entered the synagogue on the sabbath day and stood up to read. The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him; and when he unrolled the book, he found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me,
because he has anointed me
to proclaim good news to the poor;
he has sent me to heal the broken in heart,
to proclaim release to captives
and sight to the blind,
to send the broken in release,
to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and [Col. 0532] the day of recompense.”

Having folded the book, he gave it back to the attendant and sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed on him. He began to say to them, “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” All bore witness to him and marvelled at the gracious words proceeding from his mouth, and they said, “Is this not Joseph’s son?”

He said to them, “Certainly you will say to me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself. What we have heard was done in Capernaum, do here also in your native place.’” But he said, “Amen, I say to you, no prophet is accepted in his native place. [Col. 0533] In truth I say to you: there were many widows in Israel in Elijah’s days, when heaven was shut for three years and six months, so that a great famine came over all the land; and Elijah was sent to none of them, except to a widow woman at Zarephath of Sidon. And there were many lepers in Israel under Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.”

All in the synagogue, hearing these things, were filled with rage. Rising up, they cast him outside the city and led him to the brow of the hill on which their city had been built, in order to throw him down. [Col. 0534] But he, passing through their midst, went away.

He went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the sabbaths. They were astonished at his teaching, because his word was spoken with authority. In the synagogue there was a man who had an unclean demon, and he cried out in a loud voice, “What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God.” Jesus rebuked it, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him.” And the demon, throwing him down in their midst, came out of him without harming him. Fear came upon all, and they spoke with one another [Col. 0535] saying, “What word is this, that with authority and power he commands unclean spirits and they come out?” And a report about him spread to every place in the region. Rising [Note: [Col. 0535] After *autem*, “but,” *Jesus* is absent, likewise in the Greek text.] from the synagogue, he entered Simon’s house.

And having summoned the twelve Apostles, he gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases. And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God and to heal every infirmity. And he said to them: “Take nothing for the journey: neither staff, nor bag, nor bread, nor money; nor are you to have two tunics.

[Col. 0576] “Whatever house you enter, remain there until you leave. And whoever do not receive you, when you leave that city, shake the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.” And when they had gone forth, they travelled through the villages, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.

Now Herod the Tetrarch heard of all that was being done by him, and he was perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead; by others, that Elijah had appeared; and by others, that one of the prophets of old had risen. But Herod said: “I beheaded John; but who [Col. 0577] is this, of whom I hear such things?” And he sought to see him.

[Note: [Col. 0575] So also the Canterbury codex: *δέ* (“but”).]

And the Apostles, having returned to Jesus, reported to him all that they had done. And taking them with him, he withdrew privately to a deserted place called Bethsaida. But when the crowds learned this, they followed him; and he received them and spoke to them concerning the kingdom of God, and healed those who needed care.

[Note: [Col. 0577] Verona and Brescia have *followed*, perhaps because *the crowds* (*οἱ ὄχλοι*) is masculine?]

Now the day was already beginning to decline. And his twelve disciples approached him and said to him: “Dismiss the crowd, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms and buy food for themselves, because we are here in a deserted place.”

[Note: [Col. 0577] Adds “to him,” as also the Gothic version: *αὐτῷ* (“to him”).]

[Note: [Col. 0577] So also the Greek text: *τὸν ὄχλον* (“the crowd”).]

But Jesus said to them: “You give them something to eat.” But they [Col. 0578] said: “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless perhaps we ourselves go and buy food for all this crowd.” For there were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples: “Make them recline in groups of fifty.” And they did so, and made them all recline. Then, having taken the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowds. And all ate and were satisfied; and twelve baskets of fragments left over for them were taken up.

[Note: [Col. 0577] So also the Greek text: *γάρ* (“for”).]

[Note: [Col. 0577] After “disciples,” “his” is absent, as also in the Greek text.]

And it came to pass, while he was praying alone, that his disciples met with him; and he asked them, saying: “Who do the crowds say that I am?” They answered: “John the Baptist; but others, Elijah; and others, that one of the former prophets has risen.” And he said to them: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered and said: “You are the Christ, the Son of God.” But he rebuked them and commanded them to tell this to no one, saying: “For the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.”

And he said to all: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross [Col. 0580] daily, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it. For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world but loses himself, or brings ruin upon himself? For whoever is ashamed of me or of my words, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed when he comes in his own majesty, and that of the Father and of the holy angels. But I tell you truly: there are some standing here who shall not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.”

Now it came to pass about eight days after these words that he took [Col. 0581] Peter, John, and James, and went up the mountain to pray.

[Note: [Col. 0581] In accordance with the order of the Greek text: *καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον* (“and John and James”).]

And it came to pass, while he was praying, that the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing was white and gleaming. And behold, two men were speaking with him: Moses and Elijah. They appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem. But Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; yet, having awakened, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him. And it came to pass, as they were departing from him, that Peter said to Jesus: “Master, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah”—not knowing [Col. 0582] what he was saying.

While he was saying these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud. And a voice came from the cloud, saying: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.” And while the voice was occurring, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.

Now it came to pass on the following day, as they came down from the mountain, that a large crowd met him. And behold, a man from the crowd cried out, saying: “Teacher, I beg you, look upon my son, for he is my only child. And behold, an unclean spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, [Col. 0583] throws him down, and convulses him with foaming; and it scarcely leaves him, tearing him apart. And I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they could not.”

Jesus answered and said: “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and endure you? Bring your son here.” While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and restored him to his father. And all were astonished and marvelled at the greatness of God.

[Note: [Col. 0583] So also the Greek text: *ἔτι δέ* (“while still / yet”).]

And while all marvelled at everything that Jesus did, Peter said: “Lord, why were we unable to cast it out?” But he said: “This kind does not come out except by prayers and fasting.”

[Col. 0584] And he said to his disciples: “Lay up these words in your ears: for the Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.” But they did not understand this saying; it was concealed from them so that they should not comprehend it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.

Now a thought entered among them as to which of them would be greatest.

[Note: [Col. 0583] So also the Greek text: *ἐν αὐτοῖς* (“among them”).]

But Jesus, seeing the thoughts of their heart, took a child and placed him beside himself, and said to them: “Whoever receives this child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For he who is least among all of you, this one is great.”

Then John answered: “Master, we saw someone [Col. 0585] casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he does not follow with us.” And Jesus said to him: “Allow him; do not forbid him. For whoever is not against you is for you.”

Now it came to pass, when the days of his assumption were being fulfilled, that he set his face firmly to go to Jerusalem. And he sent messengers before him; and they went and entered a city of the Samaritans in order to prepare for him. But they did not receive him, because his face was set toward Jerusalem. When his disciples James and John saw this, they said: “Lord, do you wish us to say [Col. 0586] that fire should come down from heaven and consume them, as Elijah also did?” But Jesus turned and rebuked them, and said to them: “You do not know of what spirit you are. For the Son of Man did not come to destroy human souls, but to save them.” And they went away to another village.

[Note: [Col. 0585] So also the Canterbury codex: *καὶ εἶπεν* (“and he said”).]

[Note: [Col. 0585] Adds “human,” as also the Greek text: *ἀνθρώπων* (“of human beings”).]

And it came to pass, as they were travelling on the road, that someone said to him: “I will follow you wherever you go, Lord.” And Jesus said to him: “Foxes have dens, and birds of heaven nests in which to rest; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

[Note: [Col. 0585] Adds “Lord,” as likewise the Greek text: *Κύριε*.]

[Note: [Col. 0585] Adds “and,” as also the Greek text: *καί*.]

And he said to another: [Col. 0587] “Follow me.” But he said: “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.” Jesus said to him: “Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.” Another also said: “I will follow you, Lord; but first allow me to take leave of those in my household.” Jesus said to him: “No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”

After these things Jesus appointed seventy others and sent them two by two before him into every city and place to which he himself was about to come. And he said to them: “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the labourers [Col. 0588] are few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send labourers into his harvest. Go: behold, I send you as sheep among wolves.

[Note: [Col. 0587] So also the Canterbury codex: *εἰς πάντα τόπον καὶ πόλιν* (“into every place and city”).]

[Note: [Col. 0587] Before “about to come,” *himself* is absent also in the Canterbury codex.]

[Note: [Col. 0587] So also the Greek text: *ἐν μέσῳ λύκων* (“among wolves”).]

“Carry neither purse, nor bag, nor footwear; and greet no one on the road. Whatever house you enter, first say: ‘Peace to this house.’ And if a child of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; otherwise it will return to you. Remain in the same house, eating and drinking what they have, for the labourer is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house. Into whatever city you enter and they receive [Col. 0589] you, eat what is set before you; heal the sick who are there, and say to them: ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’ But into whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say: ‘Even the dust of your city that clings to our feet we shake off against you; nevertheless know this: the kingdom of God has come near to you.’ But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for Sodom on that day than for that city.

[Note: [Col. 0589] Adds “on the feet,” as also the Canterbury codex: *εἰς τοὺς πόδας*.]

“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, [Col. 0590] they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes. Yet it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you. And you, Capernaum, who have been exalted to heaven, shall be brought down to hell. Whoever hears you hears me, and whoever rejects you rejects me; and whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”

Now the seventy returned with great joy, saying: “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name.” And he said to them: [Col. 0591] “I saw Satan falling like lightning from heaven. Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall harm you. Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that demons are subject to you; rather rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

[Note: [Col. 0591] So also the Canterbury codex: *ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ (τοῦ Θεοῦ)*, “in the kingdom (of God).”]

At that very hour Jesus rejoiced in the Spirit and said: “I give thanks to you, Lord, Father of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for thus it was pleasing before you. All things have been delivered to me by my Father. [Col. 0592] And no one knows who the Son is except the Father, nor who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.”

Then, turning privately to his disciples, he said: “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see, and the ears that hear. For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.”

[Note: [Col. 0591] Before “see,” “you” is absent, likewise in the Greek text.]

[Note: [Col. 0591] Adds “you,” as also the Canterbury codex: *ὑμεῖς*.]

And as he said these things, behold, a certain expert in the Law stood up, testing him and saying: “Teacher, what shall I do to obtain eternal life?” But he said to him: “What is written in the Law? How do you read it?” He answered: [Col. 0593] “You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbour as yourself.” And Jesus said to him: “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you shall live.”

But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus: “And who is my neighbour?” Jesus replied: “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted wounds upon him, and went away, leaving him half dead. By chance a certain priest was going down on that road, and when he saw him, he passed by. Likewise [Col. 0594] a Levite, when he came to the same place and saw him, passed by. But a certain Samaritan, travelling along, came near him; and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion. Approaching him, he bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; then he placed him upon his own beast, brought him to an inn, and cared for him. On the next day he brought out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said to him: ‘Take care of him; and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I return.’ Which of these three, do you think, became a neighbour to the man who fell among the robbers?” He said: “The one who showed mercy to him.” [Col. 0595] And Jesus said to him: “Go, and do likewise.”

Now it came to pass, as they travelled, that he entered a certain village. A woman named Martha received him into her house. She had a sister named Mary, who also sat at the Lord’s feet and listened attentively to his word. But Martha was distracted with much service. She came and said: “Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her, therefore, to help me.” Jesus answered and said to her: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled [Col. 0596] about many things. Yet one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the better part, which shall not be taken away from her.”

[Note: [Col. 0595] So also the Greek text: *ὁ Ἰησοῦς* (“Jesus”).]

And it came to pass, while he was praying in a certain place, that when he ceased, one of his disciples said to him: “Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.” And he said to them: “When you pray, say: ‘Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our sins, as we also forgive [Col. 0597] all our debtors. And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil.’”

[Note: [Col. 0595] Adds “our, who art in heaven,” as also the Greek text: *ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς*.]

[Note: [Col. 0595] Adds “Thy will be done in heaven and on earth,” as also the Greek text: *γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς*.]

[Note: [Col. 0597] Adds “But deliver us from evil,” as also the Greek text: *ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ*.]

And he said to them: “Which of you has a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves, because a friend of mine has come to me from a journey and I have nothing to set before him’; and he from within will answer, saying, ‘Do not trouble me; the door is already shut and my children are with me in bed. I cannot rise and give you anything’? I tell you: even if he will not rise and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will rise and [Col. 0598] give him as much as he needs. And I say to you: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it shall be opened.

[Note: [Col. 0597] Before “I tell you,” “and if he persists in knocking” is absent, also in the Greek text and in several Latin codices and all Greek codices.]

“Which father among you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a serpent instead of a fish? Or if he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion? Therefore, if you, although evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven [Col. 0599] give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.”

[Note: [Col. 0597] Adds “if,” as also the Greek text: *εἰ*.]

Now when he had said these things, they brought to him a demoniac, and he cast out the demon; and it was mute. And it came to pass, when he had cast out the demon, the mute man spoke, and the crowds marvelled. But some of them said: “By Beelzebul, prince of demons, he casts out demons.” Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.

[Note: [Col. 0599] After “demon,” “the mute man spoke” is absent; likewise in the Canterbury codex. There: “all … were astonished,” Canterbury codex: *πάντες … ἐθαύμαζον* (“all … marvelled”).]

But he, seeing their thoughts, said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house. And if Satan also casts out Satan, [Col. 0600] he is divided against himself; how then shall his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul. But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they shall be your judges. But if I cast out demons by the finger of God, then surely the kingdom of God has come upon you. When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, all that he possesses is in peace. But when one stronger than he comes upon him and conquers him, he takes away all his armour in which he trusted and divides his spoils. Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

[Note: [Col. 0599] So also the Greek text: *ἐρημοῦται* (“is laid waste”).]

[Col. 0601] “When an unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it passes through dry places seeking rest; and, finding none, it says: ‘I will return to my house from which I came out.’ And when it comes, it finds it vacant, swept, and adorned. Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they enter and dwell there; and the last condition of that person becomes worse than the first.”

[Note: [Col. 0601] After “takes,” “with itself” is absent, likewise in the Greek text.]

And it came to pass, as he said these things, that a certain woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him: “Blessed is the womb that bore you [Col. 0602] and the breasts that you sucked.” But he said: “Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”

[Note: [Col. 0601] After “keep,” “it” is absent, also in the Canterbury codex.]

As the crowds were gathering together, he began to say: “This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet. For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so shall the Son of Man be to this generation. The queen of the South shall rise in judgment with the men of this generation and condemned them, [Col. 0603] because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here. The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching; and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.

[Note: [Col. 0603] In accordance with the Greek text: *Νινευί* (“Nineveh / Ninevites”).]

“No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place, nor under a measuring basket, but upon a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light. The lamp of your body is your eye. If your eye is sound, your whole body shall be full of light; but if it is evil, your whole body shall be dark. Therefore see to it that the light in you is not darkness. If, then, your whole body [Col. 0604] is full of light, having no part dark, it shall be wholly full of light, as when a lamp by its radiance gives you light. For if the body which is in you has no lamp shining, it is dark to you; how much more, then, shall your shining lamp give you light.”

[Note: [Col. 0603] Adds “but,” as also the Greek text: *δέ*.]

And while he was speaking these things, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He entered and reclined at table. But the Pharisee, seeing this, was astonished that he had not first been baptized before eating. And the Lord said to him: “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of cup and dish, but [Col. 0605] your inward part is full of robbery and wickedness. Fools! Did not he who made the outside also make the inside? Nevertheless, give alms from what you have, and behold, all things are clean for you. But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe mint, rue, and every herb, but pass over justice and the love of God. These things it was necessary to do, without neglecting those. Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the first seats in synagogues and greetings in the marketplace. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are [Col. 0606] like unmarked tombs, over which people walk without knowing it.”

[Note: [Col. 0605] The Greek text has: *τὰ ἐνόντα* (“the things within / what is inside”).]

[Note: [Col. 0605] Adds “scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites,” as also the Greek text: *Γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί*.]

Then one of the lawyers answered him: “Teacher, in saying these things, you insult us also.” But he said: “Woe to you lawyers also, because you burden people with burdens impossible to bear, while you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers. Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, while your fathers killed them. Therefore you bear witness that you consent to the works of your fathers: for they indeed [Col. 0607] killed them, but you build their tombs. Therefore also the wisdom of God said: ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,’ so that the blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, may be required from this generation: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, it shall be required from this generation. Woe to you lawyers, because you have taken away the key of knowledge: you yourselves did not enter, and you hindered those who were entering.”

And while he was saying these things to them before all the people, the Pharisees and lawyers began [Col. 0608] to be distressed and to dispute with him about many things, questioning him and seeking to catch something from his mouth, so that they might find an occasion to accuse him.

Now when many crowds had gathered together, so that they trampled one another, he began first to say to his disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

[Note: [Col. 0607] Adds “yourselves,” as also the Greek text: *ἑαυτοῖς*.]

“Nothing is covered that shall not be revealed, nor hidden that shall not be known. Therefore what you have said in darkness shall be heard in the light, and what you have spoken in the ear [Col. 0609] in inner rooms shall be proclaimed upon the housetops. But I tell you, my friends: do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after this have nothing more that they can do. But I shall show you whom you should fear: fear him who, after killing, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him. Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God. Even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Therefore do not fear: you are worth more than many sparrows.

[Note: [Col. 0609] After “are,” “you” is absent, also in the Greek text.]

“But I tell you: everyone who confesses me [Col. 0610] before people, the Son of Man also will confess him before the angels of God; but whoever denies me before people shall be denied before the angels of God. And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man shall be forgiven; but to one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit it shall not be forgiven. When they bring you into synagogues and before rulers and authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you should answer, or what you should say; for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say.”

[Note: [Col. 0609] So also the Greek text: *ἅ* (“what things”).]

Someone from the crowd said to him: [Col. 0611] “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.” But he said to him: “Man, who appointed me judge or divider over you?” And he said to them: “See to it, and beware of all greed, because a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.” And he told them a parable:

“The field of a certain rich man yielded abundant crops. And he thought within himself, saying: ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’ And he said: ‘This I shall do: I shall tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I shall store all my produce and goods. And I shall say to my soul: [Col. 0612] Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, and make merry.’ But God said to him: ‘Fool, this night they demand your soul from you; and whose shall be the things you have prepared?’ So it is with the one who stores treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”

And he said to his disciples: “Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you shall eat, nor about your body, what you shall wear. Life is more than food, and the body more than clothing. Consider the birds: they neither sow nor reap; they have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds! [Col. 0613] And which of you, by being anxious, can add one cubit to his stature? If, therefore, you cannot do even the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest? Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither labour nor spin; yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass, which is in the field today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith! And do not seek what you shall eat or what you shall drink, nor be anxious. For all these things [Col. 0614] the nations of this world seek; but your Father knows that you need all these things. Nevertheless, seek the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added to you. Do not fear, little flock, because your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.

[Note: [Col. 0611] After “life,” “your” is absent also in the Canterbury codex.]

[Note: [Col. 0611] So also the Greek text: *τῶν πετεινῶν* (“than the birds”).]

[Note: [Col. 0613] Adds “for,” as also the Canterbury codex: *ὅτι*.]

[Note: [Col. 0613] Before “kingdom,” “first” is absent, likewise in the Greek text. In the same passage, after “God,” “and his righteousness” is absent, as in the Vercelli, Verona, and Brescia manuscripts.]

“Sell what you possess and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys. For where your treasure is, there your heart shall be also. Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning, and [Col. 0615] be like people waiting for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once. Blessed are those servants whom the lord, when he comes, finds watching. Amen, I tell you that he will gird himself, make them recline, and come forward to serve them. And if he comes in the second watch, or if he comes in the third watch and finds them so, blessed are those servants. But know this: if the master of the house knew at what hour the thief was coming, he would surely watch and would not allow his house [Col. 0616] to be broken into. You also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour when you do not expect him.”

Peter said to him: “Lord, do you tell this parable to us, or to all?” And the Lord said: “Who then is the faithful and prudent steward whom the lord will appoint over his household, to give them their measure of grain at the proper time? Blessed is that servant whom his lord, when he comes, finds doing so. Truly I tell you that he will appoint him over all that he possesses.

[Note: [Col. 0615] Adds “his,” as also the Greek text: *αὐτοῦ*. In the same passage, “finds”: *εὑρήσει*.]

[Col. 0617] “But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays in coming,’ and begins to beat the male and female servants, to eat and drink and become drunk, the lord of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know; he will cut him off and assign him a portion with the unfaithful. That servant who knew his lord’s will and did not prepare or act according to his will shall be beaten with many blows. But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows shall be beaten with few. From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required; and from him to whom they entrusted much, they will ask more.”

[Col. 0618] “I came to cast fire upon the earth; and what do I desire but that it be kindled? But I have a baptism with which to be baptized, and how I am constrained until it is accomplished! Do you think that I came to bring peace upon earth? No, I tell you, but division. For from now on five in one household shall be divided: three against two, and two against three. Father shall be divided against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”

[Note: [Col. 0617] So also the Greek text: *βάπτισμα* (“baptism”).]

And he said [Col. 0619] also to the crowds: “When you see a cloud rising in the west, immediately you say, ‘Rain is coming,’ and so it happens. And when you see the south wind blowing, you say that there will be heat, and so it happens. Hypocrites! You know how to discern the appearance of earth and sky; but how do you not discern this time? Why do you not even judge for yourselves what is right? When you go with your adversary to the judge on the way, make an effort to be released from him, lest he deliver you to the judge, the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison. I tell you: you shall not leave there until you have paid [Col. 0620] the last quadrans.”

[Note: [Col. 0619] The Greek text: *ἐπ᾽ ἄρχοντα* (“before a ruler / magistrate”).]

Now some came at that very time reporting to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices. Jesus answered and said to them: “Do you think that these Galileans were sinners beyond all Galileans because they suffered such things? No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you shall all likewise perish. Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they too were more guilty than all the people dwelling in Jerusalem? No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you shall all likewise perish.”

And he told this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none. Then he said to the vinedresser: ‘Behold, for three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and find none. Cut it down, then. Why should it also occupy the ground?’ But he answered and said to him: ‘Lord, leave it also this year, until I dig around it and put [Col. 0621] a basket of manure around it; and if indeed [Col. 0622] it bears fruit—otherwise, in the future you shall cut it down.’”

[Note: [Col. 0621] And thus St Ambrose, in accordance with the Canterbury codex: *κόφινον κοπρίων*, “a basket of manure.”]

Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbaths. And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not at all straighten herself. When Jesus saw her, he called her to him and said: “Woman, you are released from your infirmity.” And he laid his hands upon her, and immediately she was made straight and glorified God.

[Note: [Col. 0621] So also the Greek text: *ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν* (“in one of the synagogues”).]

But the ruler of the synagogue answered indignantly because Jesus healed on the sabbath, saying to the crowd: “There are six days in which one ought [Col. 0623] to work; come therefore on those days and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.” But the Lord answered him and said: “Hypocrite, does not each one of you on the sabbath untie his ox or ass from the manger and lead it away to water it?
