And should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for eighteen years, be released from these bonds on the sabbath day?”

As he said these things, all who opposed him were put to shame; and all the people rejoiced at all the glorious works that were seen to be done by him.

[Note: [Col. 0623] So also the Greek text: *ἀπεκρίθη* (“answered”).]

[Col. 0624] Therefore he said: “To what is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it? It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and put into his garden; it grew and became a great tree, and the birds of heaven rested in its branches.”

[Note: [Col. 0623] So also the Canterbury codex: *ἐγένετο δένδρον* (“became a tree”).]

And again he said: “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God? It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened.”

And Jesus went through the cities and villages, teaching and making his way to Jerusalem. And someone said to him, “Lord, are there few who are saved?” But he said to them:

[Col. 0625] “Strive to enter through the narrow gate; for I tell you, many will seek to enter and will not be able. When the master of the house has entered and shut the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’ [Note: The Greek text likewise repeats Κύριε, ‘Lord.’] And he will answer you, ‘I do not know where you are from.’ Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank before you, and you taught in our streets.’ And he will say to you, ‘I do not know where you are from; depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’ There will be weeping there and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves [Col. 0626] cast out. And they will come from east and west, from north and south, and recline at table in the kingdom of God. And behold, there are those who are last who will be first, and those who are first who will be last.”

On that very day some Pharisees came to him, saying, “Leave and go away from here, for Herod wishes to kill you.” And Jesus said to them, “Go and tell that fox: ‘Behold, I cast out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am perfected.’ Nevertheless, I must go on today, tomorrow, and the following day; for it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem. Jerusalem, [Col. 0627] Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you—how often I wished to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not! Behold, your house will be left to you desolate. But I tell you: you will not see me until the day comes when you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

And it came to pass, when Jesus entered the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, that they were watching him. And behold, a certain man suffering from dropsy was before [Col. 0628] him. And Jesus answered and said to the lawyers and Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath [Note: The words “or not” are added, as also in the Canterbury manuscript: ἢ οὔ.] or not?” But they were silent. He took hold of the man, healed him, and dismissed him. And answering, he said to them, “Which of you, if his son or ox falls into a pit, will not immediately lift him out on the Sabbath day?” And they were unable to answer him on these matters.

He spoke a parable to those invited, observing how they chose the first places at table, and said to them, “When you are invited [Note: “By someone” is added; likewise in the Greek text: ὑπό τινος.] by someone to a wedding, do not [Col. 0629] recline in the first place, lest someone more honoured than you has been invited by him, and he who invited both you and him comes and says to you, ‘Give this man your place’; and then you will begin, with shame, to occupy the last place. But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that, when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, ‘Friend, move higher up.’ Then you will have honour before those reclining at table with you. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a luncheon or a supper, do not invite your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor [Col. 0630] rich neighbours, lest they also invite you in return and repayment be made to you. But when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind; and you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

When one of those reclining at table heard this, he said to him, “Blessed is he who shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.” But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper and invited many. At the hour of supper he sent his servant to say to those invited, [Note: So also the Greek text: ἔρχεσθε, ‘Come.’] ‘Come, for now [Col. 0631] all things are ready.’ And they all together began to make excuses. The first said to him, ‘I have bought an estate, and I must go out and see it; I ask you, have me excused.’ Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them; I ask you, have me excused.’ Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.’ And the servant returned and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house, angered, said to his servant, ‘Go quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’ And the servant said, ‘Lord, what you commanded has been done, and there is still [Col. 0632] room.’ And the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and around the hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled. For I tell you that none of those men who were invited shall taste my supper.’”

Now great crowds were going with him; and he turned and said to them, “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters—yes, even his own life—he cannot be my disciple. And whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot [Col. 0633] be my disciple. For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost, to see whether he has what is necessary to complete it? Otherwise, after he has laid the foundation and is unable to finish, all who see it may begin to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’ Or what king, going to engage in war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he can meet, with ten thousand men, one who comes against him with twenty thousand? And if he cannot, [Col. 0634] while the other is still far away, he sends an embassy and asks for terms of peace. So then, every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses cannot be my disciple.

“Salt is good; but if salt loses its savour, with what will it be seasoned? It is useful neither for the land nor for the manure pile; it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

Now all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to hear him. But the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, “This man receives sinners and eats with them.” And he spoke this parable to them, saying:

[Col. 0635] “What man among you, having a hundred sheep, if he has lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it? And when he has found it, he lays it upon his shoulders rejoicing; and, coming home, he calls together his friends and neighbours, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.’ I tell you that so there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, [Col. 0636] more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need repentance.

“Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it? And when she has found it, she calls together her women friends and neighbours, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I lost.’ Thus, I tell you, there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.”

[Col. 0637] And he said, “A certain man had two sons. The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the portion of the property that falls to me.’ And he divided the property between them. Not many days afterward, the younger son gathered everything together and went abroad into a distant country; and there he squandered his property in dissolute living. And after he had spent everything, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need. And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him into his field to feed pigs. And he desired to fill himself with the pods that the pigs [Col. 0638] were eating, and no one gave him anything. But coming to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father have an abundance of bread, while I am perishing here from hunger! I will rise and go to my father, and I will say to him: “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’ And he rose and went to his father.

“But while he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with compassion; he ran, fell upon his neck, and kissed him. And the son said to him, [Col. 0639] ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’ But the father said to his servants, ‘Quickly bring out the best robe and put it on him; put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet; bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let us eat and celebrate. For this my son was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’ And they began to celebrate.

“Now his elder son was in the field; and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing. He called one of the servants and asked what [Col. 0640] this might be. And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has received him back safe and sound.’ But he became angry and would not go in. His father [Note: So also the Canterbury manuscript: δέ, ‘but.’] went out and began to plead with him. But he answered and said to his father, ‘Behold, for so many years I have served you, and I have never transgressed your command; yet you never gave me even a young goat, that I might celebrate with my friends. But when this son of yours came, who devoured his property with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’ [Col. 0641] But he said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours. But we had to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’”

And he said to his disciples, “There was a certain very rich man who had a steward; and this man was accused before him of squandering his goods. Having called him, he said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Render an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.’ But the steward said within himself, ‘What shall I do, [Col. 0642] since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I cannot dig; I am ashamed to beg. I know what I will do, so that, when I have been removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.’ And summoning each of his master’s debtors, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’ He said, ‘A hundred measures of oil.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your bond, sit down quickly, and write fifty.’ Then he said to another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your papers [Col. 0643] and write eighty.’ And the master commended the unrighteous steward because he had acted shrewdly; for the children of this age are shrewder in their own generation than the children of light. And I say to you: make friends for yourselves from [Note: So also the Greek text: Μαμωνᾶ, Mammon.] unrighteous Mammon, so that, when you fail, they may receive you into eternal dwellings.

“He who is faithful in little is also faithful in much; and he who is unfaithful in little is also unfaithful in much. If, therefore, you have not been faithful in unrighteous Mammon, who will entrust to you what is true? And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is [Col. 0644] your own? No servant can serve two masters. For either he will hate one and love the other, or he will hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and Mammon.”

The Pharisees, who were covetous, heard all these things and mocked him. And he said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is exalted among men is an abomination before God. The Law and the Prophets were until John; from then on the kingdom of God is preached, [Col. 0645] and everyone forces his way into it. But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the Law to fall.

“Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and he who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.

“There was a certain rich man, clothed in purple and fine linen, feasting splendidly every day. But [Note: “But” is added, as also in the Greek text: δέ.] a certain beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, full of sores, desiring to be filled with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table [Note: After “rich man’s,” the words “and no one gave him anything” are absent, likewise in the Greek text.]; and dogs also came [Col. 0646] and licked his sores. And it came to pass that the beggar died and was carried by angels into Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died [Note: So also the Greek text: καὶ ἐτάφη, ‘and was buried’; Καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ ἐπάρας, ‘and, lifting up [his eyes] in Hades.’] and was buried. And in hell, lifting up his eyes while he was in torments, he saw Abraham far away and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried out, saying, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water [Note: “But” is added, as also in the Greek text: δέ.] and cool my tongue, for I am tormented in this flame.’ But Abraham said to him, ‘Son, remember that you received your good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise evil things; but now [Col. 0647] he is comforted and you are tormented. And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those wishing to cross from here to you cannot, nor can any cross over from there to us.’

“And he said, ‘Then I ask you, Father, to send him to my father’s house, for I have five brothers, so that he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torments.’ Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them.’ But he said, ‘No, Father Abraham; but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’ [Col. 0648] But he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they believe if someone rises from the dead.’”

And he [Note: So also the Greek text: δέ, ‘but.’] said also to his disciples, “It is impossible that stumbling-blocks should not come; but woe to that man through whom they come. It would be better for him if a millstone were put around his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble. Take heed to yourselves. If your brother [Note: Before “brother,” “against you” is absent, also in the Gothic Version.] sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him. And if he sins against you seven times in a day and seven times [Col. 0649] returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ forgive him.”

And the apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.” But the Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you. But which of you, having a servant ploughing or [Note: The Vercelli manuscript also appears to have read “sheep,” with the Syriac, Persian, Arabic Versions, and Augustine.] feeding sheep, will say to him when he returns from the field, ‘Come at once and recline at table’? Rather, will he not say to him, ‘Prepare something for me to eat, gird yourself, and serve me until I have eaten and drunk; and afterward you shall eat and drink’? Does he [Col. 0650] thank that servant because he did [Note: So also the Greek text: τὰ διαταχθέντα αὐτῷ, ‘the things commanded him.’] what was commanded him? I do not think so. So also you, when you have done all that was commanded you, say, ‘We are unprofitable servants; we have done what we ought to have done.’”

And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee. And as he entered a certain village, ten leprous men met him, standing at a distance; and they lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.” When he saw them, he said to them, “Go, show [Col. 0651] yourselves to the priests.” And it came to pass, as they went, they were cleansed. But one of them, seeing that he was cleansed, returned with a loud voice glorifying God; and he fell upon his face at his feet, giving thanks to him. And he was a Samaritan. Jesus answered, “Were not ten cleansed? Where are the nine? Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this foreigner?” And he said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well.”

When he was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them and said, “The kingdom of God does not come with observation, nor will they say, [Col. 0652] ‘Behold, here,’ or ‘Behold, there’; for behold, the kingdom of God is within you.” And he said to the disciples, “Days will come when you will desire to see one day of the Son of Man and will not see it. And they will say to you, ‘Behold, here,’ and ‘Behold, there.’ Do not go, nor follow them. For as lightning flashing shines from one end of the sky to the other, so will the coming of the Son of Man be in his day. But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

“And as it happened in the days of Noah, so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man. They ate and drank, took wives and gave in marriage, until the day when [Col. 0653] Noah entered the ark; and the flood came and destroyed them all. Likewise, as it happened in the days of Lot: they ate and drank, bought and sold, planted and built; but on the day when Lot went out from Sodom, fire and sulphur rained from heaven and destroyed them all. So it will be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed. On that day, whoever is on the roof and whose goods are in the house, let him not come down to take them; and likewise let the one who is in the field not turn back. Remember Lot’s wife. Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses [Col. 0654] it [Note: “For my sake” is added also in the Gothic Version.] for my sake will save it. Truly I tell you: on that night there will be two in one bed; one will be taken and the other left. Two women will be grinding together; one will be taken and the other left. Two will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.” And they answered and said to him, “Where will these things happen, Lord?” He said to them, “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered.”

He also spoke to them a parable on the necessity of always praying and not losing heart: “There was a judge in a certain city who did not fear God [Col. 0655] nor respect man. There was a widow in that city, and she came to him, saying, ‘Vindicate me against my adversary.’ For a long time he would not. But afterward he said within himself, ‘Though I do not fear God nor respect man, yet, because this widow troubles me, I will vindicate her, lest by continually coming she wear me out.’” And the Lord said, “Hear what the unrighteous judge says. And will not God bring vindication to his elect who cry to him day and night, and will he be patient with them? I tell [Col. 0656] you that he will quickly bring them vindication. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, do you suppose he will find faith on earth?”

He also spoke this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were [Note: “Were” is added, likewise in the Greek text: εἰσί; the Vercelli manuscript also has “are.”] righteous and despised others: “Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. The Pharisee, standing, prayed thus: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like other men—robbers, unrighteous, adulterers—or even [Note: It reads “as”; the Greek text likewise: ὡς.] like this tax collector. I fast twice in the week; I give tithes [Col. 0657] of all that I possess.’ But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner.’ I tell you, this tax collector went down to his house justified [Note: So also the Canterbury manuscript: μᾶλλον παρ᾽ ἐκεῖνον τὸν Φαρισαῖον, ‘rather than that Pharisee.’] rather than that Pharisee; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

They were also bringing infants to him that he might touch them; and when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them. But Jesus called them to him and said, “Allow the children to come to me, and do not [Col. 0658] forbid them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these. Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will not enter it.”

And a certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God. You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery; do not kill; do not steal; do not bear false witness; honour your father and mother.’” But he said, [Col. 0659] “I have kept all these things from my youth.” When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “One thing still lacks for you: sell all that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.” But when he heard these things, he became sorrowful, for he was very rich. And Jesus, seeing him become sorrowful, said to his disciples, “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God! For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.” And those who heard said, “Who then can be saved?” [Col. 0660] And Jesus said to them, “The things impossible with men are possible with God.”

But Peter said, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you.” And he said to them, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God, and does not receive many times more in this present time, and in the age to come eternal life.”

And Jesus took the twelve disciples aside and said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all things [Col. 0661] written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be fulfilled. For he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, and spat upon; and after they have scourged him, they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.” But they understood none of these things; this saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was said.

And it came to pass, as he drew near to Jericho, that a certain blind man sat beside the road begging. Hearing a crowd passing by, he asked what this was. They told him that Jesus [Note: So also the Greek text: (ὅτι) Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται, “that Jesus the Nazarene is passing by.”] the Nazarene was passing by. Then he cried out, saying, [Col. 0662] “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” Those going before rebuked him so that he would be silent; but he cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!” Jesus stopped and commanded that he be brought to him. And when he had drawn near, he asked him, saying, “What do you wish me to do for you?” And he said, “Lord, that I may see.” And Jesus said to him, “Receive sight; your faith has made you well.” And immediately he saw, and followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

And having entered, he was passing through Jericho. And behold, there was a man named [Col. 0663] Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector and was rich. He sought to see who Jesus was, but could not because of the crowd, for he was small in stature. Running ahead, he climbed a sycamore tree to see him, because he was about to pass that way. When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.” And he hurried down and received him joyfully. When they all saw it, they murmured, saying that he had gone in to stay with a sinful man. But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor; and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.” Jesus [Note: “But” is added, likewise in the Greek text: δέ.] said to him, [Col. 0664] “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost.”

As they heard these things, he added and spoke a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and because they thought that the kingdom of God would appear immediately.

[Col. 0665] Therefore he said, “A certain rich man went [Note: Greek text: εἰς χώραν μακράν. τὸ μακράν may be translated either ‘distant’ or ‘far away.’] into a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and return. And calling ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them, ‘Do business until I come.’ But his citizens hated him and sent an embassy after him, saying, ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’ And it came to pass, when he returned after receiving the kingdom, that he commanded those servants to be called to whom he had given the money, so that he might know how much each had gained. The first came, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has gained ten minas.’ And he said to him, ‘Well done, [Col. 0666] good and faithful servant; because you have been faithful in a little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’ The second came, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made five minas.’ And he said to him, ‘You also shall be over five cities.’ Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, here is your mina, which I kept laid away in a cloth; for I feared you, because you are a severe man: you take up what you did not lay down and reap what you did not sow.’ [Note: After *autem*, ‘but,’ *eius*, ‘his,’ is absent, also in the Canterbury manuscript.] And he said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I judge you, wicked and slothful servant. You knew that I am a severe man, [Col. 0667] taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow; [Note: So also the Greek text: καί, ‘and.’] and why did you not put my money with the bankers, so that, upon coming, I might have collected it with interest?’ And he said to those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’ And they said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’ But I tell you: to everyone who has, more will be given; but from him who does not have, even what he has will be taken away. Nevertheless, bring here those enemies of mine who did not wish me to reign over them, and kill them before me.’”

And after saying these things, [Col. 0668] he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem. And it came to pass, when he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mountain called the Mount of Olives, that he sent two of his disciples, saying, “Go into the village opposite, where, as you enter, you will find a colt of an ass tied, upon which no man has ever sat. Untie it and bring it. And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ you shall say to him, ‘Because the Lord needs it.’” Those who were sent went and found the colt standing as Jesus had told them. As they untied the colt, [Col. 0669] its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?” And they said, “Because the Lord needs it.” And they brought it to Jesus; throwing their garments on the colt, they set Jesus upon it. As he went, they spread their garments on the road. And as he now drew near to the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began joyfully to praise God in a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen, saying, “Blessed is he who comes, the King, in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest!” Some Pharisees from the crowd said [Col. 0670] to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.” He answered and said to them, “I tell you, if these are silent, the stones will cry out.”

And when he drew near, seeing the city, he wept over it, saying, “If only you too had known, on this day, the things that make for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes. For days will come upon you when your enemies will surround you with a palisade, encircle you, and hem you in on every side; they will dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and they will not leave in you one stone upon another, [Col. 0671] because you did not know the time of your visitation.”

And entering the temple, he began to cast out those selling and buying in it, saying to them, “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.” And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests, scribes, and elders of the people sought to destroy him, but did not find what they could do to him; for all the people hung upon his words as they listened to him.

And it came to pass on one of the days, while he was teaching the people in the temple [Col. 0672] and preaching the good news, that the chief priests and scribes, with the elders, came together and said to him, “Tell us: by what authority do you do these things? Or who is it who gave you this authority?” He answered and said to them, “I too will ask you one question; tell me: Was John’s baptism from heaven or from men?” They reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced [Col. 0673] that John was a prophet.” And they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

Then he began to speak this parable to the people: “A man planted a vineyard and leased it to tenant farmers, and went abroad for many years. At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenant farmers, that they might give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenant farmers beat him and sent him away empty. He added and sent another servant; but they beat and dishonoured him also, and sent him away empty. And he added and sent a third; they wounded him too and cast him out empty. Then the lord [Col. 0674] of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps, when they see him, they will respect him.’ But when the tenant farmers saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.’ And having cast him outside the vineyard, they killed him. What then will the lord of the vineyard do to them? He will come, destroy those tenant farmers, and give his vineyard to others.” When they heard this, they said, “May it never be!” But he looked at them and said, “What then is this that is written: ‘The stone rejected by the builders has become the head of the corner’? Everyone who falls [Col. 0675] upon that stone will be broken to pieces; but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him.”

The chief priests and scribes sought to lay hands on him in that hour, but they feared the people, for they understood that he had spoken this parable against them. And, withdrawing, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, in order to catch him in his words and deliver him to the rule and authority of the governor. They questioned him, saying, “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and do not show partiality, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar, [Col. 0676] or not?” But perceiving their deceit, he said, “Why do you test me? Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it bear?” They answered, “Caesar’s.” And he said to them, “Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” And they were unable to find fault with his saying before the people; and marvelling at his answer, they were silent.

Some Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection, approached and questioned him, saying, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us: if [Col. 0677] a man’s brother dies, having a wife, and dies childless, his brother shall take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother. There were therefore seven brothers. The first took a wife and died childless. The next took her and also died childless. The third took her; likewise all seven, and they left no offspring and died. Last of all the woman also died. In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven had [Col. 0678] her as wife.”

Jesus said to them, “The children of this age marry and are given in marriage; but those judged worthy of that age and of the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor take wives. For neither can they die any more, for they are like angels and are children of God, being children of the resurrection. But that the dead are raised, Moses also showed when he said, ‘I saw in the bush the Lord God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ Now God is not God of the dead but of the living; [Col. 0679] for all live to him.”

Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, you have spoken well.” And they no longer dared to question him about anything. Then Jesus said to them, “How do they say that the Christ is David’s son? For David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’ David therefore calls him Lord; how then is he his son?”

While all the people were listening, he said to his disciples, “Beware of the scribes, who wish to walk about in long robes and love greetings in the marketplace, the chief seats in synagogues, and [Col. 0680] the foremost places at feasts; who devour widows’ houses while making a show of long prayer. These will receive a greater condemnation.”

Looking up, he saw rich men putting their gifts into the treasury. He also saw a certain poor widow putting in two small copper coins. And he said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all. For all these gave from what they had in abundance into the gifts of God; but she, out of what she lacks, put in all the livelihood that she had.”

And while some were speaking of the temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones [Col. 0681] and gifts, he said, “As for these things that you see, days will come in which not one stone will be left upon another that shall not be thrown down.” They asked him, saying, “Teacher, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when they are about to happen?” But he said, “See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not therefore follow them. And when you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end is not yet.”

Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom [Col. 0682] against kingdom; there will be great earthquakes in various places, plagues and famines; and terrors and great signs from heaven. But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you into synagogues and prisons, leading [you] …
to kings and governors on account of my name. But it will turn out for you as a testimony. Therefore set it in your hearts not to prepare beforehand how you shall answer. For I will give you a mouth and wisdom which none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict. [Col. 0683] For you will be handed over by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends; and they will put you to death, and you will be hated by all people on account of my name. Yet not a hair of your head shall perish. By your endurance you will possess your souls.

But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its desolation has drawn near. Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains; let those in its midst depart; and let those in the countryside not enter it, because these are days of vengeance, that all things which have been written may be fulfilled. But woe to those who are pregnant and [Col. 0684] nursing in those days, for there will be great distress upon the earth and wrath against this people. They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive among all nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations, until the times of the nations are fulfilled.

And there will be great signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on earth distress among nations, through anxiety at the roaring of the sea and the motion of the waves, people fainting from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the whole world. For . . . the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

[Note: [Col. 0683] In the manuscript the letters are so obliterated—here represented by a space of small dots—that we have been unable in any way to recover them.]

And then they will see the Son of Man [Col. 0685] in clouds, with great power and majesty. But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.

And he told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree, and all the trees. When they begin to show fruit, you know that summer is near. So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near. Truly I say to you, this generation shall not pass away until all things happen. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

“But take heed to yourselves, lest [Col. 0686] perhaps your hearts be weighed down with dissipation, drunkenness, and the cares of this life, and that day come suddenly upon you. For like a snare it shall come upon all who dwell upon the face of the whole earth. Therefore watch at all times, praying that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things which are to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”

[Note: [Col. 0685] So also the Greek text: ἐκφυγεῖν, “to escape.”]

During the days he was teaching in the temple, but at night he went out and stayed on the mountain called Olivet. And all the people came early in the morning [Col. 0687] to him in the temple to hear him.

Now the festival day of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was drawing near. And the chief priests and scribes were seeking how they might kill him, for they feared the people.

[Note: [Col. 0687] So from the Greek text: αὐτόν, “him.”]

But Satan entered Judas, who was surnamed Scarioth, one of the twelve; and he went and spoke with the chief priests and officers about how he might hand him over to them. And they rejoiced and agreed to give him money. And he promised, and thereafter sought an opportunity to [Col. 0688] hand him over to them without a crowd.

[Note: [Col. 0687] Origen reads, as does Vercelli, Ἰσκαριώθ; and so the Latin Cantabrigiensis, *Iscarioth*. But the Greek Cantabrigiensis has Ἰσκαριώδ.]

Then came the day of Unleavened Bread, on which the Passover had to be sacrificed. And he sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat it.” But they said to him, “Where do you wish us to prepare it?” And he said to them, “Behold, when you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters, and say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you: Where is the guest-room in which I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’ And he will show you a large furnished upper room; [Col. 0689] prepare it there.” They went and found it as he had told them, and prepared the Passover.

[Note: [Col. 0687] After *homo*, “man,” *quidam*, “a certain,” is lacking, also in the Greek text.]

And when the hour had come, he reclined at table, and the twelve apostles with him. And he said to them, “With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. For I tell you that I shall no longer eat of this until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.” And having taken a cup, he gave thanks and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves. For I tell you that I shall not drink of this fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”

[Note: [Col. 0689] It adds *hoc*, “this”; so also the Greek text, τοῦτο.]

[Note: [Col. 0689] The Greek text has ἀπὸ τοῦ γεννήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου, “of the fruit of the vine.” The Veronese [codex] also frequently elsewhere translates the articles.]

And having taken bread, he gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you; do this in remembrance of me.” Likewise also the cup after they had supped, [Col. 0690] saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which shall be poured out for you. Yet behold, the hand of the one betraying me is with me at the table. Indeed, the Son of Man goes according to what has been written; yet woe to that man through whom he is betrayed.” And they began to inquire among themselves who among them it was who would do this.

And there was also a dispute among them [Col. 0691] as to which of them was greater. But he said to them, “The kings of the nations rule over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors. But you are not to be so; rather, let the greater among you become as the younger, and the leader as the servant. For who is greater, the one reclining at table or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining? But I am among you as one who serves. You are those who have remained with me in my trials. And I appoint for you, as my Father [Col. 0692] appointed for me, a kingdom, that you may sit and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

“And the Lord said, ‘Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to sift you as wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.’” But Peter said to him, “Lord, I am [Col. 0693] prepared to go with you both to prison and to death.” And Jesus said, “I tell you, Peter, the cock will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know me.”

And he said to them, “When I sent you without purse, bag, and sandals, did you lack anything?” But they said, “Nothing.” He therefore said to them, “But now, let the one who has a purse take it, likewise also a bag; and let the one who does not have one sell his tunic and buy a sword. For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘And he [Col. 0694] was counted with the lawless.’ For the things written concerning me are reaching their end.” But they said, “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” But Jesus said to them, “It is enough.”

[Note: [Col. 0693] Before *quod*, “which,” *adhuc*, “still,” is lacking, also in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript.]

And going out, he went, according to his custom, to the Mount of Olives; and his disciples followed him. When he reached the place, he said to them, “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.” And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, and, having knelt, prayed, saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. [Col. 0695] Yet not my will, but yours be done.”

[Note: [Col. 0693] It adds *ejus*, “his”; so also the Greek text, αὐτοῦ.]

And rising from prayer, and coming to the disciples, he found them sleeping because of sorrow. And he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, that you may not enter into temptation.”

While he was still speaking, behold, a crowd; and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them, and he approached Jesus to kiss him. But Jesus said to him, “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?” When those who were with him saw what was about to happen, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike [Col. 0696] with the sword?” And one of them struck the servant of the chief priest and cut off his right ear. But Jesus answered and said, “Permit it thus far.” And stretching out his hand and touching his ear, he healed him.

Then Jesus said to those who had come to him from among the chief priests, scribes, officers of the temple, and elders, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as against a robber? Daily I was with you in the temple, and you did not lay hands upon me; but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”

And having seized [Col. 0697] him, they led him to the house of the chief priest. But Peter was following him at a distance.

[Note: [Col. 0697] It adds *illum*, “him”; likewise the Cantabrigiensis manuscript, αὐτῷ; Brixianus, *eum*.]

When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter too sat among them.

[Note: [Col. 0697] So also the Greek text, ἐκάθητο καί, “he sat also,” omitting *illis*, “they,” after *circumsedentibus*, which is also lacking in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript.]

A certain maidservant, seeing him sitting by the fire and looking intently at him, said, “This man too was with him.” But he denied it, saying, “Woman, I do not know him.”

[Note: [Col. 0697] After *negavit*, “he denied,” *eum*, “him,” is lacking also in the Cantabrigiensis manuscript.]

And shortly afterward another, seeing him, said, “Man, you too were always with him.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.” And after an interval of about one hour, another insisted, saying, “Certainly this [Col. 0698] man too was with him, for he is also a Galilean.” But Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” And immediately, while he was still speaking, the cock crowed. And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, as he had said to him: “Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.” And Peter went out and wept bitterly.

[Note: [Col. 0697] So also the Greek text: εἶπεν αὐτῷ, “he said to him.”]

And the men who held him mocked him, beating him and veiling his head. They struck his face and questioned him, saying, “Prophesy: who is it that struck you?” [Col. 0699] And they spoke many other blasphemies against him.

When day came, the elders of the people, the chief priests, and the scribes assembled, and they brought him into their council and questioned him, saying, “If you are the Christ, tell us.” And he said to them, “If I tell you, you will not believe me; and if I question you, you will not answer me, nor let me go. But from now on the Son of Man will sit at the right hand of the power of God.” Then all said, “Are you therefore the Son of God?” But he said to them, “You say that I am.” But they said, “What further need have we of testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from his mouth.”

[Col. 0700] And the whole multitude of them rose up and led him to Pilate. And they began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding tribute to be given to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king.” But Pilate questioned him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered and said, “You say so.” But Pilate said to the chief priests and crowds, “I find no charge [Col. 0701] in this man.” But they grew more insistent, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee as far as this place.”

When Pilate heard “Galilee,” he asked whether the man was a Galilean. And when he learned that he was under Herod’s authority, he sent him to Herod, who was himself also in Jerusalem in those days. Now Herod, when he saw Jesus, was greatly pleased; for he had long wished to see him because he had heard many things about him, and he hoped to see some sign performed by him. He questioned him at length, but Jesus answered him nothing. [Col. 0702] The chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing him. But after Herod, with his soldiers, had despised and mocked him, he clothed him in a white garment and sent him back to Pilate.

[Note: [Col. 0701] It adds *illum*, “him,” twice; so also the Greek text, αὐτόν.]

Then Herod and Pilate became friends with one another that day; for before this they had been enemies toward one another. But Pilate, having summoned the chief priests and the leaders of the people, said to them, “You have brought this man before me as one who turns the people away; and behold, having examined him before you, I have found in this man no charge among those of which you accuse him. [Col. 0703] Nor did Herod, for he sent him back to us; and behold, nothing deserving death has been done by him. Therefore I will chastise him and release him.” Now he had to release one to them at the feast. But the whole multitude cried out together, saying, “Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us”—a man who had been put in prison for a certain insurrection made in the city and for murder. Pilate again spoke to them, wishing to release Jesus. But they cried out, saying, “Crucify him!” And he said to them a third time, “For what evil has this man done? I find no cause of death in him. Therefore, after chastising him, I will [Col. 0704] release him.” But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that he be crucified; and their voices and those of the priests prevailed. Pilate then decided that their request should be granted. He released to them the man whom they requested, who had been put in prison for murder and insurrection; but Jesus he handed over to their will.

And as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus. And a multitude of people followed him, and women who were mourning and lamenting him.

[Note: [Col. 0703] So also the Cantabrigiensis manuscript: πλῆθος λαοῦ, “a multitude of people”; Vercelli: *multitudo ingens populi*, “a vast multitude of people.”]

[Col. 0705] But Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; rather, weep for yourselves and for your children. For behold, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nurse.’ Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall upon us,’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us.’ For if they do these things in the green wood, what will happen in the dry?”

And two other criminals were also being led with him to be crucified. And when they came to the place called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left. But Jesus [Col. 0706] said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And dividing his garments, they cast lots. And the people stood watching. The leaders also mocked him with them, saying, “He saved others; let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.” The soldiers too mocked him, coming up and offering him vinegar, and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.” And there was also an inscription written over him in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew letters: “This is the King of the Jews.”

One of the [Col. 0707] criminals hanging there blasphemed him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us.” But the other answered, rebuking him and saying, “Do you not fear God, since you are under the same condemnation? And we indeed justly, for we receive what our deeds deserve; but this man has done nothing evil.” And he said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” And Jesus said to him, “Truly I say to you, today you shall be with me in Paradise.”

Now it was about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour. The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in the middle. And Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said, “Father, into your [Col. 0708] hands I commend my spirit.” Having said this, he expired. But when the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying, “Truly this man was righteous.” And all the crowd who had gathered together for this spectacle, seeing the things that happened, returned beating their breasts. But all his acquaintances stood at a distance, and the women who had followed him from Galilee, seeing these things.

And behold, there was a man named Joseph, a councillor, a good and righteous man. He had not consented to their counsel and actions. He was from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, and [Col. 0709] himself awaited the kingdom of God.

[Note: [Col. 0707] So also the Cantabrigiensis manuscript: Ἀριμαθίας.]

This man went to Pilate and requested the body of Jesus. And having taken it down, he wrapped it in linen and laid him in a hewn tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.

[Note: [Col. 0709] It adds *in*, “in”; likewise the Cantabrigiensis manuscript, ἐν.]

And it was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was dawning. The women who had come with him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how the body of Jesus had been laid. And returning, they prepared spices and ointments; and on the Sabbath indeed they rested, according to the commandment.

But on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came [Col. 0710] to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and others with them. And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb. And upon entering, they did not find the body of Jesus. And while they were perplexed about this, behold, two men stood beside them in shining clothing. But as they were afraid and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee, saying that the Son of Man must be [Col. 0711] handed over into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise again on the third day.” And they remembered his words.

And returning from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest. Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary of James, and the others with them, who told these things to the apostles. But their words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.

[Note: [Col. 0711] So also the Greek text: ἀπίστουν, “they disbelieved.”]

But Peter rose and ran to the tomb; and stooping down, he saw the linen cloths lying alone, and went away wondering to himself at what had happened. And behold, two of them were going that same day to a [Col. 0712] village, sixty stadia from Jerusalem, named Emmaus. And they were speaking with one another about all these things which had happened.

[Note: [Col. 0711] It adds *in*, “in”; so also the Greek text, ἐν.]

And it came to pass, while they were conversing and discussing together, that Jesus himself, drawing near, went with them. But their eyes were restrained, so that they did not recognize him. And he said to them, “What are these words that you are exchanging with one another as you walk and are sad?” And one of them, whose name was Cleophas, answered and said to him, “Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem and have not known the things that have happened there in these days?” He said to them, “What things?” And they said to him, “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, [Col. 0713] who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people; how our chief priests and leaders handed him over to a sentence of death and crucified him. But we were hoping that he was the one about to redeem Israel; and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened. Yet certain women of our company astonished us: they went early to the tomb, and, not finding his body, came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who say that he is alive. And some of our number went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but him they did [Col. 0714] not see.”

[Note: [Col. 0713] So also the Greek text: εἶδον, “they saw.”]

And he said to them, “Foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and thus enter into his glory?” And beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

And they drew near to the village to which they were going, and he acted as though he would go farther. But they urged him, saying, “[Col. 0715] Stay with us, because it is toward evening and the day has already declined.” And he went in to remain with them. And it came to pass, while he reclined with them, that he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. Their eyes were opened and they recognized him; and he became invisible to them.

[Note: [Col. 0715] And so also the Greek text: ἄφαντος ἐγένετο, “he became unseen.”]

And they said to one another, “Was not our heart burning within us while he spoke to us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?” And they rose that same hour and returned to Jerusalem, where they found the eleven apostles gathered together and those who were with them [Col. 0716] saying, “The Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon.” And they themselves recounted what had happened on the road, and how they recognized him in the breaking of bread.

While they were speaking these things, Jesus himself stood in their midst and said to them, “Peace to you; it is I. Do not be afraid.” But they were troubled and terrified, thinking that they saw a spirit. And he said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? See my hands and my feet, that I am myself. Touch me and see; for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, [Col. 0717] as you see that I have.”

[Note: [Col. 0715] It adds *illi*, “to them”; so also the Greek text, αὐτῶν. Brixianus supports this. In the same place, *ipse*, “he himself”; and so also the Cantabrigiensis manuscript, αὐτός.]

[Note: [Col. 0715] It adds *quare*, “why”; likewise the Greek text, διατί.]

And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and feet. But while they still did not believe because of joy and were wondering, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?” And they offered him a portion of roasted fish and a honeycomb. And taking it, he ate before them. And he said to them, “These are the words which I spoke to you while I was still with you: that all things written concerning me in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled.” Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures. And he said to them, “For thus it is written, [Col. 0718] and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day; and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. You are witnesses of all these things. And behold, I send upon you the promise of my Father; but remain in this city, Jerusalem, until you are clothed with power from on high.”

[Note: [Col. 0717] So also the Greek text: δύναμιν, “power.”]

And he led them out as far as Bethany, and, lifting up his hands, blessed them.

[Note: [Col. 0717] And so also the Greek text: αὐτούς, “them.”]

And it came to pass, while he was blessing them, that he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven. And they, worshipping him, returned [Col. 0719] to Jerusalem with great joy. And they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

[Note: [Col. 0719] Thus the codex and Cant. “The Gospel according to Luke is completed; that according to Mark begins.”] THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE ENDS. + THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MARK BEGINS.

CODEX CORBEIENSIS.

[Col. 0501]

CHAPTER I.

[Col. 0501]

1. Since indeed many have undertaken to arrange an account of the things fulfilled among us.

[Col. 0502] 5. And his wife was of the daughters.

10. The people were praying outside.

[Col. 0503] 13. And the Angel of the Lord said to him, saying: Do not fear . . . for behold, your supplication has been heard.

17. and the unbelieving to the wisdom of the righteous.

[Col. 0504] 19. and said to him: For I am the angel Gabriel, who stand.

20. because you do not believe my words.

[Col. 0505] 28. The Angel, having entered to her, blessed her and said to her . . . among women.

29. [Note: [Col. 0506] Gat. “But she, when she had seen [him], was troubled.”] But she, when she saw him, was moved at his entrance, and was considering why he had thus blessed [Col. 0506] her.

34. For I do not know a man.

35. The Holy Spirit shall come upon you . . . shall overshadow me—read, “you.” The Holy One that shall be born shall be called.

[Col. 0507] 36. Who was called barren.

37. For no word is impossible with God.

38. Let it happen to me according to your word. The Angel departed from her.

[Col. 0508] 39. Into a city of Judaea.

45. For all things that were spoken [Note: [Col. 0508] Gat. “are,” omitting “to you.”] to you by the Lord shall be fulfilled.

[Col. 0509] 50. His mercy [Note: [Col. 0509] Gat. “from generation unto generations.”] from generation unto generation.

51. In the thought of their heart.

54. His servant, [Note: [Col. 0510] So also Gat.] mindful of mercy. + A later hand adds, “his.”

59. On the eighth day, when they came to circumcise . . . and [Col. 0510] they called him Zachariah by his father’s name.

61. They said to her: There is no one called by this name. A later hand adds, “in your kindred.”

63. [Note: [Col. 0510] Gat. “and, asking for [a writing tablet], received,” etc.] And he received a writing tablet and wrote . . . And all wondered.

[Col. 0511] 64. And immediately his tongue was loosed and his mouth was opened.

66. [Note: [Col. 0512] Gat. “What do you think?”] What then will this child be?

70. As he spoke through the mouth of the holy Prophets, [Col. 0512] who have been from of old.

71. And he delivered us from our enemies.

72. And to remember his holy covenant.

[Col. 0513] 77. To give knowledge to his people.

CHAPTER II.

1. [Note: [Col. 0513] Gat. “that a census might be registered,” later hand, “that they might enroll themselves.”] That the whole world might enroll itself.

2. [Note: [Col. 0514] Gat., first corrections: “this registration.”] This [Note: [Col. 0514] So also Gat., in its second corrections.] enrollment + was first made by the Governor.

4. Of the house [Note: [Col. 0514] So also Gat.] and family of David. +
