they arrived at the land of Gennesar-

54. et.

> [Note: Col. 0769. Gat. and Mm.: “And when they had come out … the men of that place recognized him, and …” Vulgate: “And when they had come out … they recognized him, and …” [Col. 0770.]]

When they came out of the boat, immediately they recognized

55. him. And, going around that entire region, they began to bring all those who were ill upon pallets; for they carried them about wherever they heard Jesus to be.

56. And wherever

> [Note: Col. 0770. Gat.: “entered.” Mm.: “enters … into towns and streets.” Vulgate: “entered … or towns, in the streets.”]

he entered into towns, or fields,

[Col. 0769]

or cities, they placed the sick in the marketplace and the streets, and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and all who touched [it] were healed.

## CHAPTER VII

1. And Pharisees and certain scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.

2. And when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with unclean—that is, unwashed—hands, … found fault.

3. The Pharisees … and all the Jews do not eat

> [Note: Col. 0769. Adds “bread,” likewise Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἄρτον, “bread.”]

bread unless they wash their hands at once, holding to

[Col. 0771]

the tradition of the elders;

4. and, from the marketplace,

> [Note: Col. 0771. Adds “when they come,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὅταν ἔλθωσιν, “when they come.” Brix. has instead: “and returning.”]

when they have come, they do not eat unless they have been washed. And there are many other things which they have received as traditions: washings of cups, jars, pots, and beds.

5. And the Pharisees and scribes question him, saying: “Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unclean hands?”

6. But he answered and said: “Isaiah rightly prophesied concerning you hypocrites,

> [Note: Col. 0771. According to Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ εἶπεν, “and he said.”]

who said:

> [Note: Col. 0771. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἀγαπᾷ, “loves.”]

‘This people love me with their lips, but their heart is far from

[Col. 0771]

7. me. But in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of men;

8. washing jars and cups, and doing many other things

> [Note: Col. 0771. According to the order of Codex Cantabrigiensis: τοιαῦτα πολλὰ ποιεῖτε, ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολήν, “you do many such things, abandoning the commandment.”]

like these, abandoning the commandment of God, and holding to the tradition of men.”

9. And he said to them: “You finely make void the commandment of God, in order to establish your tradition.

10.

> [Note: Col. 0771. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: στήσητε, “you may establish.”]

For Moses said: ‘Honor your father and your mother’; and, ‘Whoever curses

> [Note: Col. 0771. Thus also the Greek text: πατέρα, “father.”]

father or mother shall surely die.’

11. But you say: ‘If a man says to his father or mother, “Gift,

[Col. 0773]

(that is, an offering), by which you may have been benefited from me”:

12. you no longer permit [him] to do anything for [his]

> [Note: Col. 0773. After “father,” “his” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

father

13. or mother,’ rejecting the word of God through your

> [Note: Col. 0773. Adds “foolish,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τῇ μωρᾷ, “foolish.”]

foolish tradition which you have handed down; and you do many similar things.”

14. And, calling the crowd to him again, he said to them: “Hear me, all of you, and understand.

15. There is nothing

> [Note: Col. 0773. According to the Greek text: ἔξωθεν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, “outside the person.”]

outside a person which, entering into him, can defile him; but the things which proceed from a person, those are what defile a person.

16. If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”

17. And, when he had entered a house

[Col. 0773]

away from the crowd, his disciples asked him about the saying.

18. And he said to them: “Are you also without understanding? Do you not understand that

> [Note: Col. 0773. Gat.: “everything which is from outside.” Vulgate: “because everything [which is] outside …”]

everything which enters a person from outside cannot defile him?

19.

> [Note: Col. 0773. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οὐ γάρ, “for not.”]  
> [Note: Col. 0773. Gat.: “because it does not enter his heart, but goes into the stomach and goes out into the privy, purifying.” Vulgate: “because it does not enter into his heart, but goes into the stomach and goes out into the privy, purifying.”]

For it does not enter into his heart, but into his stomach, and goes out into the privy, cleansing all foods, and goes out into a channel.

20. And he said: “The things which come out of a person, those

> [Note: Col. 0774. Gat.: “defile.” Vulgate: “make common.”]

defile a person.

21. For from within, from the hearts of people, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries,

22.

> [Note: Col. 0773. According to the order of Codex Cantabrigiensis.]  
> [Note: Col. 0773. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: πλεονεξία, “covetousness”; δόλος, “deceit”; πονηρία, “wickedness”; ἀσέλγεια, “licentiousness”; βλασφημίαι, “blasphemies.”]

thefts, fornications, murders, covetousness,

[Col. 0775]

wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride,

23. foolishness. All these evil things proceed from within and defile a person.”

24. And rising, he went into the region of

> [Note: Col. 0775. After “Tyre,” “and Sidon” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

Tyre; and, when he entered a house, he wished no one to know it, but could not

25. remain hidden. For a woman … whose little … had an unclean spirit came and fell at his feet.

26. Now the woman was Greek,

> [Note: Col. 0775. Thus the Greek text: δὲ … Ἑλληνίς, “but … Greek.”]

a Syrophoenician by birth. And she begged him to cast the demon out of

27. her daughter. And he said to her: “Let the children first be satisfied;

[Col. 0775]

for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”

28. But she answered and said to him: “Yes, Lord; for even

> [Note: Col. 0775. Gat.: “the little dogs eat.” Vulgate: “the little dogs eat.”]

the little dogs beneath the table eat from the crumbs of the children.”

29. And he said

> [Note: Col. 0775. Gat.: “Jesus said to her: Because … and [it] went out.” Vulgate: “he said to her: Because … [it] went out.” [Col. 0776.]]

to her: “Go; because of this word, the demon has gone out of your daughter.”

30. And, when she went home, she found the demon gone out and her daughter lying on the bed.

31. And again, departing from the region of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of the Decapolis.

32. And they brought to him a deaf

> [Note: Col. 0776. Gat.: “and tongue-tied.” Vulgate: “and mute.”]

and mute man, begging him

[Col. 0777]

to lay hands upon him.

33. And, taking him apart from the crowd,

> [Note: Col. 0777. According to the order of Codex Cantabrigiensis: πτύσας ἔβαλε, “having spat, he put.”]

having spat, he put his fingers into his ears and touched his tongue;

34. and, looking up to heaven, he groaned and said to him: “Epita,” that is, “Be opened.”

35. And his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke plainly, so that all were astonished.

36. And he commanded them to tell no one. The more he commanded them, … the more they proclaimed [it];

37. and they were all the more astonished, saying: “He has done all things well:

> [Note: Col. 0777. Gat.: “does … does.” Vulgate: “has done … has done.”]

he makes the deaf hear and the mute

[Col. 0777]

speak.”

## CHAPTER VIII

1. In those

> [Note: Col. 0777. Thus also the Greek text: δέ, “but.”]

days again, when there was a great crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called the disciples and said

2. to them: “I have compassion on this crowd, because already [for] three days … that [they are] here … and they have nothing to eat;

> [Note: Col. 0777. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς εἰσὶν ἀφ’ ὅτου ὧδε εἰσίν, “they have already been here three days.”]

3. and to send them away fasting to their homes, … lest they fail on the way; for some of them have come from far away.”

4. And … his disciples answered: “Whence can anyone satisfy so many [people] with bread here in a deserted place?”

5. And he asked them: “How many loaves do you have?” They

[Col. 0779]

said: “Seven.”

6. And he commanded the crowd to recline on the ground. And, taking the seven loaves, after giving thanks, he broke [them] and gave [them] to his disciples to set before [the crowd]; and they set [them] before the crowd.

7. And they had a few little fish; and he blessed these also and commanded [them]

8. to be set [before them]. And they ate and were satisfied; and they took up seven hampers of fragments left over.

> [Note: Col. 0779. Thus also the Greek text: κλασμάτων, “of fragments.”]

9. Now those who ate were about four thousand people; and he dismissed them.

10. And immediately he embarked with his disciples and came into the district of

[Col. 0779]

> [Note: Col. 0779. Thus also St Jerome, together with most other codices, as Zacharias Chrysopolitanus testifies in the *Monotessaron*. Codex Cantabrigiensis Latin has *Magidan*.]

Magedan.

11. And the Pharisees came out and be… to dispute with him, seeking from him a sign from hea… and testing him.

12. And, groaning in … spirit, he said: “Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen, I say to you, if a sign shall be given to this generation.”

13. And, leaving them, again having embarked, he departed across

14. the sea; and they forgot to take bread. … they had one loaf with them in the boat.

15. And he commanded

> [Note: Col. 0779. Gat.: “Jesus commanded them, saying: See, beware … of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and of leaven.” Vulgate: “he commanded them, saying: See and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven …”]

them, saying: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of Herod.”

16. And they reasoned with one another,

> [Note: Col. 0779. Before “that,” “saying” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

that

[Col. 0781]

they had no bread.

> [Note: Col. 0781. According to Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἶχαν, “they had,” in place of εἶχον.]

17. And, when Jesus knew, he said to them: “Why do you reason

> [Note: Col. 0781. Adds “in your hearts,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν.]

in your hearts because you have no bread? Do you not yet understand or perceive? Is your heart hardened?

18. Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember

19. when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand people, how many baskets of fragments did you take up?”

> [Note: Col. 0781. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οἱ δὲ εἶπον, “and they said.”]

And they said: “Twelve.”

20.

> [Note: Col. 0781. Gat.: “how.” Vulgate: “when.”]

When the seven [were] for the four thousand, how many hampers of fragments

[Col. 0781]

did you take up?” They said: “Seven.”

21. And

> [Note: Col. 0781. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: λέγει, “he says.”]

he said to them: “How do you not yet understand?”

22. And they came to Bethany, and brought to him a blind man, begging him to touch him.

23. And,

> [Note: Col. 0781. Gat.: “And taking the blind man’s hand, he led him … and, spitting … whether he saw anything.” Vulgate: “And taking the blind man by the hand, he led him out … and, spitting … whether he saw anything.” [Col. 0782.]]

taking the blind man by the hand, he led him outside the town; and, spitting upon his eyes, laid his hands upon him and asked him whether he saw anything.

24. And looking up, he said: “I see people, like trees, walking.”

25. Then laying his hand upon his eyes—and [sic in the Latin] he made him see—he was healed, so that he saw

[Col. 0783]

everything clearly.

26. And he sent him away to his home, saying: “Go home, and do not enter into the town, nor tell anyone.”

27. And Jesus went out with his disciples

> [Note: Col. 0783. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰς Καισάρειαν, “into Caesarea.”]

into Caesarea Philippi; and on the way he questioned his disciples,

> [Note: Col. 0783. After “saying,” “to them” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

saying: “Who do people say that I am?”

28. But they answered him, saying: “John the Baptist; others, Elijah; others, as one of the prophets.”

29. And he questioned them: “But who do you say that I am?” And Peter, answering, said to him: “You are the Christ.”

30. And he charged them not to tell anyone about

[Col. 0783]

him.

31. And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, rulers, and scribes, be killed, and rise again after the third day.

32. And he spoke the saying openly. And Peter, taking hold of him, began to rebuke him, saying: “Lord, be merciful; for this shall not be.”

33. But he, turning and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, saying: “Get behind me,

> [Note: Col. 0783. Gat.: “Satan … but the things of people.” Vulgate: “Satan … but the things that are of people.”]

Satan, for you do not think the things of God, but the things of people.”

34. And, having called the crowd together with his disciples,

> [Note: Col. 0783. After “said,” “to them” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

he said: “If anyone

> [Note: Col. 0784. Gat.: “wishes to come after me, let him deny himself.”]

wishes to follow

[Col. 0785]

me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.

35. For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it; but whoever loses his life

> [Note: Col. 0785. After “his life,” “for my sake” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.]

for the sake of the Gospel shall save it.

36. For what does it profit a person if he gains

> [Note: Col. 0785. Gat.: “the whole world.” Vulgate: “the entire world.”]

the whole age [or world] and forfeits his life?

37. Or what exchange

> [Note: Col. 0785. Thus also the Greek text: ἀντάλλαγμα, “exchange.”]

will a person give for his life? [The Latin reads *pro animam* (sic).]

38. For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in an adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him,

[Col. 0785]

when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”

39. And he said to them: “Amen, I say to you: there are some standing here

> [Note: Col. 0785. Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: μετ’ ἐμοῦ, “with me.”]

with me who shall not taste death until they see the kingdom of God coming in power.”

## CHAPTER IX
1. And after six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John, and led them apart, by themselves, up a high mountain; and he was transfigured before them.  
2. And his garments became shining, exceedingly white, as—  
3. —snow. And Elijah was seen … with Moses; and they were speaking with Jesus.  
4. And Peter said to Jesus: “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. … if you wish, let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”  
5. For he did not know what he was saying; for they were terrified with fear.  
6. And a cloud came, overshadowing them; and a voice came from the cloud, saying: “This is my most dear Son: hear him.”  
7. And immediately, looking round, they saw no one else, except … him.  
8. And as they were coming down from the mountain, he instructed them to tell no one what they had seen, except when the Son of Man should have risen from the dead.  
9. And they kept the saying among themselves, asking what it meant, “when he should have risen from the dead.”  
10. And they questioned him, saying: “Why then do the scribes say: … must come?”  
11. Answering them, he said: “Elijah, coming first, will restore all things; and how is it written concerning the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?  
12. But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wished, as it is written concerning …”  
13. And when he came to the disciples, he saw a great crowd …  
14. … and immediately, when they saw him, the whole crowd was alarmed … and ran up and greeted him.  
15. And he asked the scribes: “What were you disputing among yourselves?”  
16. And … answered …: “Teacher, I brought … my … son … having an unclean spirit; …  
17. whenever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams, gnashes his teeth, and becomes rigid; and I told your disciples to cast it out, but they were unable to cast it out.”  
18. And answering, he said to them: “O unbelieving generation, how long shall I be … with you? How long shall I endure …? Bring him … to me.” And they brought … him. And when he saw …, the spirit disturbed the boy; and, falling to the ground, he rolled about, foaming.  
19. And Jesus asked the boy’s father, saying: “How long has this been happening to him?” And he answered and said: “From childhood.  
20. And it has often thrown him into fire … and into waters, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us, Lord, having compassion on us.”  
21. And Jesus said to him: “What is this, ‘if you can’? If you can believe, all things are possible to the one who believes.”  
22. Immediately the father of the boy cried out with tears and said: “I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.”  
23. And when Jesus saw that a crowd was gathering, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying: “I command you, deaf and mute spirit: come out of him, and do not enter into him again.”  
24. And crying out, and convulsing him severely, it came out of him; and he became as though dead, so that many said that he was dead.  
25. But Jesus, taking his hand, raised him up; and he arose.  
26. And when he had entered the house, his disciples asked him privately: “Why were we unable to cast it out?”  
27. And he said to them: “This kind of demon can come out by no other means except by prayer and fasting.”  
28. And departing from there, they travelled through Galilee, and he did not wish anyone  
29. to know. For he was teaching his disciples and saying to them: “For the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and after the third day he will rise.”  
30. But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to question him.  
31. And they came to Capernaum. And when he was at home, he asked them: “What were you discussing on the way?”  
32. But they were silent; for they had been disputing among themselves on the way which of them was the greater.  
33. And when he had sat down, he called the twelve and said to them: “If anyone wishes to be first, let him become the lowliest of all and the servant of all.”  
34. And taking a child, he placed it in their midst; and, taking it in his arms, he said to them:  
35. “Whoever receives one of such children in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives not me, but him who sent me.”  
36. John answered and said: “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, who does not follow with us, and we forbade him.”  
37. But he answered and said: “Do not forbid him; for there is no one who performs a mighty work in my name and will be able to speak evil of me.  
38. For whoever is not against you is for you.  
39. For whoever gives you a cup of water in my name, because you belong to Christ, amen, I tell you, will not lose his reward.  
40. And whoever causes one of these little ones among you who have faith to stumble—it would be good for him if a millstone turned by an ass were put around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.  
41. And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is good for you to enter life maimed, rather than, having two hands, to be thrown into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,  
42. where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.  
43. And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is good for you to enter eternal life lame, rather than, having two feet, to be thrown into Gehenna, where the fire is unquenchable,  
44. where their worm does not die and their fire is not quenched.  
45. And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out: it is good for you to enter the kingdom of God one-eyed, rather than, having two eyes, to be thrown into Gehenna,  
46. where their worms do not die and the fire is not quenched.  
47. [Note: Before *every*, “for everyone will be salted with fire” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek and Latin, and in the Greek manuscripts Em. and Cov. I cited by Mill.] Every sacrifice shall be salted.  
48. And salt is good; but if salt becomes tasteless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace among yourselves.

### Apparatus to the preceding chapter

- Verse 1 [Col. 0785]: Gat. reads *adsumpsit Petrum* (“took Peter”); the Vulgate reads *assumit Jesus Petrum* (“Jesus takes Peter”).
- Verse 2 [Col. 0786]: Gat. reads *candida, velut* (“white, like”); the Vulgate, *candida nimis, velut* (“exceedingly white, like”). Gat. has *in montem altum* (“onto a high mountain”); the Vulgate, *seorsum solos* (“apart, alone”).
- Verse 5 [Col. 0787]: Gat. reads *in timore exterriti* (“terrified in fear”); the Vulgate, *timore exterriti* (“terrified by fear”).
- Verse 10 [Col. 0787]: before *Scribae* (“scribes”), *Pharisaei* (“Pharisees”) is absent, likewise in the Greek text.
- Verse 12 [Col. 0788]: Gat. reads *Helias jam venit* (“Elijah has already come”); the Vulgate, *Elias venit* (“Elijah comes/has come”).
- Verse 13 [Col. 0787]: after *discipulos* (“disciples”), *suos* (“his”) is absent, likewise in the Greek text. The Greek text has *πρὸς αὐτούς* (“to them”).
- Verse 14 [Col. 0789]: Gat. reads *omnis populus videns eum … occurrentes* (“all the people, seeing him … running to meet [him]”); the Vulgate, “… *videns Jesum … accurrentes*” (“… seeing Jesus … running up”).
- Verse 16 [Col. 0789]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ* (“answered him”).
- Verse 17 [Col. 0789]: Gat. reads *spiritum immundum; qui* (“an unclean spirit, which”); the Vulgate, *spiritum mutum; qui* (“a mute spirit, which”). [Col. 0790]: Gat. reads *duxi discipulis* (“I brought [him] to [your] disciples”); the Vulgate, *dixi discipulis* (“I told [your] disciples”).
- Verse 18 [Col. 0789]: Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *ejicere illum*, Greek *ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό* (“to cast him out”), from Matthew. [Col. 0789]: before *spiritus* (“the spirit”), *statim* (“immediately”) is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis. [Col. 0790]: Gat. reads *discerpsit eum, conturbans: et elisus* (“tore him, convulsing [him]; and, thrown down”); the Vulgate, *conturbavit illum: et elisus* (“convulsed him; and, thrown down”).
- Verse 22 [Col. 0789]: before *credenti* (“to the believer”), *sunt* (“are”) is absent, though it is present in the Greek text.
- Verse 24 [Col. 0791]: thus also the Greek text, *ὅτι ἐπισυντρέχει* (“that [the crowd] was running together”). Gat. reads *Surde et mute spiritus, tibi praecipio* (“Deaf and mute spirit, I command you”); the Vulgate, *Surde et mute spiritus, ego praecipio tibi* (“Deaf and mute spirit, I command you”).
- Verse 33 [Col. 0793]: after *enim* (“for”), *in via* (“on the way”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic [version].
- Verse 35 [Col. 0793]: Gat. reads *conspexisset, dixit* (“when he had looked upon [him], he said”); the Vulgate, *complexus esset, ait* (“when he had embraced [him], he said”).
- Verse 38 [Col. 0793]: after *prohibere* (“forbid”), *eum* (“him”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. Thus also the Greek text, *δυνήσεται* (“will be able”).
- Verse 40 [Col. 0794]: Gat. reads *aquae frigidae tantum in … quia non perdet* (“only cold water in … because he shall not lose”); the Vulgate, *aquae in … non perdet* (“water in … he shall not lose”).
- Verse 43 [Col. 0795]: Gat. reads *mitti in gehennam ignis inextinguibilis, ubi* (“to be cast into the Gehenna of unquenchable fire, where”).
- Verse 46 [Col. 0795]: after *gehennam* (“Gehenna”), *ignis* (“of fire”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 48 [Col. 0795]: before *omnis* (“every”), “for everyone shall be salted with fire” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek and Latin, and in the Greek manuscripts Em. and Cov. I cited by Mill. Gat. reads *igni salietur* (“shall be salted with fire”); the Vulgate, *igne salietur* (“shall be salted with fire”).
- Verse 49 [Col. 0796]: Gat. reads *insalsum … condietur … salem, et* (“tasteless … shall be seasoned … salt, and”); the Vulgate, *insalsum … condietis … sal, et* (“tasteless … will you season … salt, and”).

## CHAPTER X

1. And rising from there, he came into the borders of Judea … Jordan … and again a crowd came to him, and, as was his custom, he again taught them.  
2. [Note: After *and*, “the Pharisees came up” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] And they questioned him: “Is it lawful for a man to dismiss his wife?” testing him.  
3. Answering them, he said: “What did Moses command you?”  
4. They said: “He permitted a certificate of divorce to be written, and to dismiss …”  
5. Jesus said to them: “Because of the hardness of your heart he wrote this commandment for you.  
6. But from the beginning of creation God made them male and female.  
7. [Note: Gat.: *them God, saying: Therefore*. Vulg.: *them God. Therefore*.] ‘For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife;  
8. and the two shall become one flesh.’ Thus they are no longer two, but one flesh.  
9. Therefore what God has joined together, let no human being separate.”  
10. And again, in the house, the disciples questioned him concerning this.  
11. And he said to them: “If a man dismisses his wife and marries another, he commits adultery against her.  
12. And if a woman leaves her husband and marries another, she commits adultery against him. Likewise, he who marries a woman dismissed by her husband commits adultery.”  
13. And they brought children to him, that he might touch them. But his disciples rebuked those who brought them.  
14. When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said to them: “Allow the children to come to me, and do not prevent them; for to such belongs the kingdom of God.  
15. Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child shall not enter it.”  
16. And in his lap, he blessed them.  
17. And as he was setting out, one man ran up, fell on his knees, and asked him, saying: “Good Teacher, what shall I do in order to possess eternal life?”  
18. But Jesus, looking at him, said: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except the one God.  
19. You know the commandments.” He said: “Which?” “You shall not commit adultery; you shall not murder; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; you shall not deny; honour your father and your mother.”  
20. He answered and said to him: “Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth. What do I still lack?”  
21. Jesus, looking at him, loved him and said to him: “One thing is lacking to you: go, sell whatever you have and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and, taking up the cross, come, follow me.”  
22. But saddened by this saying, he went away sorrowful; for he possessed great wealth.  
23. And Jesus, looking around, said to his disciples: “How difficult those who have riches will enter the kingdom of God!”  
25. It is easier for a camel to enter through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”  
24. But the disciples were alarmed at his words. Jesus, answering again, said to them: “Children, how difficult those who have riches, or who trust in them, will enter the kingdom of God!”  
26. But they were all the more astonished, saying among themselves: “Then who can be saved?”  
27. Jesus looked at them and said: “With human beings it is impossible, but with God it is possible.”  
28. And Peter began to say to him: “See, we have left everything and followed you.”  
29. Jesus answered and said: “Amen, I tell you: there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or mother, or children, or fields, for my sake and for the sake of the Gospel,  
30. who will not receive a hundredfold in this present time: whoever has left house, and brothers, and sisters, and mother, and children, and fields, with persecutions … and in the age to come will receive eternal life,  
31. … but many who are first will be last, and the last first.”  
32. Now they were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus went before them, and they were alarmed. And taking the twelve again aside, he began to tell them what was going to happen to him.  
33. “For see, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes; and they will condemn him to death and hand him over  
34. to the Gentiles; and they will mock him, spit upon him, scourge him, and kill him; and after the third day he will rise.”  
35. And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him and said: “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”  
36. And he said to them: “What do you want me to do for you?”  
37. They said to him: “Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.”  
38. And Jesus answered and said to them: “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”  
39. But they said: “We are able.” Jesus said to them: “You will drink the cup which I am about to drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized;  
40. but to sit at my right hand or at my left is not mine to give; it is prepared for others by my Father.”  
41. When the other ten heard this, they began to be indignant with James and John.  
42. And Jesus called them and said to them: “You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.  
43. But it is not so among you. Rather, whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant,  
44. and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave.  
45. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”  
46. Then he came to Jericho; and as he was departing from there with his disciples and a great crowd, Bar-Timaeus, the blind son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road, begging.  
47. When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”  
48. Many rebuked him, telling him to be silent. But he cried out all the more: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”  
49. And Jesus stopped and ordered him to be called. They said to the blind man: “Take courage; rise,  
50. he is calling you.” He threw off his cloak, sprang up, and came to him.  
51. Jesus answered and said to him: “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him: “Lord … that I may see.”  
52. … said …: “Go; your faith has made you well.” And immediately he began to see, and followed him on the road.

### Apparatus to Chapter X

- Verse 2 [Col. 0797]: after *et* (“and”), “the Pharisees came up” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 7 [Col. 0797]: Gat. reads *illos Deus, dicens: Propter* (“them God, saying: For this reason”); the Vulgate, *eos Deus. Propter* (“them God. For this reason”). Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *suam* (“his own”), Greek *ἑαυτοῦ*.
- Verse 8 [Col. 0798]: Gat. reads *adhaerebit uxori suae* (“shall cleave to his wife”); the Vulgate, *adhaerebit ad uxorem suam* (“shall cleave to his wife”).
- Verse 14 [Col. 0799]: Gat. reads *regnum caelorum* (“kingdom of heaven”), with *Dei* (“of God”) in a later hand; the Vulgate reads *regnum Dei* (“kingdom of God”).
- Verse 17 [Col. 0799]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *λέγων* (“saying”).
- Verse 18 [Col. 0800]: Gat. reads *nisi solus Deus* (“except God alone”); the Vulgate, *nisi unus Deus* (“except one God”).
- Verse 19 [Col. 0799]: Codex Gothicus also adds *tuam* (“your”), Greek *σοῦ*.
- Verse 22 [Col. 0799]: Codex Gothicus also adds *hoc* (“this”), Greek *τούτῳ*.
- Verse 24 [Col. 0801]: Codex Cantabrigiensis places this verse after verse 24 [that is, it places verse 25 before verse 24]. Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *ejus* (“his”), Greek *αὐτοῦ*.
- Verse 28 [Col. 0801]: Gat. reads *secuti sumus te. Quid ergo erit nobis? Respondens* (“we have followed you. What then will there be for us? Answering”); the Vulgate, *secuti sumus te. Respondens* (“we have followed you. Answering”).
- Verse 30 [Col. 0801]: Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *qui autem reliquerit* (“but whoever has left”), Greek *ὃς δὲ ἀφῆκεν*. In the same place it has *domum* (“house”), also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek *οἰκίαν*.
- Verse 32 [Col. 0801]: after *et* (“and”), *stupebant, et sequentes* (“they were astonished, and those following”) is absent. Codex Cantabrigiensis reads *καὶ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο* (“and those following were afraid”): “and those following feared.”
- Verse 33 [Col. 0803]: Gat. reads *essent ventura* (“were about to happen”); the Vulgate, *essent ei eventura* (“were about to happen to him”). After *Scribis* (“scribes”), “and elders” is absent, also in the Greek text.
- Verse 37 [Col. 0803]: the Greek text also adds *ei* (“to him”), *αὐτῷ*. Gat. reads *et unus ad* (“and one at”); the Vulgate, *ut unus ad* (“that one at”).
- Verse 38 [Col. 0803]: Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *respondens* (“answering”), Greek *ἀποκριθείς*. Gat. reads *ego bibiturus sum* (“I am about to drink”); the Vulgate, *ego bibo* (“I drink”). Thus also the Greek text, *βάπτισμα ὅ* (“the baptism which”); Brix. has *baptismum, quo* (“the baptism with which”).
- Verse 39 [Col. 0803]: after *dixerunt* (“they said”), *ei* (“to him”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. [Col. 0804]: Gat. reads *Calicem, quem bibo* (“the cup which I drink”); the Vulgate, *Calicem quidem, quem ego bibo* (“indeed, the cup which I drink”).
- Verse 41 [Col. 0803]: *et* (“and”) is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 42 [Col. 0805]: according to the Greek text, *αὐτῶν* (“their”).
- Verse 43 [Col. 0805]: after *est* (“is”), *autem* (“however”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. The Greek text also adds *in vobis* (“among you”), *ἐν ὑμῖν*; likewise Codex Cantabrigiensis has *esse* (“to be”), *εἶναι*.
- Verse 46 [Col. 0805]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἔρχεται* (“comes”). Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἀπὸ ἐκεῖθεν μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν* (“from there with the disciples”). Codex Cantabrigiensis Latin has *Baritimias*; the Greek of the same codex has *Βαρτειμίας* (“Bartimaeus”).
- Verse 49 [Col. 0805]: according to Codex Cantabrigiensis, *οἱ δὲ λέγουσι τῷ τυφλῷ* (“and they say to the blind man”).
- Verse 50 [Col. 0805]: Gat. reads *vocat te Magister* (“the Teacher calls you”); the Vulgate, *vocat te* (“he calls you”).
- Verse 51 [Col. 0805]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *Κύριε Ῥαββεί* (“Lord, Rabboni”).

## CHAPTER XI

1. And when they drew near to Jerusalem and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,  
2. saying to them: “Go into the village opposite you; and immediately, when you enter it, you will find a colt tied, upon which no human being has sat. Untie it and bring it.  
3. And if anyone says to you, ‘Why are you untying the colt?’ say, ‘Its Lord has need of it,’ and immediately he will send it  
4. here.” Going out, they found the colt tied outside at a doorway in the street, and untied it.  
5. And some of those standing there said to them: “What are you doing, untying the colt?”  
6. And they told them as Jesus had instructed them; and they allowed them  
7. to bring the colt to Jesus. They spread their garments upon it, and he sat upon it.  
8. Many spread their garments on the road; others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.  
9. And those going before and those following cried out, saying: “Hosanna in the highest!  
10. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”  
11. And when he entered Jerusalem, into the temple, and looked around at everything, since the hour was already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve disciples.  
12. On the following day, when they had gone out from Bethany, he was hungry.  
13. Seeing from afar a fig tree with leaves, he came, perhaps to find something on it; but when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves—for it was not the season for figs.  
14. And he said to it: “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” And his disciples heard it.  
15. And they came again to Jerusalem. And when he entered the temple, he began to drive out those selling and buying in the temple; he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves.  
16. And he did not allow anyone to carry a vessel through  
17. the temple. And he taught, saying to them: “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”  
18. And when the chief priests and scribes heard it, they sought how to destroy him; for they feared the people, because the whole crowd was astonished at his teaching.  
19. And when evening came, he went out of the city.  
20. As the disciples passed by, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.  
21. And Peter, remembering, said to him: “Rabbi, look: the fig tree which you cursed has withered.”  
22. Jesus answered and said to them: “If you have faith,  
23. amen, I tell you: whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will happen, whatever he says will come about for him.  
24. Therefore I tell you: whatever you pray for and ask, believe that you will receive it, and it will be yours.  
25. And when you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive your sins.  
26. For if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive you your trespasses.”  
27. And they came again to Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, and elders came to him,  
28. and said to him: “By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?”  
29. Jesus answered and said to them: “I too will ask you one question; answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.  
30. Was John’s baptism from heaven or from human beings? Answer me.”  
31. But they deliberated among themselves, saying: “What shall we say? If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’  
32. But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ we fear the people; for everyone knew John to be truly a prophet.”  
33. Answering Jesus, they said: “We do not …” And Jesus said to them: “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

### Apparatus to Chapter XI

- Verse 1 [Col. 0807]: Codex Cantabrigiensis has *εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα* (“into Jerusalem”). Gat. reads *ad montem Oliveti* (“to the Mount of Olivet”); the Vulgate, *ad montem Olivarum* (“to the Mount of Olives”).
- Verse 2 [Col. 0807]: after *introeuntes* (“entering”), *illuc* (“there”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and Vercell. Gat. reads *introeuntes in illud* (“entering into it”); the Vulgate, *introeuntes illuc* (“entering there”).
- Verse 3 [Col. 0807]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *τί λύετε τὸν πῶλον* (“Why are you untying the colt?”), from Luke 19:33. [Col. 0808]: Gat. reads *Quid facitis hoc? Dicite* (“What are you doing, this? Say”); the Vulgate, *Quid facitis? Dicite* (“What are you doing? Say”).
- Verse 6 [Col. 0807]: after *dixerunt* (“they said”), *eis* (“to them”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 7 [Col. 0808]: Gat. reads *instraverunt* (“they spread [out]”); the Vulgate, *straverunt* (“they spread”).
- Verse 8 [Col. 0807]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἐστρώννυον* (“they were spreading”). Veron. has *in viam* (“on the road”), as does the Greek text, *εἰς τὴν ὁδόν*.
- Verse 10 [Col. 0809]: Codex Cantabrigiensis Latin has *Ossanna*, and Cantabrigiensis Greek, *Ὠσσαννᾶ* (“Hosanna”); in the same place, *in altissimis* (“in the highest”), as also the Greek text, *ἐν ὑψίστοις*.
- Verse 11 [Col. 0809]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *εἰσελθών* (“having entered”). Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *discipulis suis* (“his disciples”), Greek *μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ*, together with Bodl. 4 and 5 in Mill; in Veron. and Brix., *suis* (“his”) is absent.
- Verse 17 [Col. 0809]: before *domus* (“house”), *quia* (“because”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 20 [Col. 0811]: Gat. reads *cum transfretassent* (“when they had crossed over”); the Vulgate, *cum mare transirent* (“when they were crossing the sea”).
- Verse 22 [Col. 0811]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *εἰ ἔχετε* (“if you have”).
- Verse 25 [Col. 0811]: thus also the Greek text, *προσευχόμενοι* (“praying”).
- Verse 29 [Col. 0813]: before *respondete* (“answer”), *et* (“and”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 30 [Col. 0813]: thus also the Greek text, *τὸ βάπτισμα* (“the baptism”).
- Verse 31 [Col. 0813]: Gat. reads *dicet nobis: Quare* (“he will say to us: Why”); the Vulgate, *dicet: Quare* (“he will say: Why”).
- Verse 32 [Col. 0811]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἔρχεται* (“comes”).
- Verse 33 [Col. 0814]: Gat. reads *haec facio* (“I do these things”); the Vulgate, *haec faciam* (“I shall do these things”).

## CHAPTER XII

1. And he began to speak …: “A man planted a vineyard, surrounded it with a hedge, dug a winepress, and built a tower …; he leased it to tenant-farmers and went abroad.  
2. And he sent to the tenant-farmers …  
3. [Note: Codex Cantabrigiensis likewise has *and* (*καί*).] And they seized …, beat him, and sent him away empty to him.  
4. Again he sent another servant to them; and they wounded him on the head and treated him shamefully.  
5. And he sent another servant; they killed him; and many others—some they beat and others they killed.  
6. Still having one beloved only son, he sent him last of all, saying: ‘Perhaps they will respect my son.’  
7. But the tenant-farmers said among themselves: ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’  
8. And seizing him, they killed him and threw him outside the vineyard.  
9. What then will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come, destroy the tenant-farmers, and give the vineyard to others.  
10. Have you not read this Scripture: ‘The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner.  
11. This was done by the Lord; it is wonderful in our eyes’?”  
12. And they sought to seize him, but feared the crowd; for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them. And leaving him, they went away.  
13. And they sent some Pharisees and Herodians, to entrap him in speech.  
14. They came and questioned him: “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and are not concerned about anyone; for you do not regard the person of human beings, but teach the way of God in truth. Tell us, then: is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?  
15. But Jesus, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them: “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”  
16. They brought one. And he said to them: “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said: “Caesar’s.”  
17. Jesus answered and said to them: “Render, therefore, to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” And they marvelled at him.  
18. And Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no resurrection; and they questioned him,  
19. saying: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.  
20. Now there were among us seven brothers; the first took a wife, died, and left no offspring.  
21. The next took her and died, and he too left no offspring; and the third likewise.  
22. The seven took her and left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.  
23. In the resurrection, then, when she rises, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.”  
24. Jesus answered and said to them: “Because of this you are in error, knowing neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.”  
25. For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.  
26. But concerning the dead, that they rise: have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God said to him: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?  
27. He is not God of the dead but of the living. You are greatly in error.”  
28. And one of the scribes came forward. Having heard them disputing, and seeing that he had answered them well, he asked him: “Which is the first commandment?”  
29. Jesus said to him: “The first of all: ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God is one;  
30. and you shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, from your whole soul, from all your strength, and from your whole power;  
31. and your neighbour as yourself.’ This is the great commandment.”  
32. And the scribe said to him: “Truly, Teacher, you have spoken well: God is one, and there is no other besides him.  
33. And to love him with the whole heart, with all power, and with all strength, and to love one’s neighbour as oneself, is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”  
34. And when Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him: “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question him any longer.  
35. And Jesus answered, teaching in the temple: “How do the scribes say that the Christ is David’s son?  
36. David himself says in the Holy Spirit: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies as a footstool for your feet.’  
37. David himself calls him God; how then is he his son?” And the great crowd listened to him gladly.  
38. And while teaching, he said to them: “Beware of the scribes, who wish to walk in long robes, be greeted in the marketplace,  
39. and have the first seats in synagogues and the first couches at dinners;  
40. who devour the houses of widows and orphans, praying at length as a pretext. These will receive a greater punishment.”  
41. And sitting opposite the treasury (*gajophylacium*), he watched how the crowd put money into the treasury; and many rich persons put in  
42. much. But when one poor widow came, she put in two small coins, which make a quadrans.  
43. And calling his disciples, he said to them: “Amen, I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all those who have put a gift into the treasury.  
44. For all put in from what was surplus to them; but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had—that is, all her livelihood.”

- Verse 3 [Col. 0813]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *καί* (“and”). Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *ad eum* (“to him”), Greek *πρὸς αὐτόν*.
- Verse 5 [Col. 0815]: before *alium* (“another”), *iterum* (“again”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and in the Persian and Coptic versions; the same codex also adds *servum* (“a servant”), Greek *δοῦλον*.
- Verse 6 [Col. 0815]: the Syriac, Persian, and Arabic versions also add *forsitan* (“perhaps”), from Luke.

- Verse 14 [Col. 0815]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν* (“they questioned him”). Gat. reads *doces. Dic ergo nobis: Licet* (“you teach. Tell us therefore: Is it lawful”); the Vulgate, *doces: Licet* (“you teach: Is it lawful”). Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *Dic ergo nobis: Si* (“Tell us therefore: Whether”), Greek *εἰπὲ οὖν ἡμῖν εἰ*. After *non* (“not”), *dabimus* (“shall we give [it]”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 15 [Col. 0815]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς* (“but Jesus”).
- Verse 16 [Col. 0817]: after *attulerunt* (“they brought”), *ei* (“to him”) is absent, likewise in the Greek text.
- Verse 19 [Col. 0817]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *καὶ γυναῖκα ἔχῃ* (“and has a wife”).
- Verse 20 [Col. 0817]: Gat. reads *erunt, tanquam* (“will be, as”); the Vulgate, *sunt, sicut* (“are, like”). Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds *aput nos* (“among us”), Greek *παρ᾽ ἡμῖν*, from Matthew.
- Verse 25 [Col. 0817]: Gat. reads *erunt, tanquam* (“will be, as”); the Vulgate, *sunt, sicut* (“are, like”).
- Verse 27 [Col. 0819]: Gat. reads *viventium* (“of living persons”); the Vulgate, *vivorum* (“of the living”).
- Verse 28 [Col. 0819]: thus also the Greek text, *προσελθών* (“having come forward”). Gat. reads *conquirentes, quoniam … eum, Magister, quod est* (“disputing, because … him, Teacher, which is”); the Vulgate, *conquirentes; et videns, quoniam … cum, quod esset* (“disputing; and seeing that … with him, which was”).
- Verse 29 [Col. 0819]: before *primum* (“first”), *quia* (“because”) is absent, and later *est* (“is”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. Thus also the Greek text, *ἡμῶν* (“our”).
- Verse 30 [Col. 0819]: after *tuis* (“your”), “and with all your mind” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.
- Verse 33 [Col. 0819]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, *ἐξ ὅλης τῆς δυνάμεως* (“with all [one’s] strength”).
- Verse 38 [Col. 0821]: thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *ὁ δὲ διδάσκων ἅμα ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε* (“and while teaching, at the same time he said to them: Beware”); *βλέπετε* (“beware”) is also in the Greek text.
- Verse 40 [Col. 0821]: Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek, also adds *et pupillorum* (“and of orphans”), Greek *καὶ ὀρφανῶν*.
- Verse 42 [Col. 0821]: Gat. reads *vidua paupercula* (“a very poor widow”); the Vulgate, *vidua una pauper* (“one poor widow”). After *vidua* (“widow”), *pauper* (“poor”) is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.

## CHAPTER XIII
1. And as he was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him: “Teacher, look—what stones, and what buildings!” 2. And answering, [Note: [Col. 0821] Before “he said to them,” “Jesus” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. Likewise Vercelli and Verona have “to them,” together with the same Cantabrigiensis, αὐτοῖς.] he said to them +: [Note: [Col. 0821] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis, βλέπετε.] [Note: [Col. 0821] 2 Gat. “See these great [things].” Vulgate: “See all these great [buildings].”] “Do you see + these great structures? [Note: [Col. 0821] It adds, “Amen, I say to you, that,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι.] Amen, I say to you +, not one stone shall be left [Note: [Col. 0821] “Here” is also added in Codex Cantabrigiensis, ὧδε.] here + upon another, [Col. 0823] which will not be destroyed; [Note: [Col. 0823] So also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἄλλος ἀναστήσεται ἄνευ χειρῶν, “and after three days another shall rise without hands.” These words are absent from the Vulgate edition. Yet they stood in St Cyprian’s Latin copy, for he reads: “and after three days another shall be raised without hands.” A borrowing from chapter XIV, verse 58 of this Gospel.] and after three days another shall rise without hands +.” 3. And while he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned him privately: 4. “Tell us, when will these things be? And what will be the sign when all these things begin to be brought to completion?” 5. And answering, he said to them: “Take heed that no one lead you astray; 6. for many will come in my name, saying, ‘For [Note: [Col. 0823] Gat. “I am Christ, and.” Vulgate: “I am, and.”] I am’;” and they will lead many astray. 7. But when you hear of wars and reports of battles, do not be troubled; for these things must happen, but the end is not yet. 8. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be earthquakes in various places and famines: all these things are the beginning of sufferings. 9. Then they will hand you yourselves over in councils; and you will be beaten in synagogues; and you will stand before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to 10. them. And the Gospel must first be preached among all nations. 11.
