Jesus answered and said to them: [Note: [Col. 0811] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰ ἔχετε, “if you have.”] “If you have + faith in God, 23. amen I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes [Note: [Col. 0811] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: τὸ μέλλον ὃ ἐὰν εἴπῃ γενήσεται αὐτῷ, “what he says is going to happen will come to pass for him.”] that what he says will happen, it will come to pass for him +. 24. Therefore I say to you: whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you will receive it, and it will come to you. 25. And when you stand [Note: [Col. 0811] So the Greek text: προσευχόμενοι, “praying.”] praying +, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your sins. 26. If you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive you your sins.”

27. Again [Note: [Col. 0811] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔρχεται, “he comes.”] he came + to Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, and elders came to him [Col. 0814] 28. and said to him: “By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?” 29. Jesus answered and said to them: “I too will ask you one question. [Note: [Col. 0813] Before “answer,” “and” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Answer + me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things. 30. [Note: [Col. 0813] So the Greek text: τὸ βάπτισμα, “the baptism.”] The baptism + of John: was it from heaven, or from human beings? Answer me.” 31. But they reasoned among themselves, saying what they should answer him. “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ [Note: [Col. 0813] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: λέγει ἡμῖν, “he says to us.”] he says to us +, ‘Why, then, did you not believe him?’ 32. But if we say, ‘From human beings’—we fear the people; for everyone [Note: [Col. 0813] According to Codex Cantabrigiensis: ᾔδεισαν, “knew.”] knew + that John really was a prophet.” 33. Answering, they said to Jesus: [Col. 0814] “We do not know.” Jesus answered and said to them: “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

## CHAPTER XII

1. He began to speak to them in parables, saying: “A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit, built a tower, leased it to tenants, and went away abroad. 2. At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants [Note: [Col. 0813] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἵνα ἐκ τοῦ καρποῦ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος δώσουσιν αὐτῷ, “that they might give him from the fruit of the vineyard,” from Luke.] that they might give him fruit from the vineyard +. 3. [Note: [Col. 0813] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: καί, “and.”] And + they seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty [Note: [Col. 0813] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds “to him,” πρὸς αὐτόν.] back to him +. 4. Again he sent another servant to them, and they wounded him on the head and treated him shamefully. [Col. 0816] 5. And [Note: [Col. 0815] Before “another,” “again” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis, as well as in the Persian and Coptic versions. In the same place it adds “servant,” likewise Codex Cantabrigiensis: δοῦλον.] he sent another servant +; and they killed him. He sent many others: some they beat, but others they killed. 6. He still had one beloved son; he said: [Note: [Col. 0815] The Syriac, Persian, and Arabic versions also add “perhaps,” from Luke.] ‘Perhaps + they will respect my son.’ 7. But the tenants said to one another: ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill . . . . . . and the inheritance will be ours.’ 8. Having seized [him], they killed [him] outside the vineyard. 9. What then will the lord of the vineyard do when he comes?” But they said to him: “He will destroy the wicked miserably and lease his vineyard to other tenants.” 10. “Have you not read this Scripture: ‘The stone which the builders rejected has become [Col. 0816] the head of the corner. 11. This was done by the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

12. They sought to seize him, but feared the crowd; for they knew that he had spoken this parable about them. Leaving him, they went away. 13. They sent to him certain Pharisees and Herodians, to catch him in a word. 14. When they came, [Note: [Col. 0815] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν, “they questioned him.”] they questioned him + deceitfully, saying: “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and defer to no one; for you do not regard a person’s appearance, but teach the way of God truly. [Note: [Col. 0815] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds, “Tell us then whether,” εἰπὲ οὖν ἡμῖν εἰ.] Tell us, then, whether + it is lawful to give tribute to Caesar or [Note: [Col. 0815] After “or not,” “shall we give it” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] not +.” 15. [Note: [Col. 0815] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς, “but Jesus.”] But Jesus +, seeing their cunning, said to them: [Col. 0818] “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.” 16. But they [Note: [Col. 0817] After “brought,” “to him” is absent, likewise in the Greek text.] brought it +. He said to them: “Whose is this image and inscription?” They said to him: “Caesar’s.” 17. Jesus answered and said to them: “Render, therefore, what belongs to Caesar to Caesar, and what belongs to God to God.” And they marveled greatly at his answer.

18. Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no resurrection, and questioned him, saying: 19. “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that, if anyone’s brother dies [Note: [Col. 0817] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ γυναῖκα ἔχῃ, “and has a wife.”] and has a wife +, leaving no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother. 20. There were [Note: [Col. 0817] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds “among us,” παρ’ ἡμῖν, from Matthew.] among us + seven brothers. The first [Col. 0818] took a wife and died, leaving no offspring. 21. The second took her and died; and he left no offspring. And the third . . . . . 22. . . . . . her . . . . . . . . and the woman too died. 23. In the resurrection . . . . . . . . . whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as wife.”

24. Jesus answered and said to them: “Do you not err for this reason, because you understand neither the Scriptures nor the power of God? [lacuna] 25. [lacuna] marry, nor are given in marriage, but will be like angels [Note: [Col. 0817] From Matthew.] in heaven +. 26. But concerning the dead, that they rise, have you not read in the book of Moses, concerning the bush, how [Col. 0820] [God] said to him: ‘God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of 27. Jacob’? He is not God of the dead, but of the living. Therefore you are greatly mistaken.”

28. One of the scribes came forward [Note: [Col. 0819] So the Greek text: προσελθών, “having come forward.”], having heard them disputing. Seeing that he had answered them well, he asked him, [Note: [Col. 0819] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds “saying, Teacher,” λέγων διδάσκαλε.] saying: “Teacher +, what is the first commandment?” 29. [Note: [Col. 0819] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἀποκριθείς . . . εἶπεν, “answering . . . said.”] Jesus answered and said to him: [Note: [Col. 0819] Before “first,” “that” is absent, and afterwards “is” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] “The first of all + is: ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God [Note: [Col. 0819] So the Greek text: ἡμῶν, “our.”] our + is one; 30. and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength [Note: [Col. 0819] After “your strength,” “and with all your mind” is absent, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] your +, and with all your power.’ This is the first commandment. 31. The second [Note: [Col. 0819] After “like,” “and” is absent, also in the Greek text.] is like + it: ‘You shall love your neighbor [Col. 0820] as yourself.’ There is no commandment greater than these.”

32. The scribe said to him: “Well said, Teacher; in truth, there is one God, and there is no other besides 33. him; and he is to be loved with all the heart and [Note: [Col. 0819] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἐξ ὅλης τῆς δυνάμεως, “with all the strength.”] with all the strength +, and with all the soul; and to love one’s neighbor as oneself is greater than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.” 34. Jesus, seeing that he had answered wisely, said to him: “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared any longer to question him about anything.

35. Jesus answered, teaching in the temple, [Note: [Col. 0819] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἶπε, “he said.”] and said +: “How do the scribes say that the Christ is David’s son? 36. For David himself says in the Holy Spirit: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies as the footstool of your [Col. 0822] feet.’ 37. If David therefore calls him Lord, [Note: [Col. 0821] From Matthew.] how + is he his son?” And the great crowd gladly heard [Note: [Col. 0821] So the Greek text: ἤκουεν, “heard.” Codex Vercellensis supports this.] him +.

38. [Note: [Col. 0821] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ δὲ διδάσκων ἅμα ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε—“and while teaching he said to them: Beware”; βλέπετε, “beware,” is also in the Greek text.] But while teaching, he said to them: “Beware + of the scribes, who wish to walk about in robes, and to receive [Note: [Col. 0821] So the Greek text: ἀσπασμούς, “greetings.”] greetings + in 39. the marketplace, and to sit in the chief seats in synagogues and the places of honor at banquets; 40. who devour the bread of widows [Note: [Col. 0821] Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek, also adds “and of orphans,” καὶ ὀρφανῶν.] and of orphans +, under the pretext of a long prayer. All these shall receive a more severe judgment.”

41. Jesus, sitting opposite the treasury, watched how much the crowds cast in copper coins into the treasury; and many rich persons cast in much. 42. But one [Note: [Col. 0821] After “widow,” “poor” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] widow + came and put in two small coins, [Col. 0822] which make a quadrans. 43. Calling his disciples to himself, he said to them: “Amen I say to you: this needy widow has put in more than all [Note: [Col. 0821] After “put in,” “who put in” is absent, likewise in the Armenian.] have put + into the treasury 44. as an offering. For all put in from what they had in abundance; but she, from her own means, put in everything she had, that is, all her livelihood.”

## CHAPTER XIII

1. As he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him: “Teacher, look—what stones, and what a structure [Note: [Col. 0821] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds “of the temple,” τοῦ ἱεροῦ, from Matthew.] of the temple +!” 2. Answering, [Note: [Col. 0821] Before “said to them,” “Jesus” is absent also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. In Codices Vercellensis and Veronensis there is “to them,” with Codex Cantabrigiensis: αὐτοῖς.] he said to them +: “Do you not [Note: [Col. 0821] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: βλέπετε, “you see.”] see + all these great buildings? [Note: [Col. 0821] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds, “Amen I say to you that,” Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι.] Amen I say to you that + not one [Note: [Col. 0821] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds “here,” ὧδε.] stone here + will be left upon another which [Col. 0824] will not be destroyed; [Note: [Col. 0823] So Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἄλλος ἀναστήσεται ἄνευ χειρῶν, “and after three days another shall be raised without hands.” These words are absent from the Vulgate edition. They were nevertheless present in the Latin copy of St Cyprian, who read: “and after three days another will be raised without hands.” An addition from chapter XIV, verse 58 of this Gospel.] and after three days another shall be raised without hands +.”

3. As he sat [Note: [Col. 0823] So the Greek text: εἰς τὸ ὄρος, “on the mount.”] on the Mount + of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately: 4. “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign when all these things are to be fulfilled?” 5. Jesus answered and began to say to them: “See that no one deceives you. 6. For many will come in my name, saying: [Note: [Col. 0823] Before “I,” “that” is absent, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis. In the same place “Christ” is added, from Matthew.] ‘I am Christ +,’ and they will deceive many. 7. When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be afraid; for all these things must happen, but the end is not yet. 8. Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in various places and famines. These are the beginning of sufferings. [lacuna] [Col. 0824] [lacuna] [Col. 0826] [lacuna]

19. For in those days there will be tribulations such as have not been from the beginning of creation, which God created, until now, nor shall be. 20. [lacuna] And unless the Lord had shortened the days [Note: [Col. 0825] Codex Cantabrigiensis also adds “for his elect,” διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ.] for his elect [Col. 0826] +, [lacuna] no flesh would be saved; but for the elect whom he chose, those days shall be shortened. 21. And then, if anyone says to you, “Behold, here is Christ,” [Note: [Col. 0825] So also the Greek text: ἤ (“or”).] or +, “Behold, there,” do not believe it. 22. For false Christs and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders, to deceive people, if possible, even the elect. Therefore 23. take heed: behold, I have foretold all things to you. 24. [lacuna] in those days after the tribulation [lacuna]

## CODEX BRIXIANUS

[Col. 0719]

The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God. As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.” [Note: Before “I send,” *I* is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] “A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.” [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis, Latin and Greek, as well as Gothic: τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν, “of our God,” and certain other Greek codices, according to Isaiah 40:3.]

John was baptizing in the wilderness and preaching a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. And all the region of Judea and the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.

Now John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt about his loins; and he ate locusts and wild honey. And he preached, saying: “There comes after me one stronger than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy, stooping down, to untie. I indeed baptize you in water; [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: βαπτίζω, “I baptize.” In the same place it adds “in,” also the Greek text: ἐν.] but he baptized you in the Holy Spirit.” And it came to pass in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan. [Note: Thus also the Greek text: Ναζαρέτ, “Nazareth.”] And immediately, coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened and the Spirit descending upon him like a dove. And a voice came from heaven, saying: “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

And immediately the Spirit drove him into the wilderness. And he was in the wilderness forty days, [Note: After “days,” “and forty nights” is lacking, likewise in the Greek text.] and was tempted by Satan; and he was with the wild beasts, and the angels ministered to him.

Now after John had been delivered up, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of God and saying: “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent, and believe the Gospel.” And, passing along the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen. And Jesus said to them: “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men.” And immediately, leaving their nets, they followed him.

And proceeding a little farther from there, he saw James son of Zebedee and John his brother, themselves also in the boat mending their nets. And immediately he called them; and, leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants, they followed him.

And they entered Capernaum, [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰσεπορεύοντο, “they entered.”] and immediately, on the Sabbaths, Jesus entered the synagogue and taught them. And they were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

And there was in their synagogue a man who had an unclean spirit; and he cried out, saying: “What have we to do with you, Jesus the Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God.” [Note: Thus also the Greek text: οἶδά σε, “I know you.”] And Jesus rebuked it, saying: “Be silent, and come out of him.” And the unclean spirit, tearing him and crying out with a loud voice, departed from him. And all were amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying: “What is this? What is this new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.” And immediately his report went out [Note: Thus also the Greek text: ἐξῆλθε, “went out.”] throughout all the region of Galilee.

And immediately, leaving the synagogue, he came [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἦλθεν, “he came.”] into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John. Now Simon’s mother-in-law lay sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her. And coming up, he took her by the hand and raised her; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered to them. And when evening had come, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were ill and those possessed by demons. And the whole city had gathered at the door. And he healed many who were ill [Note: Thus also the Greek text: κακῶς ἔχοντας, “those who were ill.”] with various diseases, and he cast out many demons; and he did not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.

And rising very early in the morning, he went out and departed to a deserted place, and there he prayed. And Simon and those who were with him pursued [Note: Thus also the Greek text: κατεδίωξαν, “pursued.”] him. And when they found him, they said to him: “Everyone is seeking you.” And he said to them: “Let us go into the neighboring villages and towns, that I may preach there also; for this is why I came.” And he was preaching in their synagogues throughout all Galilee and casting out demons.

And a leper came to him, begging him; and, kneeling, he said: “If you will, you are able to cleanse me.” And Jesus, having compassion on him, stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him: “I will; be cleansed.” And when he had said these things, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed. And he sternly charged him and immediately sent him away. And he said to him: “See that you say nothing to anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest, [Note: Thus also the Greek text: ἱερεῖ, “to the priest.”] and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.” But he, having gone out, began to proclaim and spread abroad the report, so that Jesus could no longer [Note: According to the Greek text: μηκέτι … μηδέ, “no longer … nor.” In the same place Veronensis has “to them”; likewise Codex Cantabrigiensis: πρὸς αὐτούς, “to them.”] enter a city openly, but remained outside in deserted places; and people came to him from every direction.

And again he entered Capernaum after some days, and it was heard that he was in a house. And immediately many gathered together, so that there was no room, not even at the door; and he spoke the word to them. And they came to him, bringing a paralytic on a pallet, carried by four men. And being unable to bring him to him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where Jesus was; and, having made an opening, they lowered the pallet on which the paralytic lay. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic: “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”

Now some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts: “Why does this man speak thus? He blasphemes. Who can forgive sins except God alone?” And immediately Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they were thus reasoning within themselves, said to them: “Why do you reason these things in your hearts? Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Rise, take up your pallet, and walk’? But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—“I say to you, rise, take up your pallet, and go to your house.” And immediately he rose and, taking up his pallet, went out before them all, so that all were astonished and glorified God, saying: “We have never seen anything like this.”

And he went out again beside the sea, and all the crowd came to him, and he taught them. And passing by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax office; and he said to him: “Follow me.” And rising, he followed him. And it came to pass, as he reclined in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many who also followed him. [Note: Thus also the Greek text: ἠκολούθησαν, “followed.”] And the scribes and Pharisees, seeing him eating with tax collectors and sinners, said to his disciples: “Why does your teacher eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?” When Jesus heard this, he said to them: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do. For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

And John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting; and they came and said to him: “Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?” And Jesus said to them: “Can the sons of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them? So long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast. But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days. No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment, lest the new patch pull away from the old and the tear become worse.” [Note: Thus also the Greek text: χεῖρον, “worse.”] “And no one puts new wine into old wineskins, lest the new wine burst the skins, and the wine be spilled and the skins destroyed; rather, they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”

And it came to pass that he was walking through grainfields on the Sabbaths, and his disciples, as they went along, began to pluck ears of grain. [Note: “Again” is lacking also in the Greek text.] But the Pharisees said to him: “Look, why do your disciples [Note: Adds “your disciples,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: οἱ μαθηταί σου.] do on the Sabbaths what is not lawful?” And he said to them: “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those who were with him? How he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the priest, and ate the bread of the Presence, which it was not lawful to eat except for priests alone, [Note: Adds “alone,” also Gothic, from Matthew.] and gave it also to those who were with him?” And he said to them: “The Sabbath was made for humankind, not humankind for the Sabbath.” [Note: Before “not,” *and* is lacking, likewise in the Greek text.] “Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

And Jesus entered the synagogue again, and there was a man there with a withered hand. And they watched him to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him. And Jesus said to the man who had the withered hand: “Rise; stand in the midst.” And he said to them, [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἶπε πρὸς αὐτούς, “he said to them.”] “Is it lawful on the Sabbaths to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they were silent. And looking around at them with anger, grieved at the blindness of their hearts, he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored. But the Pharisees, going out immediately, took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

But Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea; and a great crowd from Galilee and Judea followed him. [Note: “Followed him” is lacking also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] And from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan, and from around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing how much [Note: The Greek text reads ὅσα, “how much” or “what things.”] he did, came to him. And he told his disciples that a small boat should be ready for him because of the crowd, lest they crush him. For he healed many, so that all who had afflictions rushed upon him to touch him. And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, fell down before him and cried out, saying: “You are the Son of God.” And he sternly charged them not to make him known.

And going up on the mountain, he called to himself those whom he wished, and they came to him. And he appointed twelve that [Note: Thus also the Greek text: δώδεκα, ἵνα, “twelve, that.”] they might be with him and that he might send them out to preach the Gospel [Note: Adds “the Gospel,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον.] and give them authority to heal diseases and cast out demons. And he gave Simon the name Peter; and James son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and he gave them the names Boanerges, that is, “sons of thunder”; and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

And they came into a house, and again a crowd gathered, so that they were unable even to eat bread. And when the scribes and the rest heard about him, [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ ὅτε ἤκουσαν περὶ αὐτοῦ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ λοιποί, “and when the scribes and the rest heard about him.”] they went out to seize him, for they said: “He has gone mad.” And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said: “He has Beelzebul, and by the prince of demons he casts out demons.” And calling them to him, he spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan? If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. And if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand. And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has an end. No one can enter a strong man’s house and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man; then he will plunder his house.

“Amen I say to you: every sin shall be forgiven the children of men, and whatever blasphemies they utter; but whoever blasphemes the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness for ever, but is guilty of an eternal judgment.” For they were saying: “He has an unclean spirit.”

And his mother and his brothers came; standing outside, they sent to him, calling him. [Note: Adds “his,” likewise Gothic: αὐτοῦ.] And a great crowd sat around him, and they said to him: “Behold, your mother, your brothers, and your sisters [Note: Adds “and your sisters,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαί σου.] are standing outside seeking you.” And he answered [Note: Thus also the Greek text: ἀπεκρίθη, “he answered.”] them, saying: “Who is my mother, or who are my brothers?” And looking around at those sitting in a circle about him, he said: “Behold, my mother and my brothers. For whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.”

And again Jesus began to teach by the sea. And a great crowd gathered to him, so that, getting into a boat, he sat on the sea; [Note: Adds “into,” also the Greek text: εἰς.] and all the crowd stood on the shore. [Note: Here likewise Codex Cantabrigiensis has πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης, “beyond the sea,” omitting “on the ground.”] And he taught them many things in parables, and said to them in his teaching: “Listen. Behold, the sower went out to sow. And as he sowed, some seed fell beside the road, and birds came [Note: “Of heaven” is lacking also in Gothic.] and ate it. Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil. But when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered away. Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit. And other seed fell into good soil and yielded fruit, coming up and increasing; and it bore thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.” And he said: “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

And when he was alone, those who were with him, together with the twelve, asked him, saying: “What is this parable?” And he said [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: λέγει, “he says.”] to them: “To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those outside, all things come in parables, so that, seeing, they may see and not perceive; and hearing, they may hear and not understand, lest they should at any time turn and their sins be forgiven them.”

And he said to them: “Do you not know this parable? And how will you understand all the parables? The sower sows the word. And these are those sown beside the road: [Note: According to Codex Cantabrigiensis: οἷς παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπείρεται, “those for whom it is sown beside the road.”] those who receive the word carelessly; and when they hear it, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word which was sown in their hearts. And these likewise are those sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, immediately they receive it with joy; yet they have no root in themselves, but endure only for a time. Then, when tribulation and persecution arise because of the word, immediately they fall away. And these are those sown among thorns: they hear the word, but the cares of this age, the deceitfulness of riches, and other desires entering in choke the word, and it becomes fruitless. And these are those sown on good soil: they hear the word, receive it, and bear fruit—thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

And he said to them: “Does one light a lamp and put it under a measuring basket or under a bed? Is it not put on a lampstand? For nothing is hidden except to be made manifest; nor has anything become concealed except to come into the open. If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.” And he said to them: “Take heed what you hear. By the measure with which you measure, it shall be measured to you; and more shall be added to you who believe. For to the one who has, it shall be given; and from the one who has not, even what he has shall be taken away.”

And he said to them: “The kingdom of God is as when a man casts seed upon the ground and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he himself does not know how. For the earth produces fruit of itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear. And when it has produced the fruit, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has arrived.” And he said: “To what shall we compare the kingdom of God, or by what parable shall we set it forth? It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown in the earth, is smaller than all the seeds that are in the earth; yet when it has been sown, it comes up and becomes greater than all garden plants, and makes great branches, so that the birds of heaven can dwell under its shadow.”

And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear; but without a parable he did not speak to them. Privately, however, he explained everything to his disciples.

And he said to them on that day, when evening had come: “Let us cross over to the other side.” And dismissing the crowd, they took him with them, as he was, in the boat; and other boats were with him. And a great windstorm arose, and waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was filling. But he was in the stern, asleep upon a cushion. And they awakened [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: διεγείραντες, “having awakened.”] him and said to him: “Teacher, does it not concern you that we are perishing?” And rising, he rebuked the wind and said to the sea: “Be silent; be muzzled.” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said to them: “Why are you fearful? How is it that you still have no faith?” And they feared with great fear and said to one another: “Who, do you suppose, is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

And they came across the strait [Note: After “strait,” “of the sea” is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] into the region of the Gerasenes. And when he came out of the boat, immediately a man from the tombs met him, with an unclean spirit. He had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one could any longer bind him, even with chains, because he had often been bound with fetters and chains, yet had torn the chains apart and smashed the fetters; and no one was able to subdue him. And always, night and day, among the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.

But seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran and worshiped him. And crying out with a loud voice, he said: “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, do not torment me.” For he was saying to him: “Come out of the man, unclean spirit.” And he asked him: “What is your name?” But he answered, [Note: Thus also the Greek text: ἀπεκρίθη, “he answered.”] “My name is Legion, because we are many.” And he begged him greatly not to send them out of the region. Now there was there, near the mountain, a great herd of swine feeding. And the demons begged him, saying: “Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.” And Jesus immediately permitted them. And the unclean spirits came out and entered into the swine; and the herd was hurled with great force into the sea—about two thousand of them—and they were drowned in the sea.

But those who fed them fled and reported it in the city and in the countryside. And they came out to see what had happened, and came to Jesus. And they saw the man who had been demon-possessed sitting, clothed, and in his right mind; and they were afraid. And those who had seen it told them how it had happened to the man who had had the demon, and about the swine. And they began to beg him to depart from their territory.

And when he was getting into the boat, the one who had been demon-possessed began to beg him that he might be with him. But he did not permit him; rather, he said to him: “Go to your house, to your own people, and report to them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you.” And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and all marveled.

And when Jesus had crossed back again in the boat, a great crowd gathered to him beside [Note: Before “beside,” “and he was” is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] the sea. And behold, a certain ruler of the synagogue named Jairus came; and seeing him, fell at his feet and begged him earnestly, saying: “My daughter is at the point of death. Come, lay your hand upon her, that she may be saved and live.” And he went with him; and a great crowd followed him and pressed upon him.

And a certain woman who had had an issue of blood for twelve years, and who [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἥ, “who.”] had suffered much from many physicians and had spent all that she possessed, yet had not benefited at all but had become worse, having heard about Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd and touched his garment. For she said: “If I touch even his garment, I shall be healed.” And immediately the fountain of her blood was dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed of the affliction.

And immediately Jesus, knowing in himself that power had gone out from him, turned to the crowd and said: [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: καὶ … εἶπε, “and … he said.”] “Who touched my garments?” And his disciples said to him: “You see the crowd pressing upon you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’” But he looked around to see her who had done this. And the woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth. But Jesus [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς, “but Jesus.”] said to her: “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be whole from your affliction.”

While he was still speaking, people came from the ruler of the synagogue, saying: “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?” But Jesus, hearing this word, said to the ruler of the synagogue: “Do not fear; only believe.” And he allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James. And he came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue and saw a crowd weeping and wailing loudly. [Note: According to Codex Cantabrigiensis: θόρυβον κλαιόντων καὶ ἀλαλαζόντων, “a commotion of persons weeping and lamenting.”] And entering, he said to them: “Why are you troubled, and why [Note: Adds “why,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: τί.] do you weep? The child has not died, but is sleeping.” And they laughed at him.

But he, putting them all outside, took the father and mother of the child and those who were with him, and entered [Note: According to Codex Cantabrigiensis: εἰσεπορεύετο, “he entered.”] where the child was lying. And taking the child by the hand, he said to her: “Talitha cumi,” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, arise.” And immediately the little girl arose and walked; for she was twelve years old. And they were utterly astonished. And he charged them strictly that no one should know this, and told them to give her something to eat.

And departing from there, he came into his own country, and his disciples followed him. And when the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue; and many who heard him were astonished at his teaching, saying: “Where did this man get all these things? And what is this wisdom given to him, that such mighty works are performed through his hands? Is this not the craftsman, the son of Mary, the brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them: “A prophet is not without honor except in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.” And he was unwilling to perform any mighty work there, except that he healed a few sick persons by laying his hands upon them. And he marveled because of their unbelief.

And Jesus went around the villages in a circuit, teaching. And he called the twelve together and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over unclean spirits. And he charged them to take nothing for the journey except a staff only: no bag, no bread, no copper in their belts; but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics. And he said to them: “Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you depart from that place. And whoever does not receive you or hear you, as you depart from there shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them. Amen I say to you: it shall be more tolerable for Sodom or Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.” And going out, they preached, and they anointed many sick persons with oil, and they were healed.

And King Herod heard; for his name had become known. And he said: “John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works operate in him.” But others said: “He is Elijah.” Others, however, said: “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.” When Herod heard this, he said: “John, whom I beheaded—he has risen from the dead.” For Herod himself had sent and seized John, bound him, and put him in prison [Note: Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ἔδησεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν φυλακήν, “he bound him and cast him into prison.”] because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her. For John said to Herod: “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.” But Herodias plotted against him and wanted to kill him, but could not; for Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. And when he heard him, he did many things, and gladly saw him.

And when an opportune day had come, Herod, on his birthday, gave a dinner to the leading men, military commanders, and principal persons of Galilee. And when the daughter [Note: After “daughter,” “herself” is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] of Herodias had entered and danced, and pleased Herod and those reclining with him, the king said to the girl: “Ask me whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.” And he swore to her: “Whatever you ask of me, I will give it to you, up to half my kingdom.” And the girl went out and said to her mother: “What shall I ask for?” And she said: “The head of John the Baptist.”

And she entered immediately, in haste, to the king and asked, saying: “I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist.” And the king was grieved; but because of the oath and those reclining with him, he did not wish to refuse her. Rather, he immediately [Note: Adds “immediately,” also the Greek text: εὐθέως.] sent an executioner and commanded that his head be brought. [Note: After “his,” “on a platter” is lacking, likewise in the Greek text.] And he went away [Note: Adds “and he went away,” also the Greek text: ὁ δὲ ἀπελθών, “and he, having gone away.” Brixianus: *Isque abiens*, “and he going away”; Vercellensis: *Et cum abisset*, “and when he had gone away.”] and beheaded him in prison, brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl; and the girl gave it to her mother. When his disciples heard this, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.

And the apostles gathered to Jesus and reported to him all that they had done and taught. And Jesus [Note: Adds “Jesus,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: ὁ Ἰησοῦς.] said to them: “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many were coming and going, and they had no opportunity even to eat. And they went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves. And many saw them leaving and recognized them, and on foot from all the cities they ran together there, got there ahead of them, and came together to him. And Jesus, coming out, saw a great crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.

And when the hour had already become late, his disciples came to him, saying: “This is a deserted place, [Note: Adds “because,” also the Greek text: ὅτι.] and the hour is already past. Send them away, that they may go into the neighboring farms and villages and buy themselves bread, because they have nothing to eat.” [Note: According to the Greek text: ἄρτους τί γὰρ φάγωσιν οὐκ ἔχουσι, “bread; for they have nothing to eat.” An addition from chapter 8, verse 2, of this Gospel.] And Jesus answered them: “You give them something to eat.” And they said to him: “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?” And he said to them: “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” And when they had found out, they said to him: “Five loaves and two fish.” And Jesus commanded them to make them all recline in groups on the green grass.

And they reclined in groups, in companies of a hundred and of fifty. [Note: Adds “by,” likewise the Greek text: ἀνά.] And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to heaven, he blessed, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and he divided the two fish among all. And all ate and were filled. And they took up twelve baskets of fragments left over, and some of the fish. Now those who had eaten the loaves were five thousand men.

And immediately he compelled his disciples to get into [Note: Adds “into,” likewise the Greek text: εἰς.] the boat and go ahead of him across the strait to Bethsaida, while he dismissed the people. And after he had taken leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray. And when evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on land. And seeing them straining at the oars, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night Jesus came to them walking on the sea, and he intended to pass them by. But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a phantom and cried out; for they all saw him and were troubled. But immediately he spoke to them and said: “Take courage; it is I. Do not be afraid.” And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased. And they were exceedingly more astonished within themselves and marveled, [Note: Adds “and marveled,” also the Greek text: καὶ ἐθαύμαζον. Vercellensis has “with astonishment.”] for they had not understood about the loaves, because their hearts were hardened.

And having crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and moored there. And when they came out of the boat, immediately people recognized him. And running throughout that whole region, they began to carry around on pallets those who were ill wherever they heard he was. And wherever he entered, into villages or cities or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and all who touched him were made well.

And Pharisees and some scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him. And when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with common—that is, unwashed—hands, they found fault with them. For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands repeatedly, holding the tradition of the elders; and when they return from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash themselves. And there are many other observances that have been handed down to them to keep: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and beds. Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him: “Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?” [Note: Thus also the Greek text: ἀνίπτοις, “unwashed.”] But he answered and said to them: “Isaiah rightly prophesied concerning you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. Yet in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of men.’”

For you abandon the commandment of God and keep the traditions handed down by men: washings of pitchers and cups, and many other things like these you do. And he said to them, “Well do you make void the commandment of God, in order to establish your tradition.” [Note: [Col. 0771] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *stēsēte* (“you may establish”).] For Moses said, “Honor your father and your mother”; and, “Whoever curses father or mother shall surely die.” But you say, “If a man says to father or mother, ‘Corban’”—that is, “an offering”—“whatever benefit you might have received from me [Col. 0773] is [Corban],” then you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or mother, setting aside the word of God through your tradition which you have handed down. And many such things you do.

And summoning the whole crowd, he said to them, “Hear me, all of you, and understand. There is nothing outside a person which, entering into him, can defile him; rather, the things which come out from a person are those which defile a person. If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.” And when he had entered the house, away from [Col. 0774] the crowd, his disciples asked him about this parable. And he said to them, “Are you too without understanding? Do you not yet understand that nothing external which enters into a person can defile him, because it does not enter into his heart, but into his belly, and goes out into the privy, purging all foods?” But he said that the things which come out of a person, those defile a person. For from within, from the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, [Note: [Col. 0773] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *pleonexia* (“covetousness”), *(dolos)* (“deceit”), *ponēria* (“wickedness”), *aselgeia* (“licentiousness”), *blasphēmiai* (“blasphemies”).] covetousness, [Col. 0775] wickedness, deceit, envy, shamelessness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and folly. All these evils proceed from within and defile a person.

And rising from there, he went away into the region of Tyre and Sidon. Having entered a house, he wished no one to know it, yet he could not remain hidden. But immediately, when a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him, she came to him and fell at his feet. The woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by race. And she begged him to cast the demon out of her daughter. But Jesus said [Col. 0776] to her, “Let the children first be filled; for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.” But she answered and said to him, “Yes indeed, Lord; for even the little dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.” Then he said to her, “Go; because of this saying, the demon has gone out of your daughter.” And when she had gone home, she found her daughter lying upon the bed, and the demon gone out.

And again, departing from the region of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the territory of the Decapolis. And they brought to him a deaf and mute man, and begged [Col. 0777] him to lay his hand upon him. And taking him apart from the crowd privately, he put his fingers into his ears; and spitting, he touched his tongue. And looking up to heaven, he groaned and said to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “to open.” And immediately his ears were opened, the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke correctly. And he commanded them to tell no one. But the more he commanded them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it; and they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “He has done all things well: he makes the deaf hear [Col. 0778] and the mute speak.” In those [Note: [Col. 0777] Thus also the Greek text: *de* (“but”).] days, again, when there was a great crowd and they had nothing to eat, Jesus summoned his disciples and said to them, “I have compassion on this crowd, because, behold, they have already remained with me for three days and have nothing to eat. And if I send them away fasting to their homes, they will faint on the way; for some of them have come from far away.”

And his disciples answered him, “From where can anyone here satisfy these people with bread in a desert place?” And he asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” But they [Col. 0779] said, “Seven.” And he commanded the crowd to recline upon the ground. Taking the seven loaves and giving thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and they set them before the crowds. They also had a few small fish; and he blessed these too and commanded them to be set out. And they ate and were filled, and they took up seven baskets of the fragments left over. Now those who had eaten were about four thousand; and he dismissed them. And immediately he entered the boat with his disciples and came into the region of Dalmanutha. And [Col. 0780] the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, testing him.

And groaning in his spirit, he said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen, I say to you: no sign shall be given to this generation.” And leaving them, he entered the boat again and went across the water. They forgot to take bread, and had only one loaf with them in the boat. And he charged them, saying, “See and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of Herod.” And they reasoned among themselves, saying, “Because [Col. 0781] we have no bread.” When Jesus perceived this, he said to them, “Why do you reason because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive or understand? Do you still have your heart blinded? Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? Do you not remember, when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments you took up?” And they said to him, “Twelve.” “And when [I broke] the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you take up?” [Note: [Col. 0781] And thus Codex Cantabrigiensis: *hoi de eipon* (“and they said”).] But they said [Col. 0782], “Seven.” And [Note: [Col. 0781] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *legei* (“he says”).] he said to them, “Why then do you not understand?”

And they came to Bethany, and they brought him a blind man and begged him to touch him. Taking the blind man by the hand, he led him outside the village; and having spat upon his eyes and laid his hands upon him, he asked him whether he saw anything. And looking up, he said, “I see people, like trees walking.” Then again he laid his hands upon his eyes and made him see; and he was restored, so that he saw [Col. 0783] all things clearly. And he sent him away to his house, saying, “Go to your house; and if you enter the villages, tell no one.”

And Jesus and his disciples went out into the villages of Caesarea Philippi; and on the road he questioned his disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say that I am?” They answered, saying, “John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and others, as one of the prophets.” Then he said to his disciples, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered and said to him, “You are the Christ.” And he sternly charged them not to tell anyone about him. And he began to teach them [Col. 0784] that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise again after three days. And he spoke the saying openly.

And Peter, taking him aside, began to rebuke him. But Jesus, turning and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter sternly, saying, “Get behind me, Satan, because you do not understand the things of God, but the things of men.” And having summoned the crowd to himself with his disciples, he said to them, “If anyone wishes [Note: [Col. 0783] Thus also the Greek text: *opisō mou* (“after me”).] to follow [Col. 0785] me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake and the Gospel’s will save it. For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world and suffers loss of his life? Or what will a person give as an exchange [Note: [Col. 0785] Thus also the Greek text: *antallagma* (“exchange”).] for his life? For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, of him the Son of Man also will be ashamed when he comes in the glory of his Father [Col. 0786] with the holy angels.”

And he said to them, “Amen, I say to you: there are some standing here who shall not taste death until they see the kingdom of God coming in power.” And after six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain apart by themselves; and he was transfigured before them. And his garments became shining, exceedingly white as snow, such as no fuller on earth can make white. And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were speaking [Col. 0787] with Jesus. Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and, if you wish, let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” For he did not know what to say, for they were terrified with fear. And a cloud arose, overshadowing them; and a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son; hear him.” And immediately, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.

As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them to relate to no one what they had seen, except when the Son of Man should rise from the dead. And they kept the saying among [Col. 0788] themselves, questioning what the rising from the dead might mean. And they asked him, saying, “Why then do [Note: [Col. 0787] Before “scribes,” “Pharisees” is lacking, likewise in the Greek text.] the scribes say that Elijah must come first?” He answered and said to them, “Elijah, when he comes first, restores all things. And how is it written concerning the Son of Man—that he should suffer many things and be despised? But I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did to him whatever they wished, as it is written concerning him.”

And when he came to his disciples, he saw a great crowd around [Col. 0789] them and scribes disputing with them. And immediately all the people, seeing him, were astonished; and running to him, they did him homage. And he asked them, “What are you discussing among yourselves?”

And one from the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought my son to you, having a mute spirit. Wherever it seizes him, it throws him down; he foams, grinds his teeth [Note: [Col. 0789] Adds “his,” also the Greek text: *autou* (“his”).] and becomes rigid. And I told your disciples to cast it out, but they were unable.” And he answered them and said, “O unbelieving generation, [Col. 0790] how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.” And they brought him to him. When the unclean spirit saw him, it immediately convulsed him; and falling on the ground, he rolled about foaming. And Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He said, “From childhood. For it has often thrown him both into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us and have mercy on us.” But Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to one who believes.” [Col. 0791] And immediately the father of the boy cried out with tears, saying, “I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.” But when Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, he sternly rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Deaf and mute spirit, I command you: come out of him, and enter into him no more.” And crying out and violently convulsing him, it came out of him; and he became like one dead, so that many said that he was dead. But Jesus, taking his hand, raised him, and he stood up.

And when he had entered the house, his disciples asked him privately, saying, “Why were we unable [Col. 0792] to cast it out?” And he said to them, “This kind can be driven out by nothing except prayer and fasting.” And departing from there, they journeyed through Galilee, and he did not wish anyone to know. For he taught his disciples and said to them, “The Son of Man shall be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and, having been killed, he will rise on the third day.” But they did not understand this saying and were afraid to ask him.

And he came to Capernaum. Having entered the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing with one another on the way?” But they were silent, for [Col. 0793] they had been discussing among themselves [Note: [Col. 0793] After “for,” “on the way” is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis and the Gothic version.] who was the greatest among them. And sitting down, he called the Twelve and said to them, “If anyone wishes to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.” And taking a child, he set him in their midst; and embracing him, he said to them, “Whoever receives one of such children in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.”

John answered him, saying, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade [Col. 0794] him, because he does not follow us.” But Jesus said, “Do not forbid him; for no one who performs a mighty work in my name can quickly speak evil of me. For whoever is not against you is for you. For whoever gives you a cup of cold water to drink in my name, because you belong to Christ—amen, I say to you—shall not lose his reward. And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it is better for him if a millstone turned by an ass were hung around [Col. 0795] his neck and he were thrown into the sea.

“And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than, having two hands, to be thrown into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire, where their worm does not die. And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire, where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched. [Col. 0796] And if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire, where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched. For everyone shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt. Salt is good; but if salt becomes tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace among yourselves.”

And rising from there, he came into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan. Crowds again came together [Col. 0797] to him, and, as was his custom, he again taught them. And Pharisees approached and questioned him, testing him: “Is it lawful for a man to dismiss his wife?” He answered and said to them, “What did Moses command you?” They said, “Moses permitted a certificate of divorce to be written and a wife to be dismissed.” Jesus answered and said to them, “Because of the hardness of your heart Moses wrote this commandment for you. But from the beginning of creation God made [Note: [Col. 0797] Before “God,” “them” is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis, Greek, Latin, and Gothic. In the same place, with the same Codex Cantabrigiensis, it adds “and said,” from Matthew. Yet some Greek manuscripts cited by Mill also have it.] them male and female. Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother [Note: [Col. 0797] Adds “his,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *heautou* (“his own”).] and shall cleave to his wife [Col. 0798], and the two shall become one flesh. Thus they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined, let no person separate.”

And in the house his disciples again asked him about the same matter. And he said to them, “Whoever dismisses his wife and marries another commits adultery against her. And if a woman dismisses her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.” And they brought little children to him so that he might touch them; but his disciples sternly rebuked those bringing them. When Jesus saw it, he was indignant and said to them, “Allow [Col. 0799] the little children to come to me, and do not forbid them; for to such belongs the kingdom of God. Amen, I say to you: whoever does not receive the kingdom as a little child shall not enter it.” And gathering them, he laid his hands upon them and blessed them.

And as he was going out onto the road, a certain man ran up, bent the knee before him, and asked him [Note: [Col. 0799] And thus Codex Cantabrigiensis: *legōn* (“saying”).], saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do in order to possess eternal life?” But Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except the one God. You know the commandments: Do not [Col. 0800] commit adultery. Do not bear false witness. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother [Note: [Col. 0799] Adds “your,” also the Gothic codex: *sou* (“your”).].” He answered and said to him, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.” Jesus, looking at him, loved him and said to him, “One thing is lacking to you: go, sell all that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” But he, saddened by [Note: [Col. 0799] Adds “this,” likewise the Gothic codex: *toutō* (“this”).] this saying, went away sorrowful, for he had many possessions.

And Jesus, looking around, said to his disciples, [Col. 0801] “How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter into the kingdom of God!” But the disciples [Note: [Col. 0801] Adds “his,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *autou* (“his”).] were astonished at his words. Jesus again answered and said to them, “Children, how difficult it is for those who trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God. It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter into the kingdom of God.” But they were still more astonished, saying to themselves, “Then who can be saved?” Jesus looked at them and said, “With men it is impossible, but with God it is possible; for all things are possible with God.” Peter began to say to him, “Behold, we have left everything and followed [Col. 0802] you.” Jesus answered and said, “Amen, I say to you: there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or mother, or father, or wife, or children, or possessions, for my sake and for the Gospel’s, who shall not receive a hundredfold now in this present time—houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and lands, with persecutions—and in the age to come eternal life. But many who are first shall be last, and the last first.”

Now they were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going before them. They were astonished, and those following him were afraid. And again taking the Twelve, [Col. 0803] he began to tell them what was going to happen to him: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered to the chief priests and [Note: [Col. 0803] After “scribes,” “and elders” is lacking, also in the Greek text.] scribes; they shall condemn him to death and deliver him to the Gentiles. They shall mock him, spit upon him, scourge him, kill him, and on the third day he shall rise again.”

And James and John, sons of Zebedee, approached him, saying, “Teacher, we wish you to do for us whatever we ask of you.” But Jesus said to them, “What do you wish me to do for you?” They said [Col. 0804] [Note: [Col. 0803] Adds “to him,” also the Greek text: *autō*.] to him, “Grant to us that one may sit at your right hand and the other at your left in your glory.” But Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup which I am about to drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?” They said to him, “We are able.” Jesus said to them, “The cup which I drink, you shall indeed drink; and with the baptism with which I am baptized, you shall be baptized. But to sit at my right hand or at my left is not mine to give to you, but belongs to those for whom it has been prepared.”

When the ten heard it, they began to be indignant [Col. 0805] concerning James and John. But Jesus, calling them, said to them, “You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their chiefs exercise authority over them. But it is not so [Note: [Col. 0805] After “is,” “but” is lacking, also in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] among you. Rather, whoever wishes to be great [Note: [Col. 0805] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *einai* (“to be”).] among you [Note: [Col. 0805] Adds “among you,” also the Greek text: *en hymin*.] shall be your servant; and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be servant of all. For even the Son of Man came not [Note: [Col. 0805] Thus also the Greek text: *diakonēthēnai, alla diakonēsai* (“to be served, but to serve”).] to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

And they came to Jericho. And as he was going out from there with his disciples [Note: [Col. 0805] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *apo ekeinthen meta tōn mathētōn* (“from there with the disciples”).] and a very great [Col. 0806] crowd, behold, a certain blind man, the son of Timaeus—Bartimaeus—was sitting beside the road, begging. When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.” Many sternly rebuked him, telling him to be silent; but he cried out much more, “Son of David, have mercy on me.” Jesus stopped and ordered him to be called. They called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage; rise, he calls you.” Throwing off his garment, he sprang up and came to Jesus. Jesus answered and said to him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see.” [Col. 0807] Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has made you well.” And immediately he saw and followed him on the road.

And when he drew near [Note: [Col. 0807] Codex Cantabrigiensis has: *eis Hierosolyma* (“to Jerusalem”).] to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the village opposite you. Immediately upon entering it, you will find there a colt tied, upon which no human being has yet sat. Untie it and bring it. And if anyone says to you, [Note: [Col. 0807] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *ti lyete ton pōlon* (“Why are you untying the colt?”), from Luke, ch. XIX, v. 33.] ‘Why are you untying the colt?’ say, ‘The Lord has need of it,’ and immediately he will send it here.”

They went away and found the colt tied before [Col. 0808] the outer door, at the crossroads, and untied it. Some who stood there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?” But they told them as Jesus had commanded them, and they allowed them to go. They brought the colt to Jesus, put their garments upon it, and he sat upon it. Many spread their garments on the road; others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road. Those going before and those following cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed [Col. 0809] is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!” And when [Note: [Col. 0809] Thus also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *eiselthōn* (“having entered”).] Jesus entered Jerusalem and the temple, he looked around at everything; and, since the hour was already late, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve [Note: [Col. 0809] Adds “his disciples,” also Codex Cantabrigiensis: *mathētōn autou*, together with Bodleian 4 and 5 in Mill. In the Veronese and Brescian [codices], “his” is lacking.].

On the next day, as they went out from Bethany, he was hungry. Seeing from afar a fig tree with leaves, he came, perhaps to find something on it. But when he came to it, he found nothing on it except leaves, for it was not the season for figs. And he answered and said to it, “May no one ever again [Col. 0810] eat fruit from you forever.” And his disciples heard it.

And they came again to Jerusalem. When Jesus entered the temple, he began to drive out those selling and buying in the temple; he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves. He did not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple. And he taught, saying to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.” When the chief priests and scribes heard this, [Col. 0811] they sought how they might destroy him; for they feared him, because all the people were astonished at his teaching. And when evening came, he went out of the city.

As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. Peter remembered and said to him, “Rabbi, behold, the fig tree which you cursed has withered.” Jesus answered and said to them, “Have faith in God. Amen, I say to you: whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up from here and cast into the sea,’ and does not doubt [Col. 0812] in his heart, but believes that what he says will happen, it shall happen for him. Therefore I say to you: whatever things you ask in prayer, believe that you will receive them, and they shall come to you. And when you stand to pray, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive you your sins.”

And they came again to Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, [Col. 0813] and elders came to him and said, “By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority to do these things?” Jesus answered and said to them, “I too shall ask you one question. [Note: [Col. 0813] Before “answer,” “also” is lacking, likewise in Codex Cantabrigiensis.] Answer me, and I shall tell you by what authority I do these things. Was John’s baptism from heaven or from men? Answer me.” They reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From men’—we fear the people, for all [Note: [Col. 0813] In accordance with Codex Cantabrigiensis: *ēdeisan* (“knew”).] knew that John was truly a prophet.” And answering, they said to Jesus [Col. 0814], “We do not know.” And Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

And he began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, surrounded it with a hedge, dug a winepress-pit, built a tower, leased it to tenants, and went abroad. At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants, that they might give him of the fruit of the vineyard. But they seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed. Again he sent them another servant; and they wounded him on the head and treated him shamefully. [Col. 0815] And again.”

At this point the Silver Codex is mutilated by an entire quire; for what we read in the Vulgate from chapter XII, verse 5, through XIII, verse 32, is missing here. Whether through the carelessness of the binder or through another act of sacrilege is uncertain. After [Col. 0816] the final words, “And again,” which close the facing page, the note “Q. XLVI.” is written below in the corner of the margin; after as many other [quires] comes “Q. XLVIII.” Then the sequence of this Gospel continues as follows.

[Col. 0817] At this point the Silver Codex is mutilated by an entire quire; for what we read in the Vulgate from chapter XII, [Col. 0818] verse 5, through XIII, verse 32, is missing here. Whether through the carelessness of the binder or through another act of sacrilege is uncertain.
